# Staff Health Reimbursement Plan Rules
Issued by the Staff Welfare Fund

## 1. Definitions
- **1.1** Major restorative work means crowns, bridges, root canal treatment and implants.
- **1.2** Orthodontics means braces and clear aligners.
- **1.3** Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.

## 2. Limits and deductible
- **2.1** Dental Care: limit $1,500 per treatment; deductible $50 per claim.
- **2.2** Vision Care: limit $400 per treatment; deductible $40 per claim.
- **2.3** Therapy Services: limit $2,000 per treatment; deductible $50 per claim.
- **2.4** Hearing Care: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $150 per claim.
- **2.5** The deductible is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

## 3. Dental Care
- **3.1** We will reimburse the cost of dental treatment provided by a licensed dentist.
- **3.2** No cover applies under this section to any treatment that happens within the first 90 days after the policy start date.
- **3.3** The most we will pay for Major restorative work under this section is $750 per treatment.
- **3.4** The most we will pay for Orthodontics under this section is $600 per treatment.
- **3.5** We will not pay for treatment that is mainly cosmetic, such as whitening or veneers. This exclusion does not apply to treatment needed to repair damage caused by an accident.
- **3.6** We will not pay for treatment by a provider outside the plan's network. This exclusion does not apply to emergency treatment for sudden severe pain.

## 4. General exclusions
- **4.1** We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
- **4.2** We will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits us from paying.
- **4.3** We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.

## 5. Making a claim
- **5.1** You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
- **5.2** We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
- **5.3** You must notify us of a claim within 60 days of the treatment. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.

## 6. Currency
- **6.1** All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
- **6.2** Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

## 7. Communication
- **7.1** We will communicate with you in English.
- **7.2** We may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

## 8. Recovery of costs
- **8.1** If we pay a claim that is later found not to be covered, we may ask you to repay the amount.

## 9. Salvage
- **9.1** When we replace an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes our property.
- **9.2** If stolen property is recovered after we have paid a claim, you must tell us and either return the payment or give us the property.

=== CLAIM ===
From: Mateo Iyer

Hello,

I would like to claim under Dental Care for root canal treatment. My policy started on October 2, 2025 and my schedule lists Dental Care, Vision Care, Therapy Services (extensions: none). The treatment happened on January 4, 2026. The dentist recommended the treatment after a routine check-up. Mateo joined the company's finance team two years ago. Mateo's spouse is also enrolled in the plan. The provider issued an itemised invoice.

I am sending this on January 20, 2026, which is when I first notified you. Your adjuster assessed the loss at $704.

Thanks,
Mateo

policy: STAFF HEALTH REIMBURSEMENT PLAN RULES
Issued by the Staff Welfare Fund

PART I: Definitions
I.1  Frames means spectacle frames bought without new lenses.
I.2  Hearing accessories means batteries, chargers and cleaning kits.
I.3  Hearing aid replacement period means 24 months from the purchase of hearing aids funded by the plan.
I.4  Limit means the most the Plan will pay for all claims under a section arising from one treatment.
I.5  Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
I.6  Replacement period means 24 months from the date of the Member's last eyewear claim.

PART II: Limits and deductible
II.1  Dental Care: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $50 per claim.
II.2  Vision Care: limit $500 per treatment; deductible $25 per claim.
II.3  Therapy Services: limit $2,000 per treatment; deductible $50 per claim.
II.4  Hearing Care: limit $2,000 per treatment; deductible $100 per claim.
II.5  Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the deductible is then deducted from the result.

PART III: Optional cover: Hearing Care
III.1  The Plan will reimburse hearing tests and hearing aids.
III.2  This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Member's schedule.
III.3  The most the Plan will pay for Hearing accessories under this section is $150 per treatment.
III.4  The Plan will not pay for replacement hearing aids bought within the hearing aid replacement period.

PART IV: Instalment agreements
IV.1  If the Member pays by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
IV.2  Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

PART V: Vision Care
V.1  The Plan will reimburse eye tests and prescription eyewear.
V.2  The most the Plan will pay for Frames under this section is $150 per treatment.
V.3  The Plan will not pay for eyewear without prescription lenses.
V.4  The Plan will not pay for a further eyewear claim within the replacement period.

PART VI: Environmental commitment
VI.1  Where practical, the Plan will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
VI.2  The Member may ask for a new part instead, and the Plan will tell the Member whether any additional cost would apply.

PART VII: General exclusions
VII.1  The Plan will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Member.
VII.2  The Plan will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
VII.3  The Plan will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.

PART VIII: Data protection
VIII.1  The Plan will use the personal information the Member provides to administer this policy and to handle claims.
VIII.2  The Plan will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
VIII.3  The Member can ask for a copy of the personal information the Plan holds by writing to the Plan's data protection officer.

PART IX: Making a claim
IX.1  The Member must notify the Plan of a claim within 14 days of the treatment. The Plan will not pay any claim notified after that time.
IX.2  The Member must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
IX.3  The Plan may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

PART X: Renewal
X.1  The Plan will write to the Member at least 21 days before the end of the policy period with the renewal terms.
X.2  The Plan is not obliged to offer renewal.

Issued by Hearthstone Insurance plc

PART I: Definitions
I.1  Art and antiques means paintings, antiques, rugs and other works of art.
I.2  Garden items means garden furniture, plants and outdoor tools.
I.3  Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in the Policyholder's schedule.
I.4  Portable electronics means laptops, tablets and mobile phones.
I.5  Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.

PART II: Limits and excess
II.1  Theft: limit $10,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
II.2  Escape of Water: limit $30,000 per incident; excess $1,000 per claim.
II.3  Accidental Damage: limit $2,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
II.4  Flood: limit $20,000 per incident; excess $1,000 per claim.
II.5  The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

PART III: Optional cover: Accidental Damage
III.1  The Insurer will pay for sudden and unexpected accidental damage to the Policyholder's contents inside the home.
III.2  This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Policyholder's schedule.
III.3  The most the Insurer will pay for Portable electronics under this section is $500 per incident.
III.4  The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by pets.
III.5  The Insurer will not pay for wear and tear, or damage that happens gradually.

PART IV: Escape of Water
IV.1  The Insurer will pay for contents damaged by water escaping from a fixed pipe, tank or domestic appliance.
IV.2  The most the Insurer will pay for Art and antiques under this section is $2,000 per incident.
IV.3  The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by water leaking gradually over a period of time.
IV.4  The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by the failure of grout or sealant around baths and showers.

PART V: Flood
V.1  The Insurer will pay for contents damaged by flood water entering the Policyholder's home.
V.2  No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 60 days after the policy start date.
V.3  The most the Insurer will pay for Garden items under this section is $1,000 per incident.
V.4  The Insurer will not pay for flood damage where a flood warning for the Policyholder's area had been issued before the policy started.

PART VI: General exclusions
VI.1  The Insurer will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
VI.2  The Insurer will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Policyholder.
VI.3  The Insurer will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.

PART VII: Making a claim
VII.1  The Policyholder must notify the Insurer of a claim within 14 days of the incident. The Insurer will not pay any claim notified after that time.
VII.2  The Insurer may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
VII.3  The Policyholder must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.

state: Gundam Wing is a fun show. I appreciate it for getting me into Gundam and anime in general. However, after watching its predecessors, such as Mobile Suit Gundam, Zeta Gundam, and even G Gundam, I find Wing to be Gundam Lite. Characters: An aspect long held by Gundam is to have their characters thrust into difficulties and grow into maturity. This does not happen in Wing. Heero is top dog at the beginning, and he's top dog at the end. Personalities do not change, growth is never achieved. The best character is Zechs, who is for all intents and purposes a hero throughout most of the series. But suddenly the series betrays him and turns him into a villain for no apparent reason. Mecha: Wing has great suit designs. The Gundams are super cool, with the Epyon being my favorite. I even consider a few of the OZ suit designs to be on par with some of the classic Zeon suits. But sweet suit designs doesn't quite save the series from boring characters. Conclusion: In the end, Wing has cool fight scenes, though riddled with recycled animation, but shallow plot and character development. Enjoyable, but not moving like previous Gundam outings.

(a) Contents means household goods and personal possessions that belong to the Policyholder or the Policyholder's family.
(b) Garden items means garden furniture, plants and outdoor tools.

Article 3. Flood
(a) The Insurer will pay for contents damaged by flood water entering the Policyholder's home.
(b) No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 14 days after the policy start date.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Garden items under this section is $500 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for flood damage where a flood warning for the Policyholder's area had been issued before the policy started.

Article 4. General exclusions
(a) The Insurer will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
(b) The Insurer will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits the Insurer from paying.

Article 5. Making a claim
(a) The Policyholder must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
(b) The Insurer may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
(c) The Policyholder must notify the Insurer of a claim within 21 days of the incident. The Insurer will not pay any claim notified after that time.

Article 6. Payment of claims
(a) The Insurer will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in the Policyholder's name.
(b) The Insurer aims to pay accepted claims within 10 working days of receiving all the documents the Insurer needs.

Article 7. Tenant's improvements
(a) If the Policyholder rents the home, the Insurer will pay for damage to fixtures and fittings that the Policyholder installed and are responsible for.
(b) This cover applies only to improvements the Policyholder paid for, not to items provided by the landlord.

Article 8. Salvage
(a) When the Insurer replaces an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes the Insurer's property.
(b) If stolen property is recovered after the Insurer has paid a claim, the Policyholder must tell the Insurer and either return the payment or give the Insurer the property.

Article 9. Complaints
(a) If the Policyholder has a complaint, the Policyholder should first contact the Insurer's customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
(b) The Insurer will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
(c) If the Policyholder remains dissatisfied, the Policyholder may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

Article 10. Notices
(a) Any notice the Insurer gives under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address the Insurer holds.
(b) Notices from the Policyholder should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

Article 11. Exchange of information
(a) To prevent fraud, the Insurer may check the details the Policyholder gives against public records and industry databases.
(b) The Insurer may contact previous insurers to confirm the Policyholder's claims history.

# Single-Trip Travel Protection Plan
Issued by Bluewater Assurance

## 1. Definitions
- **1.1** Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by us, before any excess, limit or sublimit is applied.
- **1.2** Dental treatment means treatment of the teeth or gums.
- **1.3** Excursions and tickets means pre-booked excursions, tours, and event or theatre tickets.
- **1.4** Family means your spouse or partner and any children who live with you.
- **1.5** Hazardous activity means skydiving, motor racing, or trekking or climbing above 4,500 metres.
- **1.6** Physiotherapy means treatment of muscles and joints by a physiotherapist.
- **1.7** Pre-existing condition means any illness or injury for which you received treatment or advice in the 6 months before the policy start date.
- **1.8** Qualifying delay means a delay to the scheduled departure of more than 8 hours.

## 2. Limits and excess
- **2.1** Baggage and Personal Belongings: limit $1,500 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
- **2.2** Emergency Medical Expenses: limit $25,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
- **2.3** Trip Cancellation: limit $2,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
- **2.4** Travel Delay: limit $300 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
- **2.5** Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the excess is then deducted from the result.

## 3. Emergency Medical Expenses
- **3.1** We will pay reasonable and necessary emergency medical costs incurred during the trip.
- **3.2** The most we will pay for Dental treatment under this section is $400 per incident.
- **3.3** The most we will pay for Physiotherapy under this section is $300 per incident.
- **3.4** We will not pay for treatment of a pre-existing condition.
- **3.5** We will not pay for injury or illness arising from a hazardous activity. This exclusion does not apply if the Adventure Sports extension is shown in your schedule.
- **3.6** We will not pay for any claim arising from your being under the influence of alcohol or drugs.

## 4. Optional cover: Travel Delay
- **4.1** We will pay reasonable costs of meals and accommodation if your outbound departure is delayed.
- **4.2** This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
- **4.3** We will not pay for any delay that is not a qualifying delay.

## 5. Trip Cancellation
- **5.1** We will pay non-refundable travel and accommodation costs if you must cancel the trip for a reason beyond your control.
- **5.2** No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 10 days after the policy start date.
- **5.3** The most we will pay for Excursions and tickets under this section is $200 per incident.
- **5.4** We will not pay for cancellation caused by a strike or other event that had been publicly announced before you bought the policy.
- **5.5** We will not pay for cancellation because you no longer wish to travel.

## 6. General exclusions
- **6.1** We will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by you.
- **6.2** We will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
- **6.3** We will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.

## 7. Making a claim
- **7.1** You must notify us of a claim within 90 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.
- **7.2** You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
- **7.3** We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

=== CLAIM ===
From: Mateo Laine
Subject: Claim on policy B499145

Hello,

I would like to claim under Travel Delay for meals and taxis during a long airport delay. My policy started on June 21, 2025 and my schedule lists Baggage and Personal Belongings, Emergency Medical Expenses, Trip Cancellation, Travel Delay (extensions: none). The incident happened on February 13, 2026. The departure was delayed by 10 hours. The delay was caused by a technical fault with the aircraft. The trip was booked through an online travel agent. The destination was a coastal town Mateo had visited before. Mateo paid for the trip with a credit card.

I am sending this on May 16, 2026, which is when I first notified you. Your adjuster assessed the loss at $365.25.

Thanks,
Mateo

policy: HOME CONTENTS INSURANCE POLICY
Issued by Lantern General Insurance

PART I: Definitions
I.1  Art and antiques means paintings, antiques, rugs and other works of art.
I.2  Bicycles means bicycles and electric scooters.
I.3  Contents means household goods and personal possessions that belong to the Policyholder or the Policyholder's family.
I.4  Family means the Policyholder's spouse or partner and any children who live with the Policyholder.
I.5  Garden items means garden furniture, plants and outdoor tools.
I.6  High-risk items means jewellery, watches, laptops, games consoles and cameras.
I.7  Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows the Policyholder's details, the covers the Policyholder bought and any extensions.
I.8  Unoccupied means not lived in by the Policyholder or a member of the Policyholder's family for more than 30 consecutive days.

PART II: Limits and excess
II.1  Theft: limit $10,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
II.2  Escape of Water: limit $15,000 per incident; excess $1,000 per claim.
II.3  Accidental Damage: limit $5,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
II.4  Flood: limit $20,000 per incident; excess $1,000 per claim.
II.5  The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

PART III: Escape of Water
III.1  The Insurer will pay for contents damaged by water escaping from a fixed pipe, tank or domestic appliance.
III.2  The most the Insurer will pay for Art and antiques under this section is $1,000 per incident.
III.3  The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by water leaking gradually over a period of time.
III.4  The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by the failure of grout or sealant around baths and showers.

PART IV: Flood
IV.1  The Insurer will pay for contents damaged by flood water entering the Policyholder's home.
IV.2  No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 30 days after the policy start date.
IV.3  The most the Insurer will pay for Garden items under this section is $500 per incident.
IV.4  The Insurer will not pay for flood damage where a flood warning for the Policyholder's area had been issued before the policy started.

PART V: Theft
V.1  The Insurer will pay for contents stolen from the Policyholder's home.
V.2  The most the Insurer will pay for High-risk items under this section is $1,000 per incident.
V.3  The most the Insurer will pay for Bicycles under this section is $800 per incident.
V.4  The Insurer will not pay for theft while the home is unoccupied.
V.5  The Insurer will not pay for theft where there is no sign of forced entry to the home. This exclusion does not apply where the thief gained entry by deception, for example by posing as a utility worker.
V.6  The Insurer will not pay for theft from sheds, garages or other outbuildings. This exclusion does not apply if the outbuilding was locked and the theft involved forcible entry.

PART VI: General exclusions
VI.1  The Insurer will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Policyholder.
VI.2  The Insurer will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits the Insurer from paying.

PART VII: Making a claim
VII.1  The Policyholder must notify the Insurer of a claim within 14 days of the incident. The Insurer will not pay any claim notified after that time.
VII.2  The Policyholder must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
VII.3  The Insurer may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

## 1. Definitions

- **2.4** Hearing Care: limit $2,000 per treatment; deductible $150 per claim.

Issued by Brightline Device Cover

PART I: Definitions
I.1  Battery replacement means replacement batteries and battery repairs.
I.2  Breakdown means the failure of a part to work as the manufacturer intended, from an internal electrical or mechanical fault.
I.3  Family means the Customer's spouse or partner and any children who live with the Customer.
I.4  Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
I.5  Manufacturer's warranty period means the first 12 months after the device was bought.

PART II: Limits and service fee
II.1  Accidental Damage: limit $800 per incident; service fee $99 per claim.
II.2  Breakdown: limit $1,000 per incident; service fee $25 per claim.
II.3  Theft and Loss: limit $800 per incident; service fee $99 per claim.
II.4  The service fee is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

PART III: Breakdown
III.1  The Provider will repair or replace the Customer's device if it stops working because of an electrical or mechanical fault.
III.2  No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 45 days after the policy start date.
III.3  The most the Provider will pay for Battery replacement under this section is $80 per incident.
III.4  The Provider will not pay for breakdowns during the manufacturer's warranty period.
III.5  The Provider will not pay for breakdown caused by liquid getting into the device.

PART IV: General exclusions
IV.1  The Provider will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
IV.2  The Provider will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
IV.3  The Provider will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits the Provider from paying.

PART V: Making a claim
V.1  The Provider may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
V.2  The Customer must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
V.3  The Customer must notify the Provider of a claim within 14 days of the incident. The Provider will not pay any claim notified after that time.

PART VI: Software support
VI.1  The Provider's helpline can give advice on setting up and using the Customer's device.
VI.2  Software support does not include fixing problems caused by third-party apps or unofficial operating systems.

PART VII: Claims documents
VII.1  The Customer must provide, at the Customer's own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence the Provider reasonably ask for.
VII.2  The Provider may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

PART VIII: Salvage
VIII.1  When the Provider replaces an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes the Provider's property.
VIII.2  If stolen property is recovered after the Provider has paid a claim, the Customer must tell the Provider and either return the payment or give the Provider the property.

PART IX: Market conditions
IX.1  If the replacement item is no longer available, the Provider will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

Issued by Wellspring Benefits Administration

PART I: Definitions
I.1  Frames means spectacle frames bought without new lenses.

VIII.1  The Plan will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Member.

policy: RENTERS CONTENTS PROTECTION
Issued by Keystone Home Mutual

PART I: Definitions
I.1  Art and antiques means paintings, antiques, rugs and other works of art.
I.2  Bicycles means bicycles and electric scooters.
I.3  Family means the Policyholder's spouse or partner and any children who live with the Policyholder.
I.4  Forcible entry means entry to the home that leaves visible damage to doors, windows or locks.
I.5  Garden items means garden furniture, plants and outdoor tools.
I.6  High-risk items means jewellery, watches, laptops, games consoles and cameras.
I.7  Unoccupied means not lived in by the Policyholder or a member of the Policyholder's family for more than 30 consecutive days.

PART II: Limits and excess
II.1  Theft: limit $40,000 per incident; excess $250 per claim.
II.2  Escape of Water: limit $30,000 per incident; excess $1,000 per claim.
II.3  Accidental Damage: limit $3,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
II.4  Flood: limit $40,000 per incident; excess $1,000 per claim.
II.5  The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

PART III: Theft
III.1  The Insurer will pay for contents stolen from the Policyholder's home.
III.2  The most the Insurer will pay for High-risk items under this section is $2,500 per incident.
III.3  The most the Insurer will pay for Bicycles under this section is $500 per incident.
III.4  The Insurer will not pay for theft while the home is unoccupied.
III.5  The Insurer will not pay for theft where there is no sign of forced entry to the home. This exclusion does not apply where the thief gained entry by deception, for example by posing as a utility worker.
III.6  The Insurer will not pay for theft from sheds, garages or other outbuildings. This exclusion does not apply if the outbuilding was locked and the theft involved forcible entry.

PART IV: Flood
IV.1  The Insurer will pay for contents damaged by flood water entering the Policyholder's home.
IV.2  No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 30 days after the policy start date.
IV.3  The most the Insurer will pay for Garden items under this section is $1,000 per incident.
IV.4  The Insurer will not pay for flood damage where a flood warning for the Policyholder's area had been issued before the policy started.

PART V: Escape of Water
V.1  The Insurer will pay for contents damaged by water escaping from a fixed pipe, tank or domestic appliance.
V.2  The most the Insurer will pay for Art and antiques under this section is $1,000 per incident.
V.3  The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by water leaking gradually over a period of time.
V.4  The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by the failure of grout or sealant around baths and showers.

PART VI: General exclusions
VI.1  The Insurer will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Policyholder.
VI.2  The Insurer will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.

PART VII: Making a claim
VII.1  The Insurer may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
VII.2  The Policyholder must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
VII.3  The Policyholder must notify the Insurer of a claim within 21 days of the incident. The Insurer will not pay any claim notified after that time.

Sidney Lumet, a legendary director of some of the best films of the 20th century, really misstepped here by making one of the biggest mistakes a filmmaker can: filling a film's cast with thoroughly unlikeable characters with no real redeeming qualities whatsoever. I like films with flawed characters, but no matter how dark someone's personality is we all have a bit of light in there too, we're all shades of gray with some darker or brighter than others. # Household Contents Cover: Policy Booklet
Issued by Hearthstone Insurance plc

## 1. Definitions
- **1.1** Bicycles means bicycles and electric scooters.
- **1.2** High-risk items means jewellery, watches, laptops, games consoles and cameras.
- **1.3** Limit means the most we will pay for all claims under a section arising from one incident.
- **1.4** Portable electronics means laptops, tablets and mobile phones.
- **1.5** Unoccupied means not lived in by you or a member of your family for more than 45 consecutive days.

## 2. Limits and excess
- **2.1** Theft: limit $10,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
- **2.2** Escape of Water: limit $15,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
- **2.3** Accidental Damage: limit $5,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
- **2.4** Flood: limit $40,000 per incident; excess $1,000 per claim.
- **2.5** The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

## 3. Optional cover: Accidental Damage
- **3.1** We will pay for sudden and unexpected accidental damage to your contents inside the home.
- **3.2** This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
- **3.3** The most we will pay for Portable electronics under this section is $500 per incident.
- **3.4** We will not pay for damage caused by pets.
- **3.5** We will not pay for wear and tear, or damage that happens gradually.

## 4. Alternative accommodation
- **4.1** If your home cannot be lived in after damage covered by this policy, we will pay the reasonable cost of comparable temporary accommodation.
- **4.2** We will also pay for the temporary housing of pets that live with you.
- **4.3** Cover ends when the home is fit to live in again or after twelve months, whichever is sooner.

## 5. Theft
- **5.1** We will pay for contents stolen from your home.
- **5.2** The most we will pay for High-risk items under this section is $1,500 per incident.
- **5.3** The most we will pay for Bicycles under this section is $800 per incident.
- **5.4** We will not pay for theft while the home is unoccupied.
- **5.5** We will not pay for theft where there is no sign of forced entry to the home. This exclusion does not apply where the thief gained entry by deception, for example by posing as a utility worker.
- **5.6** We will not pay for theft from sheds, garages or other outbuildings. This exclusion does not apply if the outbuilding was locked and the theft involved forcible entry.

## 6. General exclusions
- **6.1** We will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits us from paying.
- **6.2** We will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
- **6.3** We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.

## 7. Making a claim
- **7.1** You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
- **7.2** You must notify us of a claim within 90 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.
- **7.3** We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

Jonas

state: In my opinion, this is one of the greatest movies ever made in America and it deserved every single award it won and it's place on the AFI Top 100 list (though it's shamefully too low on the IMDB Top 250 list, at only #183 as of this writing). If you enjoy acting of the highest calibre (Voight and Hoffman are a superb match), well-drawn characterizations and inventive direction, editing and cinematography, you'll love this just as much as I did. Schlesinger paints a vivid, always credible picture of the late 60s New York City scene and it's many victims struggling to overcome personal demons and survive amidst the amorality, poverty and hopelessness of 42nd Street, New York City. The filmmaking techniques employed here brilliantly capture the feel of the underground New York film movement (and of the city) and are nothing less than dazzling. I've seen many ideas (including the rapid-fire editing, the handling of the voice-over flashbacks, the drug/trip sequences and the cartoonish face slipped in during a murder scene to convey angst and terror) stolen by other filmmakers. The relationship between Joe and Ratso is handled in such a way as to be viewed as an unusually strong friendship OR having it's homosexual underpinnings. # Travel Insurance Policy Wording
Issued by Northstar Underwriting

## 1. Definitions
- **1.1** Dental treatment means treatment of the teeth or gums.
- **1.2** Excursions and tickets means pre-booked excursions, tours, and event or theatre tickets.
- **1.3** Hazardous activity means skydiving, motor racing, or trekking or climbing above 4,000 metres.
- **1.4** Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
- **1.5** Physiotherapy means treatment of muscles and joints by a physiotherapist.
- **1.6** Pre-existing condition means any illness or injury for which you received treatment or advice in the 6 months before the policy start date.
- **1.7** Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
- **1.8** Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows your details, the covers you bought and any extensions.

## 2. Limits and excess
- **2.1** Baggage and Personal Belongings: limit $1,500 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
- **2.2** Emergency Medical Expenses: limit $25,000 per incident; excess $150 per claim.
- **2.3** Trip Cancellation: limit $2,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
- **2.4** Travel Delay: limit $750 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
- **2.5** The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

## 3. Trip Cancellation
- **3.1** We will pay non-refundable travel and accommodation costs if you must cancel the trip for a reason beyond your control.
- **3.2** No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 10 days after the policy start date.
- **3.3** The most we will pay for Excursions and tickets under this section is $300 per incident.
- **3.4** We will not pay for cancellation caused by a strike or other event that had been publicly announced before you bought the policy.
- **3.5** We will not pay for cancellation because you no longer wish to travel.

## 4. Emergency Medical Expenses
- **4.1** We will pay reasonable and necessary emergency medical costs incurred during the trip.
- **4.2** The most we will pay for Dental treatment under this section is $250 per incident.
- **4.3** The most we will pay for Physiotherapy under this section is $500 per incident.
- **4.4** We will not pay for treatment of a pre-existing condition.
- **4.5** We will not pay for injury or illness arising from a hazardous activity. This exclusion does not apply if the Adventure Sports extension is shown in your schedule.
- **4.6** We will not pay for any claim arising from your being under the influence of alcohol or drugs.

## 5. General exclusions
- **5.1** We will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by you.
- **5.2** We will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.

## 6. Compensation scheme
- **6.1** We are covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
- **6.2** If we cannot meet our obligations, you may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

## 7. Making a claim
- **7.1** You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
- **7.2** You must notify us of a claim within 14 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.
- **7.3** We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

It's your standard Capriotti's-pretty small on the inside, nothing fancy. The employees are nice and the dining area is always clean. I wouldn't suggest making plans to dine here during the lunch hours though. This location is always packed and if you don't want to wait, call your order in. I always do and my sandwich is always ready and waiting so I don't have to wait awkwardly in the dining area and watch other people get to enjoy their tasty sandwiches.

I really like their selection of chips which I don't think you can really get anywhere else and the fact that they offer Tastykakes, which I've never had, but have read enough Stephanie Plum books to appreciate the novelty.

I guess my only beef with Capriotti's is that they serve Pepsi. That's a personal preference though, so I just never get drinks here. 

Bottom line: average Capriotti's, call ahead.

# Group Health Cash Plan
Issued by the Staff Welfare Fund

## 1. Definitions
- **1.1** Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by us, before any deductible, limit or sublimit is applied.
- **1.2** Dependant means your spouse or partner, or a child under 21 who is enrolled in the plan.
- **1.3** Hearing accessories means batteries, chargers and cleaning kits.
- **1.4** Hearing aid replacement period means 24 months from the purchase of hearing aids funded by the plan.
- **1.5** Massage therapy means sports massage, massage therapy and reflexology.
- **1.6** Premium means the amount you must pay for this policy, including any taxes.

## 2. Limits and deductible
- **2.1** Dental Care: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $100 per claim.
- **2.2** Vision Care: limit $500 per treatment; deductible $25 per claim.
- **2.3** Therapy Services: limit $2,000 per treatment; deductible $50 per claim.
- **2.4** Hearing Care: limit $2,000 per treatment; deductible $150 per claim.
- **2.5** The deductible is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

## 3. Optional cover: Hearing Care
- **3.1** We will reimburse hearing tests and hearing aids.
- **3.2** This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
- **3.3** The most we will pay for Hearing accessories under this section is $150 per treatment.
- **3.4** We will not pay for replacement hearing aids bought within the hearing aid replacement period.

## 4. Data protection
- **4.1** We will use the personal information you provide to administer this policy and to handle claims.
- **4.2** We will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
- **4.3** You can ask for a copy of the personal information we hold by writing to our data protection officer.

## 5. Therapy Services
- **5.1** We will reimburse physiotherapy, osteopathy and counselling provided by a registered practitioner.
- **5.2** The most we will pay for Massage therapy under this section is $200 per treatment.
- **5.3** We will not pay for treatment of an injury covered by workers' compensation.
- **5.4** We will not pay for treatment by a practitioner who is not registered with the relevant professional body.

## 6. General exclusions
- **6.1** We will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by you.
- **6.2** We will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.

## 7. Making a claim
- **7.1** We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
- **7.2** You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
- **7.3** You must notify us of a claim within 60 days of the treatment. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.

## 8. Fraud
- **8.1** If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, we will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
- **8.2** We may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

STAFF HEALTH REIMBURSEMENT PLAN RULES
Issued by the Benefits Trust

SECTION 1 - DEFINITIONS
1.1 Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by us, before any deductible, limit or sublimit is applied.
1.2 Hearing accessories means batteries, chargers and cleaning kits.
1.3 Hearing aid replacement period means 24 months from the purchase of hearing aids funded by the plan.
1.4 Major restorative work means crowns, bridges, root canal treatment and implants.
1.5 Orthodontics means braces and clear aligners.
1.6 Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in your schedule.

SECTION 2 - LIMITS AND DEDUCTIBLE
2.1 Dental Care: limit $2,000 per treatment; deductible $50 per claim.
2.2 Vision Care: limit $400 per treatment; deductible $40 per claim.
2.3 Therapy Services: limit $2,000 per treatment; deductible $75 per claim.
2.4 Hearing Care: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $100 per claim.
2.5 Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the deductible is then deducted from the result.

SECTION 3 - DENTAL CARE
3.1 We will reimburse the cost of dental treatment provided by a licensed dentist.
3.2 No cover applies under this section to any treatment that happens within the first 90 days after the policy start date.
3.3 The most we will pay for Major restorative work under this section is $500 per treatment.
3.4 The most we will pay for Orthodontics under this section is $600 per treatment.
3.5 We will not pay for treatment that is mainly cosmetic, such as whitening or veneers. This exclusion does not apply to treatment needed to repair damage caused by an accident.
3.6 We will not pay for treatment by a provider outside the plan's network. This exclusion does not apply to emergency treatment for sudden severe pain.

SECTION 4 - OPTIONAL COVER: HEARING CARE
4.1 We will reimburse hearing tests and hearing aids.
4.2 This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
4.3 The most we will pay for Hearing accessories under this section is $100 per treatment.
4.4 We will not pay for replacement hearing aids bought within the hearing aid replacement period.

SECTION 5 - GENERAL EXCLUSIONS
5.1 We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
5.2 We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
5.3 We will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.

SECTION 6 - MAKING A CLAIM
6.1 You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
6.2 You must notify us of a claim within 90 days of the treatment. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.
6.3 We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

SECTION 7 - CHANGE OF ADDRESS
7.1 You must tell us within 30 days if you change your address.
7.2 We may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

SECTION 8 - AUTOMATIC RENEWAL
8.1 Unless you tell us otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details we hold.
8.2 You can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting our helpline.

My parents moved to the United States from Rome in 1985, so I was very much looking forward to eating at Giada's new restaurant in Las Vegas. 

I enjoyed everything I ate; however, there were several textural issues, and salt issues with my plates. 

I began my lunch with the Burrata appetizer. Burrata (from burro, the Italian word for butter) is an extremely creamy cheese that can be pulled apart with a fork, and is often spread on bread. The Burrata was excellent, drizzled with olive oil, and served with a line of salt on the plate. Unfortunately, Giada's house bread is akin to pita bread, it consists of their pizza dough undercooked, and is served with a small ramekin of pesto, which was almost inedibly salty. Burrata really needs to be spread on hearty, crunchy bread otherwise every bite is devoid of any texture but mushiness. 

My second appetizer consisted of baby peppers stuffed with goat cheese. They were delicious; sweet, and creamy. 

For my entree I had the infamous $35 lobster roll. Again, this plate suffered from salt, and textural issues. The lobster roll consisted of one thick piece of Italian bread with a heaping pile of the lobster-centric filling on top. I tasted NO salt in the filling; however, that's an easy fix as you can always

# Electronics Care Plan
Issued by Brightline Device Cover

## 1. Definitions
- **1.1** Accessories means cases, chargers, earbuds and styluses.
- **1.2** Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
- **1.3** Wearables means smartwatches and fitness trackers.

## 2. Limits and service fee
- **2.1** Accidental Damage: limit $1,200 per incident; service fee $99 per claim.
- **2.2** Breakdown: limit $600 per incident; service fee $25 per claim.
- **2.3** Theft and Loss: limit $800 per incident; service fee $99 per claim.
- **2.4** Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the service fee is then deducted from the result.

## 3. Accidental Damage
- **3.1** We will repair or replace your device if it is accidentally damaged.
- **3.2** The most we will pay for Accessories under this section is $100 per incident.
- **3.3** The most we will pay for Wearables under this section is $250 per incident.
- **3.4** We will not pay for cosmetic damage, such as scratches or dents, that does not affect how the device works.
- **3.5** We will not pay for damage following a repair by anyone other than us or an authorised repairer. This exclusion does not apply if we approved the repair in writing beforehand.

## 4. General exclusions
- **4.1** We will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
- **4.2** We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.

## 5. Fraud
- **5.1** If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, we will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
- **5.2** We may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

## 6. Currency
- **6.1** All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
- **6.2** Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

## 7. Making a claim
- **7.1** We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
- **7.2** You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
- **7.3** You must notify us of a claim within 30 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.

## 8. Governing law
- **8.1** This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
- **8.2** Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

Issued by Circuit Care Services
In this policy, "the Provider" means Circuit Care Services and "the Customer" means the person named in the schedule.

Article 1. Definitions
(a) Authorised repairer means a repairer approved in writing by the Provider.
(b) Battery replacement means replacement batteries and battery repairs.
(c) Breakdown means the failure of a part to work as the manufacturer intended, from an internal electrical or mechanical fault.
(d) Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
(e) Manufacturer's warranty period means the first 12 months after the device was bought.

Article 2. Limits and service fee
(a) Accidental Damage: limit $1,500 per incident; service fee $99 per claim.
(b) Breakdown: limit $600 per incident; service fee $49 per claim.
(c) Theft and Loss: limit $1,200 per incident; service fee $99 per claim.
(d) Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the service fee is then deducted from the result.

Article 3. How to read this document
(a) This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.
(b) Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
(c) Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

Article 4. Breakdown
(a) The Provider will repair or replace the Customer's device if it stops working because of an electrical or mechanical fault.
(b) No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 30 days after the policy start date.
(c) The most the Provider will pay for Battery replacement under this section is $80 per incident.
(d) The Provider will not pay for breakdowns during the manufacturer's warranty period.
(e) The Provider will not pay for breakdown caused by liquid getting into the device.

Article 5. General exclusions
(a) The Provider will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits the Provider from paying.
(b) The Provider will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
(c) The Provider will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.

Article 6. Making a claim
(a) The Customer must notify the Provider of a claim within 21 days of the incident. The Provider will not pay any claim notified after that time.
(b) The Customer must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
(c) The Provider may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

policy: ANNUAL MULTI-TRIP TRAVEL COVER
Issued by Meridian Travel Insurance Ltd

PART I: Definitions
I.1  Excursions and tickets means pre-booked excursions, tours, and event or theatre tickets.
I.2  Limit means the most the Insurer will pay for all claims under a section arising from one incident.
I.3  Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in the Insured Person's schedule.
I.4  Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.

PART II: Limits and excess
II.1  Baggage and Personal Belongings: limit $2,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
II.2  Emergency Medical Expenses: limit $10,000 per incident; excess $250 per claim.
II.3  Trip Cancellation: limit $5,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
II.4  Travel Delay: limit $500 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
II.5  The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

PART III: Cooperation
III.1  The Insured Person must give the Insurer all the help and information the Insurer reasonably need to settle a claim.
III.2  The Insured Person must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without the Insurer's written permission.

PART IV: Trip Cancellation
IV.1  The Insurer will pay non-refundable travel and accommodation costs if the Insured Person must cancel the trip for a reason beyond the Insured Person's control.
IV.2  No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 7 days after the policy start date.
IV.3  The most the Insurer will pay for Excursions and tickets under this section is $200 per incident.
IV.4  The Insurer will not pay for cancellation caused by a strike or other event that had been publicly announced before the Insured Person bought the policy.
IV.5  The Insurer will not pay for cancellation because the Insured Person no longer wish to travel.

PART V: General exclusions
V.1  The Insurer will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits the Insurer from paying.
V.2  The Insurer will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.

PART VI: Third-party administrators
VI.1  The Insurer may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on the Insurer's behalf.
VI.2  Any company the Insurer appoints must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

PART VII: Making a claim
VII.1  The Insured Person must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
VII.2  The Insured Person must notify the Insurer of a claim within 21 days of the incident. The Insurer will not pay any claim notified after that time.
VII.3  The Insurer may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

In this policy, "the Plan" means Cedar Benefits Services and "the Member" means the person named in the schedule.

Article 1. Definitions
(a) Frames means spectacle frames bought without new lenses.

(a) Dental Care: limit $1,500 per treatment; deductible $50 per claim.
(b) Vision Care: limit $300 per treatment; deductible $40 per claim.
(c) Therapy Services: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $75 per claim.

(c) The Plan will not pay for eyewear without prescription lenses.

Parkey Posey is Fay Grim, an unwitting Mata Hari caught between the love of her exiled husband Henry Fool and the questionable intentions of a charming CIA operative. As Agent Fulbright, Jeff Goldblum is a master of wit and sarcasm, in a role that seems tailored to his talents. He has never been better. Issued by Lantern General Insurance

SECTION 1 - DEFINITIONS
1.1 Contents means household goods and personal possessions that belong to you or your family.
1.2 Garden items means garden furniture, plants and outdoor tools.
1.3 Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.

SECTION 2 - LIMITS AND EXCESS
2.1 Theft: limit $20,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
2.2 Escape of Water: limit $30,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
2.3 Accidental Damage: limit $5,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
2.4 Flood: limit $20,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
2.5 The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

SECTION 3 - OPTIONAL COVER: ACCIDENTAL DAMAGE
3.1 We will pay for sudden and unexpected accidental damage to your contents inside the home.
3.2 This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
3.3 The most we will pay for Portable electronics under this section is $750 per incident.
3.4 We will not pay for damage caused by pets.
3.5 We will not pay for wear and tear, or damage that happens gradually.

SECTION 4 - FLOOD
4.1 We will pay for contents damaged by flood water entering your home.
4.2 No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 60 days after the policy start date.
4.3 The most we will pay for Garden items under this section is $500 per incident.
4.4 We will not pay for flood damage where a flood warning for your area had been issued before the policy started.

SECTION 5 - GENERAL EXCLUSIONS
5.1 We will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
5.2 We will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits us from paying.
5.3 We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.

SECTION 6 - MAKING A CLAIM
6.1 You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
6.2 We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
6.3 You must notify us of a claim within 90 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.

8.1 If you rent the home, we will pay for damage to fixtures and fittings that you installed and are responsible for.
8.2 This cover applies only to improvements you paid for, not to items provided by the landlord.

SECTION 9 - GEOGRAPHICAL LIMITS
9.1 Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
9.2 Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

SECTION 10 - CLAIMS DOCUMENTS
10.1 You must provide, at your own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence we reasonably ask for.
10.2 We may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

# Travel Insurance Policy Wording
Issued by Meridian Travel Insurance Ltd

## 1. Definitions
- **1.1** Dental treatment means treatment of the teeth or gums.
- **1.2** Excursions and tickets means pre-booked excursions, tours, and event or theatre tickets.
- **1.3** Hazardous activity means skydiving, motor racing, or trekking or climbing above 4,500 metres.
- **1.4** Physiotherapy means treatment of muscles and joints by a physiotherapist.
- **1.5** Pre-existing condition means any illness or injury for which you received treatment or advice in the 3 months before the policy start date.
- **1.6** Qualifying delay means a delay to the scheduled departure of more than 12 hours.
- **1.7** Trip means a journey that starts and ends in your home country during the policy period.

## 2. Limits and excess
- **2.1** Baggage and Personal Belongings: limit $3,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
- **2.2** Emergency Medical Expenses: limit $10,000 per incident; excess $150 per claim.
- **2.3** Trip Cancellation: limit $2,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
- **2.4** Travel Delay: limit $300 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
- **2.5** Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the excess is then deducted from the result.

## 3. Optional cover: Travel Delay
- **3.1** We will pay reasonable costs of meals and accommodation if your outbound departure is delayed.
- **3.2** This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
- **3.3** We will not pay for any delay that is not a qualifying delay.

## 4. Emergency Medical Expenses
- **4.1** We will pay reasonable and necessary emergency medical costs incurred during the trip.
- **4.2** The most we will pay for Dental treatment under this section is $400 per incident.
- **4.3** The most we will pay for Physiotherapy under this section is $300 per incident.
- **4.4** We will not pay for treatment of a pre-existing condition.
- **4.5** We will not pay for injury or illness arising from a hazardous activity. This exclusion does not apply if the Adventure Sports extension is shown in your schedule.
- **4.6** We will not pay for any claim arising from your being under the influence of alcohol or drugs.

## 5. Trip Cancellation
- **5.1** We will pay non-refundable travel and accommodation costs if you must cancel the trip for a reason beyond your control.
- **5.2** No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 10 days after the policy start date.
- **5.3** The most we will pay for Excursions and tickets under this section is $200 per incident.
- **5.4** We will not pay for cancellation caused by a strike or other event that had been publicly announced before you bought the policy.
- **5.5** We will not pay for cancellation because you no longer wish to travel.

## 6. General exclusions
- **6.1** We will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by you.
- **6.2** We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.

## 7. Making a claim
- **7.1** We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
- **7.2** You must notify us of a claim within 90 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.
- **7.3** You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.

state: The film begins with promise, but lingers too long in a sepia world of distance and alienation. We are left hanging, but with nothing much else save languid shots of grave and pensive male faces to savour. Certainly no rope up the wall to help us climb over. It's a shame, because the concept is not without merit. We are left wondering why a loving couple - a father and son no less - should be so estranged from the real world that their own world is preferable when claustrophobic beyond all imagining. This loss of presence in the real world is, rather too obviously and unnecessarily, contrasted with the son having enlisted in the armed forces. Why not the circus, so we can at least appreciate some colour? We are left with a gnawing sense of loss, but sadly no enlightenment, which is bewildering given the film is apparently about some form of attainment not available to us all.

state: One of Cary Grant's most enduring comedies is Mr. Blandings Builds His Dream House. Although judging by the size of it the dwelling would be a dream mansion today. Still Cary was making a good living in the advertising field even though he was having a devil of a time trying to come up with a slogan for ham with the brand name of Wham. What made this film so popular was the housing shortage of the post World War II years. Returning veterans from the war were claiming their entitlements under the GI Bill of Rights which included home loans. The problem was there literally were not enough houses to satisfy the demand. Around the time the book by Eric Hodgins and the film were so popular Congress passed and President Truman signed the Taft-Ellender- Wagner Housing law which put the government for the first time in the home building business. policy: ELECTRONICS CARE PLAN
Issued by Circuit Care Services
In this policy, "the Provider" means Circuit Care Services and "the Customer" means the person named in the schedule.

Article 1. Definitions
(a) Accessories means cases, chargers and earbuds.
(b) Device means the item shown in the schedule, bought new from an authorised retailer.
(c) Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in the Customer's schedule.
(d) Replacement device means a device of the same or similar specification, which may be refurbished.

Article 2. Limits and service fee
(a) Accidental Damage: limit $800 per incident; service fee $99 per claim.
(b) Breakdown: limit $1,000 per incident; service fee $49 per claim.
(c) Theft and Loss: limit $800 per incident; service fee $99 per claim.
(d) The service fee is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

Article 3. Optional cover: Theft and Loss
(a) The Provider will replace the Customer's device if it is stolen or lost.
(b) This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Customer's schedule.
(c) The most the Provider will pay for Accessories under this section is $100 per incident.
(d) The Provider will not pay for loss or theft of property left unattended in a vehicle or in a public place. This exclusion does not apply to property locked out of sight in the boot or trunk of a locked vehicle.
(e) The Provider will not pay for theft that was not reported to the police.

Article 4. General exclusions
(a) The Provider will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
(b) The Provider will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.

Article 5. Making a claim
(a) The Customer must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
(b) The Customer must notify the Provider of a claim within 60 days of the incident. The Provider will not pay any claim notified after that time.
(c) The Provider may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

Article 6. Cooperation
(a) The Customer must give the Provider all the help and information the Provider reasonably need to settle a claim.
(b) The Customer must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without the Provider's written permission.

Article 7. Software support
(a) The Provider's helpline can give advice on setting up and using the Customer's device.
(b) Software support does not include fixing problems caused by third-party apps or unofficial operating systems.

Article 8. Governing law
(a) This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
(b) Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

Article 9. Repair process
(a) After a claim is accepted, the Provider will send a prepaid mailer or book a courier collection.
(b) The Provider aims to return repaired devices within 5 business days of receiving them.

Article 10. Complaints
(a) If the Customer has a complaint, the Customer should first contact the Provider's customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
(b) The Provider will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
(c) If the Customer remains dissatisfied, the Customer may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

Article 11. Claims documents
(a) The Customer must provide, at the Customer's own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence the Provider reasonably ask for.
(b) The Provider may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

Article 12. Joint policyholders
(a) Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.
(b) A notice sent to one named person is treated as sent to all of them.

state: There is some discussion as to whether achromats can see color or not. As illustrated in The Island of the Colorblind by Oliver Sacks, some achromats cannot see color, only black, white, and shades of grey. With five different genes currently known to cause similar symptoms, it may be that some do see marginal levels of color differentiation due to different gene characteristics. With such small sample sizes and low response rates, it is difficult to accurately diagnose the 'typical achromatic conditions'. If the light level during testing is optimized for them, they may achieve corrected visual acuity of 20/100 to 20/150 at lower light levels, regardless of the absence of color. One common trait is hemeralopia or blindness in full sun. In patients with achromatopsia, the cone system and fibres carrying color information remain intact. This indicates that the mechanism used to construct colors is defective.

answer.instructions: is it possible to only see black and white?

Before him, Commodore Perry basically pushed into Japan with gunboats and forced a treaty upon the Japanese in 1853. Harris, who arrived just a bit later, worked through the details and helped ensure compliance--as many of the Japanese felt no particular inclination to honor the first treaty. All this is true and shown in the film. According to some other sources I found, the romance between Harris and a Japanese Geisha is mostly fiction and this romance is much of the focus of this film (hence, the title). My first reaction the first time I saw this movie was one of surprise. John Wayne as a diplomat?! When he's being diplomatic in most films, he says please and thank you as he pummels people!!!! So seeing him playing a man who is NOT a man of action and is able to play the diplomatic game seemed very odd indeed. In fact, I can't think of too many actors in 1958 who would have been more unusual for this role. By the way, I've seen photos of Harris and Wayne has practically no resemblance to him at all.

After Taylor left the band, Ronnie Wood took his place in 1975 and continues on guitar in tandem with Richards. Following Wyman's departure in 1993, Darryl Jones joined as their touring bassist. - **5.2** We aim to pay accepted claims within 10 working days of receiving all the documents we need.

- **6.2** We will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.

- **7.2** You must notify us of a claim within 21 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.

## 8. Renewal
- **8.1** We will write to you at least 21 days before the end of the policy period with the renewal terms.

## 9. Governing law
- **9.1** This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
- **9.2** Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

## 10. Interpretation
- **10.1** Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
- **10.2** Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
- **10.3** Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

## 11. Freezer contents

- **11.2** We will not pay if the freezer is more than fifteen years old, or if the electricity supplier cut the supply deliberately.

## 1. Definitions
- **1.1** Limit means the most we will pay for all claims under a section arising from one treatment.
- **1.2** Major restorative work means crowns, bridges, root canal treatment and implants.
- **1.3** Network provider means a practitioner or clinic that has an agreement with us to provide treatment.
- **1.4** Orthodontics means braces and clear aligners.
- **1.5** Plan year means the twelve months starting on your coverage start date.

## 2. Limits and deductible
- **2.1** Dental Care: limit $2,000 per treatment; deductible $100 per claim.
- **2.2** Vision Care: limit $500 per treatment; deductible $25 per claim.
- **2.3** Therapy Services: limit $2,000 per treatment; deductible $50 per claim.
- **2.4** Hearing Care: limit $2,000 per treatment; deductible $150 per claim.
- **2.5** Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the deductible is then deducted from the result.

## 3. Dental Care
- **3.1** We will reimburse the cost of dental treatment provided by a licensed dentist.
- **3.2** No cover applies under this section to any treatment that happens within the first 60 days after the policy start date.

- **3.6** We will not pay for treatment by a provider outside the plan's network. This exclusion does not apply to emergency treatment for sudden severe pain.

## 4. General exclusions

- **4.2** We will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by you.
- **4.3** We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.

# Single-Trip Travel Protection Plan
Issued by Bluewater Assurance

## 1. Definitions
- **1.1** Dental treatment means treatment of the teeth or gums.
- **1.2** Hazardous activity means skydiving, motor racing, or trekking or climbing above 3,000 metres.
- **1.3** Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
- **1.4** Physiotherapy means treatment of muscles and joints by a physiotherapist.
- **1.5** Pre-existing condition means any illness or injury for which you received treatment or advice in the 6 months before the policy start date.
- **1.6** Sports equipment means skis, snowboards, golf clubs, surfboards and bicycles.
- **1.7** Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.
- **1.8** Valuables means laptops, tablets, mobile phones, cameras, watches and jewellery.

## 2. Limits and excess
- **2.1** Baggage and Personal Belongings: limit $2,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
- **2.2** Emergency Medical Expenses: limit $25,000 per incident; excess $250 per claim.
- **2.3** Trip Cancellation: limit $5,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
- **2.4** Travel Delay: limit $500 per incident; excess $25 per claim.
- **2.5** Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the excess is then deducted from the result.

## 3. Taxes
- **3.1** The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
- **3.2** If the tax rate changes, we may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

## 4. Emergency Medical Expenses
- **4.1** We will pay reasonable and necessary emergency medical costs incurred during the trip.
- **4.2** The most we will pay for Dental treatment under this section is $250 per incident.
- **4.3** The most we will pay for Physiotherapy under this section is $300 per incident.
- **4.4** We will not pay for treatment of a pre-existing condition.
- **4.5** We will not pay for injury or illness arising from a hazardous activity. This exclusion does not apply if the Adventure Sports extension is shown in your schedule.
- **4.6** We will not pay for any claim arising from your being under the influence of alcohol or drugs.

## 5. Baggage and Personal Belongings
- **5.1** We will pay for the loss of, theft of, or damage to your baggage and personal belongings during the trip.
- **5.2** The most we will pay for Valuables under this section is $250 per incident.
- **5.3** The most we will pay for Sports equipment under this section is $450 per incident.
- **5.4** We will not pay for loss or theft of property left unattended in a vehicle or in a public place. This exclusion does not apply to property locked out of sight in the boot or trunk of a locked vehicle.
- **5.5** We will not pay for loss caused by confiscation or detention by customs or other officials.
- **5.6** We will not pay for damage caused by wear and tear or gradual deterioration.

## 6. General exclusions
- **6.1** We will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
- **6.2** We will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by you.
- **6.3** We will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits us from paying.

## 7. Making a claim
- **7.1** We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
- **7.2** You must notify us of a claim within 21 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.
- **7.3** You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.

SECTION 1 - DEFINITIONS

2.2 Vision Care: limit $500 per treatment; deductible $40 per claim.

3.1 We will reimburse the cost of dental treatment provided by a licensed dentist.

4.1 We will reimburse hearing tests and hearing aids.
4.2 This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
4.3 The most we will pay for Hearing accessories under this section is $150 per treatment.
4.4 We will not pay for replacement hearing aids bought within the hearing aid replacement period.

SECTION 5 - GENERAL EXCLUSIONS
5.1 We will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by you.
5.2 We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
5.3 We will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.

SECTION 6 - MAKING A CLAIM
6.1 You must notify us of a claim within 90 days of the treatment. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.
6.2 You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
6.3 We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

SECTION 7 - ENVIRONMENTAL COMMITMENT
7.1 Where practical, we will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
7.2 You may ask for a new part instead, and we will tell you whether any additional cost would apply.

SECTION 8 - INTERPRETATION
8.1 Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
8.2 Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
8.3 Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

SECTION 9 - PAYMENT OF CLAIMS
9.1 We will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in your name.
9.2 We aim to pay accepted claims within 5 working days of receiving all the documents we need.

state: Lost isn't the greatest TV show in history, but it's not far off. It doesn't have the plot or characterisation of The West Wing or possibly even early ER, however, it is arguably the most continuously gripping show I have every come across. I love the way I can't guess what's going to happen. I love the re-telling of the characters' back stories which often give rise to new dimensions for us to see them in. In some ways I want the show to last forever, but I think they can get 6-7 seasons out of it before they have to end it on a glorious high. The combination of the characters and their nationalities coupled with the show's fluidity for moving backwards and forwards thus extending dead characters "life spans" all adds to the overwhelming sense that this show is something very different from what we are used to. It's captivating, surprising and (here's a little suggestion for all of you conspiracy theorists) more than a little interactive- keep those internet discussions going- you're only adding to the plot...

Then the movie came out, and the Kubrick cultists have been bickering with the King cultists ever since. The King cultists say Stanley Kubrick took a great horror tale and ruined it. The Kubrick cultists don't give a damn about King's story. They talk about Steadicams, tracking shots, camera angles.This is a film, they insist: It should be considered on its own. As it happens, both camps are correct. Unfortunately. If one views it purely as an adaptation of King's novel, "The Shining" is indeed a failure, a wasted opportunity, a series of botched narrative gambits. I used to blame that on Kubrick's screenwriter. The writer Diane Johnson (author of Le Marriage, L'Affaire, Le Divorce, etc.) has a reputation as an novelist of social manners. state: On September 12, George Mason of Virginia suggested the addition of a Bill of Rights to the Constitution modeled on previous state declarations, and Elbridge Gerry of Massachusetts made it a formal motion. However, the motion was defeated by a unanimous vote of the state delegations after only a brief discussion. Madison, then an opponent of a Bill of Rights, later explained the vote by calling the state bills of rights ``parchment barriers'' that offered only an illusion of protection against tyranny. Another delegate, James Wilson of Pennsylvania, later argued that the act of enumerating the rights of the people would have been dangerous, because it would imply that rights not explicitly mentioned did not exist; Hamilton echoed this point in Federalist No. 84. Because Mason and Gerry had emerged as opponents of the proposed new Constitution, their motion--introduced five days before the end of the convention--may also have been seen by other delegates as a delaying tactic. The quick rejection of this motion, however, later endangered the entire ratification process. Author David O. Stewart characterizes the omission of a Bill of Rights in the original Constitution as ``a political blunder of the first magnitude'' while historian Jack N. Rakove calls it ``the one serious miscalculation the framers made as they looked ahead to the struggle over ratification''.

II.1  Baggage and Personal Belongings: limit $1,500 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
II.2  Emergency Medical Expenses: limit $50,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
II.3  Trip Cancellation: limit $5,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
