PART III: Repatriation
III.1  If the Insurer's medical adviser agrees it is necessary, the Insurer will arrange and pay for the Insured Person to be brought home.
III.2  The Insurer will decide the method of transport and the time of repatriation after speaking to the treating doctor.

PART IV: Interest
IV.1  The Insurer will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

PART V: Baggage and Personal Belongings
V.1  The Insurer will pay for the loss of, theft of, or damage to the Insured Person's baggage and personal belongings during the trip.
V.2  The most the Insurer will pay for Valuables under this section is $400 per incident.
V.3  The most the Insurer will pay for Sports equipment under this section is $300 per incident.
V.4  The Insurer will not pay for loss or theft of property left unattended in a vehicle or in a public place. This exclusion does not apply to property locked out of sight in the boot or trunk of a locked vehicle.

V.6  The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by wear and tear or gradual deterioration.

PART VI: General exclusions
VI.1  The Insurer will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
VI.2  The Insurer will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Insured Person.
VI.3  The Insurer will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits the Insurer from paying.

PART VII: Making a claim
VII.1  The Insurer may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
VII.2  The Insured Person must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
VII.3  The Insured Person must notify the Insurer of a claim within 60 days of the incident. The Insurer will not pay any claim notified after that time.

VIII.1  Where practical, the Insurer will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
VIII.2  The Insured Person may ask for a new part instead, and the Insurer will tell the Insured Person whether any additional cost would apply.

PART IX: Payment of claims
IX.1  The Insurer will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in the Insured Person's name.
IX.2  The Insurer aims to pay accepted claims within 15 working days of receiving all the documents the Insurer needs.

PART X: Missed departure
X.1  The Insurer will pay reasonable additional travel and accommodation costs to reach the Insured Person's destination if the Insured Person arrives too late to board the Insured Person's booked transport because public transport fails.
X.2  The Insured Person must allow enough time to reach the departure point, and must obtain written confirmation of the delay from the transport operator.

policy: ELECTRONICS CARE PLAN
Issued by Voltguard Protection Ltd
In this policy, "the Provider" means Voltguard Protection Ltd and "the Customer" means the person named in the schedule.

Article 1. Definitions
(a) Accessories means cases, chargers, earbuds and styluses.
(b) Accessories means cases, chargers and earbuds.
(c) Battery replacement means replacement batteries and battery repairs.
(d) Manufacturer's warranty period means the first 24 months after the device was bought.
(e) Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in the Customer's schedule.
(f) Wearables means smartwatches and fitness trackers.

Article 2. Limits and service fee
(a) Accidental Damage: limit $1,200 per incident; service fee $99 per claim.
(b) Breakdown: limit $1,000 per incident; service fee $49 per claim.
(c) Theft and Loss: limit $800 per incident; service fee $149 per claim.
(d) Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the service fee is then deducted from the result.

Article 3. Breakdown
(a) The Provider will repair or replace the Customer's device if it stops working because of an electrical or mechanical fault.
(b) No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 30 days after the policy start date.
(c) The most the Provider will pay for Battery replacement under this section is $120 per incident.
(d) The Provider will not pay for breakdowns during the manufacturer's warranty period.
(e) The Provider will not pay for breakdown caused by liquid getting into the device.

Article 4. Accidental Damage
(a) The Provider will repair or replace the Customer's device if it is accidentally damaged.
(b) The most the Provider will pay for Accessories under this section is $100 per incident.
(c) The most the Provider will pay for Wearables under this section is $300 per incident.
(d) The Provider will not pay for cosmetic damage, such as scratches or dents, that does not affect how the device works.
(e) The Provider will not pay for damage following a repair by anyone other than the Provider or an authorised repairer. This exclusion does not apply if the Provider approved the repair in writing beforehand.

Article 5. Optional cover: Theft and Loss
(a) The Provider will replace the Customer's device if it is stolen or lost.
(b) This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Customer's schedule.
(c) The most the Provider will pay for Accessories under this section is $50 per incident.
(d) The Provider will not pay for loss or theft of property left unattended in a vehicle or in a public place. This exclusion does not apply to property locked out of sight in the boot or trunk of a locked vehicle.
(e) The Provider will not pay for theft that was not reported to the police.

Article 6. General exclusions
(a) The Provider will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
(b) The Provider will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
(c) The Provider will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Customer.

Article 7. Making a claim
(a) The Customer must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
(b) The Provider may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
(c) The Customer must notify the Provider of a claim within 21 days of the incident. The Provider will not pay any claim notified after that time.

state: Director Vincenzo Natali's Cypher is a complex and imaginative thriller which, although requiring some suspension of belief and plenty of concentration, manages to be a thoroughly entertaining experience. Morgan Sullivan (Jeremy Northam), a stay-at-home husband with an overbearing wife, decides to add a bit of spice to his mundane existence by getting a job as an industrial spy at high-tech company Digi Corp. His job is to travel to conferences across the country (under the assumed identity of Jack Thursby) and secretly broadcast the speeches given back to his bosses, via a nifty little electronic pen-gizmo. In reality, however, the speeches are merely a cover for far more nefarious activities. Morgan, along with his fellow conference attendees, is being brainwashed. The drugged water they are drinking puts them into a temporary coma, during which they are told to forget their pasts and permanently adopt their new identities. Once they are totally convinced that they are someone else, they are told to apply for jobs with rival companies, where they are able to indulge in corporate espionage without suspicion. But Digi Corp's plans are scuppered by the intervention of shady operative-for-hire Rita Foster (Lucy Liu), who opens Morgan's eyes to what is really happening. policy: ANNUAL MULTI-TRIP TRAVEL COVER
Issued by Meridian Travel Insurance Ltd

PART I: Definitions
I.1  Excursions and tickets means pre-booked excursions, tours, and event or theatre tickets.
I.2  Premium means the amount the Insured Person must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
I.3  Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
I.4  Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows the Insured Person's details, the covers the Insured Person bought and any extensions.

PART II: Limits and excess
II.1  Baggage and Personal Belongings: limit $3,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
II.2  Emergency Medical Expenses: limit $10,000 per incident; excess $250 per claim.
II.3  Trip Cancellation: limit $3,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
II.4  Travel Delay: limit $300 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
II.5  Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the excess is then deducted from the result.

PART III: Trip Cancellation
III.1  The Insurer will pay non-refundable travel and accommodation costs if the Insured Person must cancel the trip for a reason beyond the Insured Person's control.
III.2  No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 14 days after the policy start date.
III.3  The most the Insurer will pay for Excursions and tickets under this section is $300 per incident.
III.4  The Insurer will not pay for cancellation caused by a strike or other event that had been publicly announced before the Insured Person bought the policy.
III.5  The Insurer will not pay for cancellation because the Insured Person no longer wish to travel.

PART IV: General exclusions
IV.1  The Insurer will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
IV.2  The Insurer will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
IV.3  The Insurer will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Insured Person.

PART V: Making a claim
V.1  The Insured Person must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
V.2  The Insured Person must notify the Insurer of a claim within 30 days of the incident. The Insurer will not pay any claim notified after that time.
V.3  The Insurer may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

Tacos And Beer is awesome!

My husband and I have eaten here several times, and we love it more with each visit.

The atmosphere is great. The decor is really unique and inviting.

The staff is friendly, and helpful. The bartenders were very knowledgeable of their extensive beer menu. If you're a fan of great craft beer, Tacos and Beer is the place to go. They have an amazing selection of hard to find craft brews. Everything from imperial stouts for my husband, to wild sour beers, and even honey mead for me. The general manager, Dave, knows more about beer than anyone I've ever met. He was kind enough to introduce us to, what are now, several of our favorite beers!


And the food is absolutely delicious! Chips and guacamole are great. Oh and the beer cheese dip is ridiculous. We've tried most of the tacos and love them all. Our favorites are; the crunchy tacos with mash potatoes, the puerco verde with pork rinds, the beef adobada, and the pork al pastor. The flautas are also great! We have also eaten dessert there, and my goodness, the flan is amazing, definitely the best flan I've ever had. The churros are really great as well.

Overall, this is just a great restaurant in Las Vegas!

- **1.1** Accessories means cases, chargers, earbuds and styluses.

policy: ANNUAL MULTI-TRIP TRAVEL COVER
Issued by Bluewater Assurance
In this policy, "the Insurer" means Bluewater Assurance and "the Insured Person" means the person named in the schedule.

Article 1. Definitions
(a) Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by the Insurer, before any excess, limit or sublimit is applied.
(b) Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
(c) Dental treatment means treatment of the teeth or gums.
(d) Excursions and tickets means pre-booked excursions, tours, and event or theatre tickets.
(e) Hazardous activity means skydiving, motor racing, or trekking or climbing above 4,000 metres.
(f) Physiotherapy means treatment of muscles and joints by a physiotherapist.
(g) Pre-existing condition means any illness or injury for which the Insured Person received treatment or advice in the 3 months before the policy start date.
(h) Public transport means any scheduled train, bus, coach, ferry or aircraft.
(i) Qualifying delay means a delay to the scheduled departure of more than 8 hours.

Article 2. Limits and excess
(a) Baggage and Personal Belongings: limit $1,500 per incident; excess $75 per claim.
(b) Emergency Medical Expenses: limit $10,000 per incident; excess $150 per claim.
(c) Trip Cancellation: limit $2,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
(d) Travel Delay: limit $300 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
(e) The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

Article 3. Emergency Medical Expenses
(a) The Insurer will pay reasonable and necessary emergency medical costs incurred during the trip.
(b) The most the Insurer will pay for Dental treatment under this section is $250 per incident.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Physiotherapy under this section is $500 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for treatment of a pre-existing condition.
(e) The Insurer will not pay for injury or illness arising from a hazardous activity. This exclusion does not apply if the Adventure Sports extension is shown in the Insured Person's schedule.
(f) The Insurer will not pay for any claim arising from the Insured Person's being under the influence of alcohol or drugs.

Article 4. Trip Cancellation
(a) The Insurer will pay non-refundable travel and accommodation costs if the Insured Person must cancel the trip for a reason beyond the Insured Person's control.
(b) No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 14 days after the policy start date.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Excursions and tickets under this section is $300 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for cancellation caused by a strike or other event that had been publicly announced before the Insured Person bought the policy.
(e) The Insurer will not pay for cancellation because the Insured Person no longer wish to travel.

Article 5. Optional cover: Travel Delay
(a) The Insurer will pay reasonable costs of meals and accommodation if the Insured Person's outbound departure is delayed.
(b) This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Insured Person's schedule.
(c) The Insurer will not pay for any delay that is not a qualifying delay.

Article 6. General exclusions
(a) The Insurer will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
(b) The Insurer will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.

Article 7. Making a claim
(a) The Insured Person must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
(b) The Insured Person must notify the Insurer of a claim within 90 days of the incident. The Insurer will not pay any claim notified after that time.
(c) The Insurer may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

Gable, Harlow, and Owen try pulling a badger game on a drunken Paul Hurst, but then Gable won't go through with it. The rest of the film is her's and her adjustment to prison life. Her interaction with the other female prisoners give her some very good scenes. policy: RENTERS CONTENTS PROTECTION
Issued by Hearthstone Insurance plc
In this policy, "the Insurer" means Hearthstone Insurance plc and "the Policyholder" means the person named in the schedule.

Article 1. Definitions
(a) Forcible entry means entry to the home that leaves visible damage to doors, windows or locks.
(b) Garden items means garden furniture, plants and outdoor tools.
(c) Outbuilding means a shed, garage or greenhouse within the boundaries of the home.
(d) Portable electronics means laptops, tablets and mobile phones.

Article 2. Limits and excess
(a) Theft: limit $40,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
(b) Escape of Water: limit $30,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
(c) Accidental Damage: limit $5,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
(d) Flood: limit $20,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
(e) Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the excess is then deducted from the result.

Article 3. Discounts
(a) Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
(b) If a condition for a discount stops being met, the Insurer may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

Article 4. Optional cover: Accidental Damage
(a) The Insurer will pay for sudden and unexpected accidental damage to the Policyholder's contents inside the home.
(b) This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Policyholder's schedule.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Portable electronics under this section is $750 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by pets.
(e) The Insurer will not pay for wear and tear, or damage that happens gradually.

Article 5. Flood
(a) The Insurer will pay for contents damaged by flood water entering the Policyholder's home.
(b) No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 60 days after the policy start date.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Garden items under this section is $1,000 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for flood damage where a flood warning for the Policyholder's area had been issued before the policy started.

Article 6. General exclusions
(a) The Insurer will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
(b) The Insurer will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Policyholder.

Article 7. Exchange of information
(a) To prevent fraud, the Insurer may check the details the Policyholder gives against public records and industry databases.
(b) The Insurer may contact previous insurers to confirm the Policyholder's claims history.

Article 8. Making a claim
(a) The Insurer may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
(b) The Policyholder must notify the Insurer of a claim within 60 days of the incident. The Insurer will not pay any claim notified after that time.
(c) The Policyholder must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.

Article 9. Cancellation
(a) The Policyholder can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
(b) After the first 14 days the Policyholder can cancel at any time; the Insurer will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $25.
(c) The Insurer can cancel this policy by giving the Policyholder 30 days' written notice to the last address the Insurer holds.

# Employee Health Benefits Plan: Summary Plan Description
Issued by the Benefits Trust

## 1. Definitions
- **1.1** Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
- **1.2** Frames means spectacle frames bought without new lenses.
- **1.3** Major restorative work means crowns, bridges, root canal treatment and implants.
- **1.4** Orthodontics means braces and clear aligners.
- **1.5** Replacement period means 12 months from the date of your last eyewear claim.

## 2. Limits and deductible
- **2.1** Dental Care: limit $1,500 per treatment; deductible $100 per claim.
- **2.2** Vision Care: limit $400 per treatment; deductible $25 per claim.
- **2.3** Therapy Services: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $50 per claim.
- **2.4** Hearing Care: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $100 per claim.
- **2.5** Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the deductible is then deducted from the result.

## 3. Vision Care
- **3.1** We will reimburse eye tests and prescription eyewear.
- **3.2** The most we will pay for Frames under this section is $150 per treatment.
- **3.3** We will not pay for eyewear without prescription lenses.
- **3.4** We will not pay for a further eyewear claim within the replacement period.

## 4. Dental Care
- **4.1** We will reimburse the cost of dental treatment provided by a licensed dentist.
- **4.2** No cover applies under this section to any treatment that happens within the first 90 days after the policy start date.
- **4.3** The most we will pay for Major restorative work under this section is $500 per treatment.
- **4.4** The most we will pay for Orthodontics under this section is $600 per treatment.
- **4.5** We will not pay for treatment that is mainly cosmetic, such as whitening or veneers. This exclusion does not apply to treatment needed to repair damage caused by an accident.
- **4.6** We will not pay for treatment by a provider outside the plan's network. This exclusion does not apply to emergency treatment for sudden severe pain.

## 5. General exclusions
- **5.1** We will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits us from paying.
- **5.2** We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
- **5.3** We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.

## 6. Making a claim
- **6.1** We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
- **6.2** You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
- **6.3** You must notify us of a claim within 60 days of the treatment. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.

Emeka joined the company's finance team two years ago.

I am sending this on April 12, 2026, which is when I first notified you. Your adjuster assessed the loss at $1,880.

Thanks,
Emeka

Issued by the Staff Welfare Fund
In this policy, "the Plan" means the Staff Welfare Fund and "the Member" means the person named in the schedule.

Article 1. Definitions
(a) Hearing accessories means batteries, chargers and cleaning kits.
(b) Hearing aid replacement period means 24 months from the purchase of hearing aids funded by the plan.

PART I: Definitions
I.1  Art and antiques means paintings, antiques, rugs and other works of art.
I.2  Bicycles means bicycles and electric scooters.
I.3  Contents means household goods and personal possessions that belong to the Policyholder or the Policyholder's family.
I.4  High-risk items means jewellery, watches, laptops, games consoles and cameras.
I.5  Unoccupied means not lived in by the Policyholder or a member of the Policyholder's family for more than 60 consecutive days.

PART II: Limits and excess
II.1  Theft: limit $10,000 per incident; excess $250 per claim.
II.2  Escape of Water: limit $15,000 per incident; excess $250 per claim.
II.3  Accidental Damage: limit $5,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
II.4  Flood: limit $40,000 per incident; excess $1,000 per claim.
II.5  The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

PART III: Accessibility
III.1  This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

PART IV: Theft
IV.1  The Insurer will pay for contents stolen from the Policyholder's home.
IV.2  The most the Insurer will pay for High-risk items under this section is $2,500 per incident.
IV.3  The most the Insurer will pay for Bicycles under this section is $800 per incident.
IV.4  The Insurer will not pay for theft while the home is unoccupied.
IV.5  The Insurer will not pay for theft where there is no sign of forced entry to the home. This exclusion does not apply where the thief gained entry by deception, for example by posing as a utility worker.
IV.6  The Insurer will not pay for theft from sheds, garages or other outbuildings. This exclusion does not apply if the outbuilding was locked and the theft involved forcible entry.

PART V: Waiver
V.1  If the Insurer does not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean the Insurer has given up the right to enforce it later.

PART VI: Notices
VI.1  Any notice the Insurer gives under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address the Insurer holds.
VI.2  Notices from the Policyholder should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

PART VII: Escape of Water
VII.1  The Insurer will pay for contents damaged by water escaping from a fixed pipe, tank or domestic appliance.
VII.2  The most the Insurer will pay for Art and antiques under this section is $2,000 per incident.
VII.3  The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by water leaking gradually over a period of time.
VII.4  The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by the failure of grout or sealant around baths and showers.

PART VIII: General exclusions
VIII.1  The Insurer will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
VIII.2  The Insurer will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits the Insurer from paying.

PART IX: Making a claim
IX.1  The Insurer may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
IX.2  The Policyholder must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
IX.3  The Policyholder must notify the Insurer of a claim within 90 days of the incident. The Insurer will not pay any claim notified after that time.

Issued by the Staff Welfare Fund

## 1. Definitions
- **1.1** Frames means spectacle frames bought without new lenses.
- **1.2** Massage therapy means sports massage, massage therapy and reflexology.
- **1.3** Plan year means the twelve months starting on your coverage start date.
- **1.4** Premium means the amount you must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
- **1.5** Replacement period means 24 months from the date of your last eyewear claim.
- **1.6** Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.

## 2. Limits and deductible
- **2.1** Dental Care: limit $1,500 per treatment; deductible $50 per claim.
- **2.2** Vision Care: limit $300 per treatment; deductible $25 per claim.
- **2.3** Therapy Services: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $50 per claim.
- **2.4** Hearing Care: limit $2,000 per treatment; deductible $150 per claim.

## 3. Vision Care
- **3.1** We will reimburse eye tests and prescription eyewear.
- **3.2** The most we will pay for Frames under this section is $150 per treatment.
- **3.3** We will not pay for eyewear without prescription lenses.

## 4. Therapy Services
- **4.1** We will reimburse physiotherapy, osteopathy and counselling provided by a registered practitioner.

- **4.3** We will not pay for treatment of an injury covered by workers' compensation.

## 5. General exclusions
- **5.1** We will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
- **5.2** We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
- **5.3** We will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by you.

## 6. Making a claim
- **6.1** You must notify us of a claim within 60 days of the treatment. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.

policy: ANNUAL MULTI-TRIP TRAVEL COVER
Issued by Bluewater Assurance
In this policy, "the Insurer" means Bluewater Assurance and "the Insured Person" means the person named in the schedule.

Article 1. Definitions
(a) Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by the Insurer, before any excess, limit or sublimit is applied.
(b) Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
(c) Excursions and tickets means pre-booked excursions, tours, and event or theatre tickets.
(d) Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.

Article 2. Limits and excess
(a) Baggage and Personal Belongings: limit $1,500 per incident; excess $75 per claim.
(b) Emergency Medical Expenses: limit $50,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
(c) Trip Cancellation: limit $5,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
(d) Travel Delay: limit $300 per incident; excess $25 per claim.
(e) Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the excess is then deducted from the result.

Article 3. Trip Cancellation
(a) The Insurer will pay non-refundable travel and accommodation costs if the Insured Person must cancel the trip for a reason beyond the Insured Person's control.
(b) No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 10 days after the policy start date.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Excursions and tickets under this section is $200 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for cancellation caused by a strike or other event that had been publicly announced before the Insured Person bought the policy.
(e) The Insurer will not pay for cancellation because the Insured Person no longer wish to travel.

Article 4. General exclusions
(a) The Insurer will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
(b) The Insurer will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Insured Person.
(c) The Insurer will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.

Article 5. Making a claim
(a) The Insurer may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
(b) The Insured Person must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
(c) The Insured Person must notify the Insurer of a claim within 14 days of the incident. The Insurer will not pay any claim notified after that time.

Article 6. Missed departure
(a) The Insurer will pay reasonable additional travel and accommodation costs to reach the Insured Person's destination if the Insured Person arrives too late to board the Insured Person's booked transport because public transport fails.
(b) The Insured Person must allow enough time to reach the departure point, and must obtain written confirmation of the delay from the transport operator.

Article 7. Interpretation
(a) Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
(b) Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
(c) Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

Article 8. Cancellation
(a) The Insured Person can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
(b) After the first 14 days the Insured Person can cancel at any time; the Insurer will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $15.
(c) The Insurer can cancel this policy by giving the Insured Person 30 days' written notice to the last address the Insurer holds.

Article 9. Notices
(a) Any notice the Insurer gives under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address the Insurer holds.
(b) Notices from the Insured Person should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

# Device Protection Plan Terms
Issued by Voltguard Protection Ltd

## 1. Definitions
- **1.1** Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by us, before any service fee, limit or sublimit is applied.
- **1.2** Battery replacement means replacement batteries and battery repairs.
- **1.3** Breakdown means the failure of a part to work as the manufacturer intended, from an internal electrical or mechanical fault.
- **1.4** Manufacturer's warranty period means the first 12 months after the device was bought.
- **1.5** Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in your schedule.

## 2. Limits and service fee
- **2.1** Accidental Damage: limit $1,200 per incident; service fee $49 per claim.
- **2.2** Breakdown: limit $1,500 per incident; service fee $25 per claim.
- **2.3** Theft and Loss: limit $800 per incident; service fee $99 per claim.
- **2.4** Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the service fee is then deducted from the result.

## 3. Breakdown
- **3.1** We will repair or replace your device if it stops working because of an electrical or mechanical fault.
- **3.2** No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 45 days after the policy start date.
- **3.3** The most we will pay for Battery replacement under this section is $120 per incident.
- **3.4** We will not pay for breakdowns during the manufacturer's warranty period.
- **3.5** We will not pay for breakdown caused by liquid getting into the device.

## 4. Payment of claims
- **4.1** We will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in your name.
- **4.2** We aim to pay accepted claims within 15 working days of receiving all the documents we need.

## 5. General exclusions
- **5.1** We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
- **5.2** We will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits us from paying.
- **5.3** We will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by you.

## 6. Environmental commitment
- **6.1** Where practical, we will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
- **6.2** You may ask for a new part instead, and we will tell you whether any additional cost would apply.

## 7. Making a claim
- **7.1** You must notify us of a claim within 14 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.
- **7.2** We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
- **7.3** You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.

state: document: The 1933 Chesapeake--Potomac hurricane was among the most damaging hurricanes in the Mid-Atlantic states in the eastern United States. The sixth storm and third hurricane of the very active 1933 Atlantic hurricane season, it formed in the eastern Atlantic, where it moved west-northwestward and eventually became a Category 4 on the Saffir-Simpson hurricane wind scale. A strong ridge over New England allowed a continued northwest course, bringing the storm south of Bermuda and later toward the middle coast of the eastern United States. Advance warning allowed hundreds of people to evacuate ahead of the hurricane making landfall. It did so in northeastern North Carolina on August 23 with winds of about 90 mph (150 km/h). Soon after, the eye crossed over Norfolk, Virginia, the first time that happened since 1821. The hurricane weakened into a tropical storm over northern Virginia shortly before passing near Washington, D.C., becoming the worst tropical cyclone there since 1896. Curving northward, the storm moved through Pennsylvania and New York before losing tropical characteristics on August 25. Now extratropical, the former hurricane moved across Atlantic Canada, dissipating on August 28.

# Travel Insurance Policy Wording
Issued by Compass Mutual

## 1. Definitions
- **1.1** Excursions and tickets means pre-booked excursions, tours, and event or theatre tickets.
- **1.2** Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
- **1.3** Qualifying delay means a delay to the scheduled departure of more than 12 hours.

## 2. Limits and excess
- **2.1** Baggage and Personal Belongings: limit $1,500 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
- **2.2** Emergency Medical Expenses: limit $25,000 per incident; excess $250 per claim.
- **2.3** Trip Cancellation: limit $3,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
- **2.4** Travel Delay: limit $300 per incident; excess $25 per claim.
- **2.5** Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the excess is then deducted from the result.

## 3. Legal expenses abroad
- **3.1** We will pay legal costs to pursue compensation for your injury or death caused by a third party during the trip.
- **3.2** We will not pay legal costs unless our legal adviser agrees that the claim has a reasonable prospect of success.

## 4. Optional cover: Travel Delay
- **4.1** We will pay reasonable costs of meals and accommodation if your outbound departure is delayed.
- **4.2** This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
- **4.3** We will not pay for any delay that is not a qualifying delay.

## 5. Trip Cancellation
- **5.1** We will pay non-refundable travel and accommodation costs if you must cancel the trip for a reason beyond your control.
- **5.2** No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 14 days after the policy start date.
- **5.3** The most we will pay for Excursions and tickets under this section is $200 per incident.
- **5.4** We will not pay for cancellation caused by a strike or other event that had been publicly announced before you bought the policy.
- **5.5** We will not pay for cancellation because you no longer wish to travel.

## 6. General exclusions
- **6.1** We will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits us from paying.
- **6.2** We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.

## 7. Making a claim
- **7.1** You must notify us of a claim within 14 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.
- **7.2** We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
- **7.3** You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.

## 8. Market conditions
- **8.1** If the replacement item is no longer available, we will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

Issued by Hearthstone Insurance plc

PART I: Definitions
I.1  Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by the Insurer, before any excess, limit or sublimit is applied.
I.2  Garden items means garden furniture, plants and outdoor tools.

PART II: Limits and excess
II.1  Theft: limit $40,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
II.2  Escape of Water: limit $30,000 per incident; excess $1,000 per claim.
II.3  Accidental Damage: limit $2,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
II.4  Flood: limit $40,000 per incident; excess $1,000 per claim.
II.5  Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the excess is then deducted from the result.

PART III: Flood
III.1  The Insurer will pay for contents damaged by flood water entering the Policyholder's home.
III.2  No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 30 days after the policy start date.
III.3  The most the Insurer will pay for Garden items under this section is $500 per incident.
III.4  The Insurer will not pay for flood damage where a flood warning for the Policyholder's area had been issued before the policy started.

PART IV: General exclusions
IV.1  The Insurer will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits the Insurer from paying.
IV.2  The Insurer will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.

PART V: Making a claim
V.1  The Insurer may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
V.2  The Policyholder must notify the Insurer of a claim within 90 days of the incident. The Insurer will not pay any claim notified after that time.
V.3  The Policyholder must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.

PART VI: Locks and keys
VI.1  If the keys to the Policyholder's home are lost or stolen, the Insurer will pay the cost of replacing the locks to the outside doors.
VI.2  The most the Insurer will pay under this clause is $500 for any one claim.

PART VII: Discounts
VII.1  Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
VII.2  If a condition for a discount stops being met, the Insurer may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

PART VIII: Salvage
VIII.1  When the Insurer replaces an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes the Insurer's property.
VIII.2  If stolen property is recovered after the Insurer has paid a claim, the Policyholder must tell the Insurer and either return the payment or give the Insurer the property.

PART IX: Severability
IX.1  If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

PART X: Data protection
X.1  The Insurer will use the personal information the Policyholder provides to administer this policy and to handle claims.
X.2  The Insurer will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
X.3  The Policyholder can ask for a copy of the personal information the Insurer holds by writing to the Insurer's data protection officer.

PART XI: Records and evidence
XI.1  The Policyholder should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.
XI.2  Where proof of value is missing, the Insurer may base any settlement on the price of a comparable item.
XI.3  The Insurer may ask for evidence of how and when an item was acquired.

policy: HOUSEHOLD CONTENTS COVER: POLICY BOOKLET
Issued by Hearthstone Insurance plc
In this policy, "the Insurer" means Hearthstone Insurance plc and "the Policyholder" means the person named in the schedule.

Article 1. Definitions
(a) Art and antiques means paintings, antiques, rugs and other works of art.
(b) Outbuilding means a shed, garage or greenhouse within the boundaries of the home.
(c) Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.

Article 2. Limits and excess
(a) Theft: limit $40,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
(b) Escape of Water: limit $30,000 per incident; excess $250 per claim.
(c) Accidental Damage: limit $5,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
(d) Flood: limit $40,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
(e) The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

Article 3. Escape of Water
(a) The Insurer will pay for contents damaged by water escaping from a fixed pipe, tank or domestic appliance.
(b) The most the Insurer will pay for Art and antiques under this section is $2,000 per incident.
(c) The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by water leaking gradually over a period of time.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by the failure of grout or sealant around baths and showers.

Article 4. General exclusions
(a) The Insurer will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits the Insurer from paying.
(b) The Insurer will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
(c) The Insurer will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.

Article 5. Making a claim
(a) The Policyholder must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
(b) The Insurer may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
(c) The Policyholder must notify the Insurer of a claim within 14 days of the incident. The Insurer will not pay any claim notified after that time.

Article 6. Electronic documents
(a) The Insurer will send documents by email unless the Policyholder asks for paper copies.
(b) The Policyholder must tell the Insurer if the Policyholder's email address changes.
(c) Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

Article 7. Reasonable precautions
(a) The Policyholder must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
(b) The Policyholder must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

Article 8. Duty of fair presentation
(a) The Policyholder must answer all questions the Insurer asks honestly and to the best of the Policyholder's knowledge.
(b) If the Policyholder gives incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, the Insurer may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
(c) If the Policyholder gives incorrect information carelessly, the Insurer may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

state: document: Like Ishtar and King of Comedy, other great, misunderstood comedies, Envy has great performances by two actors playing essentially, losers (may be too harsh a word, I will call them suburban under-achievers). This film was a dark comedy gem, and I'm not sure what people expect. I relish seeing a major studio comedy that isn't filled with obvious humor, and I believe that the small moments in this movie make it worthwhile. The look on Stiller's face when he sees the dog doo disappear for the first time captures a moment, a moment that most people should be able to recognize in themselves. Yes, it was a fairly simple story, but it examined the root of envy in a really interesting way. There were a lot of great scenes (the J-Man's decrepit "cabin by the lake", Corky's unceremonious burial, Weitz's wife role, and Walken's J-Man -- all great stuff. I can't stand people that get on IMDb and mercilessly trash films when they have absolutely no idea what it takes to make one. I will take Envy over almost any of the top ten grossing comedies of the year (save Napoleon Dynamite.) It's wittier, wackier, and an offbeat, enjoyable gem. Remember this people; Most times, Popular doesn't equal Good.

# Home Contents Insurance Policy
Issued by Lantern General Insurance

## 1. Definitions
- **1.1** Home means the private residence at the address shown in the schedule.
- **1.2** Portable electronics means laptops, tablets and mobile phones.

## 2. Limits and excess
- **2.1** Theft: limit $40,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
- **2.2** Escape of Water: limit $15,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
- **2.3** Accidental Damage: limit $3,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
- **2.4** Flood: limit $20,000 per incident; excess $1,000 per claim.
- **2.5** Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the excess is then deducted from the result.

## 3. Payment of claims
- **3.1** We will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in your name.
- **3.2** We aim to pay accepted claims within 15 working days of receiving all the documents we need.

## 4. Subrogation
- **4.1** We will be entitled to take over and conduct in your name the defence or settlement of any claim.
- **4.2** We can take action in your name to recover any payment we make from anyone responsible for the loss.

## 5. Optional cover: Accidental Damage
- **5.1** We will pay for sudden and unexpected accidental damage to your contents inside the home.
- **5.2** This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
- **5.3** The most we will pay for Portable electronics under this section is $750 per incident.
- **5.4** We will not pay for damage caused by pets.
- **5.5** We will not pay for wear and tear, or damage that happens gradually.

## 6. General exclusions
- **6.1** We will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by you.
- **6.2** We will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
- **6.3** We will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits us from paying.

## 7. Making a claim
- **7.1** We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
- **7.2** You must notify us of a claim within 90 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.
- **7.3** You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.

## 8. Environmental commitment
- **8.1** Where practical, we will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
- **8.2** You may ask for a new part instead, and we will tell you whether any additional cost would apply.

## 9. Exchange of information
- **9.1** To prevent fraud, we may check the details you give against public records and industry databases.
- **9.2** We may contact previous insurers to confirm your claims history.

## 10. Customer support
- **10.1** Our helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
- **10.2** Outside these hours you can leave a message and we will call back on the next working day.

policy: TRAVEL INSURANCE POLICY WORDING
Issued by Compass Mutual
In this policy, "the Insurer" means Compass Mutual and "the Insured Person" means the person named in the schedule.

Article 1. Definitions
(a) Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
(b) Excursions and tickets means pre-booked excursions, tours, and event or theatre tickets.
(c) Qualifying delay means a delay to the scheduled departure of more than 6 hours.

Article 2. Limits and excess
(a) Baggage and Personal Belongings: limit $3,000 per incident; excess $75 per claim.
(b) Emergency Medical Expenses: limit $10,000 per incident; excess $250 per claim.
(c) Trip Cancellation: limit $5,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
(d) Travel Delay: limit $300 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
(e) The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

Article 3. Trip Cancellation
(a) The Insurer will pay non-refundable travel and accommodation costs if the Insured Person must cancel the trip for a reason beyond the Insured Person's control.
(b) No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 7 days after the policy start date.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Excursions and tickets under this section is $200 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for cancellation caused by a strike or other event that had been publicly announced before the Insured Person bought the policy.
(e) The Insurer will not pay for cancellation because the Insured Person no longer wish to travel.

Article 4. Optional cover: Travel Delay
(a) The Insurer will pay reasonable costs of meals and accommodation if the Insured Person's outbound departure is delayed.
(b) This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Insured Person's schedule.
(c) The Insurer will not pay for any delay that is not a qualifying delay.

Article 5. General exclusions
(a) The Insurer will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits the Insurer from paying.
(b) The Insurer will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.

Article 6. Making a claim
(a) The Insured Person must notify the Insurer of a claim within 21 days of the incident. The Insurer will not pay any claim notified after that time.
(b) The Insurer may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
(c) The Insured Person must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.

Article 7. Payment of claims
(a) The Insurer will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in the Insured Person's name.
(b) The Insurer aims to pay accepted claims within 5 working days of receiving all the documents the Insurer needs.

PART I: Definitions
I.1  Bicycles means bicycles and electric scooters.
I.2  High-risk items means jewellery, watches, laptops, games consoles and cameras.
I.3  Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
I.4  Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
I.5  Unoccupied means not lived in by the Policyholder or a member of the Policyholder's family for more than 60 consecutive days.

PART II: Limits and excess
II.1  Theft: limit $40,000 per incident; excess $250 per claim.
II.2  Escape of Water: limit $30,000 per incident; excess $250 per claim.
II.3  Accidental Damage: limit $2,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
II.4  Flood: limit $20,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
II.5  Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the excess is then deducted from the result.

PART III: Reasonable precautions
III.1  The Policyholder must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
III.2  The Policyholder must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

PART IV: Geographical limits
IV.1  Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
IV.2  Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

PART V: Theft
V.1  The Insurer will pay for contents stolen from the Policyholder's home.
V.2  The most the Insurer will pay for High-risk items under this section is $1,500 per incident.
V.3  The most the Insurer will pay for Bicycles under this section is $500 per incident.
V.4  The Insurer will not pay for theft while the home is unoccupied.
V.5  The Insurer will not pay for theft where there is no sign of forced entry to the home. This exclusion does not apply where the thief gained entry by deception, for example by posing as a utility worker.
V.6  The Insurer will not pay for theft from sheds, garages or other outbuildings. This exclusion does not apply if the outbuilding was locked and the theft involved forcible entry.

PART VI: General exclusions
VI.1  The Insurer will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
VI.2  The Insurer will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits the Insurer from paying.
VI.3  The Insurer will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Policyholder.

PART VII: Alternative accommodation
VII.1  If the Policyholder's home cannot be lived in after damage covered by this policy, the Insurer will pay the reasonable cost of comparable temporary accommodation.
VII.2  The Insurer will also pay for the temporary housing of pets that live with the Policyholder.
VII.3  Cover ends when the home is fit to live in again or after twelve months, whichever is sooner.

PART VIII: Customer support
VIII.1  The Insurer's helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
VIII.2  Outside these hours the Policyholder can leave a message and the Insurer will call back on the next working day.

PART IX: Making a claim
IX.1  The Insurer may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
IX.2  The Policyholder must notify the Insurer of a claim within 30 days of the incident. The Insurer will not pay any claim notified after that time.
IX.3  The Policyholder must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.

PART X: Taxes
X.1  The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
X.2  If the tax rate changes, the Insurer may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

state: document: A yellow line (solid or dashed) indicates that crossing the line will place a driver in a lane where opposing traffic is coming at the driver. A double yellow line is a painted marking separating two lanes of a road. It consists of two parallel, solid yellow lines, and its presence usually indicates a no-passing restriction or no passing zone, where crossing the line is prohibited. Obvious exceptions to this no-passing restriction include emergency maneuvers or temporary traffic flow changes due to road work. Often the double yellow line has sections where one of the lines becomes dashed (in which case it is no longer a ``double yellow''), indicating to the drivers traveling on the side closest to the dashed line that they may pass when it is safe. Double-yellow lines may be used to separate lanes of traffic traveling in opposite directions where passing would be dangerous, or to restrict access to lanes traveling in the same direction, such as HOV and express lanes on a highway.

## 1. Definitions
- **1.1** Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.

- **3.1** We will pay for sudden and unexpected accidental damage to your contents inside the home.
- **3.2** This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
- **3.3** The most we will pay for Portable electronics under this section is $750 per incident.
- **3.4** We will not pay for damage caused by pets.

- **4.1** We will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.

- **6.2** If we cannot meet our obligations, you may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

- **7.1** We may adjust limits at renewal in line with a published index of consumer prices.
- **7.2** Any adjustment will be shown in your renewal documents; limits do not change during a policy period.

- **8.1** Where practical, we will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.

- **9.1** When we replace an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes our property.

- **10.1** You cannot transfer your interest in this policy to anyone else without our written consent.

policy: HOME CONTENTS INSURANCE POLICY
Issued by Lantern General Insurance
In this policy, "the Insurer" means Lantern General Insurance and "the Policyholder" means the person named in the schedule.

Article 1. Definitions
(a) Art and antiques means paintings, antiques, rugs and other works of art.
(b) Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by the Insurer, before any excess, limit or sublimit is applied.
(c) Garden items means garden furniture, plants and outdoor tools.
(d) Home means the private residence at the address shown in the schedule.
(e) Portable electronics means laptops, tablets and mobile phones.
(f) Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.

Article 2. Limits and excess
(a) Theft: limit $40,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
(b) Escape of Water: limit $30,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
(c) Accidental Damage: limit $3,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
(d) Flood: limit $40,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
(e) The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

Article 3. Flood
(a) The Insurer will pay for contents damaged by flood water entering the Policyholder's home.
(b) No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 14 days after the policy start date.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Garden items under this section is $1,000 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for flood damage where a flood warning for the Policyholder's area had been issued before the policy started.

Article 4. Optional cover: Accidental Damage
(a) The Insurer will pay for sudden and unexpected accidental damage to the Policyholder's contents inside the home.
(b) This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Policyholder's schedule.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Portable electronics under this section is $750 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by pets.
(e) The Insurer will not pay for wear and tear, or damage that happens gradually.

Article 5. Escape of Water
(a) The Insurer will pay for contents damaged by water escaping from a fixed pipe, tank or domestic appliance.
(b) The most the Insurer will pay for Art and antiques under this section is $1,000 per incident.
(c) The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by water leaking gradually over a period of time.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by the failure of grout or sealant around baths and showers.

Article 6. General exclusions
(a) The Insurer will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits the Insurer from paying.
(b) The Insurer will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Policyholder.

Article 7. Making a claim
(a) The Policyholder must notify the Insurer of a claim within 14 days of the incident. The Insurer will not pay any claim notified after that time.
(b) The Insurer may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
(c) The Policyholder must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.

I rented it and snuggled down to enjoy a classic holiday story brought to life on screen. Boy, was I disappointed. This movie veered off from the book more times than is forgivable. George C. Scott is an excellent actor but in this, it seemed that he was fully into character only about 20% of the time. The rest of the time he was quite flat. I realize that this was made in '84, pre-CG effects, for the most part. But it looked to be very B-movie quality, especially the encounter with Jacob Marley. The biggest disappointment was the fact that they left out one of the most moving parts of the story: When the Spirit of Christmas Present takes Scrooge on the whirlwind tour of the world, observing people in the bleakest of circumstances still having the light and love of Christmastime. I will admit that Mr. Scott did a good job with the "reformed" Scrooge at the end. That was a refreshing portrayal. I wish that Bob Cratchit had been portrayed as a little more ragged and down-trodden. And Tiny Tim... oh don't even get me started on bad child actors...

policy: GADGET COVER: TERMS AND CONDITIONS
Issued by Voltguard Protection Ltd
In this policy, "the Provider" means Voltguard Protection Ltd and "the Customer" means the person named in the schedule.

Article 1. Definitions
(a) Accessories means cases, chargers, earbuds and styluses.
(b) Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by the Provider, before any service fee, limit or sublimit is applied.
(c) Authorised repairer means a repairer approved in writing by the Provider.
(d) Premium means the amount the Customer must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
(e) Wearables means smartwatches and fitness trackers.

Article 2. Limits and service fee
(a) Accidental Damage: limit $800 per incident; service fee $49 per claim.
(b) Breakdown: limit $1,500 per incident; service fee $25 per claim.
(c) Theft and Loss: limit $1,200 per incident; service fee $99 per claim.
(d) Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the service fee is then deducted from the result.

Article 3. Notices
(a) Any notice the Provider gives under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address the Provider holds.
(b) Notices from the Customer should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

Article 4. Arbitration
(a) If the Provider accepts a claim but disagree with the Customer about the amount, the difference will be referred to an arbitrator appointed by both parties.
(b) Where arbitration applies, obtaining an award is a condition precedent to any legal action against the Provider.

Article 5. Fraud
(a) If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, the Provider will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
(b) The Provider may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

Article 6. Duty of fair presentation
(a) The Customer must answer all questions the Provider asks honestly and to the best of the Customer's knowledge.
(b) If the Customer gives incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, the Provider may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
(c) If the Customer gives incorrect information carelessly, the Provider may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

Article 7. Repair process
(a) After a claim is accepted, the Provider will send a prepaid mailer or book a courier collection.
(b) The Provider aims to return repaired devices within 5 business days of receiving them.

Article 8. Accidental Damage
(a) The Provider will repair or replace the Customer's device if it is accidentally damaged.
(b) The most the Provider will pay for Accessories under this section is $100 per incident.
(c) The most the Provider will pay for Wearables under this section is $300 per incident.
(d) The Provider will not pay for cosmetic damage, such as scratches or dents, that does not affect how the device works.
(e) The Provider will not pay for damage following a repair by anyone other than the Provider or an authorised repairer. This exclusion does not apply if the Provider approved the repair in writing beforehand.

Article 9. General exclusions
(a) The Provider will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
(b) The Provider will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.

Article 10. Making a claim
(a) The Provider may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
(b) The Customer must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
(c) The Customer must notify the Provider of a claim within 60 days of the incident. The Provider will not pay any claim notified after that time.

Article 11. Assignment
(a) The Customer cannot transfer the Customer's interest in this policy to anyone else without the Provider's written consent.

# Single-Trip Travel Protection Plan
Issued by Bluewater Assurance

## 1. Definitions
- **1.1** Dental treatment means treatment of the teeth or gums.
- **1.2** Hazardous activity means skydiving, motor racing, or trekking or climbing above 4,000 metres.
- **1.3** Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
- **1.4** Physiotherapy means treatment of muscles and joints by a physiotherapist.
- **1.5** Pre-existing condition means any illness or injury for which you received treatment or advice in the 12 months before the policy start date.
- **1.6** Sports equipment means skis, snowboards, golf clubs, surfboards and bicycles.
- **1.7** Territory means the countries in which cover applies, as shown in the schedule.
- **1.8** Valuables means laptops, tablets, mobile phones, cameras, watches and jewellery.

## 2. Limits and excess
- **2.1** Baggage and Personal Belongings: limit $1,500 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
- **2.2** Emergency Medical Expenses: limit $50,000 per incident; excess $150 per claim.
- **2.3** Trip Cancellation: limit $2,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
- **2.4** Travel Delay: limit $500 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
- **2.5** The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

## 3. Baggage and Personal Belongings
- **3.1** We will pay for the loss of, theft of, or damage to your baggage and personal belongings during the trip.
- **3.2** The most we will pay for Valuables under this section is $500 per incident.
- **3.3** The most we will pay for Sports equipment under this section is $450 per incident.
- **3.4** We will not pay for loss or theft of property left unattended in a vehicle or in a public place. This exclusion does not apply to property locked out of sight in the boot or trunk of a locked vehicle.
- **3.5** We will not pay for loss caused by confiscation or detention by customs or other officials.
- **3.6** We will not pay for damage caused by wear and tear or gradual deterioration.

## 4. Emergency Medical Expenses
- **4.1** We will pay reasonable and necessary emergency medical costs incurred during the trip.

policy: RENTERS CONTENTS PROTECTION
Issued by Oakfield Assurance

PART I: Definitions
I.1  Art and antiques means paintings, antiques, rugs and other works of art.
I.2  Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
I.3  Outbuilding means a shed, garage or greenhouse within the boundaries of the home.

PART II: Limits and excess
II.1  Theft: limit $40,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
II.2  Escape of Water: limit $30,000 per incident; excess $250 per claim.
II.3  Accidental Damage: limit $2,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
II.4  Flood: limit $40,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
II.5  The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

PART III: Escape of Water
III.1  The Insurer will pay for contents damaged by water escaping from a fixed pipe, tank or domestic appliance.
III.2  The most the Insurer will pay for Art and antiques under this section is $1,000 per incident.
III.3  The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by water leaking gradually over a period of time.
III.4  The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by the failure of grout or sealant around baths and showers.

PART IV: Data protection
IV.1  The Insurer will use the personal information the Policyholder provides to administer this policy and to handle claims.
IV.2  The Insurer will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
IV.3  The Policyholder can ask for a copy of the personal information the Insurer holds by writing to the Insurer's data protection officer.

PART V: Compensation scheme
V.1  The Insurer is covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
V.2  If the Insurer cannot meet the Insurer's obligations, the Policyholder may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

PART VI: Severability
VI.1  If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

PART VII: General exclusions
VII.1  The Insurer will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
VII.2  The Insurer will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.

PART VIII: Electronic documents
VIII.1  The Insurer will send documents by email unless the Policyholder asks for paper copies.
VIII.2  The Policyholder must tell the Insurer if the Policyholder's email address changes.
VIII.3  Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

PART IX: Salvage
IX.1  When the Insurer replaces an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes the Insurer's property.
IX.2  If stolen property is recovered after the Insurer has paid a claim, the Policyholder must tell the Insurer and either return the payment or give the Insurer the property.

PART X: Making a claim
X.1  The Insurer may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
X.2  The Policyholder must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
X.3  The Policyholder must notify the Insurer of a claim within 60 days of the incident. The Insurer will not pay any claim notified after that time.

PART XI: Accessibility
XI.1  This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

PART XII: Market conditions
XII.1  If the replacement item is no longer available, the Insurer will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

PART XIII: Arbitration
XIII.1  If the Insurer accepts a claim but disagree with the Policyholder about the amount, the difference will be referred to an arbitrator appointed by both parties.
XIII.2  Where arbitration applies, obtaining an award is a condition precedent to any legal action against the Insurer.

policy: EMPLOYEE HEALTH BENEFITS PLAN: SUMMARY PLAN DESCRIPTION
Issued by Wellspring Benefits Administration

PART I: Definitions
I.1  Frames means spectacle frames bought without new lenses.
I.2  Major restorative work means crowns, bridges, root canal treatment and implants.
I.3  Orthodontics means braces and clear aligners.
I.4  Replacement period means 12 months from the date of the Member's last eyewear claim.
I.5  Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.

PART II: Limits and deductible
II.1  Dental Care: limit $2,000 per treatment; deductible $100 per claim.
II.2  Vision Care: limit $300 per treatment; deductible $25 per claim.
II.3  Therapy Services: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $50 per claim.
II.4  Hearing Care: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $100 per claim.
II.5  Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the deductible is then deducted from the result.

PART III: Vision Care
III.1  The Plan will reimburse eye tests and prescription eyewear.
III.2  The most the Plan will pay for Frames under this section is $120 per treatment.
III.3  The Plan will not pay for eyewear without prescription lenses.
III.4  The Plan will not pay for a further eyewear claim within the replacement period.

PART IV: Dental Care
IV.1  The Plan will reimburse the cost of dental treatment provided by a licensed dentist.
IV.2  No cover applies under this section to any treatment that happens within the first 90 days after the policy start date.
IV.3  The most the Plan will pay for Major restorative work under this section is $500 per treatment.
IV.4  The most the Plan will pay for Orthodontics under this section is $800 per treatment.
IV.5  The Plan will not pay for treatment that is mainly cosmetic, such as whitening or veneers. This exclusion does not apply to treatment needed to repair damage caused by an accident.
IV.6  The Plan will not pay for treatment by a provider outside the plan's network. This exclusion does not apply to emergency treatment for sudden severe pain.

PART V: General exclusions
V.1  The Plan will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
V.2  The Plan will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
V.3  The Plan will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.

PART VI: Making a claim
VI.1  The Plan may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
VI.2  The Member must notify the Plan of a claim within 90 days of the treatment. The Plan will not pay any claim notified after that time.
VI.3  The Member must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.

state: The time of sunset varies throughout the year, and is determined by the viewer's position on Earth, specified by longitude and latitude, and elevation. Small daily changes and noticeable semi-annual changes in the timing of sunsets are driven by the axial tilt of Earth, daily rotation of the Earth, the planet's movement in its annual elliptical orbit around the Sun, and the Earth and Moon's paired revolutions around each other. During winter and spring, the days get longer and sunsets occur later every day until the day of the latest sunset, which occurs after the summer solstice. In the Northern Hemisphere, the latest sunset occurs late in June or in early July, but not on the summer solstice of June 21. This date depends on the viewer's latitude (connected with the Earth's slower movement around the aphelion around July 4). Likewise, the earliest sunset does not occur on the winter solstice, but rather about two weeks earlier, again depending on the viewer's latitude. In the Northern Hemisphere, it occurs in early December or late November (influenced by the Earth's faster movement near its perihelion, which occurs around January 3).

## 4. General exclusions
- **4.1** We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.

- **7.1** If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, we will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.

- **8.1** A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

- **10.1** If a device is found after we have replaced it, the found device becomes our property and must be sent to us.
- **10.2** We may block devices reported as lost or stolen so that they cannot be used on mobile networks.

Issued by Tessera Warranty Company

## 1. Definitions
- **1.1** Accessories means cases, chargers and earbuds.
- **1.2** Family means your spouse or partner and any children who live with you.
- **1.3** Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in your schedule.

## 2. Limits and service fee
- **2.1** Accidental Damage: limit $1,500 per incident; service fee $79 per claim.
- **2.2** Breakdown: limit $600 per incident; service fee $25 per claim.
- **2.3** Theft and Loss: limit $800 per incident; service fee $149 per claim.
- **2.4** Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the service fee is then deducted from the result.

## 3. Optional cover: Theft and Loss
- **3.1** We will replace your device if it is stolen or lost.
- **3.2** This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
- **3.3** The most we will pay for Accessories under this section is $100 per incident.
- **3.4** We will not pay for loss or theft of property left unattended in a vehicle or in a public place. This exclusion does not apply to property locked out of sight in the boot or trunk of a locked vehicle.
- **3.5** We will not pay for theft that was not reported to the police.

## 4. General exclusions
- **4.1** We will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by you.
- **4.2** We will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.

## 5. Making a claim
- **5.1** We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
- **5.2** You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
- **5.3** You must notify us of a claim within 60 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.

## 6. Discounts
- **6.1** Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
- **6.2** If a condition for a discount stops being met, we may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

## 7. Cancellation
- **7.1** You can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
- **7.2** After the first 14 days you can cancel at any time; we will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $30.
- **7.3** We can cancel this policy by giving you 30 days' written notice to the last address we hold.

## 8. Reasonable precautions
- **8.1** You must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
- **8.2** You must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

## 9. Unrecoverable devices
- **9.1** If a device is found after we have replaced it, the found device becomes our property and must be sent to us.
- **9.2** We may block devices reported as lost or stolen so that they cannot be used on mobile networks.

=== CLAIM ===
From: Owen Zeller
Subject: Claim on policy K138152

Hello,

I would like to claim under Theft and Loss for a pair of earbuds. My policy started on July 14, 2026 and my schedule lists Accidental Damage, Breakdown, Theft and Loss (extensions: none). The incident happened on March 14, 2027. The earbuds were taken from Owen's bag on a crowded train. Owen bought the device from an authorised retailer. Owen uses the device mainly for work. The device is registered in Owen's name.

I am sending this on March 27, 2027, which is when I first notified you. Your adjuster assessed the loss at $293.

Thanks,
Owen

The most depressing ramen experience since... well... ever. I have never left a bowl of ramen unfinished--half my bowl remained untouched. -___-'

Ordered Shoku from the Bachi Burger side of the restaurant a couple days ago. I've been a little burger'd out lately and figured this was the perfect opportunity to try their ramen. I've been putting it off for something like 2 years. When I go to Bachi, I usually want burgers & oxtail fries--not soup! My Spicy Miso Ramen w/ Extra Menma made me wish I had just thrown my money at a burger T___T

As an appetizer, we ordered calamari. It was fine I guess.The breading was a little soft but the dipping sauces tasted pretty good. It was served with an aioli and a zingy citrusy oil. The ramen broth is alright. It's somewhat rich, saltiness is right, but the flavor is very strange. I'm not sure if they're taking a lot of liberties with their ramen or someone put something they shouldn't have in there but the flavor profile was extremely different from what I have ever had at any ramen place (in Cali or Vegas). Whatever region of Japan this came out of, something was definitely amiss. At least their noodles were good though. Good flavor, right texture, and slightly chewy. Just how I like them!
