# Annual Multi-Trip Travel Cover
Issued by Northstar Underwriting

## 1. Definitions
- **1.1** Excursions and tickets means pre-booked excursions, tours, and event or theatre tickets.
- **1.2** Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in your schedule.
- **1.3** Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
- **1.4** Travelling companion means a person who has booked to travel with you on the same trip.

## 2. Limits and excess
- **2.1** Baggage and Personal Belongings: limit $2,000 per incident; excess $75 per claim.
- **2.2** Emergency Medical Expenses: limit $50,000 per incident; excess $150 per claim.
- **2.3** Trip Cancellation: limit $3,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
- **2.4** Travel Delay: limit $500 per incident; excess $25 per claim.
- **2.5** The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

## 3. Trip Cancellation
- **3.1** We will pay non-refundable travel and accommodation costs if you must cancel the trip for a reason beyond your control.
- **3.2** No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 10 days after the policy start date.
- **3.3** The most we will pay for Excursions and tickets under this section is $200 per incident.
- **3.4** We will not pay for cancellation caused by a strike or other event that had been publicly announced before you bought the policy.
- **3.5** We will not pay for cancellation because you no longer wish to travel.

## 4. General exclusions
- **4.1** We will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
- **4.2** We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
- **4.3** We will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by you.

## 5. Sanctions
- **5.1** We will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose us to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

## 6. Missed departure
- **6.1** We will pay reasonable additional travel and accommodation costs to reach your destination if you arrive too late to board your booked transport because public transport fails.
- **6.2** You must allow enough time to reach the departure point, and must obtain written confirmation of the delay from the transport operator.

## 7. Environmental commitment
- **7.1** Where practical, we will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
- **7.2** You may ask for a new part instead, and we will tell you whether any additional cost would apply.

## 8. Electronic documents
- **8.1** We will send documents by email unless you ask for paper copies.
- **8.2** You must tell us if your email address changes.
- **8.3** Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

## 9. Making a claim
- **9.1** You must notify us of a claim within 90 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.
- **9.2** We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
- **9.3** You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.

My policy started on May 9, 2025 and my schedule lists Baggage and Personal Belongings, Emergency Medical Expenses, Trip Cancellation, Travel Delay (extensions: none). The incident happened on May 14, 2025. The trip was cancelled because Maya was admitted to hospital a week before departure. Maya paid for the trip with a credit card. I am sending this on July 8, 2025, which is when I first notified you. Your adjuster assessed the loss at $3,599.

## 1. Definitions
- **1.1** Hearing accessories means batteries, chargers and cleaning kits.
- **1.2** Hearing aid replacement period means 36 months from the purchase of hearing aids funded by the plan.
- **1.3** Massage therapy means sports massage, massage therapy and reflexology.

## 2. Limits and deductible
- **2.1** Dental Care: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $100 per claim.
- **2.2** Vision Care: limit $500 per treatment; deductible $40 per claim.

- **2.4** Hearing Care: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $150 per claim.

## 3. Therapy Services
- **3.1** We will reimburse physiotherapy, osteopathy and counselling provided by a registered practitioner.

- **5.1** We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.

policy: GROUP HEALTH CASH PLAN
Issued by Cedar Benefits Services
In this policy, "the Plan" means Cedar Benefits Services and "the Member" means the person named in the schedule.

Article 1. Definitions
(a) Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
(b) Frames means spectacle frames bought without new lenses.
(c) Major restorative work means crowns, bridges, root canal treatment and implants.
(d) Orthodontics means braces and clear aligners.
(e) Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in the Member's schedule.
(f) Premium means the amount the Member must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
(g) Replacement period means 24 months from the date of the Member's last eyewear claim.

Article 2. Limits and deductible
(a) Dental Care: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $50 per claim.
(b) Vision Care: limit $400 per treatment; deductible $40 per claim.
(c) Therapy Services: limit $2,000 per treatment; deductible $75 per claim.
(d) Hearing Care: limit $2,000 per treatment; deductible $100 per claim.
(e) The deductible is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

Article 3. Vision Care
(a) The Plan will reimburse eye tests and prescription eyewear.
(b) The most the Plan will pay for Frames under this section is $120 per treatment.
(c) The Plan will not pay for eyewear without prescription lenses.
(d) The Plan will not pay for a further eyewear claim within the replacement period.

Article 4. Dental Care
(a) The Plan will reimburse the cost of dental treatment provided by a licensed dentist.
(b) No cover applies under this section to any treatment that happens within the first 90 days after the policy start date.
(c) The most the Plan will pay for Major restorative work under this section is $750 per treatment.
(d) The most the Plan will pay for Orthodontics under this section is $800 per treatment.
(e) The Plan will not pay for treatment that is mainly cosmetic, such as whitening or veneers. This exclusion does not apply to treatment needed to repair damage caused by an accident.
(f) The Plan will not pay for treatment by a provider outside the plan's network. This exclusion does not apply to emergency treatment for sudden severe pain.

Article 5. General exclusions
(a) The Plan will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits the Plan from paying.
(b) The Plan will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.

Article 6. Making a claim
(a) The Member must notify the Plan of a claim within 30 days of the treatment. The Plan will not pay any claim notified after that time.
(b) The Member must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
(c) The Plan may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

Article 7. Waiver
(a) If the Plan does not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean the Plan has given up the right to enforce it later.

Article 8. Cancellation
(a) The Member can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
(b) After the first 14 days the Member can cancel at any time; the Plan will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $30.
(c) The Plan can cancel this policy by giving the Member 30 days' written notice to the last address the Plan holds.

Article 9. Accessibility
(a) This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

policy: GADGET COVER: TERMS AND CONDITIONS
Issued by Tessera Warranty Company
In this policy, "the Provider" means Tessera Warranty Company and "the Customer" means the person named in the schedule.

Article 1. Definitions
(a) Accessories means cases, chargers, earbuds and styluses.
(b) Battery replacement means replacement batteries and battery repairs.
(c) Device means the item shown in the schedule, bought new from an authorised retailer.
(d) Manufacturer's warranty period means the first 24 months after the device was bought.
(e) Premium means the amount the Customer must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
(f) Wearables means smartwatches and fitness trackers.

Article 2. Limits and service fee
(a) Accidental Damage: limit $1,500 per incident; service fee $49 per claim.
(b) Breakdown: limit $600 per incident; service fee $49 per claim.
(c) Theft and Loss: limit $1,200 per incident; service fee $149 per claim.
(d) Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the service fee is then deducted from the result.

Article 3. Accidental Damage
(a) The Provider will repair or replace the Customer's device if it is accidentally damaged.
(b) The most the Provider will pay for Accessories under this section is $100 per incident.
(c) The most the Provider will pay for Wearables under this section is $300 per incident.
(d) The Provider will not pay for cosmetic damage, such as scratches or dents, that does not affect how the device works.
(e) The Provider will not pay for damage following a repair by anyone other than the Provider or an authorised repairer. This exclusion does not apply if the Provider approved the repair in writing beforehand.

Article 4. Breakdown
(a) The Provider will repair or replace the Customer's device if it stops working because of an electrical or mechanical fault.
(b) No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 30 days after the policy start date.
(c) The most the Provider will pay for Battery replacement under this section is $120 per incident.
(d) The Provider will not pay for breakdowns during the manufacturer's warranty period.
(e) The Provider will not pay for breakdown caused by liquid getting into the device.

Article 5. General exclusions
(a) The Provider will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
(b) The Provider will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.

Article 6. Making a claim
(a) The Provider may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
(b) The Customer must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
(c) The Customer must notify the Provider of a claim within 14 days of the incident. The Provider will not pay any claim notified after that time.

Article 7. Other insurance
(a) If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, the Provider will pay only the Provider's proportionate share.
(b) The Customer must tell the Provider about any other insurance that covers the same loss when the Customer makes a claim.

# Device Protection Plan Terms
Issued by Circuit Care Services

## 1. Definitions
- **1.1** Accessories means cases, chargers and earbuds.
- **1.2** Battery replacement means replacement batteries and battery repairs.
- **1.3** Manufacturer's warranty period means the first 24 months after the device was bought.
- **1.4** Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in your schedule.
- **1.5** Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
- **1.6** Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows your details, the covers you bought and any extensions.

## 2. Limits and service fee
- **2.1** Accidental Damage: limit $800 per incident; service fee $79 per claim.
- **2.2** Breakdown: limit $600 per incident; service fee $25 per claim.
- **2.3** Theft and Loss: limit $800 per incident; service fee $149 per claim.
- **2.4** The service fee is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

## 3. Optional cover: Theft and Loss
- **3.1** We will replace your device if it is stolen or lost.
- **3.2** This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
- **3.3** The most we will pay for Accessories under this section is $100 per incident.
- **3.4** We will not pay for loss or theft of property left unattended in a vehicle or in a public place. This exclusion does not apply to property locked out of sight in the boot or trunk of a locked vehicle.
- **3.5** We will not pay for theft that was not reported to the police.

## 4. Breakdown
- **4.1** We will repair or replace your device if it stops working because of an electrical or mechanical fault.
- **4.2** No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 30 days after the policy start date.
- **4.3** The most we will pay for Battery replacement under this section is $80 per incident.
- **4.4** We will not pay for breakdowns during the manufacturer's warranty period.
- **4.5** We will not pay for breakdown caused by liquid getting into the device.

## 5. General exclusions
- **5.1** We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
- **5.2** We will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
- **5.3** We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.

## 6. Making a claim
- **6.1** You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
- **6.2** You must notify us of a claim within 21 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.
- **6.3** We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

policy: HOME CONTENTS INSURANCE POLICY
Issued by Hearthstone Insurance plc

PART I: Definitions
I.1  Art and antiques means paintings, antiques, rugs and other works of art.
I.2  Bicycles means bicycles and electric scooters.
I.3  Forcible entry means entry to the home that leaves visible damage to doors, windows or locks.
I.4  Garden items means garden furniture, plants and outdoor tools.
I.5  High-risk items means jewellery, watches, laptops, games consoles and cameras.
I.6  Unoccupied means not lived in by the Policyholder or a member of the Policyholder's family for more than 45 consecutive days.

PART II: Limits and excess
II.1  Theft: limit $20,000 per incident; excess $250 per claim.
II.2  Escape of Water: limit $15,000 per incident; excess $250 per claim.
II.3  Accidental Damage: limit $2,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
II.4  Flood: limit $20,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
II.5  The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

PART III: Flood
III.1  The Insurer will pay for contents damaged by flood water entering the Policyholder's home.
III.2  No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 60 days after the policy start date.
III.3  The most the Insurer will pay for Garden items under this section is $1,000 per incident.
III.4  The Insurer will not pay for flood damage where a flood warning for the Policyholder's area had been issued before the policy started.

PART IV: Theft
IV.1  The Insurer will pay for contents stolen from the Policyholder's home.
IV.2  The most the Insurer will pay for High-risk items under this section is $1,000 per incident.
IV.3  The most the Insurer will pay for Bicycles under this section is $500 per incident.
IV.4  The Insurer will not pay for theft while the home is unoccupied.
IV.5  The Insurer will not pay for theft where there is no sign of forced entry to the home. This exclusion does not apply where the thief gained entry by deception, for example by posing as a utility worker.
IV.6  The Insurer will not pay for theft from sheds, garages or other outbuildings. This exclusion does not apply if the outbuilding was locked and the theft involved forcible entry.

PART V: Escape of Water
V.1  The Insurer will pay for contents damaged by water escaping from a fixed pipe, tank or domestic appliance.
V.2  The most the Insurer will pay for Art and antiques under this section is $1,000 per incident.
V.3  The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by water leaking gradually over a period of time.
V.4  The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by the failure of grout or sealant around baths and showers.

PART VI: General exclusions
VI.1  The Insurer will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits the Insurer from paying.
VI.2  The Insurer will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.

PART VII: Making a claim
VII.1  The Policyholder must notify the Insurer of a claim within 14 days of the incident. The Insurer will not pay any claim notified after that time.
VII.2  The Policyholder must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
VII.3  The Insurer may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

policy: GROUP HEALTH CASH PLAN
Issued by the Benefits Trust

PART I: Definitions
I.1  Major restorative work means crowns, bridges, root canal treatment and implants.
I.2  Orthodontics means braces and clear aligners.
I.3  Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.

PART II: Limits and deductible
II.1  Dental Care: limit $2,000 per treatment; deductible $100 per claim.
II.2  Vision Care: limit $400 per treatment; deductible $40 per claim.
II.3  Therapy Services: limit $2,000 per treatment; deductible $75 per claim.
II.4  Hearing Care: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $100 per claim.
II.5  The deductible is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

PART III: Dental Care
III.1  The Plan will reimburse the cost of dental treatment provided by a licensed dentist.
III.2  No cover applies under this section to any treatment that happens within the first 90 days after the policy start date.
III.3  The most the Plan will pay for Major restorative work under this section is $750 per treatment.
III.4  The most the Plan will pay for Orthodontics under this section is $800 per treatment.
III.5  The Plan will not pay for treatment that is mainly cosmetic, such as whitening or veneers. This exclusion does not apply to treatment needed to repair damage caused by an accident.
III.6  The Plan will not pay for treatment by a provider outside the plan's network. This exclusion does not apply to emergency treatment for sudden severe pain.

PART IV: General exclusions
IV.1  The Plan will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
IV.2  The Plan will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits the Plan from paying.
IV.3  The Plan will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.

PART V: Making a claim
V.1  The Member must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
V.2  The Plan may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
V.3  The Member must notify the Plan of a claim within 21 days of the treatment. The Plan will not pay any claim notified after that time.

PART VI: Contracts (Rights of Third Parties)
VI.1  A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

PART VII: Exchange of information
VII.1  To prevent fraud, the Plan may check the details the Member gives against public records and industry databases.
VII.2  The Plan may contact previous insurers to confirm the Member's claims history.

PART VIII: How to read this document
VIII.1  This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.
VIII.2  Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
VIII.3  Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

PART IX: Arbitration
IX.1  If the Plan accepts a claim but disagree with the Member about the amount, the difference will be referred to an arbitrator appointed by both parties.
IX.2  Where arbitration applies, obtaining an award is a condition precedent to any legal action against the Plan.

PART X: Assignment
X.1  The Member cannot transfer the Member's interest in this policy to anyone else without the Plan's written consent.

PART XI: Automatic renewal
XI.1  Unless the Member tells the Plan otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details the Plan holds.
XI.2  The Member can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting the Plan's helpline.

policy: ANNUAL MULTI-TRIP TRAVEL COVER
Issued by Meridian Travel Insurance Ltd
In this policy, "the Insurer" means Meridian Travel Insurance Ltd and "the Insured Person" means the person named in the schedule.

Article 1. Definitions
(a) Dental treatment means treatment of the teeth or gums.
(b) Excursions and tickets means pre-booked excursions, tours, and event or theatre tickets.
(c) Hazardous activity means skydiving, motor racing, or trekking or climbing above 3,000 metres.
(d) Physiotherapy means treatment of muscles and joints by a physiotherapist.
(e) Pre-existing condition means any illness or injury for which the Insured Person received treatment or advice in the 3 months before the policy start date.
(f) Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
(g) Qualifying delay means a delay to the scheduled departure of more than 8 hours.

Article 2. Limits and excess
(a) Baggage and Personal Belongings: limit $1,500 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
(b) Emergency Medical Expenses: limit $25,000 per incident; excess $250 per claim.
(c) Trip Cancellation: limit $3,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
(d) Travel Delay: limit $500 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
(e) Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the excess is then deducted from the result.

Article 3. Optional cover: Travel Delay
(a) The Insurer will pay reasonable costs of meals and accommodation if the Insured Person's outbound departure is delayed.
(b) This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Insured Person's schedule.
(c) The Insurer will not pay for any delay that is not a qualifying delay.

Article 4. Trip Cancellation
(a) The Insurer will pay non-refundable travel and accommodation costs if the Insured Person must cancel the trip for a reason beyond the Insured Person's control.
(b) No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 7 days after the policy start date.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Excursions and tickets under this section is $200 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for cancellation caused by a strike or other event that had been publicly announced before the Insured Person bought the policy.
(e) The Insurer will not pay for cancellation because the Insured Person no longer wish to travel.

Article 5. Emergency Medical Expenses
(a) The Insurer will pay reasonable and necessary emergency medical costs incurred during the trip.
(b) The most the Insurer will pay for Dental treatment under this section is $400 per incident.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Physiotherapy under this section is $300 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for treatment of a pre-existing condition.
(e) The Insurer will not pay for injury or illness arising from a hazardous activity. This exclusion does not apply if the Adventure Sports extension is shown in the Insured Person's schedule.
(f) The Insurer will not pay for any claim arising from the Insured Person's being under the influence of alcohol or drugs.

Article 6. General exclusions
(a) The Insurer will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
(b) The Insurer will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.

Article 7. Making a claim
(a) The Insurer may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
(b) The Insured Person must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
(c) The Insured Person must notify the Insurer of a claim within 60 days of the incident. The Insurer will not pay any claim notified after that time.

Issued by the Benefits Trust
In this policy, "the Plan" means the Benefits Trust and "the Member" means the person named in the schedule.

Article 1. Definitions
(a) Hearing accessories means batteries, chargers and cleaning kits.
(b) Hearing aid replacement period means 24 months from the purchase of hearing aids funded by the plan.
(c) Major restorative work means crowns, bridges, root canal treatment and implants.
(d) Orthodontics means braces and clear aligners.
(e) Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.

Article 2. Limits and deductible
(a) Dental Care: limit $1,500 per treatment; deductible $100 per claim.
(b) Vision Care: limit $400 per treatment; deductible $25 per claim.
(c) Therapy Services: limit $2,000 per treatment; deductible $75 per claim.
(d) Hearing Care: limit $2,000 per treatment; deductible $100 per claim.
(e) The deductible is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

Article 3. Optional cover: Hearing Care
(a) The Plan will reimburse hearing tests and hearing aids.
(b) This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Member's schedule.
(c) The most the Plan will pay for Hearing accessories under this section is $150 per treatment.
(d) The Plan will not pay for replacement hearing aids bought within the hearing aid replacement period.

Article 4. Dental Care
(a) The Plan will reimburse the cost of dental treatment provided by a licensed dentist.
(b) No cover applies under this section to any treatment that happens within the first 60 days after the policy start date.
(c) The most the Plan will pay for Major restorative work under this section is $500 per treatment.
(d) The most the Plan will pay for Orthodontics under this section is $800 per treatment.
(e) The Plan will not pay for treatment that is mainly cosmetic, such as whitening or veneers. This exclusion does not apply to treatment needed to repair damage caused by an accident.
(f) The Plan will not pay for treatment by a provider outside the plan's network. This exclusion does not apply to emergency treatment for sudden severe pain.

Article 5. Premium payment
(a) The Member must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
(b) If an instalment is not paid within 7 days of its due date, the Plan may cancel the policy after giving notice.

Article 6. General exclusions
(a) The Plan will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Member.
(b) The Plan will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
(c) The Plan will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.

Article 7. Making a claim
(a) The Member must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
(b) The Member must notify the Plan of a claim within 14 days of the treatment. The Plan will not pay any claim notified after that time.
(c) The Plan may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

state: Lars Von Trier is never backward in trying out new techniques. Some of them are very original while others are best forgotten. He depicts postwar Germany as a nightmarish train journey. With so many cities lying in ruins, Leo Kessler a young American of German descent feels obliged to help in their restoration. It is not a simple task as he quickly finds out. His uncle finds him a job as a night conductor on the Zentropa Railway Line. His job is to attend to the needs of the passengers. When the shoes are polished a chalk mark is made on the soles. A terrible argument ensues when a passenger's shoes are not chalked despite the fact they have been polished. There are many allusions to the German fanaticism of adherence to such stupid details. The railway journey is like an allegory representing man's procession through life with all its trials and tribulations. In one sequence Leo dashes through the back carriages to discover them filled with half-starved bodies appearing to have just escaped from Auschwitz . These images, horrible as they are, are fleeting as in a dream, each with its own terrible impact yet unconnected. At a station called Urmitz Leo jumps from the train with a parceled bomb. state:
# Travel Insurance Policy Wording
Issued by Northstar Underwriting

## 1. Definitions
- **1.1** Dental treatment means treatment of the teeth or gums.
- **1.2** Excursions and tickets means pre-booked excursions, tours, and event or theatre tickets.
- **1.3** Hazardous activity means skydiving, motor racing, or trekking or climbing above 4,000 metres.
- **1.4** Limit means the most we will pay for all claims under a section arising from one incident.
- **1.5** Physiotherapy means treatment of muscles and joints by a physiotherapist.
- **1.6** Pre-existing condition means any illness or injury for which you received treatment or advice in the 3 months before the policy start date.
- **1.7** Qualifying delay means a delay to the scheduled departure of more than 12 hours.

## 2. Limits and excess
- **2.1** Baggage and Personal Belongings: limit $2,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
- **2.2** Emergency Medical Expenses: limit $25,000 per incident; excess $150 per claim.
- **2.3** Trip Cancellation: limit $3,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
- **2.4** Travel Delay: limit $500 per incident; excess $25 per claim.
- **2.5** The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

## 3. Trip Cancellation
- **3.1** We will pay non-refundable travel and accommodation costs if you must cancel the trip for a reason beyond your control.
- **3.2** No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 10 days after the policy start date.
- **3.3** The most we will pay for Excursions and tickets under this section is $200 per incident.
- **3.4** We will not pay for cancellation caused by a strike or other event that had been publicly announced before you bought the policy.
- **3.5** We will not pay for cancellation because you no longer wish to travel.

## 4. Emergency Medical Expenses
- **4.1** We will pay reasonable and necessary emergency medical costs incurred during the trip.
- **4.2** The most we will pay for Dental treatment under this section is $400 per incident.
- **4.3** The most we will pay for Physiotherapy under this section is $500 per incident.
- **4.4** We will not pay for treatment of a pre-existing condition.
- **4.5** We will not pay for injury or illness arising from a hazardous activity. This exclusion does not apply if the Adventure Sports extension is shown in your schedule.
- **4.6** We will not pay for any claim arising from your being under the influence of alcohol or drugs.

## 5. Optional cover: Travel Delay
- **5.1** We will pay reasonable costs of meals and accommodation if your outbound departure is delayed.
- **5.2** This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
- **5.3** We will not pay for any delay that is not a qualifying delay.

## 6. General exclusions
- **6.1** We will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
- **6.2** We will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by you.

## 7. Making a claim
- **7.1** You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
- **7.2** We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
- **7.3** You must notify us of a claim within 30 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.

=== CLAIM ===
From: Luca Horvat
Subject: Claim on policy T438032

Hello,

I would like to claim under Trip Cancellation for pre-booked concert and excursion tickets. My policy started on November 25, 2025 and my schedule lists Baggage and Personal Belongings, Emergency Medical Expenses, Trip Cancellation, Travel Delay (extensions: none). The incident happened on July 5, 2026. The trip was cancelled because Luca was admitted to hospital a week before departure. Luca was travelling with two colleagues. The destination was a coastal town Luca had visited before. The return flight was scheduled for the following week.

I am sending this on July 17, 2026, which is when I first notified you. Your adjuster assessed the loss at $420.25.

Thanks,
Luca

policy: ANNUAL MULTI-TRIP TRAVEL COVER
Issued by Compass Mutual
In this policy, "the Insurer" means Compass Mutual and "the Insured Person" means the person named in the schedule.

Article 1. Definitions
(a) Excursions and tickets means pre-booked excursions, tours, and event or theatre tickets.
(b) Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in the Insured Person's schedule.
(c) Territory means the countries in which cover applies, as shown in the schedule.
(d) Trip means a journey that starts and ends in the Insured Person's home country during the policy period.

Article 2. Limits and excess
(a) Baggage and Personal Belongings: limit $2,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
(b) Emergency Medical Expenses: limit $10,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
(c) Trip Cancellation: limit $5,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
(d) Travel Delay: limit $300 per incident; excess $25 per claim.
(e) The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

Article 3. Trip Cancellation
(a) The Insurer will pay non-refundable travel and accommodation costs if the Insured Person must cancel the trip for a reason beyond the Insured Person's control.
(b) No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 7 days after the policy start date.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Excursions and tickets under this section is $300 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for cancellation caused by a strike or other event that had been publicly announced before the Insured Person bought the policy.
(e) The Insurer will not pay for cancellation because the Insured Person no longer wish to travel.

Article 4. General exclusions
(a) The Insurer will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits the Insurer from paying.
(b) The Insurer will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
(c) The Insurer will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Insured Person.

Article 5. Complaints
(a) If the Insured Person has a complaint, the Insured Person should first contact the Insurer's customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
(b) The Insurer will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
(c) If the Insured Person remains dissatisfied, the Insured Person may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

Article 6. Making a claim
(a) The Insurer may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
(b) The Insured Person must notify the Insurer of a claim within 14 days of the incident. The Insurer will not pay any claim notified after that time.
(c) The Insured Person must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.

Article 7. Customer support

state: A vastly underrated black comedy, the finest in a series of grand guignol movies to follow 'Baby Jane'. Reynolds and Winters are mothers of young convicted murderers (a nod to 'Compulsion') who run away to hide in Hollywood. They run a school for would-be movie tots, a bunch of hilariously untalented kids attended by awful stage moms. Debbie, in her blonde wig ('I'm a Harlow, you're more a Marion Davies' she tells Winters) leads the tots at their concert and wins a rich dad, Weaver. She also does a deliciously funny tango and, over all, gives an outstanding performance, unlike anything she'd done before. The atmosphere is a fine mix of comic and eerie. It looks wonderful with great period detail (30's). Lots of lovely swipes at Hollywood and the terrifying movie tot. Micheal MacLiammoir has a ball as the drama coach: 'Hamilton Starr', he purrs, 'two r's but prophetic nonetheless'. See it and love it.

SECTION 1 - DEFINITIONS

9.1 You must tell us as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.

state: The birth certificate is the initial identification document issued to parents shortly after the birth of their child. The birth certificate is typically issued by local governments, usually the city or county where a child is born. It is an important record, often called a ``feeder document,'' because it establishes U.S. citizenship through birthright citizenship, which is then used to obtain, or is the basis for, all other identity documents. By itself, the birth certificate is usually only considered proof of citizenship but not proof of identity, since it is issued without a photograph at birth, containing no identifying features. state: Oh, dear lord.... They've turned what was a fairly thought provoking movie into a swaggering testosterone fest. The original 1971 version of this movie was beautifully vague about our hero Kowalski. He was a man trying to drive from Denver to San Fransisco to win a bet. Why was he willing to risk his life for the price of a handful of uppers? We're not really sure. We had a few flashbacks that gave us the picture that he was an adrenaline junkie, and presumably he had led his entire life trying to make it to the vanishing point. That point you see off in the distance where the left and right shoulders of the road come together, and the road itself vanishes. He lives only to be free, and means no ill on anyone. We saw several times when there were accidents he stopped to make sure the other driver was okay before moving on, even the cops that were chasing him. When he saw the futility of his quest he took his life rather than be arrested and live a life of captivity. He died like he lived, running wide open. # Single-Trip Travel Protection Plan
Issued by Bluewater Assurance

## 1. Definitions
- **1.1** Qualifying delay means a delay to the scheduled departure of more than 6 hours.
- **1.2** Travelling companion means a person who has booked to travel with you on the same trip.
- **1.3** Trip means a journey that starts and ends in your home country during the policy period.

## 2. Limits and excess
- **2.1** Baggage and Personal Belongings: limit $3,000 per incident; excess $75 per claim.
- **2.2** Emergency Medical Expenses: limit $50,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
- **2.3** Trip Cancellation: limit $3,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
- **2.4** Travel Delay: limit $750 per incident; excess $25 per claim.
- **2.5** The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

## 3. Optional cover: Travel Delay
- **3.1** We will pay reasonable costs of meals and accommodation if your outbound departure is delayed.
- **3.2** This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
- **3.3** We will not pay for any delay that is not a qualifying delay.

## 4. General exclusions
- **4.1** We will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
- **4.2** We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
- **4.3** We will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by you.

## 5. Making a claim
- **5.1** You must notify us of a claim within 14 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.
- **5.2** You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
- **5.3** We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

## 6. Accessibility
- **6.1** This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

## 7. Other insurance
- **7.1** If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, we will pay only our proportionate share.
- **7.2** You must tell us about any other insurance that covers the same loss when you make a claim.

## 8. Repatriation
- **8.1** If our medical adviser agrees it is necessary, we will arrange and pay for you to be brought home.
- **8.2** We will decide the method of transport and the time of repatriation after speaking to the treating doctor.

## 9. Claims documents
- **9.1** You must provide, at your own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence we reasonably ask for.
- **9.2** We may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

## 10. Assignment
- **10.1** You cannot transfer your interest in this policy to anyone else without our written consent.

## 11. Environmental commitment
- **11.1** Where practical, we will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
- **11.2** You may ask for a new part instead, and we will tell you whether any additional cost would apply.

## 12. Geographical limits
- **12.1** Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
- **12.2** Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

# Employee Health Benefits Plan: Summary Plan Description
Issued by Cedar Benefits Services

## 1. Definitions
- **1.1** Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by us, before any deductible, limit or sublimit is applied.
- **1.2** Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
- **1.3** Frames means spectacle frames bought without new lenses.
- **1.4** Massage therapy means sports massage, massage therapy and reflexology.
- **1.5** Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
- **1.6** Replacement period means 24 months from the date of your last eyewear claim.

## 2. Limits and deductible
- **2.1** Dental Care: limit $2,000 per treatment; deductible $100 per claim.
- **2.2** Vision Care: limit $400 per treatment; deductible $25 per claim.
- **2.3** Therapy Services: limit $2,000 per treatment; deductible $75 per claim.
- **2.4** Hearing Care: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $150 per claim.
- **2.5** The deductible is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

## 3. Vision Care
- **3.1** We will reimburse eye tests and prescription eyewear.
- **3.2** The most we will pay for Frames under this section is $150 per treatment.
- **3.3** We will not pay for eyewear without prescription lenses.
- **3.4** We will not pay for a further eyewear claim within the replacement period.

## 4. Therapy Services
- **4.1** We will reimburse physiotherapy, osteopathy and counselling provided by a registered practitioner.
- **4.2** The most we will pay for Massage therapy under this section is $200 per treatment.
- **4.3** We will not pay for treatment of an injury covered by workers' compensation.
- **4.4** We will not pay for treatment by a practitioner who is not registered with the relevant professional body.

## 5. General exclusions
- **5.1** We will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by you.
- **5.2** We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.

## 6. Making a claim
- **6.1** We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
- **6.2** You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
- **6.3** You must notify us of a claim within 30 days of the treatment. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.

I am sending this on February 17, 2026, which is when I first notified you. Your adjuster assessed the loss at $164.25.

Thanks,
Owen

state: document: The term shrimp is used to refer to some decapod crustaceans, although the exact animals covered can vary. Used broadly, it may cover any of the groups with elongated bodies and a primarily swimming mode of locomotion -- most commonly Caridea and Dendrobranchiata. In some fields, however, the term is used more narrowly and may be restricted to Caridea, to smaller species of either group or to only the marine species. Under the broader definition, shrimp may be synonymous with prawn, covering stalk-eyed swimming crustaceans with long narrow muscular tails (abdomens), long whiskers (antennae), and slender legs. Any small crustacean which resembles a shrimp tends to be called one. They swim forward by paddling with swimmerets on the underside of their abdomens, although their escape response is typically repeated flicks with the tail driving them backwards very quickly. Crabs and lobsters have strong walking legs, whereas shrimp have thin, fragile legs which they use primarily for perching.

As much as I wanted to like this movie, I have to agree with many others who have commented on it. It is very confusing and also extremely slow. Because all of the film appears to have been shot with a hand held camera, significant portions of it are out of focus. The film has very little dialog and what there is doesn't tell you much. There are endless scenes of people just standing around smoking cigarettes or sitting in a room staring at each other with no conversation. The way the film time shifts is also very confusing and hard to follow. policy: STAFF HEALTH REIMBURSEMENT PLAN RULES
Issued by the Staff Welfare Fund
In this policy, "the Plan" means the Staff Welfare Fund and "the Member" means the person named in the schedule.

Article 1. Definitions
(a) Dependant means the Member's spouse or partner, or a child under 21 who is enrolled in the plan.
(b) Frames means spectacle frames bought without new lenses.
(c) Massage therapy means sports massage, massage therapy and reflexology.
(d) Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
(e) Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
(f) Replacement period means 12 months from the date of the Member's last eyewear claim.

Article 2. Limits and deductible
(a) Dental Care: limit $2,000 per treatment; deductible $100 per claim.
(b) Vision Care: limit $400 per treatment; deductible $40 per claim.
(c) Therapy Services: limit $1,500 per treatment; deductible $50 per claim.

Article 4. Vision Care

(a) The Plan will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits the Plan from paying.

policy: HOME CONTENTS INSURANCE POLICY
Issued by Hearthstone Insurance plc

PART I: Definitions
I.1  Art and antiques means paintings, antiques, rugs and other works of art.
I.2  Bicycles means bicycles and electric scooters.
I.3  Forcible entry means entry to the home that leaves visible damage to doors, windows or locks.
I.4  High-risk items means jewellery, watches, laptops, games consoles and cameras.
I.5  Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
I.6  Portable electronics means laptops, tablets and mobile phones.
I.7  Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.
I.8  Unoccupied means not lived in by the Policyholder or a member of the Policyholder's family for more than 30 consecutive days.

PART II: Limits and excess
II.1  Theft: limit $40,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
II.2  Escape of Water: limit $30,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
II.3  Accidental Damage: limit $5,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
II.4  Flood: limit $20,000 per incident; excess $1,000 per claim.
II.5  The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

PART III: Optional cover: Accidental Damage
III.1  The Insurer will pay for sudden and unexpected accidental damage to the Policyholder's contents inside the home.
III.2  This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Policyholder's schedule.
III.3  The most the Insurer will pay for Portable electronics under this section is $500 per incident.
III.4  The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by pets.
III.5  The Insurer will not pay for wear and tear, or damage that happens gradually.

PART IV: Escape of Water
IV.1  The Insurer will pay for contents damaged by water escaping from a fixed pipe, tank or domestic appliance.
IV.2  The most the Insurer will pay for Art and antiques under this section is $1,000 per incident.
IV.3  The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by water leaking gradually over a period of time.
IV.4  The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by the failure of grout or sealant around baths and showers.

PART V: Theft
V.1  The Insurer will pay for contents stolen from the Policyholder's home.
V.2  The most the Insurer will pay for High-risk items under this section is $1,000 per incident.
V.3  The most the Insurer will pay for Bicycles under this section is $500 per incident.
V.4  The Insurer will not pay for theft while the home is unoccupied.
V.5  The Insurer will not pay for theft where there is no sign of forced entry to the home. This exclusion does not apply where the thief gained entry by deception, for example by posing as a utility worker.
V.6  The Insurer will not pay for theft from sheds, garages or other outbuildings. This exclusion does not apply if the outbuilding was locked and the theft involved forcible entry.

PART VI: General exclusions
VI.1  The Insurer will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Policyholder.
VI.2  The Insurer will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.

PART VII: Making a claim
VII.1  The Insurer may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
VII.2  The Policyholder must notify the Insurer of a claim within 90 days of the incident. The Insurer will not pay any claim notified after that time.
VII.3  The Policyholder must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.

PART I: Definitions
I.1  Art and antiques means paintings, antiques, rugs and other works of art.

I.3  Garden items means garden furniture, plants and outdoor tools.

PART II: Limits and excess
II.1  Theft: limit $10,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
II.2  Escape of Water: limit $15,000 per incident; excess $250 per claim.
II.3  Accidental Damage: limit $5,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
II.4  Flood: limit $20,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
II.5  Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the excess is then deducted from the result.

PART III: Escape of Water
III.1  The Insurer will pay for contents damaged by water escaping from a fixed pipe, tank or domestic appliance.
III.2  The most the Insurer will pay for Art and antiques under this section is $1,000 per incident.
III.3  The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by water leaking gradually over a period of time.
III.4  The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by the failure of grout or sealant around baths and showers.

PART IV: Flood
IV.1  The Insurer will pay for contents damaged by flood water entering the Policyholder's home.
IV.2  No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 60 days after the policy start date.
IV.3  The most the Insurer will pay for Garden items under this section is $1,000 per incident.
IV.4  The Insurer will not pay for flood damage where a flood warning for the Policyholder's area had been issued before the policy started.

PART V: Optional cover: Accidental Damage
V.1  The Insurer will pay for sudden and unexpected accidental damage to the Policyholder's contents inside the home.
V.2  This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Policyholder's schedule.
V.3  The most the Insurer will pay for Portable electronics under this section is $500 per incident.
V.4  The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by pets.
V.5  The Insurer will not pay for wear and tear, or damage that happens gradually.

PART VI: General exclusions
VI.1  The Insurer will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Policyholder.
VI.2  The Insurer will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.

PART VII: Making a claim
VII.1  The Policyholder must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
VII.2  The Policyholder must notify the Insurer of a claim within 60 days of the incident. The Insurer will not pay any claim notified after that time.
VII.3  The Insurer may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

Originally my sister and I were going to go to the Wynn for the breakfast buffet but we found out it was the Saturday brunch and not a regular buffet, so I remembered about Terrace Pointe and we headed there. Actually a lot of people ended up venturing over to Terrace Pointe because of the non-buffet. 

From the time we walked into the restaurant to the time we sat at our table was about 10 min. which was great. The ambiance is nice, quaint and very "Wynn". The menu was short and sweet - pancakes, waffles, fruit, pastries, etc. I ordered the strawberry belgian waffle, my sister got pancakes. My waffle was great! So delicious - crispy, flavorful, the strawberries were fresh and the whipped cream was yummy. My sister's pancakes were huge, she couldn't even finish them. 

The only minus is it took a good while for our food to come. Luckily we weren't starving, because if we were I would have been a lil ticked off at having to wait so long. Overall I really liked my food, it was a great alternative to the breakfast buffet. I will definetly go back on my next trip to Las Vegas.

PART I: Definitions
I.1  Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in the Insured Person's schedule.
I.2  Public transport means any scheduled train, bus, coach, ferry or aircraft.
I.3  Qualifying delay means a delay to the scheduled departure of more than 6 hours.

PART II: Limits and excess
II.1  Baggage and Personal Belongings: limit $1,500 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
II.2  Emergency Medical Expenses: limit $10,000 per incident; excess $150 per claim.
II.3  Trip Cancellation: limit $5,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
II.4  Travel Delay: limit $750 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
II.5  Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the excess is then deducted from the result.

PART III: Optional cover: Travel Delay
III.1  The Insurer will pay reasonable costs of meals and accommodation if the Insured Person's outbound departure is delayed.
III.2  This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Insured Person's schedule.
III.3  The Insurer will not pay for any delay that is not a qualifying delay.

PART IV: General exclusions
IV.1  The Insurer will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
IV.2  The Insurer will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.

PART V: Currency
V.1  All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
V.2  Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

PART VI: Exchange of information
VI.1  To prevent fraud, the Insurer may check the details the Insured Person gives against public records and industry databases.
VI.2  The Insurer may contact previous insurers to confirm the Insured Person's claims history.

PART VII: Making a claim
VII.1  The Insurer may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
VII.2  The Insured Person must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
VII.3  The Insured Person must notify the Insurer of a claim within 90 days of the incident. The Insurer will not pay any claim notified after that time.

PART VIII: Instalment agreements
VIII.1  If the Insured Person pays by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
VIII.2  Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

# Single-Trip Travel Protection Plan
Issued by Bluewater Assurance

## 1. Definitions
- **1.1** Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
- **1.2** Excursions and tickets means pre-booked excursions, tours, and event or theatre tickets.
- **1.3** Limit means the most we will pay for all claims under a section arising from one incident.
- **1.4** Qualifying delay means a delay to the scheduled departure of more than 8 hours.

## 2. Limits and excess
- **2.1** Baggage and Personal Belongings: limit $2,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
- **2.2** Emergency Medical Expenses: limit $50,000 per incident; excess $150 per claim.
- **2.3** Trip Cancellation: limit $3,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
- **2.4** Travel Delay: limit $300 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
- **2.5** Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the excess is then deducted from the result.

## 3. Trip Cancellation
- **3.1** We will pay non-refundable travel and accommodation costs if you must cancel the trip for a reason beyond your control.
- **3.2** No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 10 days after the policy start date.
- **3.3** The most we will pay for Excursions and tickets under this section is $200 per incident.
- **3.4** We will not pay for cancellation caused by a strike or other event that had been publicly announced before you bought the policy.
- **3.5** We will not pay for cancellation because you no longer wish to travel.

## 4. Optional cover: Travel Delay
- **4.1** We will pay reasonable costs of meals and accommodation if your outbound departure is delayed.
- **4.2** This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
- **4.3** We will not pay for any delay that is not a qualifying delay.

## 5. General exclusions
- **5.1** We will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
- **5.2** We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
- **5.3** We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.

## 6. Making a claim
- **6.1** You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
- **6.2** We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
- **6.3** You must notify us of a claim within 90 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.

Colm paid for the trip with a credit card. Colm was travelling with two colleagues.

I am sending this on June 23, 2027, which is when I first notified you. Your adjuster assessed the loss at $402.25.

Thanks,
Colm

What I hate the most is waiting in line to pay the cashier to get into the buffet. When you go to a buffet, you're already starving. Delegate one person to pay for everything for god's sake! Decide how much each person is going to pay later! Ugh. Anywho, the people who run this buffet got smart and set up self-paying kiosks in place of cashiers. Tap the touch-screen a few times, insert money or a credit card, take your receipt and show it to the hostess who will lead you to your table. Genius! state: document: The '60s is an occasionally entertaining film, most of this entertainment is from laughing at the film. It is extremely uneven, and includes many annoying elements. Take for instance the switch between black & white, and color. If done right, this could of been fairly effective, but because it was done poorly , it turned into a nuisance and only detracted from the already bad experience; much of the film had an odd feel to it. The acting wasn't extremely bad for a made for TV flick, but then again it was downright embarrassing at other times. Many of the events were not coherent, and ending up being confusing. How did this family somehow end up being at many of the big events during the 1960's? The ending was much too sappy for my tastes; because it was hollywoodized, everything had to turn out right in the end. I would advise you to not waste your time on The '60s and do something else with your time. I'm glad I watched this in class, and not on my own time. # Electronics Care Plan
Issued by Brightline Device Cover

## 1. Definitions
- **1.1** Accessories means cases, chargers and earbuds.
- **1.2** Battery replacement means replacement batteries and battery repairs.
- **1.3** Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
- **1.4** Manufacturer's warranty period means the first 12 months after the device was bought.

## 2. Limits and service fee
- **2.1** Accidental Damage: limit $1,500 per incident; service fee $99 per claim.
- **2.2** Breakdown: limit $1,500 per incident; service fee $25 per claim.
- **2.3** Theft and Loss: limit $800 per incident; service fee $99 per claim.
- **2.4** Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the service fee is then deducted from the result.

## 3. Breakdown
- **3.1** We will repair or replace your device if it stops working because of an electrical or mechanical fault.
- **3.2** No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 45 days after the policy start date.
- **3.3** The most we will pay for Battery replacement under this section is $120 per incident.
- **3.4** We will not pay for breakdowns during the manufacturer's warranty period.
- **3.5** We will not pay for breakdown caused by liquid getting into the device.

## 4. Optional cover: Theft and Loss
- **4.1** We will replace your device if it is stolen or lost.
- **4.2** This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
- **4.3** The most we will pay for Accessories under this section is $100 per incident.
- **4.4** We will not pay for loss or theft of property left unattended in a vehicle or in a public place. This exclusion does not apply to property locked out of sight in the boot or trunk of a locked vehicle.
- **4.5** We will not pay for theft that was not reported to the police.

## 5. General exclusions
- **5.1** We will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits us from paying.
- **5.2** We will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.

## 6. Making a claim
- **6.1** You must notify us of a claim within 30 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.
- **6.2** You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
- **6.3** We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

state: Robert Siodmak does a fabulous job with this B noir starring Ella Raines, Franchot Tone, and Alan Curtis. And he does it, I might add, without a lot of help from his male actors, i.e., Curtis and Tone. It's Raines all the way, a pretty, leggy actress who for one reason or another never reached the status of some of her "noir" counterparts. Siodmak's use of sex, light, shadows, and music is truly remarkable as he tackles this genre. The shadows, lighting effects, and camera angles are all effective. But the highlight of the film takes place in a nightclub with a very sexual drum riff by Elisha Cook, egged on by an excited Raines. It's this scene that brings "Phantom Lady" into new territory. Siodmak's commitment to the material is matched only by Raines, who gives a sincere performance as a woman in love trying to save her man. Franchot Tone phoned this one in. Alan Curtis didn't seem upset that he might die and didn't seem happy that he lived. And he never, except for a brief moment in prison, seemed to be in love with Raines. policy: SINGLE-TRIP TRAVEL PROTECTION PLAN
Issued by Bluewater Assurance

PART I: Definitions
I.1  Dental treatment means treatment of the teeth or gums.
I.2  Excursions and tickets means pre-booked excursions, tours, and event or theatre tickets.
I.3  Hazardous activity means skydiving, motor racing, or trekking or climbing above 4,500 metres.
I.4  Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
I.5  Physiotherapy means treatment of muscles and joints by a physiotherapist.
I.6  Pre-existing condition means any illness or injury for which the Insured Person received treatment or advice in the 3 months before the policy start date.
I.7  Qualifying delay means a delay to the scheduled departure of more than 8 hours.

PART II: Limits and excess
II.1  Baggage and Personal Belongings: limit $2,000 per incident; excess $75 per claim.
II.2  Emergency Medical Expenses: limit $50,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
II.3  Trip Cancellation: limit $5,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
II.4  Travel Delay: limit $300 per incident; excess $25 per claim.
II.5  The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

PART III: Emergency Medical Expenses
III.1  The Insurer will pay reasonable and necessary emergency medical costs incurred during the trip.
III.2  The most the Insurer will pay for Dental treatment under this section is $400 per incident.
III.3  The most the Insurer will pay for Physiotherapy under this section is $500 per incident.
III.4  The Insurer will not pay for treatment of a pre-existing condition.
III.5  The Insurer will not pay for injury or illness arising from a hazardous activity. This exclusion does not apply if the Adventure Sports extension is shown in the Insured Person's schedule.
III.6  The Insurer will not pay for any claim arising from the Insured Person's being under the influence of alcohol or drugs.

PART IV: Optional cover: Travel Delay
IV.1  The Insurer will pay reasonable costs of meals and accommodation if the Insured Person's outbound departure is delayed.
IV.2  This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Insured Person's schedule.
IV.3  The Insurer will not pay for any delay that is not a qualifying delay.

PART V: Trip Cancellation
V.1  The Insurer will pay non-refundable travel and accommodation costs if the Insured Person must cancel the trip for a reason beyond the Insured Person's control.
V.2  No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 14 days after the policy start date.
V.3  The most the Insurer will pay for Excursions and tickets under this section is $300 per incident.
V.4  The Insurer will not pay for cancellation caused by a strike or other event that had been publicly announced before the Insured Person bought the policy.
V.5  The Insurer will not pay for cancellation because the Insured Person no longer wish to travel.

PART VI: General exclusions
VI.1  The Insurer will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
VI.2  The Insurer will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits the Insurer from paying.

PART VII: Making a claim
VII.1  The Insured Person must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
VII.2  The Insurer may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
VII.3  The Insured Person must notify the Insurer of a claim within 30 days of the incident. The Insurer will not pay any claim notified after that time.

# Home Contents Insurance Policy
Issued by Lantern General Insurance

## 1. Definitions
- **1.1** Bicycles means bicycles and electric scooters.
- **1.2** Garden items means garden furniture, plants and outdoor tools.
- **1.3** High-risk items means jewellery, watches, laptops, games consoles and cameras.
- **1.4** Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows your details, the covers you bought and any extensions.
- **1.5** Unoccupied means not lived in by you or a member of your family for more than 45 consecutive days.

## 2. Limits and excess
- **2.1** Theft: limit $40,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
- **2.2** Escape of Water: limit $15,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
- **2.3** Accidental Damage: limit $5,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
- **2.4** Flood: limit $20,000 per incident; excess $1,000 per claim.
- **2.5** Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the excess is then deducted from the result.

## 3. Flood
- **3.1** We will pay for contents damaged by flood water entering your home.
- **3.2** No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 30 days after the policy start date.
- **3.3** The most we will pay for Garden items under this section is $1,000 per incident.
- **3.4** We will not pay for flood damage where a flood warning for your area had been issued before the policy started.

## 4. Theft
- **4.1** We will pay for contents stolen from your home.
- **4.2** The most we will pay for High-risk items under this section is $1,000 per incident.
- **4.3** The most we will pay for Bicycles under this section is $500 per incident.
- **4.4** We will not pay for theft while the home is unoccupied.
- **4.5** We will not pay for theft where there is no sign of forced entry to the home. This exclusion does not apply where the thief gained entry by deception, for example by posing as a utility worker.
- **4.6** We will not pay for theft from sheds, garages or other outbuildings. This exclusion does not apply if the outbuilding was locked and the theft involved forcible entry.

## 5. General exclusions
- **5.1** We will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
- **5.2** We will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits us from paying.
- **5.3** We will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.

## 6. Making a claim
- **6.1** We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
- **6.2** You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
- **6.3** You must notify us of a claim within 30 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.

## 7. Governing law
- **7.1** This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
- **7.2** Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

## 8. Locks and keys
- **8.1** If the keys to your home are lost or stolen, we will pay the cost of replacing the locks to the outside doors.
- **8.2** The most we will pay under this clause is $750 for any one claim.

Kenji

# Travel Insurance Policy Wording
Issued by Meridian Travel Insurance Ltd

## 1. Definitions
- **1.1** Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
- **1.2** Dental treatment means treatment of the teeth or gums.
- **1.3** Hazardous activity means skydiving, motor racing, or trekking or climbing above 4,000 metres.
- **1.4** Physiotherapy means treatment of muscles and joints by a physiotherapist.
- **1.5** Pre-existing condition means any illness or injury for which you received treatment or advice in the 12 months before the policy start date.
- **1.6** Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
- **1.7** Qualifying delay means a delay to the scheduled departure of more than 12 hours.
- **1.8** Travelling companion means a person who has booked to travel with you on the same trip.

## 2. Limits and excess
- **2.1** Baggage and Personal Belongings: limit $1,500 per incident; excess $75 per claim.
- **2.2** Emergency Medical Expenses: limit $25,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
- **2.3** Trip Cancellation: limit $3,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
- **2.4** Travel Delay: limit $300 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
- **2.5** The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

## 3. Emergency Medical Expenses
- **3.1** We will pay reasonable and necessary emergency medical costs incurred during the trip.
- **3.2** The most we will pay for Dental treatment under this section is $400 per incident.
- **3.3** The most we will pay for Physiotherapy under this section is $500 per incident.
- **3.4** We will not pay for treatment of a pre-existing condition.
- **3.5** We will not pay for injury or illness arising from a hazardous activity. This exclusion does not apply if the Adventure Sports extension is shown in your schedule.
- **3.6** We will not pay for any claim arising from your being under the influence of alcohol or drugs.

## 4. Optional cover: Travel Delay
- **4.1** We will pay reasonable costs of meals and accommodation if your outbound departure is delayed.
- **4.2** This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
- **4.3** We will not pay for any delay that is not a qualifying delay.

## 5. General exclusions
- **5.1** We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
- **5.2** We will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
- **5.3** We will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by you.

## 6. Making a claim
- **6.1** We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
- **6.2** You must notify us of a claim within 30 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.
- **6.3** You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.

policy: GROUP HEALTH CASH PLAN
Issued by Cedar Benefits Services

PART I: Definitions
I.1  Frames means spectacle frames bought without new lenses.
I.2  Hearing accessories means batteries, chargers and cleaning kits.
I.3  Hearing aid replacement period means 36 months from the purchase of hearing aids funded by the plan.
I.4  Massage therapy means sports massage, massage therapy and reflexology.
I.5  Plan year means the twelve months starting on the Member's coverage start date.
I.6  Replacement period means 12 months from the date of the Member's last eyewear claim.

PART II: Limits and deductible
II.1  Dental Care: limit $2,000 per treatment; deductible $50 per claim.
II.2  Vision Care: limit $300 per treatment; deductible $40 per claim.
II.3  Therapy Services: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $75 per claim.
II.4  Hearing Care: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $150 per claim.
II.5  The deductible is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

PART III: Therapy Services
III.1  The Plan will reimburse physiotherapy, osteopathy and counselling provided by a registered practitioner.
III.2  The most the Plan will pay for Massage therapy under this section is $300 per treatment.
III.3  The Plan will not pay for treatment of an injury covered by workers' compensation.
III.4  The Plan will not pay for treatment by a practitioner who is not registered with the relevant professional body.

PART IV: Vision Care
IV.1  The Plan will reimburse eye tests and prescription eyewear.
IV.2  The most the Plan will pay for Frames under this section is $120 per treatment.
IV.3  The Plan will not pay for eyewear without prescription lenses.
IV.4  The Plan will not pay for a further eyewear claim within the replacement period.

PART V: Optional cover: Hearing Care
V.1  The Plan will reimburse hearing tests and hearing aids.
V.2  This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Member's schedule.
V.3  The most the Plan will pay for Hearing accessories under this section is $100 per treatment.
V.4  The Plan will not pay for replacement hearing aids bought within the hearing aid replacement period.

PART VI: General exclusions
VI.1  The Plan will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
VI.2  The Plan will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Member.

PART VII: Making a claim
VII.1  The Member must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
VII.2  The Plan may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
VII.3  The Member must notify the Plan of a claim within 14 days of the treatment. The Plan will not pay any claim notified after that time.

PART VIII: Compensation scheme
VIII.1  The Plan is covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
VIII.2  If the Plan cannot meet the Plan's obligations, the Member may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

PART IX: Contracts (Rights of Third Parties)
IX.1  A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

PART X: Complaints
X.1  If the Member has a complaint, the Member should first contact the Plan's customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
X.2  The Plan will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
X.3  If the Member remains dissatisfied, the Member may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

PART XI: Governing law
XI.1  This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
XI.2  Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.
