policy: GROUP HEALTH CASH PLAN
Issued by Cedar Benefits Services
In this policy, "the Plan" means Cedar Benefits Services and "the Member" means the person named in the schedule.

Article 1. Definitions
(a) Massage therapy means sports massage, massage therapy and reflexology.
(b) Plan year means the twelve months starting on the Member's coverage start date.
(c) Registered practitioner means a practitioner registered with the professional body for their discipline.

Article 2. Limits and deductible
(a) Dental Care: limit $2,000 per treatment; deductible $100 per claim.
(b) Vision Care: limit $400 per treatment; deductible $40 per claim.
(c) Therapy Services: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $50 per claim.
(d) Hearing Care: limit $2,000 per treatment; deductible $150 per claim.
(e) The deductible is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

Article 3. Therapy Services
(a) The Plan will reimburse physiotherapy, osteopathy and counselling provided by a registered practitioner.
(b) The most the Plan will pay for Massage therapy under this section is $200 per treatment.
(c) The Plan will not pay for treatment of an injury covered by workers' compensation.
(d) The Plan will not pay for treatment by a practitioner who is not registered with the relevant professional body.

Article 4. General exclusions
(a) The Plan will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
(b) The Plan will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
(c) The Plan will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.

Article 5. Making a claim
(a) The Member must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
(b) The Member must notify the Plan of a claim within 60 days of the treatment. The Plan will not pay any claim notified after that time.
(c) The Plan may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

Article 6. Sanctions
(a) The Plan will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose the Plan to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

Article 7. Arbitration
(a) If the Plan accepts a claim but disagree with the Member about the amount, the difference will be referred to an arbitrator appointed by both parties.
(b) Where arbitration applies, obtaining an award is a condition precedent to any legal action against the Plan.

Article 8. Exchange of information
(a) To prevent fraud, the Plan may check the details the Member gives against public records and industry databases.
(b) The Plan may contact previous insurers to confirm the Member's claims history.

Article 9. Leaving the plan
(a) Cover ends on the day the Member's employment ends or the day the Member stops being eligible, whichever is earlier.
(b) Claims for treatment received before cover ended may be submitted up to 90 days afterwards.

Article 10. Changes in circumstances
(a) The Member must tell the Plan as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
(b) The Plan may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

Article 11. Duty of fair presentation
(a) The Member must answer all questions the Plan asks honestly and to the best of the Member's knowledge.
(b) If the Member gives incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, the Plan may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
(c) If the Member gives incorrect information carelessly, the Plan may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

state: Jafar Panahi's comedy-drama "Offside" portrays some women trying to enter a Tehran sports arena from which women are banned. The official reason: lots of foul language, and the soccer players have their legs showing. But of course, it's really a case of sexism. So, most of the movie consists of mild comic relief as the women try to ask the men serious questions about why women are banned from the stadium, and one woman even comes up with her own scheme to defy the men. As I understand, all of Jafar Panahi's movies (this one included) are banned in Iran. The real tragedy is that the CIA's 1953 overthrow of the prime minister and subsequent backing of the brutal shah gave Ayatollah Khomeini an excuse to use his narrow interpretation of the Koran to establish a chauvinistic society, and that George W. Bush's current policy towards Iran gives Mahmoud Ahmadinejad an excuse to act the cowboy and tighten censorship. Above all, this is a neat look at people coming up with ways to challenge the system. Not a great movie, but worth seeing. Considering that all Jafar Panahi's movies are banned, I wonder how he's able to even make them.

Issued by Hearthstone Insurance plc

SECTION 1 - DEFINITIONS
1.1 Art and antiques means paintings, antiques, rugs and other works of art.
1.2 Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by us, before any excess, limit or sublimit is applied.
1.3 Bicycles means bicycles and electric scooters.

1.7 Unoccupied means not lived in by you or a member of your family for more than 30 consecutive days.

SECTION 2 - LIMITS AND EXCESS
2.1 Theft: limit $20,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
2.2 Escape of Water: limit $15,000 per incident; excess $1,000 per claim.
2.3 Accidental Damage: limit $3,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
2.4 Flood: limit $20,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
2.5 The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

SECTION 3 - THEFT
3.1 We will pay for contents stolen from your home.
3.2 The most we will pay for High-risk items under this section is $2,500 per incident.
3.3 The most we will pay for Bicycles under this section is $500 per incident.
3.4 We will not pay for theft while the home is unoccupied.
3.5 We will not pay for theft where there is no sign of forced entry to the home. This exclusion does not apply where the thief gained entry by deception, for example by posing as a utility worker.
3.6 We will not pay for theft from sheds, garages or other outbuildings. This exclusion does not apply if the outbuilding was locked and the theft involved forcible entry.

SECTION 4 - ESCAPE OF WATER
4.1 We will pay for contents damaged by water escaping from a fixed pipe, tank or domestic appliance.
4.2 The most we will pay for Art and antiques under this section is $1,000 per incident.
4.3 We will not pay for damage caused by water leaking gradually over a period of time.
4.4 We will not pay for damage caused by the failure of grout or sealant around baths and showers.

SECTION 5 - FLOOD
5.1 We will pay for contents damaged by flood water entering your home.
5.2 No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 60 days after the policy start date.
5.3 The most we will pay for Garden items under this section is $500 per incident.
5.4 We will not pay for flood damage where a flood warning for your area had been issued before the policy started.

SECTION 6 - GENERAL EXCLUSIONS
6.1 We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
6.2 We will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by you.

SECTION 7 - MAKING A CLAIM
7.1 We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
7.2 You must notify us of a claim within 90 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.
7.3 You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.

8.1 If the replacement item is no longer available, we will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

state: The music and Laurence Olivier's sombre delivery set the tone perfectly for this outstanding documentary. This is still a must see for WW II buffs, descendants of the participants of that conflict, politicians who think things always go their way when they extend their foreign policy via the deck of an aircraft carrier (did you hear that George Bush?) and anyone else curious or needing to know the whys whos and hows of some aspect of that conflict. The 26 episodes are roughly in chronological order but can be seen out of sequence since they are more or less self contained. There is bound to be new insight for the new viewer because of the sheer volume presented. Actual footage of the battles is interspersed with interviews of those involved in the stories. Many of the interviews are with second line authorities, that is, support personnel to the main characters, privates, captains, secretaries, eyewitnesses and the like. You get a real upfront taste of what war is all about. I am presently watching the DVD version of the original television documentary. I strongly recommend this over the worn out, gaptoothed, overpriced VHS offerings available on eBay. I paid $120 Cdn for five 2-sided DVD discs. Significant lava flows in addition to the previously much more common fragmented and pulverized lavas and rocks (tephra) distinguished this period. Large lava flows of andesite and basalt covered parts of the mountain, including one around the year 100 BCE that traveled all the way into the Lewis and Kalama river valleys. Others, such as Cave Basalt (known for its system of lava tubes), flowed up to 9 miles (14 km) from their vents. Tsunamis affect New Zealand's coastline reasonably frequently and tend to be caused by earthquakes on the Pacific Plate both locally and as far away as South America, Japan, and Alaska. Some have been attributed to undersea landslides, volcanoes, and at least one meteor strike. New Zealand is affected by at least one tsunami with the a wave height greater than one metre every ten years on average. The history of tsunamis is limited by the country's written history only dating from the early to mid-1800s with Māori oral traditions and paleotsunami research prior to that time. This movie is based on an award winning novel and chronicles a family starting with the son's arranged marriage to a slave girl. The movie does a good job of keeping your interest despite a somewhat hammy performance by the lead played by Paul Muni. It chronicles , Wong Long(the character played by Muni) and how he works the land, buys more land, eventually becomes very rich but then returns to the land where he originally started. The relationship between him and his wife, played by Luise Rainer, is the main thread of the story(besides the land itself) and despite the obvious non-Chinese actors it does a pretty good job of displaying the country and it's people. It's obvious that MGM used it's money to create a really good epic with this one in an era where they could probably afford it. The scene with the locusts is done exceedingly well and the rest of th movie really looks good warranting the Best Cinematography award at the Oscars in that year. The definitive definition of an epic is what this story is and it's pulled off pretty well.

policy: EMPLOYEE HEALTH BENEFITS PLAN: SUMMARY PLAN DESCRIPTION
Issued by Cedar Benefits Services
In this policy, "the Plan" means Cedar Benefits Services and "the Member" means the person named in the schedule.

Article 1. Definitions
(a) Hearing accessories means batteries, chargers and cleaning kits.
(b) Hearing aid replacement period means 24 months from the purchase of hearing aids funded by the plan.
(c) Limit means the most the Plan will pay for all claims under a section arising from one treatment.
(d) Massage therapy means sports massage, massage therapy and reflexology.
(e) Network provider means a practitioner or clinic that has an agreement with the Plan to provide treatment.
(f) Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows the Member's details, the covers the Member bought and any extensions.

Article 2. Limits and deductible
(a) Dental Care: limit $2,000 per treatment; deductible $50 per claim.
(b) Vision Care: limit $300 per treatment; deductible $25 per claim.
(c) Therapy Services: limit $2,000 per treatment; deductible $75 per claim.
(d) Hearing Care: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $150 per claim.
(e) Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the deductible is then deducted from the result.

Article 3. How to read this document
(a) This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.
(b) Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
(c) Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

Article 4. Therapy Services
(a) The Plan will reimburse physiotherapy, osteopathy and counselling provided by a registered practitioner.
(b) The most the Plan will pay for Massage therapy under this section is $200 per treatment.
(c) The Plan will not pay for treatment of an injury covered by workers' compensation.

(c) The most the Plan will pay for Hearing accessories under this section is $100 per treatment.

(a) If the Plan pays a claim that is later found not to be covered, the Plan may ask the Member to repay the amount.

Article 7. General exclusions
(a) The Plan will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
(b) The Plan will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits the Plan from paying.

Article 8. Interpretation
(a) Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
(b) Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
(c) Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

Article 9. Making a claim
(a) The Member must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.

In this policy, "the Plan" means Cedar Benefits Services and "the Member" means the person named in the schedule.

Article 1. Definitions
(a) Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
(b) Dependant means the Member's spouse or partner, or a child under 21 who is enrolled in the plan.
(c) Massage therapy means sports massage, massage therapy and reflexology.

(b) Vision Care: limit $400 per treatment; deductible $25 per claim.

(b) The most the Plan will pay for Massage therapy under this section is $300 per treatment.
(c) The Plan will not pay for treatment of an injury covered by workers' compensation.
(d) The Plan will not pay for treatment by a practitioner who is not registered with the relevant professional body.

Article 4. Geographical limits
(a) Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
(b) Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

Article 5. Assignment
(a) The Member cannot transfer the Member's interest in this policy to anyone else without the Plan's written consent.

Article 6. Wellness allowance
(a) Each plan year the Member may claim up to $250 towards a gym membership or fitness class.
(b) The wellness allowance is not subject to any deductible and does not count towards other limits.

(b) An appeal will be reviewed by someone who was not involved in the original decision.

Article 9. Premium payment
(a) The Member must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.

Article 10. Leaving the plan
(a) Cover ends on the day the Member's employment ends or the day the Member stops being eligible, whichever is earlier.
(b) Claims for treatment received before cover ended may be submitted up to 90 days afterwards.

Article 11. General exclusions
(a) The Plan will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits the Plan from paying.
(b) The Plan will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.

Article 12. Making a claim
(a) The Member must notify the Plan of a claim within 14 days of the treatment. The Plan will not pay any claim notified after that time.
(b) The Member must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
(c) The Plan may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

Article 13. Environmental commitment
(a) Where practical, the Plan will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
(b) The Member may ask for a new part instead, and the Plan will tell the Member whether any additional cost would apply.

Article 14. Change of address
(a) The Member must tell the Plan within 30 days if the Member changes the Member's address.
(b) The Plan may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

Article 15. Recovery of costs
(a) If the Plan pays a claim that is later found not to be covered, the Plan may ask the Member to repay the amount.

policy: EMPLOYEE HEALTH BENEFITS PLAN: SUMMARY PLAN DESCRIPTION
Issued by Cedar Benefits Services

PART I: Definitions
I.1  Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by the Plan, before any deductible, limit or sublimit is applied.
I.2  Frames means spectacle frames bought without new lenses.
I.3  Major restorative work means crowns, bridges, root canal treatment and implants.
I.4  Massage therapy means sports massage, massage therapy and reflexology.
I.5  Orthodontics means braces and clear aligners.
I.6  Replacement period means 12 months from the date of the Member's last eyewear claim.

PART II: Limits and deductible
II.1  Dental Care: limit $2,000 per treatment; deductible $100 per claim.
II.2  Vision Care: limit $500 per treatment; deductible $25 per claim.
II.3  Therapy Services: limit $1,500 per treatment; deductible $75 per claim.
II.4  Hearing Care: limit $2,000 per treatment; deductible $150 per claim.
II.5  The deductible is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

PART III: Therapy Services
III.1  The Plan will reimburse physiotherapy, osteopathy and counselling provided by a registered practitioner.
III.2  The most the Plan will pay for Massage therapy under this section is $300 per treatment.
III.3  The Plan will not pay for treatment of an injury covered by workers' compensation.
III.4  The Plan will not pay for treatment by a practitioner who is not registered with the relevant professional body.

PART IV: Vision Care
IV.1  The Plan will reimburse eye tests and prescription eyewear.
IV.2  The most the Plan will pay for Frames under this section is $120 per treatment.
IV.3  The Plan will not pay for eyewear without prescription lenses.
IV.4  The Plan will not pay for a further eyewear claim within the replacement period.

PART V: Dental Care
V.1  The Plan will reimburse the cost of dental treatment provided by a licensed dentist.
V.2  No cover applies under this section to any treatment that happens within the first 60 days after the policy start date.
V.3  The most the Plan will pay for Major restorative work under this section is $500 per treatment.
V.4  The most the Plan will pay for Orthodontics under this section is $600 per treatment.
V.5  The Plan will not pay for treatment that is mainly cosmetic, such as whitening or veneers. This exclusion does not apply to treatment needed to repair damage caused by an accident.
V.6  The Plan will not pay for treatment by a provider outside the plan's network. This exclusion does not apply to emergency treatment for sudden severe pain.

PART VI: General exclusions
VI.1  The Plan will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
VI.2  The Plan will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.

PART VII: Making a claim
VII.1  The Plan may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
VII.2  The Member must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
VII.3  The Member must notify the Plan of a claim within 90 days of the treatment. The Plan will not pay any claim notified after that time.

policy: TRAVEL INSURANCE POLICY WORDING
Issued by Bluewater Assurance
In this policy, "the Insurer" means Bluewater Assurance and "the Insured Person" means the person named in the schedule.

Article 1. Definitions
(a) Dental treatment means treatment of the teeth or gums.
(b) Hazardous activity means skydiving, motor racing, or trekking or climbing above 4,500 metres.
(c) Physiotherapy means treatment of muscles and joints by a physiotherapist.
(d) Pre-existing condition means any illness or injury for which the Insured Person received treatment or advice in the 12 months before the policy start date.
(e) Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
(f) Qualifying delay means a delay to the scheduled departure of more than 12 hours.
(g) Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.

Article 2. Limits and excess
(a) Baggage and Personal Belongings: limit $2,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
(b) Emergency Medical Expenses: limit $10,000 per incident; excess $250 per claim.
(c) Trip Cancellation: limit $3,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
(d) Travel Delay: limit $500 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
(e) Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the excess is then deducted from the result.

Article 3. Optional cover: Travel Delay
(a) The Insurer will pay reasonable costs of meals and accommodation if the Insured Person's outbound departure is delayed.
(b) This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Insured Person's schedule.
(c) The Insurer will not pay for any delay that is not a qualifying delay.

Article 4. Emergency Medical Expenses
(a) The Insurer will pay reasonable and necessary emergency medical costs incurred during the trip.
(b) The most the Insurer will pay for Dental treatment under this section is $250 per incident.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Physiotherapy under this section is $300 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for treatment of a pre-existing condition.
(e) The Insurer will not pay for injury or illness arising from a hazardous activity. This exclusion does not apply if the Adventure Sports extension is shown in the Insured Person's schedule.
(f) The Insurer will not pay for any claim arising from the Insured Person's being under the influence of alcohol or drugs.

Article 5. General exclusions
(a) The Insurer will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
(b) The Insurer will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.

Article 6. Making a claim
(a) The Insured Person must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
(b) The Insurer may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
(c) The Insured Person must notify the Insurer of a claim within 60 days of the incident. The Insurer will not pay any claim notified after that time.

Article 7. Salvage
(a) When the Insurer replaces an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes the Insurer's property.
(b) If stolen property is recovered after the Insurer has paid a claim, the Insured Person must tell the Insurer and either return the payment or give the Insurer the property.

state: There's more to offer in the opening of The Odd Couple than in the entirety of most films. Felix Unger (the poor guy's monogram even curses him) checks into a New York hotel. A cleaning lady says "Good night." "Goodbye," he answers back. In his room he empties his pockets, then struggles to take off his wedding ring only to put the objects neatly into an envelope, addressed to his wife and beloved children. When the viewer finally puts it together  aha, he's going to off himself  we watch him struggle to open the window  oh no, he's going to jump  The poor guy injures his lower back. This is all you need to know about Felix Unger  his wife has left him, he's a compulsive cleaner and he's a hypochondriac. And all in one scene. This is the particular genius of Neil Simon's comedy  it's about situation and character. There are few obvious physical jokes  no kicks to the groin, no cheap gags  just funny characters in uncomfortable situations. And, of course, he is a master of manipulating the audience's expectations. Coming from the Swingers era, imagine what I thought in the date scene when Felix starts lamenting about the breakup of his marriage to the girls his roommate Oscar has

# Annual Multi-Trip Travel Cover
Issued by Compass Mutual

## 1. Definitions
- **1.1** Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
- **1.2** Sports equipment means skis, snowboards, golf clubs, surfboards and bicycles.
- **1.3** Valuables means laptops, tablets, mobile phones, cameras, watches and jewellery.

## 2. Limits and excess
- **2.1** Baggage and Personal Belongings: limit $1,500 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
- **2.2** Emergency Medical Expenses: limit $25,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
- **2.3** Trip Cancellation: limit $2,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
- **2.4** Travel Delay: limit $750 per incident; excess $25 per claim.
- **2.5** Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the excess is then deducted from the result.

## 3. Baggage and Personal Belongings
- **3.1** We will pay for the loss of, theft of, or damage to your baggage and personal belongings during the trip.
- **3.2** The most we will pay for Valuables under this section is $250 per incident.
- **3.3** The most we will pay for Sports equipment under this section is $300 per incident.
- **3.4** We will not pay for loss or theft of property left unattended in a vehicle or in a public place. This exclusion does not apply to property locked out of sight in the boot or trunk of a locked vehicle.
- **3.5** We will not pay for loss caused by confiscation or detention by customs or other officials.
- **3.6** We will not pay for damage caused by wear and tear or gradual deterioration.

## 4. General exclusions
- **4.1** We will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
- **4.2** We will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.

## 5. Making a claim
- **5.1** You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
- **5.2** You must notify us of a claim within 21 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.
- **5.3** We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

## 6. Personal liability
- **6.1** We will pay damages you become legally liable to pay for accidental injury to another person or accidental damage to their property during the trip.
- **6.2** This section does not cover liability arising from the use of motor vehicles, boats or aircraft.
- **6.3** The most we will pay under this section is $1,000,000 for all claims arising from one event.

## 7. Arbitration
- **7.1** If we accept a claim but disagree with you about the amount, the difference will be referred to an arbitrator appointed by both parties.
- **7.2** Where arbitration applies, obtaining an award is a condition precedent to any legal action against us.

## 8. Changes in circumstances
- **8.1** You must tell us as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
- **8.2** We may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

## 1. Definitions

## 3. Vision Care
- **3.1** We will reimburse eye tests and prescription eyewear.
- **3.2** The most we will pay for Frames under this section is $150 per treatment.

## 4. Optional cover: Hearing Care

- **4.2** This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
- **4.3** The most we will pay for Hearing accessories under this section is $150 per treatment.

state: Alive Alive is a very entertaining SCI-FI movie from Japan. I have noticed a lot of disappointed film geeks who loved Versus this director's debut film or his third film Azumi. If you are looking for beginning to end wall to wall action then Alive is not your pick. There is plenty of action however it comes as pay-off for a whole hour of character driven build-up. Personally I think it is well done and worth it. Of course some of the plot is silly as with many SCI-Fi action films and I think the subtitles using the term foreign object could have replaced with parasite for greater effect. This film is brutal when it needs to be so faint of heart need not apply. They kept the budget down by for the most part confining all the action to one underground building(taking a cue from the cube) but the film doesn't suffer for it. PART I: Definitions
I.1  Art and antiques means paintings, antiques, rugs and other works of art.
I.2  Bicycles means bicycles and electric scooters.
I.3  High-risk items means jewellery, watches, laptops, games consoles and cameras.
I.4  Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in the Policyholder's schedule.
I.5  Unoccupied means not lived in by the Policyholder or a member of the Policyholder's family for more than 60 consecutive days.

PART II: Limits and excess
II.1  Theft: limit $20,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
II.2  Escape of Water: limit $15,000 per incident; excess $250 per claim.
II.3  Accidental Damage: limit $5,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
II.4  Flood: limit $40,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
II.5  The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

PART III: Theft
III.1  The Insurer will pay for contents stolen from the Policyholder's home.
III.2  The most the Insurer will pay for High-risk items under this section is $1,500 per incident.
III.3  The most the Insurer will pay for Bicycles under this section is $800 per incident.
III.4  The Insurer will not pay for theft while the home is unoccupied.
III.5  The Insurer will not pay for theft where there is no sign of forced entry to the home. This exclusion does not apply where the thief gained entry by deception, for example by posing as a utility worker.
III.6  The Insurer will not pay for theft from sheds, garages or other outbuildings. This exclusion does not apply if the outbuilding was locked and the theft involved forcible entry.

PART IV: Escape of Water
IV.1  The Insurer will pay for contents damaged by water escaping from a fixed pipe, tank or domestic appliance.
IV.2  The most the Insurer will pay for Art and antiques under this section is $2,000 per incident.
IV.3  The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by water leaking gradually over a period of time.
IV.4  The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by the failure of grout or sealant around baths and showers.

PART V: General exclusions
V.1  The Insurer will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
V.2  The Insurer will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
V.3  The Insurer will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits the Insurer from paying.

PART VI: Making a claim
VI.1  The Policyholder must notify the Insurer of a claim within 90 days of the incident. The Insurer will not pay any claim notified after that time.
VI.2  The Policyholder must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
VI.3  The Insurer may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

Issued by Hearthstone Insurance plc

SECTION 1 - DEFINITIONS
1.1 Garden items means garden furniture, plants and outdoor tools.

SECTION 2 - LIMITS AND EXCESS
2.1 Theft: limit $20,000 per incident; excess $250 per claim.
2.2 Escape of Water: limit $30,000 per incident; excess $250 per claim.
2.3 Accidental Damage: limit $2,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
2.4 Flood: limit $40,000 per incident; excess $1,000 per claim.
2.5 The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

SECTION 3 - FLOOD
3.1 We will pay for contents damaged by flood water entering your home.
3.2 No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 60 days after the policy start date.
3.3 The most we will pay for Garden items under this section is $1,000 per incident.
3.4 We will not pay for flood damage where a flood warning for your area had been issued before the policy started.

SECTION 4 - GENERAL EXCLUSIONS
4.1 We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
4.2 We will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.

SECTION 5 - MAKING A CLAIM
5.1 We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
5.2 You must notify us of a claim within 21 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.
5.3 You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.

SECTION 6 - INTEREST
6.1 We will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

SECTION 7 - ELECTRONIC DOCUMENTS
7.1 We will send documents by email unless you ask for paper copies.
7.2 You must tell us if your email address changes.
7.3 Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

SECTION 8 - RENEWAL
8.1 We will write to you at least 21 days before the end of the policy period with the renewal terms.
8.2 We are not obliged to offer renewal.

SECTION 9 - ALTERNATIVE ACCOMMODATION
9.1 If your home cannot be lived in after damage covered by this policy, we will pay the reasonable cost of comparable temporary accommodation.
9.2 We will also pay for the temporary housing of pets that live with you.
9.3 Cover ends when the home is fit to live in again or after twelve months, whichever is sooner.

SECTION 10 - CLAIMS DOCUMENTS
10.1 You must provide, at your own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence we reasonably ask for.
10.2 We may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

SECTION 11 - INFLATION
11.1 We may adjust limits at renewal in line with a published index of consumer prices.
11.2 Any adjustment will be shown in your renewal documents; limits do not change during a policy period.

SECTION 12 - FREEZER CONTENTS
12.1 We will pay for food in a domestic freezer that spoils because of a rise or fall in temperature.
12.2 We will not pay if the freezer is more than fifteen years old, or if the electricity supplier cut the supply deliberately.

SECTION 13 - GEOGRAPHICAL LIMITS
13.1 Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
13.2 Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

SECTION 14 - GARDEN AND OUTDOOR COVER
14.1 We will pay for plants, trees and shrubs in the garden of the home that are damaged by fire, lightning or theft.
14.2 We will not pay for damage caused by frost, storms, drought or animals.

# Home Contents Insurance Policy
Issued by Hearthstone Insurance plc

## 1. Definitions
- **1.1** Bicycles means bicycles and electric scooters.
- **1.2** High-risk items means jewellery, watches, laptops, games consoles and cameras.
- **1.3** Limit means the most we will pay for all claims under a section arising from one incident.
- **1.4** Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows your details, the covers you bought and any extensions.
- **1.5** Unoccupied means not lived in by you or a member of your family for more than 60 consecutive days.

## 2. Limits and excess
- **2.1** Theft: limit $40,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
- **2.2** Escape of Water: limit $30,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
- **2.3** Accidental Damage: limit $3,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
- **2.4** Flood: limit $20,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
- **2.5** The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

## 3. Data protection
- **3.1** We will use the personal information you provide to administer this policy and to handle claims.
- **3.2** We will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
- **3.3** You can ask for a copy of the personal information we hold by writing to our data protection officer.

## 4. Arbitration
- **4.1** If we accept a claim but disagree with you about the amount, the difference will be referred to an arbitrator appointed by both parties.
- **4.2** Where arbitration applies, obtaining an award is a condition precedent to any legal action against us.

## 5. Complaints
- **5.1** If you have a complaint, you should first contact our customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
- **5.2** We will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
- **5.3** If you remain dissatisfied, you may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

## 6. Theft
- **6.1** We will pay for contents stolen from your home.
- **6.2** The most we will pay for High-risk items under this section is $2,500 per incident.
- **6.3** The most we will pay for Bicycles under this section is $500 per incident.
- **6.4** We will not pay for theft while the home is unoccupied.
- **6.5** We will not pay for theft where there is no sign of forced entry to the home. This exclusion does not apply where the thief gained entry by deception, for example by posing as a utility worker.
- **6.6** We will not pay for theft from sheds, garages or other outbuildings. This exclusion does not apply if the outbuilding was locked and the theft involved forcible entry.

## 7. General exclusions
- **7.1** We will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
- **7.2** We will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by you.
- **7.3** We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.

## 8. Making a claim
- **8.1** You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
- **8.2** We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
- **8.3** You must notify us of a claim within 60 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.

## 9. Tenant's improvements
- **9.1** If you rent the home, we will pay for damage to fixtures and fittings that you installed and are responsible for.
- **9.2** This cover applies only to improvements you paid for, not to items provided by the landlord.

Issued by Oakfield Assurance

## 1. Definitions
- **1.1** Bicycles means bicycles and electric scooters.
- **1.2** Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
- **1.3** High-risk items means jewellery, watches, laptops, games consoles and cameras.
- **1.4** Portable electronics means laptops, tablets and mobile phones.
- **1.5** Premium means the amount you must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
- **1.6** Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
- **1.7** Unoccupied means not lived in by you or a member of your family for more than 45 consecutive days.

## 2. Limits and excess
- **2.1** Theft: limit $10,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
- **2.2** Escape of Water: limit $30,000 per incident; excess $250 per claim.
- **2.3** Accidental Damage: limit $3,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
- **2.4** Flood: limit $40,000 per incident; excess $1,000 per claim.
- **2.5** Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the excess is then deducted from the result.

## 3. Theft
- **3.1** We will pay for contents stolen from your home.
- **3.2** The most we will pay for High-risk items under this section is $1,000 per incident.
- **3.3** The most we will pay for Bicycles under this section is $800 per incident.
- **3.4** We will not pay for theft while the home is unoccupied.
- **3.5** We will not pay for theft where there is no sign of forced entry to the home. This exclusion does not apply where the thief gained entry by deception, for example by posing as a utility worker.
- **3.6** We will not pay for theft from sheds, garages or other outbuildings. This exclusion does not apply if the outbuilding was locked and the theft involved forcible entry.

## 4. Optional cover: Accidental Damage
- **4.1** We will pay for sudden and unexpected accidental damage to your contents inside the home.
- **4.2** This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
- **4.3** The most we will pay for Portable electronics under this section is $750 per incident.
- **4.4** We will not pay for damage caused by pets.
- **4.5** We will not pay for wear and tear, or damage that happens gradually.

## 5. General exclusions
- **5.1** We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
- **5.2** We will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
- **5.3** We will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits us from paying.

## 6. Making a claim
- **6.1** You must notify us of a claim within 21 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.
- **6.2** You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
- **6.3** We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

## 7. Fraud
- **7.1** If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, we will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
- **7.2** We may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

## 8. Garden and outdoor cover
- **8.1** We will pay for plants, trees and shrubs in the garden of the home that are damaged by fire, lightning or theft.
- **8.2** We will not pay for damage caused by frost, storms, drought or animals.

# Annual Multi-Trip Travel Cover
Issued by Compass Mutual

## 1. Definitions
- **1.1** Qualifying delay means a delay to the scheduled departure of more than 8 hours.
- **1.2** Sports equipment means skis, snowboards, golf clubs, surfboards and bicycles.
- **1.3** Travelling companion means a person who has booked to travel with you on the same trip.
- **1.4** Valuables means laptops, tablets, mobile phones, cameras, watches and jewellery.

## 2. Limits and excess
- **2.1** Baggage and Personal Belongings: limit $1,500 per incident; excess $75 per claim.
- **2.2** Emergency Medical Expenses: limit $50,000 per incident; excess $150 per claim.
- **2.3** Trip Cancellation: limit $3,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
- **2.4** Travel Delay: limit $500 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
- **2.5** The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

## 3. Baggage and Personal Belongings
- **3.1** We will pay for the loss of, theft of, or damage to your baggage and personal belongings during the trip.
- **3.2** The most we will pay for Valuables under this section is $400 per incident.
- **3.3** The most we will pay for Sports equipment under this section is $300 per incident.
- **3.4** We will not pay for loss or theft of property left unattended in a vehicle or in a public place. This exclusion does not apply to property locked out of sight in the boot or trunk of a locked vehicle.
- **3.5** We will not pay for loss caused by confiscation or detention by customs or other officials.
- **3.6** We will not pay for damage caused by wear and tear or gradual deterioration.

## 4. Optional cover: Travel Delay
- **4.1** We will pay reasonable costs of meals and accommodation if your outbound departure is delayed.
- **4.2** This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
- **4.3** We will not pay for any delay that is not a qualifying delay.

## 5. General exclusions
- **5.1** We will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits us from paying.
- **5.2** We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
- **5.3** We will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.

## 6. Making a claim
- **6.1** You must notify us of a claim within 30 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.
- **6.2** You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
- **6.3** We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

=== CLAIM ===
From: Yusuf Novak
Subject: Claim on policy D464029

Hello,

I would like to claim under Travel Delay for meals and taxis during a long airport delay. My policy started on May 8, 2025 and my schedule lists Baggage and Personal Belongings, Emergency Medical Expenses, Trip Cancellation, Travel Delay (extensions: none). The incident happened on December 22, 2025. The departure was delayed by 9 hours. The delay was caused by a technical fault with the aircraft. The trip was booked through an online travel agent. Yusuf was travelling with two colleagues.

I am sending this on December 25, 2025, which is when I first notified you. Your adjuster assessed the loss at $785.

Thanks,
Yusuf

PART I: Definitions
I.1  Garden items means garden furniture, plants and outdoor tools.
I.2  Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.

PART II: Limits and excess
II.1  Theft: limit $10,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
II.2  Escape of Water: limit $15,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
II.3  Accidental Damage: limit $5,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
II.4  Flood: limit $20,000 per incident; excess $1,000 per claim.
II.5  Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the excess is then deducted from the result.

PART III: Tenant's improvements
III.1  If the Policyholder rents the home, the Insurer will pay for damage to fixtures and fittings that the Policyholder installed and are responsible for.
III.2  This cover applies only to improvements the Policyholder paid for, not to items provided by the landlord.

PART IV: Reasonable precautions
IV.1  The Policyholder must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
IV.2  The Policyholder must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

PART V: Flood
V.1  The Insurer will pay for contents damaged by flood water entering the Policyholder's home.
V.2  No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 60 days after the policy start date.
V.3  The most the Insurer will pay for Garden items under this section is $500 per incident.
V.4  The Insurer will not pay for flood damage where a flood warning for the Policyholder's area had been issued before the policy started.

PART VI: Communication
VI.1  The Insurer will communicate with the Policyholder in English.
VI.2  The Insurer may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

PART VII: Premium payment
VII.1  The Policyholder must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
VII.2  If an instalment is not paid within 7 days of its due date, the Insurer may cancel the policy after giving notice.

PART VIII: General exclusions
VIII.1  The Insurer will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits the Insurer from paying.
VIII.2  The Insurer will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
VIII.3  The Insurer will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.

PART IX: Geographical limits
IX.1  Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
IX.2  Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

PART X: Salvage
X.1  When the Insurer replaces an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes the Insurer's property.
X.2  If stolen property is recovered after the Insurer has paid a claim, the Policyholder must tell the Insurer and either return the payment or give the Insurer the property.

PART XI: Making a claim
XI.1  The Insurer may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
XI.2  The Policyholder must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
XI.3  The Policyholder must notify the Insurer of a claim within 60 days of the incident. The Insurer will not pay any claim notified after that time.

It was the first Gable-Crawford pairing, and made it evident to MGM and to audiences that they were a sizzling team, leading the studio to make seven more films with them as co-stars. The film convincingly depicts the downward slide of a brother and sister who, after their father loses everything in the stock market crash, must fend for themselves and work for a living. Life is hard in the Depression, and soon even their attempts at finding legitimate work prove futile, and they resort to underworld activity. Joan Crawford is excellent as the socialite-turned-moll. She's smart, complex, and believable. She even tempers the theatrical stiffness of the other actors' early Talkie acting style. Clark Gable is a diamond-in-the rough, masculine and gruff as the no-nonsense gangster who becomes involved with Crawford's character. The same year he would play a similar and even more successful role opposite Norma Shearer in "A Free Soul", securing his position as top male sex symbol at MGM. If you like Crawford in this type of role, don't miss "Paid", which she did a year earlier, which is also among her best early Talkie performances.

policy: HOME CONTENTS INSURANCE POLICY
Issued by Keystone Home Mutual
In this policy, "the Insurer" means Keystone Home Mutual and "the Policyholder" means the person named in the schedule.

Article 1. Definitions
(a) Art and antiques means paintings, antiques, rugs and other works of art.
(b) Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.

Article 2. Limits and excess
(a) Theft: limit $10,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
(b) Escape of Water: limit $15,000 per incident; excess $250 per claim.
(c) Accidental Damage: limit $2,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
(d) Flood: limit $20,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
(e) Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the excess is then deducted from the result.

Article 3. Escape of Water
(a) The Insurer will pay for contents damaged by water escaping from a fixed pipe, tank or domestic appliance.
(b) The most the Insurer will pay for Art and antiques under this section is $2,000 per incident.
(c) The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by water leaking gradually over a period of time.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by the failure of grout or sealant around baths and showers.

Article 4. General exclusions
(a) The Insurer will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
(b) The Insurer will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Policyholder.

Article 5. Other insurance
(a) If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, the Insurer will pay only the Insurer's proportionate share.
(b) The Policyholder must tell the Insurer about any other insurance that covers the same loss when the Policyholder makes a claim.

Article 6. Making a claim
(a) The Insurer may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
(b) The Policyholder must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
(c) The Policyholder must notify the Insurer of a claim within 30 days of the incident. The Insurer will not pay any claim notified after that time.

Article 7. Instalment agreements
(a) If the Policyholder pays by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.

STAFF HEALTH REIMBURSEMENT PLAN RULES
Issued by the Staff Welfare Fund

SECTION 1 - DEFINITIONS
1.1 Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
1.2 Limit means the most we will pay for all claims under a section arising from one treatment.
1.3 Major restorative work means crowns, bridges, root canal treatment and implants.
1.4 Massage therapy means sports massage, massage therapy and reflexology.
1.5 Orthodontics means braces and clear aligners.
1.6 Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows your details, the covers you bought and any extensions.

SECTION 2 - LIMITS AND DEDUCTIBLE
2.1 Dental Care: limit $1,500 per treatment; deductible $100 per claim.
2.2 Vision Care: limit $300 per treatment; deductible $25 per claim.
2.3 Therapy Services: limit $2,000 per treatment; deductible $75 per claim.
2.4 Hearing Care: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $150 per claim.
2.5 The deductible is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

SECTION 3 - DENTAL CARE
3.1 We will reimburse the cost of dental treatment provided by a licensed dentist.
3.2 No cover applies under this section to any treatment that happens within the first 90 days after the policy start date.
3.3 The most we will pay for Major restorative work under this section is $500 per treatment.
3.4 The most we will pay for Orthodontics under this section is $600 per treatment.
3.5 We will not pay for treatment that is mainly cosmetic, such as whitening or veneers. This exclusion does not apply to treatment needed to repair damage caused by an accident.
3.6 We will not pay for treatment by a provider outside the plan's network. This exclusion does not apply to emergency treatment for sudden severe pain.

SECTION 4 - THERAPY SERVICES
4.1 We will reimburse physiotherapy, osteopathy and counselling provided by a registered practitioner.
4.2 The most we will pay for Massage therapy under this section is $200 per treatment.
4.3 We will not pay for treatment of an injury covered by workers' compensation.
4.4 We will not pay for treatment by a practitioner who is not registered with the relevant professional body.

SECTION 5 - GENERAL EXCLUSIONS
5.1 We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
5.2 We will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
5.3 We will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by you.

SECTION 6 - MAKING A CLAIM
6.1 We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
6.2 You must notify us of a claim within 14 days of the treatment. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.
6.3 You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.

In the film, Ryan Phillippe is the main character, based on an actual employee of Studio from 1977 - 1982. The film's problem is that it's all glitter and style and no substance. It tries to be a really grimy and probing satire like "Boogie Nights" but ultimately comes across as an inferior wannabe. Mike Myers is given the thankless task of playing cocaine-snorting club owner Steve Rubell. It's only a slightly comedic role and if this was Myers' best attempts at sliding into drama like Lemmon and other comedic actors did in their time, it's a total failure. state: French film directors continue to amaze with their extraordinary ability to simulate the sights and sounds of ordinary, everyday suburban life. This was readily apparent with the release early in 2002 of L'Emploi du temps ( Time Out ) , a brilliant character study of of a white collar worker's descent into melancholy after having been fired from his job. As is the penchant of French filmmakers , many scenes were shot on real streets and in public places, giving a cinema verite feel to the story , yet L'Emploi du temps also possessed an elegant look thanks to excellent camera work and some stunning location footage ( most notably a Swiss mountain retreat ). state: I've always enjoyed Kenneth Branagh's versions of the Shakespeare classics, as he always does a very good job, but in this movie, the one who lifts the whole movie, is none other than "the-always-great-actor" Laurence Fishburne. Surely he has made some poor choices in films, even though he's a wonderful actor, but in this one we're truly given the real Othello: the passion, the intensity of jealousy as it grows stronger alongside with Fishburne's well portrayed paranoia and, furthermore, we're finally given a black Othello! I don't think they could have chosen a better Othello. Who else could have given him that blend of sympathy/antipathy, love/hatred and, not to forget, those fiery eyes...? Branagh is good as always, but not at his peak, Iréne Jacob's Desdemona is fairly good but a bit bleak, whilst Laurence Fishburne truly lifts it and makes it a very interesting and enjoyable movie. Do watch it.

# Device Protection Plan Terms
Issued by Brightline Device Cover

## 1. Definitions
- **1.1** Accessories means cases, chargers, earbuds and styluses.
- **1.2** Accessories means cases, chargers and earbuds.
- **1.3** Battery replacement means replacement batteries and battery repairs.
- **1.4** Manufacturer's warranty period means the first 24 months after the device was bought.
- **1.5** Premium means the amount you must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
- **1.6** Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
- **1.7** Wearables means smartwatches and fitness trackers.

## 2. Limits and service fee
- **2.1** Accidental Damage: limit $1,200 per incident; service fee $79 per claim.
- **2.2** Breakdown: limit $1,000 per incident; service fee $25 per claim.
- **2.3** Theft and Loss: limit $1,200 per incident; service fee $149 per claim.
- **2.4** Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the service fee is then deducted from the result.

## 3. Optional cover: Theft and Loss
- **3.1** We will replace your device if it is stolen or lost.
- **3.2** This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
- **3.3** The most we will pay for Accessories under this section is $100 per incident.
- **3.4** We will not pay for loss or theft of property left unattended in a vehicle or in a public place. This exclusion does not apply to property locked out of sight in the boot or trunk of a locked vehicle.
- **3.5** We will not pay for theft that was not reported to the police.

## 4. Breakdown
- **4.1** We will repair or replace your device if it stops working because of an electrical or mechanical fault.
- **4.2** No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 30 days after the policy start date.
- **4.3** The most we will pay for Battery replacement under this section is $120 per incident.
- **4.4** We will not pay for breakdowns during the manufacturer's warranty period.
- **4.5** We will not pay for breakdown caused by liquid getting into the device.

## 5. Accidental Damage
- **5.1** We will repair or replace your device if it is accidentally damaged.
- **5.2** The most we will pay for Accessories under this section is $50 per incident.
- **5.3** The most we will pay for Wearables under this section is $300 per incident.
- **5.4** We will not pay for cosmetic damage, such as scratches or dents, that does not affect how the device works.
- **5.5** We will not pay for damage following a repair by anyone other than us or an authorised repairer. This exclusion does not apply if we approved the repair in writing beforehand.

## 6. General exclusions
- **6.1** We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
- **6.2** We will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.

## 7. Making a claim
- **7.1** We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
- **7.2** You must notify us of a claim within 90 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.
- **7.3** You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.

=== CLAIM ===

Hello,

I would like to claim under Theft and Loss for a pair of earbuds. My policy started on November 26, 2025 and my schedule lists Accidental Damage, Breakdown, Theft and Loss (extensions: none). The incident happened on April 27, 2026. Idris had left the earbuds in a parked car while visiting a museum. The vehicle was locked, and the earbuds were stowed in the covered trunk where it could not be seen. Idris bought the device from an authorised retailer. The retailer's receipt was uploaded with the claim.

I am sending this on July 28, 2026, which is when I first notified you. Your adjuster assessed the loss at $241.

Thanks,
Idris

state:
Circa 2002, I was pretty obsessed with Serendipity -- ya know, the romantic comedy with John Cusak and Kate Beckinsale. There was that one scene where they were sharing that amazing looking frozen hot chocolate. Because of that, I always vowed that I would make it to Serendipity in NYC and try the hot chocolate myself. 

However, as many times as I visited NYC, i NEVER made it to Serendipity. So, on this last trip to Vegas, my girlfriends and I made it a point to put it on our to-do list to make it there.

We fulfilled this goal right away as we made Serendipity our first food stop in Vegas. The inside is cute and old-school ice cream fountain like, but we sat outside on their large patio. Serendipity has a great location (in front of Cessar's on the Strip), but that's about all it has going for it. Granted, it's the Strip, but their food is ridiculously overpriced (entrees AND ice cream). I get that the ice cream portions are huge, but $15 for dessert?! C'mon now people. The experience was pretty underwhelming, to be honest.

My tip? Check your hotel for coupons! We, sadly, saw coupons for a free frozen hot chocolate in one of the coupon booklets once we got back to the hotel. Save yourself $10!

Issued by Northstar Underwriting

PART I: Definitions
I.1  Excursions and tickets means pre-booked excursions, tours, and event or theatre tickets.
I.2  Qualifying delay means a delay to the scheduled departure of more than 6 hours.
I.3  Travelling companion means a person who has booked to travel with the Insured Person on the same trip.

PART II: Limits and excess
II.1  Baggage and Personal Belongings: limit $1,500 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
II.2  Emergency Medical Expenses: limit $50,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
II.3  Trip Cancellation: limit $5,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
II.4  Travel Delay: limit $500 per incident; excess $25 per claim.
II.5  Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the excess is then deducted from the result.

PART III: Optional cover: Travel Delay
III.1  The Insurer will pay reasonable costs of meals and accommodation if the Insured Person's outbound departure is delayed.
III.2  This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Insured Person's schedule.
III.3  The Insurer will not pay for any delay that is not a qualifying delay.

PART IV: Trip Cancellation
IV.1  The Insurer will pay non-refundable travel and accommodation costs if the Insured Person must cancel the trip for a reason beyond the Insured Person's control.
IV.2  No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 10 days after the policy start date.
IV.3  The most the Insurer will pay for Excursions and tickets under this section is $200 per incident.
IV.4  The Insurer will not pay for cancellation caused by a strike or other event that had been publicly announced before the Insured Person bought the policy.
IV.5  The Insurer will not pay for cancellation because the Insured Person no longer wish to travel.

PART V: General exclusions
V.1  The Insurer will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
V.2  The Insurer will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.

PART VI: Making a claim
VI.1  The Insurer may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
VI.2  The Insured Person must notify the Insurer of a claim within 30 days of the incident. The Insurer will not pay any claim notified after that time.
VI.3  The Insured Person must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.

# Employee Health Benefits Plan: Summary Plan Description
Issued by the Staff Welfare Fund

## 1. Definitions
- **1.1** Major restorative work means crowns, bridges, root canal treatment and implants.
- **1.2** Orthodontics means braces and clear aligners.
- **1.3** Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in your schedule.
- **1.4** Premium means the amount you must pay for this policy, including any taxes.

## 2. Limits and deductible
- **2.1** Dental Care: limit $2,000 per treatment; deductible $100 per claim.
- **2.2** Vision Care: limit $400 per treatment; deductible $25 per claim.
- **2.3** Therapy Services: limit $2,000 per treatment; deductible $75 per claim.
- **2.4** Hearing Care: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $100 per claim.
- **2.5** Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the deductible is then deducted from the result.

## 3. Severability
- **3.1** If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

## 4. Dental Care
- **4.1** We will reimburse the cost of dental treatment provided by a licensed dentist.
- **4.2** No cover applies under this section to any treatment that happens within the first 90 days after the policy start date.
- **4.3** The most we will pay for Major restorative work under this section is $500 per treatment.
- **4.4** The most we will pay for Orthodontics under this section is $800 per treatment.
- **4.5** We will not pay for treatment that is mainly cosmetic, such as whitening or veneers. This exclusion does not apply to treatment needed to repair damage caused by an accident.
- **4.6** We will not pay for treatment by a provider outside the plan's network. This exclusion does not apply to emergency treatment for sudden severe pain.

## 5. General exclusions
- **5.1** We will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits us from paying.
- **5.2** We will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
- **5.3** We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.

## 6. Arbitration
- **6.1** If we accept a claim but disagree with you about the amount, the difference will be referred to an arbitrator appointed by both parties.
- **6.2** Where arbitration applies, obtaining an award is a condition precedent to any legal action against us.

## 7. Currency
- **7.1** All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
- **7.2** Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

## 8. Making a claim
- **8.1** You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
- **8.2** We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
- **8.3** You must notify us of a claim within 90 days of the treatment. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.

## 9. Geographical limits
- **9.1** Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
- **9.2** Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

## 10. Taxes
- **10.1** The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
- **10.2** If the tax rate changes, we may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

Issued by Hearthstone Insurance plc

PART I: Definitions
I.1  Bicycles means bicycles and electric scooters.
I.2  Garden items means garden furniture, plants and outdoor tools.
I.3  High-risk items means jewellery, watches, laptops, games consoles and cameras.
I.4  Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
I.5  Unoccupied means not lived in by the Policyholder or a member of the Policyholder's family for more than 30 consecutive days.

PART II: Limits and excess
II.1  Theft: limit $40,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
II.2  Escape of Water: limit $15,000 per incident; excess $250 per claim.
II.3  Accidental Damage: limit $5,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
II.4  Flood: limit $40,000 per incident; excess $1,000 per claim.
II.5  The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

PART III: Theft
III.1  The Insurer will pay for contents stolen from the Policyholder's home.
III.2  The most the Insurer will pay for High-risk items under this section is $1,000 per incident.
III.3  The most the Insurer will pay for Bicycles under this section is $800 per incident.
III.4  The Insurer will not pay for theft while the home is unoccupied.
III.5  The Insurer will not pay for theft where there is no sign of forced entry to the home. This exclusion does not apply where the thief gained entry by deception, for example by posing as a utility worker.
III.6  The Insurer will not pay for theft from sheds, garages or other outbuildings. This exclusion does not apply if the outbuilding was locked and the theft involved forcible entry.

PART IV: Flood
IV.1  The Insurer will pay for contents damaged by flood water entering the Policyholder's home.
IV.2  No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 60 days after the policy start date.
IV.3  The most the Insurer will pay for Garden items under this section is $500 per incident.
IV.4  The Insurer will not pay for flood damage where a flood warning for the Policyholder's area had been issued before the policy started.

PART V: General exclusions
V.1  The Insurer will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
V.2  The Insurer will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Policyholder.

PART VI: Making a claim
VI.1  The Policyholder must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
VI.2  The Insurer may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
VI.3  The Policyholder must notify the Insurer of a claim within 30 days of the incident. The Insurer will not pay any claim notified after that time.

PART VII: Instalment agreements
VII.1  If the Policyholder pays by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
VII.2  Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

PART VIII: Electronic documents
VIII.1  The Insurer will send documents by email unless the Policyholder asks for paper copies.
VIII.2  The Policyholder must tell the Insurer if the Policyholder's email address changes.
VIII.3  Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

PART IX: Garden and outdoor cover
IX.1  The Insurer will pay for plants, trees and shrubs in the garden of the home that are damaged by fire, lightning or theft.
IX.2  The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by frost, storms, drought or animals.

PART X: Discounts
X.1  Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
X.2  If a condition for a discount stops being met, the Insurer may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

# Annual Multi-Trip Travel Cover
Issued by Northstar Underwriting

## 1. Definitions
- **1.1** Dental treatment means treatment of the teeth or gums.
- **1.2** Excursions and tickets means pre-booked excursions, tours, and event or theatre tickets.
- **1.3** Hazardous activity means skydiving, motor racing, or trekking or climbing above 3,000 metres.
- **1.4** Physiotherapy means treatment of muscles and joints by a physiotherapist.
- **1.5** Pre-existing condition means any illness or injury for which you received treatment or advice in the 12 months before the policy start date.
- **1.6** Premium means the amount you must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
- **1.7** Qualifying delay means a delay to the scheduled departure of more than 12 hours.

## 2. Limits and excess
- **2.1** Baggage and Personal Belongings: limit $1,500 per incident; excess $75 per claim.
- **2.2** Emergency Medical Expenses: limit $10,000 per incident; excess $250 per claim.
- **2.3** Trip Cancellation: limit $2,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
- **2.4** Travel Delay: limit $300 per incident; excess $25 per claim.
- **2.5** The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

## 3. Optional cover: Travel Delay
- **3.1** We will pay reasonable costs of meals and accommodation if your outbound departure is delayed.
- **3.2** This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
- **3.3** We will not pay for any delay that is not a qualifying delay.

## 4. Trip Cancellation
- **4.1** We will pay non-refundable travel and accommodation costs if you must cancel the trip for a reason beyond your control.
- **4.2** No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 7 days after the policy start date.
- **4.3** The most we will pay for Excursions and tickets under this section is $300 per incident.
- **4.4** We will not pay for cancellation caused by a strike or other event that had been publicly announced before you bought the policy.
- **4.5** We will not pay for cancellation because you no longer wish to travel.

## 5. Emergency Medical Expenses
- **5.1** We will pay reasonable and necessary emergency medical costs incurred during the trip.
- **5.2** The most we will pay for Dental treatment under this section is $250 per incident.
- **5.3** The most we will pay for Physiotherapy under this section is $500 per incident.
- **5.4** We will not pay for treatment of a pre-existing condition.
- **5.5** We will not pay for injury or illness arising from a hazardous activity. This exclusion does not apply if the Adventure Sports extension is shown in your schedule.
- **5.6** We will not pay for any claim arising from your being under the influence of alcohol or drugs.

## 6. General exclusions
- **6.1** We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
- **6.2** We will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by you.

## 7. Making a claim
- **7.1** We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
- **7.2** You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
- **7.3** You must notify us of a claim within 90 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.

# Device Protection Plan Terms
Issued by Circuit Care Services

## 1. Definitions
- **1.1** Accessories means cases, chargers, earbuds and styluses.
- **1.2** Accessories means cases, chargers and earbuds.
- **1.3** Authorised repairer means a repairer approved in writing by us.
- **1.4** Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
- **1.5** Wearables means smartwatches and fitness trackers.

## 2. Limits and service fee
- **2.1** Accidental Damage: limit $1,500 per incident; service fee $79 per claim.
- **2.2** Breakdown: limit $1,000 per incident; service fee $49 per claim.
- **2.3** Theft and Loss: limit $800 per incident; service fee $149 per claim.
- **2.4** Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the service fee is then deducted from the result.

## 3. Change of address
- **3.1** You must tell us within 30 days if you change your address.
- **3.2** We may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

## 4. Optional cover: Theft and Loss
- **4.1** We will replace your device if it is stolen or lost.
- **4.2** This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
- **4.3** The most we will pay for Accessories under this section is $50 per incident.
- **4.4** We will not pay for loss or theft of property left unattended in a vehicle or in a public place. This exclusion does not apply to property locked out of sight in the boot or trunk of a locked vehicle.
- **4.5** We will not pay for theft that was not reported to the police.

## 5. Accidental Damage
- **5.1** We will repair or replace your device if it is accidentally damaged.
- **5.2** The most we will pay for Accessories under this section is $50 per incident.
- **5.3** The most we will pay for Wearables under this section is $300 per incident.
- **5.4** We will not pay for cosmetic damage, such as scratches or dents, that does not affect how the device works.
- **5.5** We will not pay for damage following a repair by anyone other than us or an authorised repairer. This exclusion does not apply if we approved the repair in writing beforehand.

## 6. General exclusions
- **6.1** We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
- **6.2** We will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits us from paying.
- **6.3** We will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.

## 7. Making a claim
- **7.1** You must notify us of a claim within 90 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.
- **7.2** We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
- **7.3** You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.

## 8. Governing law
- **8.1** This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
- **8.2** Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

III.1  The Provider will replace the Customer's device if it is stolen or lost.

PART IV: Electronic documents
IV.1  The Provider will send documents by email unless the Customer asks for paper copies.
IV.2  The Customer must tell the Provider if the Customer's email address changes.
IV.3  Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

V.1  The Provider will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits the Provider from paying.
V.2  The Provider will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Customer.

PART VII: Third-party administrators

PART VIII: Making a claim
VIII.1  The Customer must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
