policy: HOME CONTENTS INSURANCE POLICY
Issued by Oakfield Assurance

PART I: Definitions
I.1  Art and antiques means paintings, antiques, rugs and other works of art.
I.2  Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by the Insurer, before any excess, limit or sublimit is applied.
I.3  Contents means household goods and personal possessions that belong to the Policyholder or the Policyholder's family.
I.4  Portable electronics means laptops, tablets and mobile phones.

PART II: Limits and excess
II.1  Theft: limit $20,000 per incident; excess $250 per claim.
II.2  Escape of Water: limit $15,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
II.3  Accidental Damage: limit $2,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
II.4  Flood: limit $40,000 per incident; excess $1,000 per claim.
II.5  Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the excess is then deducted from the result.

PART III: Escape of Water
III.1  The Insurer will pay for contents damaged by water escaping from a fixed pipe, tank or domestic appliance.
III.2  The most the Insurer will pay for Art and antiques under this section is $2,000 per incident.
III.3  The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by water leaking gradually over a period of time.
III.4  The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by the failure of grout or sealant around baths and showers.

PART IV: Exchange of information
IV.1  To prevent fraud, the Insurer may check the details the Policyholder gives against public records and industry databases.
IV.2  The Insurer may contact previous insurers to confirm the Policyholder's claims history.

PART V: Optional cover: Accidental Damage
V.1  The Insurer will pay for sudden and unexpected accidental damage to the Policyholder's contents inside the home.
V.2  This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Policyholder's schedule.
V.3  The most the Insurer will pay for Portable electronics under this section is $750 per incident.
V.4  The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by pets.
V.5  The Insurer will not pay for wear and tear, or damage that happens gradually.

PART VI: Premium payment
VI.1  The Policyholder must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
VI.2  If an instalment is not paid within 7 days of its due date, the Insurer may cancel the policy after giving notice.

PART VII: General exclusions
VII.1  The Insurer will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
VII.2  The Insurer will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits the Insurer from paying.
VII.3  The Insurer will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Policyholder.

PART VIII: Third-party administrators
VIII.1  The Insurer may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on the Insurer's behalf.
VIII.2  Any company the Insurer appoints must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

PART IX: Change of address
IX.1  The Policyholder must tell the Insurer within 30 days if the Policyholder changes the Policyholder's address.
IX.2  The Insurer may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

PART X: Making a claim
X.1  The Policyholder must notify the Insurer of a claim within 30 days of the incident. The Insurer will not pay any claim notified after that time.
X.2  The Insurer may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
X.3  The Policyholder must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.

  content: In humans, cold shock response is perhaps the most common cause of death from immersion in very cold water, such as by falling through thin ice. Issued by Voltguard Protection Ltd

PART I: Definitions
I.1  Accessories means cases, chargers, earbuds and styluses.
I.2  Battery replacement means replacement batteries and battery repairs.
I.3  Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
I.4  Limit means the most the Provider will pay for all claims under a section arising from one incident.
I.5  Manufacturer's warranty period means the first 12 months after the device was bought.
I.6  Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
I.7  Wearables means smartwatches and fitness trackers.

PART II: Limits and service fee
II.1  Accidental Damage: limit $1,200 per incident; service fee $79 per claim.
II.2  Breakdown: limit $600 per incident; service fee $25 per claim.
II.3  Theft and Loss: limit $1,200 per incident; service fee $99 per claim.
II.4  The service fee is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

PART III: Accidental Damage
III.1  The Provider will repair or replace the Customer's device if it is accidentally damaged.
III.2  The most the Provider will pay for Accessories under this section is $50 per incident.
III.3  The most the Provider will pay for Wearables under this section is $300 per incident.
III.4  The Provider will not pay for cosmetic damage, such as scratches or dents, that does not affect how the device works.
III.5  The Provider will not pay for damage following a repair by anyone other than the Provider or an authorised repairer. This exclusion does not apply if the Provider approved the repair in writing beforehand.

PART IV: Breakdown
IV.1  The Provider will repair or replace the Customer's device if it stops working because of an electrical or mechanical fault.
IV.2  No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 30 days after the policy start date.
IV.3  The most the Provider will pay for Battery replacement under this section is $80 per incident.
IV.4  The Provider will not pay for breakdowns during the manufacturer's warranty period.
IV.5  The Provider will not pay for breakdown caused by liquid getting into the device.

PART V: General exclusions
V.1  The Provider will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
V.2  The Provider will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Customer.

PART VI: Making a claim
VI.1  The Customer must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
VI.2  The Customer must notify the Provider of a claim within 14 days of the incident. The Provider will not pay any claim notified after that time.
VI.3  The Provider may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

policy: GADGET COVER: TERMS AND CONDITIONS
Issued by Circuit Care Services
In this policy, "the Provider" means Circuit Care Services and "the Customer" means the person named in the schedule.

Article 1. Definitions
(a) Accessories means cases, chargers, earbuds and styluses.
(b) Authorised repairer means a repairer approved in writing by the Provider.
(c) Battery replacement means replacement batteries and battery repairs.
(d) Manufacturer's warranty period means the first 24 months after the device was bought.
(e) Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
(f) Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.
(g) Wearables means smartwatches and fitness trackers.

Article 2. Limits and service fee
(a) Accidental Damage: limit $1,200 per incident; service fee $99 per claim.
(b) Breakdown: limit $600 per incident; service fee $25 per claim.
(c) Theft and Loss: limit $1,200 per incident; service fee $99 per claim.
(d) Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the service fee is then deducted from the result.

Article 3. Breakdown
(a) The Provider will repair or replace the Customer's device if it stops working because of an electrical or mechanical fault.
(b) No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 30 days after the policy start date.
(c) The most the Provider will pay for Battery replacement under this section is $80 per incident.
(d) The Provider will not pay for breakdowns during the manufacturer's warranty period.
(e) The Provider will not pay for breakdown caused by liquid getting into the device.

Article 4. Accidental Damage
(a) The Provider will repair or replace the Customer's device if it is accidentally damaged.
(b) The most the Provider will pay for Accessories under this section is $50 per incident.
(c) The most the Provider will pay for Wearables under this section is $300 per incident.
(d) The Provider will not pay for cosmetic damage, such as scratches or dents, that does not affect how the device works.
(e) The Provider will not pay for damage following a repair by anyone other than the Provider or an authorised repairer. This exclusion does not apply if the Provider approved the repair in writing beforehand.

Article 5. General exclusions
(a) The Provider will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
(b) The Provider will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
(c) The Provider will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits the Provider from paying.

Article 6. Making a claim
(a) The Customer must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
(b) The Customer must notify the Provider of a claim within 60 days of the incident. The Provider will not pay any claim notified after that time.
(c) The Provider may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

# Employee Health Benefits Plan: Summary Plan Description
Issued by Wellspring Benefits Administration

## 1. Definitions
- **1.1** Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by us, before any deductible, limit or sublimit is applied.
- **1.2** Dependant means your spouse or partner, or a child under 21 who is enrolled in the plan.
- **1.3** Hearing accessories means batteries, chargers and cleaning kits.
- **1.4** Hearing aid replacement period means 24 months from the purchase of hearing aids funded by the plan.
- **1.5** Major restorative work means crowns, bridges, root canal treatment and implants.
- **1.6** Orthodontics means braces and clear aligners.

## 2. Limits and deductible
- **2.1** Dental Care: limit $2,000 per treatment; deductible $100 per claim.
- **2.2** Vision Care: limit $400 per treatment; deductible $40 per claim.
- **2.3** Therapy Services: limit $1,500 per treatment; deductible $75 per claim.
- **2.4** Hearing Care: limit $2,000 per treatment; deductible $100 per claim.
- **2.5** The deductible is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

## 3. Optional cover: Hearing Care
- **3.1** We will reimburse hearing tests and hearing aids.
- **3.2** This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
- **3.3** The most we will pay for Hearing accessories under this section is $100 per treatment.
- **3.4** We will not pay for replacement hearing aids bought within the hearing aid replacement period.

## 4. Dental Care
- **4.1** We will reimburse the cost of dental treatment provided by a licensed dentist.
- **4.2** No cover applies under this section to any treatment that happens within the first 60 days after the policy start date.
- **4.3** The most we will pay for Major restorative work under this section is $750 per treatment.
- **4.4** The most we will pay for Orthodontics under this section is $600 per treatment.
- **4.5** We will not pay for treatment that is mainly cosmetic, such as whitening or veneers. This exclusion does not apply to treatment needed to repair damage caused by an accident.
- **4.6** We will not pay for treatment by a provider outside the plan's network. This exclusion does not apply to emergency treatment for sudden severe pain.

## 5. General exclusions
- **5.1** We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
- **5.2** We will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.

## 6. Making a claim
- **6.1** We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
- **6.2** You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
- **6.3** You must notify us of a claim within 60 days of the treatment. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.

policy: EMPLOYEE HEALTH BENEFITS PLAN: SUMMARY PLAN DESCRIPTION
Issued by the Staff Welfare Fund
In this policy, "the Plan" means the Staff Welfare Fund and "the Member" means the person named in the schedule.

Article 1. Definitions
(a) Frames means spectacle frames bought without new lenses.
(b) Massage therapy means sports massage, massage therapy and reflexology.
(c) Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
(d) Replacement period means 12 months from the date of the Member's last eyewear claim.

Article 2. Limits and deductible
(a) Dental Care: limit $2,000 per treatment; deductible $100 per claim.
(b) Vision Care: limit $300 per treatment; deductible $40 per claim.
(c) Therapy Services: limit $1,500 per treatment; deductible $50 per claim.
(d) Hearing Care: limit $2,000 per treatment; deductible $100 per claim.
(e) Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the deductible is then deducted from the result.

Article 3. Therapy Services
(a) The Plan will reimburse physiotherapy, osteopathy and counselling provided by a registered practitioner.
(b) The most the Plan will pay for Massage therapy under this section is $300 per treatment.
(c) The Plan will not pay for treatment of an injury covered by workers' compensation.
(d) The Plan will not pay for treatment by a practitioner who is not registered with the relevant professional body.

Article 4. Vision Care
(a) The Plan will reimburse eye tests and prescription eyewear.
(b) The most the Plan will pay for Frames under this section is $120 per treatment.
(c) The Plan will not pay for eyewear without prescription lenses.
(d) The Plan will not pay for a further eyewear claim within the replacement period.

Article 5. General exclusions
(a) The Plan will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
(b) The Plan will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits the Plan from paying.
(c) The Plan will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.

Article 6. Making a claim
(a) The Member must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
(b) The Member must notify the Plan of a claim within 90 days of the treatment. The Plan will not pay any claim notified after that time.
(c) The Plan may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

Article 7. Compensation scheme
(a) The Plan is covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
(b) If the Plan cannot meet the Plan's obligations, the Member may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

Article 8. Contracts (Rights of Third Parties)
(a) A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

Article 9. Geographical limits
(a) Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
(b) Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

# Staff Health Reimbursement Plan Rules
Issued by the Benefits Trust

## 1. Definitions
- **1.1** Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by us, before any deductible, limit or sublimit is applied.
- **1.2** Family means your spouse or partner and any children who live with you.
- **1.3** Hearing accessories means batteries, chargers and cleaning kits.
- **1.4** Hearing aid replacement period means 36 months from the purchase of hearing aids funded by the plan.
- **1.5** Major restorative work means crowns, bridges, root canal treatment and implants.
- **1.6** Orthodontics means braces and clear aligners.

## 2. Limits and deductible
- **2.1** Dental Care: limit $2,000 per treatment; deductible $50 per claim.
- **2.2** Vision Care: limit $500 per treatment; deductible $25 per claim.
- **2.3** Therapy Services: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $50 per claim.
- **2.4** Hearing Care: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $100 per claim.
- **2.5** Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the deductible is then deducted from the result.

## 3. Optional cover: Hearing Care
- **3.1** We will reimburse hearing tests and hearing aids.
- **3.2** This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
- **3.3** The most we will pay for Hearing accessories under this section is $150 per treatment.
- **3.4** We will not pay for replacement hearing aids bought within the hearing aid replacement period.

## 4. Dental Care
- **4.1** We will reimburse the cost of dental treatment provided by a licensed dentist.
- **4.2** No cover applies under this section to any treatment that happens within the first 60 days after the policy start date.
- **4.3** The most we will pay for Major restorative work under this section is $500 per treatment.
- **4.4** The most we will pay for Orthodontics under this section is $800 per treatment.
- **4.5** We will not pay for treatment that is mainly cosmetic, such as whitening or veneers. This exclusion does not apply to treatment needed to repair damage caused by an accident.
- **4.6** We will not pay for treatment by a provider outside the plan's network. This exclusion does not apply to emergency treatment for sudden severe pain.

## 5. General exclusions
- **5.1** We will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
- **5.2** We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
- **5.3** We will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits us from paying.

## 6. Salvage
- **6.1** When we replace an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes our property.
- **6.2** If stolen property is recovered after we have paid a claim, you must tell us and either return the payment or give us the property.

## 7. Making a claim
- **7.1** We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
- **7.2** You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.

state: Since the founding of the republic, there has been a tension between the practice of judicial review and the democratic ideals of egalitarianism, self-government, self-determination and freedom of conscience. At one pole are those who view the Federal Judiciary and especially the Supreme Court as being ``the most separated and least checked of all branches of government.'' Indeed, federal judges and justices on the Supreme Court are not required to stand for election by virtue of their tenure ``during good behavior,'' and their pay may ``not be diminished'' while they hold their position (Section 1 of Article Three). Though subject to the process of impeachment, only one Justice has ever been impeached and no Supreme Court Justice has been removed from office. At the other pole are those who view the judiciary as the least dangerous branch, with little ability to resist the exhortations of the other branches of government. The Supreme Court, it is noted, cannot directly enforce its rulings; instead, it relies on respect for the Constitution and for the law for adherence to its judgments. One notable instance of nonacquiescence came in 1832, when the state of Georgia ignored the Supreme Court's decision in Worcester v. Georgia. President Andrew Jackson, who sided with the Georgia courts, is supposed to have remarked, ``John Marshall has made his decision; now let him enforce it!''; however, this alleged quotation has been disputed. Some state governments in the South also resisted the desegregation of public schools after the 1954 judgment Brown v. Board of Education. More recently, many feared that President Nixon would refuse to comply with the Court's order in United States v. Nixon (1974) to surrender the Watergate tapes. Nixon, however, ultimately complied with the Supreme Court's ruling.

policy: RENTERS CONTENTS PROTECTION
Issued by Hearthstone Insurance plc

PART I: Definitions
I.1  Forcible entry means entry to the home that leaves visible damage to doors, windows or locks.
I.2  Garden items means garden furniture, plants and outdoor tools.
I.3  Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows the Policyholder's details, the covers the Policyholder bought and any extensions.

PART II: Limits and excess
II.1  Theft: limit $40,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
II.2  Escape of Water: limit $15,000 per incident; excess $250 per claim.
II.3  Accidental Damage: limit $2,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
II.4  Flood: limit $40,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
II.5  The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

PART III: Flood
III.1  The Insurer will pay for contents damaged by flood water entering the Policyholder's home.
III.2  No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 30 days after the policy start date.
III.3  The most the Insurer will pay for Garden items under this section is $1,000 per incident.
III.4  The Insurer will not pay for flood damage where a flood warning for the Policyholder's area had been issued before the policy started.

PART IV: General exclusions
IV.1  The Insurer will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
IV.2  The Insurer will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Policyholder.
IV.3  The Insurer will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.

PART V: Making a claim
V.1  The Policyholder must notify the Insurer of a claim within 14 days of the incident. The Insurer will not pay any claim notified after that time.
V.2  The Insurer may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
V.3  The Policyholder must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.

PART VI: Alternative accommodation
VI.1  If the Policyholder's home cannot be lived in after damage covered by this policy, the Insurer will pay the reasonable cost of comparable temporary accommodation.
VI.2  The Insurer will also pay for the temporary housing of pets that live with the Policyholder.
VI.3  Cover ends when the home is fit to live in again or after twelve months, whichever is sooner.

state: document: The optic nerve is the second of twelve paired cranial nerves and is technically part of the central nervous system, rather than the peripheral nervous system because it is derived from an out-pouching of the diencephalon (optic stalks) during embryonic development. As a consequence, the fibers of the optic nerve are covered with myelin produced by oligodendrocytes, rather than Schwann cells of the peripheral nervous system, and are encased within the meninges. Peripheral neuropathies like Guillain--Barré syndrome do not affect the optic nerve. However, most typically the optic nerve is grouped with the other eleven cranial nerves and considered to be part of the peripheral nervous system.

state: Atrial septal defect (ASD) is a heart defect in which blood flows between the atria (upper chambers) of the heart. Some flow is a normal condition both pre-birth and immediately post-birth via the foramen ovale, however when this does not naturally close after birth it is referred to as a patent (open) foramen ovale (PFO). Normally, after PFO closure, the atria are separated by a dividing wall, the interatrial septum. If this septum is defective or absent, then oxygen-rich blood can flow directly from the left side of the heart to mix with the oxygen-poor blood in the right side of the heart, or vice versa. This can lead to lower-than-normal oxygen levels in the arterial blood that supplies the brain, organs, and tissues. However, an ASD may not produce noticeable signs or symptoms, especially if the defect is small. Also, in terms of health risks, people who have had a cryptogenic stroke are more likely to have a PFO than the general population.

instructions.question: is a patent foramen ovale an atrial septal defect?

# Renters Contents Protection
Issued by Keystone Home Mutual

## 1. Definitions
- **1.1** Art and antiques means paintings, antiques, rugs and other works of art.
- **1.2** Bicycles means bicycles and electric scooters.
- **1.3** Garden items means garden furniture, plants and outdoor tools.
- **1.4** High-risk items means jewellery, watches, laptops, games consoles and cameras.
- **1.5** Outbuilding means a shed, garage or greenhouse within the boundaries of the home.
- **1.6** Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in your schedule.
- **1.7** Unoccupied means not lived in by you or a member of your family for more than 45 consecutive days.

## 2. Limits and excess
- **2.1** Theft: limit $40,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
- **2.2** Escape of Water: limit $15,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
- **2.3** Accidental Damage: limit $2,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
- **2.4** Flood: limit $20,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
- **2.5** The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

## 3. Flood
- **3.1** We will pay for contents damaged by flood water entering your home.
- **3.2** No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 30 days after the policy start date.
- **3.3** The most we will pay for Garden items under this section is $500 per incident.
- **3.4** We will not pay for flood damage where a flood warning for your area had been issued before the policy started.

## 4. Theft
- **4.1** We will pay for contents stolen from your home.
- **4.2** The most we will pay for High-risk items under this section is $1,000 per incident.
- **4.3** The most we will pay for Bicycles under this section is $500 per incident.
- **4.4** We will not pay for theft while the home is unoccupied.
- **4.5** We will not pay for theft where there is no sign of forced entry to the home. This exclusion does not apply where the thief gained entry by deception, for example by posing as a utility worker.
- **4.6** We will not pay for theft from sheds, garages or other outbuildings. This exclusion does not apply if the outbuilding was locked and the theft involved forcible entry.

## 5. Escape of Water
- **5.1** We will pay for contents damaged by water escaping from a fixed pipe, tank or domestic appliance.
- **5.2** The most we will pay for Art and antiques under this section is $2,000 per incident.
- **5.3** We will not pay for damage caused by water leaking gradually over a period of time.
- **5.4** We will not pay for damage caused by the failure of grout or sealant around baths and showers.

## 6. General exclusions
- **6.1** We will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by you.
- **6.2** We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.

## 7. Making a claim
- **7.1** We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
- **7.2** You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
- **7.3** You must notify us of a claim within 14 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.

=== CLAIM ===
From: Mira Sato
Subject: Claim on policy T537015

Hello,

I would like to claim under Flood for garden furniture and tools. My policy started on January 18, 2026 and my schedule lists Theft, Escape of Water, Flood (extensions: none). The incident happened on October 12, 2026. Heavy rain caused the nearby river to burst its banks and flood the street. The building is a converted warehouse with six flats.

I am sending this on October 28, 2026, which is when I first notified you. Your adjuster assessed the loss at $954.

Thanks,
Mira

state: As may be the case with other contracts, real estate contracts may be formed by one party making an offer and another party accepting the offer. To be enforceable, the offers and acceptances must be in writing (Statute of Frauds, Common Law)and signed by the parties agreeing to the contract. Often, the party making the offer prepares a written real estate contract, signs it, and transmits it to the other party who would accept the offer by signing the contract. As with all other types of legal offers, the other party may accept the offer, reject it (in which case the offer is terminated), make a counteroffer (in which case the original offer is terminated), or not respond to the offer (in which case the offer terminates by the expiration date in it). Before the offer (or counteroffer) is accepted, the offering (or countering) party can withdraw it. A counteroffer may be countered with yet another offer, and a counteroffering process may go on indefinitely between the parties.

4.1 We will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits us from paying.
4.2 We will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by you.
4.3 We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.

10.1 Where practical, we will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.

11.1 Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.

policy: RENTERS CONTENTS PROTECTION
Issued by Lantern General Insurance
In this policy, "the Insurer" means Lantern General Insurance and "the Policyholder" means the person named in the schedule.

Article 1. Definitions
(a) Art and antiques means paintings, antiques, rugs and other works of art.
(b) Garden items means garden furniture, plants and outdoor tools.
(c) Limit means the most the Insurer will pay for all claims under a section arising from one incident.
(d) Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in the Policyholder's schedule.
(e) Portable electronics means laptops, tablets and mobile phones.
(f) Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.

Article 2. Limits and excess
(a) Theft: limit $40,000 per incident; excess $250 per claim.
(b) Escape of Water: limit $15,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
(c) Accidental Damage: limit $5,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
(d) Flood: limit $20,000 per incident; excess $1,000 per claim.
(e) Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the excess is then deducted from the result.

Article 3. Optional cover: Accidental Damage
(a) The Insurer will pay for sudden and unexpected accidental damage to the Policyholder's contents inside the home.
(b) This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Policyholder's schedule.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Portable electronics under this section is $750 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by pets.
(e) The Insurer will not pay for wear and tear, or damage that happens gradually.

Article 4. Flood
(a) The Insurer will pay for contents damaged by flood water entering the Policyholder's home.
(b) No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 14 days after the policy start date.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Garden items under this section is $1,000 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for flood damage where a flood warning for the Policyholder's area had been issued before the policy started.

Article 5. Escape of Water
(a) The Insurer will pay for contents damaged by water escaping from a fixed pipe, tank or domestic appliance.
(b) The most the Insurer will pay for Art and antiques under this section is $1,000 per incident.
(c) The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by water leaking gradually over a period of time.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by the failure of grout or sealant around baths and showers.

Article 6. General exclusions
(a) The Insurer will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits the Insurer from paying.
(b) The Insurer will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
(c) The Insurer will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.

Article 7. Making a claim
(a) The Insurer may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
(b) The Policyholder must notify the Insurer of a claim within 60 days of the incident. The Insurer will not pay any claim notified after that time.
(c) The Policyholder must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.

In this policy, "the Insurer" means Keystone Home Mutual and "the Policyholder" means the person named in the schedule.

Article 1. Definitions
(a) Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
(b) Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
(c) Portable electronics means laptops, tablets and mobile phones.
(d) Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.

Article 2. Limits and excess
(a) Theft: limit $10,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
(b) Escape of Water: limit $15,000 per incident; excess $250 per claim.
(c) Accidental Damage: limit $5,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
(d) Flood: limit $40,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
(e) Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the excess is then deducted from the result.

Article 3. Optional cover: Accidental Damage
(a) The Insurer will pay for sudden and unexpected accidental damage to the Policyholder's contents inside the home.
(b) This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Policyholder's schedule.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Portable electronics under this section is $750 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by pets.
(e) The Insurer will not pay for wear and tear, or damage that happens gradually.

Article 4. General exclusions
(a) The Insurer will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits the Insurer from paying.
(b) The Insurer will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.

Article 5. Making a claim
(a) The Policyholder must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
(b) The Insurer may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
(c) The Policyholder must notify the Insurer of a claim within 60 days of the incident. The Insurer will not pay any claim notified after that time.

Article 6. Premium payment
(a) The Policyholder must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
(b) If an instalment is not paid within 7 days of its due date, the Insurer may cancel the policy after giving notice.

Article 7. Notices
(a) Any notice the Insurer gives under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address the Insurer holds.
(b) Notices from the Policyholder should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

Article 8. Contracts (Rights of Third Parties)
(a) A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

Article 9. How to read this document
(a) This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.
(b) Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
(c) Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

state: Because kerosene heaters are usually unvented, all combustion products are released into the indoor air. Among these are low levels of nitrogen dioxide and carbon monoxide. An improperly adjusted, fueled, or poorly maintained kerosene heater will release more pollutants, particularly through incomplete combustion. Use of a kerosene heater in an improperly ventilated home poses an extreme risk to life. If oxygen is burnt faster than the extraneous atmosphere can leak into the room to replenish the burnt oxygen, the proportion of carbon monoxide rapidly increases. Since the monoxide can not escape, any person in the room will fatally succumb to the poisonous gas. Human senses only detect an excess of carbon dioxide, and death occurs before any occupants of the room sense there is something amiss. Most manufacturers recommend that a window or door be left cracked open. Kerosene heaters should not be left unattended, especially when sleeping. A kerosene heater, as any heater that uses organic fuel, can produce dangerously high amounts of soot and carbon monoxide when running out of oxygen. Failure to follow safety precautions could result in asphyxiation or carbon monoxide poisoning.

Working from a dreadful script by Brian Eklund (which relies heavily on liberal use of the f-bomb) director Sheets delivers yet another embarrassingly amateurish effort featuring some mind-numbingly awful performances from his talent-free cast, dreadful visual effects (some crap CGI and what looks like the front of a giant cardboard space-shuttle) and his trademark shoddy gore (handfuls of offal pulled from beneath his victims' clothing). # Travel Insurance Policy Wording
Issued by Bluewater Assurance

## 1. Definitions
- **1.1** Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
- **1.2** Dental treatment means treatment of the teeth or gums.
- **1.3** Hazardous activity means skydiving, motor racing, or trekking or climbing above 3,000 metres.
- **1.4** Physiotherapy means treatment of muscles and joints by a physiotherapist.
- **1.5** Pre-existing condition means any illness or injury for which you received treatment or advice in the 12 months before the policy start date.
- **1.6** Qualifying delay means a delay to the scheduled departure of more than 8 hours.
- **1.7** Trip means a journey that starts and ends in your home country during the policy period.

## 2. Limits and excess
- **2.1** Baggage and Personal Belongings: limit $3,000 per incident; excess $75 per claim.
- **2.2** Emergency Medical Expenses: limit $50,000 per incident; excess $150 per claim.
- **2.3** Trip Cancellation: limit $5,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
- **2.4** Travel Delay: limit $300 per incident; excess $25 per claim.
- **2.5** The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

## 3. Optional cover: Travel Delay
- **3.1** We will pay reasonable costs of meals and accommodation if your outbound departure is delayed.
- **3.2** This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
- **3.3** We will not pay for any delay that is not a qualifying delay.

## 4. Emergency Medical Expenses
- **4.1** We will pay reasonable and necessary emergency medical costs incurred during the trip.
- **4.2** The most we will pay for Dental treatment under this section is $400 per incident.
- **4.3** The most we will pay for Physiotherapy under this section is $300 per incident.
- **4.4** We will not pay for treatment of a pre-existing condition.
- **4.5** We will not pay for injury or illness arising from a hazardous activity. This exclusion does not apply if the Adventure Sports extension is shown in your schedule.
- **4.6** We will not pay for any claim arising from your being under the influence of alcohol or drugs.

## 5. General exclusions
- **5.1** We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
- **5.2** We will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.

## 6. Making a claim
- **6.1** You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
- **6.2** You must notify us of a claim within 14 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.
- **6.3** We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

## 7. Emergency assistance
- **7.1** Our emergency assistance service is available 24 hours a day on the number shown in the schedule.
- **7.2** You must contact the assistance service before being admitted to hospital as an in-patient, unless it is an emergency.
- **7.3** The assistance service can arrange payment guarantees, interpreters and transport home.

## 8. Claims documents
- **8.1** You must provide, at your own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence we reasonably ask for.
- **8.2** We may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

=== CLAIM ===
From: Leila Brennan
Subject: Claim on policy B866284

Hello,

I would like to claim under Travel Delay for meals and taxis during a long airport delay. My policy started on July 31, 2025 and my schedule lists Baggage and Personal Belongings, Emergency Medical Expenses, Trip Cancellation (extensions: none). The incident happened on June 4, 2026. The delay was caused by a technical fault with the aircraft. The departure was delayed by 9 hours. The destination was a coastal town Leila had visited before.

I am sending this on June 16, 2026, which is when I first notified you. Your adjuster assessed the loss at $401.40.

Thanks,
Leila

I had the Ma's Spicy Diced Chicken, and had to persuade the waitress to make it good and spicy. I also had the stir-fried eggplant and long beans because they were out of ong choy. The only thing I didn't care for was that both dishes were too similar in color and flavor, although individually each dish was really, really good. The chicken was extremely salty (probably from all the preserved black beans) and chewy without being stringy. And there were plenty of both fresh and dried hot peppers. Chewy chicken suited the dish far better than mystery soft meat or tender chunks of white meat ever would (ugh).

Next time I'll have a lamb dish, or a dried tofu dish, or chairman Mao's pork, or some other pork dish. There are lots of appealing offerings on the menu.

state: One of the last classics of the French New Wave. For direction, cineaste Jean Eustache drew from the simplicity of early-century cinema; for story, Eustache drew on the torments of his own complicated love life. So many things can be said of this film - observationally brilliant; self indulgently overlong; occasionally hilarious; emotionally draining...etc. etc. In my mind, whatever complaints that can be leveled against this film are easily overshadowed by its numerous strengths. Every film student, writer, or simply anyone willing to handle a 3 hour film with no abrupt cuts, no music video overstyling, no soap opera-like plot twists, and no banal dialogue should make it a point to see this movie. Everything is to be admired: the writing (concise, clever, surprisingly funny), acting (everyone, quite simply, is perfect in their respective roles), and, simple direction (the viewer feels like a casual observer within the film) make this film unforgettable. This is undoubtedly a film that stays with you.

## 1. Definitions

Issued by Bluewater Assurance
In this policy, "the Insurer" means Bluewater Assurance and "the Insured Person" means the person named in the schedule.

Article 1. Definitions
(a) Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
(b) Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
(c) Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows the Insured Person's details, the covers the Insured Person bought and any extensions.
(d) Sports equipment means skis, snowboards, golf clubs, surfboards and bicycles.
(e) Valuables means laptops, tablets, mobile phones, cameras, watches and jewellery.

Article 2. Limits and excess
(a) Baggage and Personal Belongings: limit $1,500 per incident; excess $75 per claim.
(b) Emergency Medical Expenses: limit $10,000 per incident; excess $250 per claim.
(c) Trip Cancellation: limit $2,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
(d) Travel Delay: limit $300 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
(e) Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the excess is then deducted from the result.

Article 3. Baggage and Personal Belongings
(a) The Insurer will pay for the loss of, theft of, or damage to the Insured Person's baggage and personal belongings during the trip.
(b) The most the Insurer will pay for Valuables under this section is $400 per incident.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Sports equipment under this section is $300 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for loss or theft of property left unattended in a vehicle or in a public place. This exclusion does not apply to property locked out of sight in the boot or trunk of a locked vehicle.
(e) The Insurer will not pay for loss caused by confiscation or detention by customs or other officials.
(f) The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by wear and tear or gradual deterioration.

Article 4. General exclusions
(a) The Insurer will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
(b) The Insurer will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Insured Person.

Article 5. Making a claim
(a) The Insured Person must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
(b) The Insured Person must notify the Insurer of a claim within 21 days of the incident. The Insurer will not pay any claim notified after that time.
(c) The Insurer may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

# Single-Trip Travel Protection Plan
Issued by Northstar Underwriting

## 1. Definitions
- **1.1** Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by us, before any excess, limit or sublimit is applied.
- **1.2** Family means your spouse or partner and any children who live with you.
- **1.3** Qualifying delay means a delay to the scheduled departure of more than 8 hours.
- **1.4** Travelling companion means a person who has booked to travel with you on the same trip.

## 2. Limits and excess
- **2.1** Baggage and Personal Belongings: limit $2,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
- **2.2** Emergency Medical Expenses: limit $25,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
- **2.3** Trip Cancellation: limit $2,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
- **2.4** Travel Delay: limit $750 per incident; excess $25 per claim.
- **2.5** The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

## 3. Optional cover: Travel Delay
- **3.1** We will pay reasonable costs of meals and accommodation if your outbound departure is delayed.
- **3.2** This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
- **3.3** We will not pay for any delay that is not a qualifying delay.

## 4. General exclusions
- **4.1** We will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
- **4.2** We will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by you.

## 5. Making a claim
- **5.1** You must notify us of a claim within 30 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.
- **5.2** You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
- **5.3** We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

## 6. Data protection
- **6.1** We will use the personal information you provide to administer this policy and to handle claims.
- **6.2** We will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
- **6.3** You can ask for a copy of the personal information we hold by writing to our data protection officer.

## 7. Claims documents
- **7.1** You must provide, at your own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence we reasonably ask for.
- **7.2** We may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

PART I: Definitions
I.1  Garden items means garden furniture, plants and outdoor tools.

II.1  Theft: limit $20,000 per incident; excess $250 per claim.
II.2  Escape of Water: limit $15,000 per incident; excess $1,000 per claim.
II.3  Accidental Damage: limit $5,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
II.4  Flood: limit $40,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.

III.1  The Insurer will pay for sudden and unexpected accidental damage to the Policyholder's contents inside the home.

III.5  The Insurer will not pay for wear and tear, or damage that happens gradually.

PART IV: Flood
IV.1  The Insurer will pay for contents damaged by flood water entering the Policyholder's home.
IV.2  No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 60 days after the policy start date.
IV.3  The most the Insurer will pay for Garden items under this section is $1,000 per incident.
IV.4  The Insurer will not pay for flood damage where a flood warning for the Policyholder's area had been issued before the policy started.

PART V: General exclusions
V.1  The Insurer will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Policyholder.
V.2  The Insurer will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
V.3  The Insurer will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.

PART VI: Making a claim
VI.1  The Insurer may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
VI.2  The Policyholder must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.

In this policy, "the Provider" means Tessera Warranty Company and "the Customer" means the person named in the schedule.

Article 1. Definitions
(a) Accessories means cases, chargers and earbuds.

(b) Breakdown: limit $1,500 per incident; service fee $49 per claim.
(c) Theft and Loss: limit $1,200 per incident; service fee $149 per claim.

Article 3. Notices
(a) Any notice the Provider gives under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address the Provider holds.
(b) Notices from the Customer should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

Article 4. Optional cover: Theft and Loss
(a) The Provider will replace the Customer's device if it is stolen or lost.
(b) This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Customer's schedule.
(c) The most the Provider will pay for Accessories under this section is $100 per incident.
(d) The Provider will not pay for loss or theft of property left unattended in a vehicle or in a public place. This exclusion does not apply to property locked out of sight in the boot or trunk of a locked vehicle.

Article 5. How to read this document
(a) This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.
(b) Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
(c) Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

Article 6. General exclusions
(a) The Provider will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Customer.
(b) The Provider will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.

Article 7. Making a claim
(a) The Provider may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
(b) The Customer must notify the Provider of a claim within 21 days of the incident. The Provider will not pay any claim notified after that time.

# Home Contents Insurance Policy
Issued by Oakfield Assurance

## 1. Definitions
- **1.1** Garden items means garden furniture, plants and outdoor tools.
- **1.2** Limit means the most we will pay for all claims under a section arising from one incident.
- **1.3** Outbuilding means a shed, garage or greenhouse within the boundaries of the home.

## 2. Limits and excess
- **2.1** Theft: limit $20,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
- **2.2** Escape of Water: limit $30,000 per incident; excess $1,000 per claim.
- **2.3** Accidental Damage: limit $3,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
- **2.4** Flood: limit $20,000 per incident; excess $1,000 per claim.
- **2.5** The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

## 3. Flood
- **3.1** We will pay for contents damaged by flood water entering your home.
- **3.2** No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 14 days after the policy start date.
- **3.3** The most we will pay for Garden items under this section is $500 per incident.
- **3.4** We will not pay for flood damage where a flood warning for your area had been issued before the policy started.

## 4. General exclusions
- **4.1** We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
- **4.2** We will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
- **4.3** We will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.

## 5. Making a claim
- **5.1** You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
- **5.2** You must notify us of a claim within 30 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.
- **5.3** We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

## 6. Subrogation
- **6.1** We will be entitled to take over and conduct in your name the defence or settlement of any claim.
- **6.2** We can take action in your name to recover any payment we make from anyone responsible for the loss.

## 7. Complaints
- **7.1** If you have a complaint, you should first contact our customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
- **7.2** We will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
- **7.3** If you remain dissatisfied, you may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

## 8. Renewal
- **8.1** We will write to you at least 21 days before the end of the policy period with the renewal terms.
- **8.2** We are not obliged to offer renewal.

## 9. Market conditions
- **9.1** If the replacement item is no longer available, we will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

## 10. Reasonable precautions
- **10.1** You must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
- **10.2** You must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

# Annual Multi-Trip Travel Cover
Issued by Bluewater Assurance

## 1. Definitions
- **1.1** Excursions and tickets means pre-booked excursions, tours, and event or theatre tickets.
- **1.2** Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
- **1.3** Qualifying delay means a delay to the scheduled departure of more than 6 hours.

## 2. Limits and excess
- **2.1** Baggage and Personal Belongings: limit $2,000 per incident; excess $75 per claim.
- **2.2** Emergency Medical Expenses: limit $10,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
- **2.3** Trip Cancellation: limit $3,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
- **2.4** Travel Delay: limit $300 per incident; excess $25 per claim.
- **2.5** The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

## 3. Change of address
- **3.1** You must tell us within 30 days if you change your address.
- **3.2** We may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

## 4. Waiver
- **4.1** If we do not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean we have given up the right to enforce it later.

## 5. Optional cover: Travel Delay
- **5.1** We will pay reasonable costs of meals and accommodation if your outbound departure is delayed.
- **5.2** This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
- **5.3** We will not pay for any delay that is not a qualifying delay.

## 6. Trip Cancellation
- **6.1** We will pay non-refundable travel and accommodation costs if you must cancel the trip for a reason beyond your control.
- **6.2** No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 14 days after the policy start date.
- **6.3** The most we will pay for Excursions and tickets under this section is $200 per incident.
- **6.4** We will not pay for cancellation caused by a strike or other event that had been publicly announced before you bought the policy.
- **6.5** We will not pay for cancellation because you no longer wish to travel.

## 7. Assignment
- **7.1** You cannot transfer your interest in this policy to anyone else without our written consent.

## 8. General exclusions
- **8.1** We will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
- **8.2** We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
- **8.3** We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.

## 9. Making a claim
- **9.1** You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
- **9.2** You must notify us of a claim within 30 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.
- **9.3** We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

## 1. Definitions
- **1.1** Bicycles means bicycles and electric scooters.
- **1.2** Contents means household goods and personal possessions that belong to you or your family.
- **1.3** High-risk items means jewellery, watches, laptops, games consoles and cameras.
- **1.4** Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in your schedule.
- **1.5** Portable electronics means laptops, tablets and mobile phones.
- **1.6** Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.
- **1.7** Unoccupied means not lived in by you or a member of your family for more than 30 consecutive days.

## 2. Limits and excess
- **2.1** Theft: limit $10,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
- **2.2** Escape of Water: limit $30,000 per incident; excess $1,000 per claim.
- **2.3** Accidental Damage: limit $5,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
- **2.4** Flood: limit $20,000 per incident; excess $1,000 per claim.
- **2.5** Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the excess is then deducted from the result.

## 3. Theft
- **3.1** We will pay for contents stolen from your home.
- **3.2** The most we will pay for High-risk items under this section is $2,500 per incident.
- **3.3** The most we will pay for Bicycles under this section is $800 per incident.
- **3.4** We will not pay for theft while the home is unoccupied.
- **3.5** We will not pay for theft where there is no sign of forced entry to the home. This exclusion does not apply where the thief gained entry by deception, for example by posing as a utility worker.
- **3.6** We will not pay for theft from sheds, garages or other outbuildings. This exclusion does not apply if the outbuilding was locked and the theft involved forcible entry.

state: As a lifelong fan of Dickens, I have invariably been disappointed by adaptations of his novels. Although his works presented an extremely accurate re-telling of human life at every level in Victorian Britain, throughout them all was a pervasive thread of humour that could be both playful or sarcastic as the narrative dictated. In a way, he was a literary caricaturist and cartoonist. He could be serious and hilarious in the same sentence. He pricked pride, lampooned arrogance, celebrated modesty, and empathised with loneliness and poverty. It may be a cliché, but he was a people's writer. And it is the comedy that is so often missing from his interpretations. At the time of writing, Oliver Twist is being dramatised in serial form on BBC television. All of the misery and cruelty is their, but non of the humour, irony, and savage lampoonery. The result is just a dark, dismal experience: the story penned by a journalist rather than a novelist. It's not really Dickens at all. 'Oliver!', on the other hand, is much closer to the mark. The mockery of officialdom is perfectly interpreted, from the blustering beadle to the drunken magistrate. PART I: Definitions
I.1  Art and antiques means paintings, antiques, rugs and other works of art.
I.2  Contents means household goods and personal possessions that belong to the Policyholder or the Policyholder's family.
I.3  Outbuilding means a shed, garage or greenhouse within the boundaries of the home.

PART II: Limits and excess
II.1  Theft: limit $10,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
II.2  Escape of Water: limit $30,000 per incident; excess $1,000 per claim.
II.3  Accidental Damage: limit $3,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
II.4  Flood: limit $40,000 per incident; excess $1,000 per claim.
II.5  The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

PART III: Optional cover: Accidental Damage
III.1  The Insurer will pay for sudden and unexpected accidental damage to the Policyholder's contents inside the home.
III.2  This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Policyholder's schedule.
III.3  The most the Insurer will pay for Portable electronics under this section is $750 per incident.
III.4  The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by pets.
III.5  The Insurer will not pay for wear and tear, or damage that happens gradually.

PART IV: Escape of Water
IV.1  The Insurer will pay for contents damaged by water escaping from a fixed pipe, tank or domestic appliance.
IV.2  The most the Insurer will pay for Art and antiques under this section is $2,000 per incident.
IV.3  The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by water leaking gradually over a period of time.
IV.4  The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by the failure of grout or sealant around baths and showers.

PART V: General exclusions
V.1  The Insurer will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
V.2  The Insurer will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits the Insurer from paying.
V.3  The Insurer will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.

PART VI: Making a claim
VI.1  The Policyholder must notify the Insurer of a claim within 14 days of the incident. The Insurer will not pay any claim notified after that time.

Article 1. Definitions
(a) Art and antiques means paintings, antiques, rugs and other works of art.
(b) Forcible entry means entry to the home that leaves visible damage to doors, windows or locks.
(c) Garden items means garden furniture, plants and outdoor tools.
(d) Limit means the most the Insurer will pay for all claims under a section arising from one incident.
(e) Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in the Policyholder's schedule.

Article 2. Limits and excess
(a) Theft: limit $40,000 per incident; excess $250 per claim.
(b) Escape of Water: limit $30,000 per incident; excess $250 per claim.
(c) Accidental Damage: limit $2,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
(d) Flood: limit $20,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
(e) Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the excess is then deducted from the result.

Article 3. Escape of Water
(a) The Insurer will pay for contents damaged by water escaping from a fixed pipe, tank or domestic appliance.
(b) The most the Insurer will pay for Art and antiques under this section is $1,000 per incident.
(c) The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by water leaking gradually over a period of time.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by the failure of grout or sealant around baths and showers.

Article 4. Flood
(a) The Insurer will pay for contents damaged by flood water entering the Policyholder's home.

(d) The Insurer will not pay for flood damage where a flood warning for the Policyholder's area had been issued before the policy started.

Article 5. General exclusions
(a) The Insurer will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Policyholder.
(b) The Insurer will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.

Article 6. Making a claim

## 1. Definitions
- **1.1** Frames means spectacle frames bought without new lenses.

# Staff Health Reimbursement Plan Rules

## 1. Definitions
- **1.1** Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by us, before any deductible, limit or sublimit is applied.
- **1.2** Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
- **1.3** Frames means spectacle frames bought without new lenses.
- **1.4** Hearing accessories means batteries, chargers and cleaning kits.
- **1.5** Hearing aid replacement period means 24 months from the purchase of hearing aids funded by the plan.
- **1.6** Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in your schedule.
- **1.7** Replacement period means 24 months from the date of your last eyewear claim.

## 2. Limits and deductible
- **2.1** Dental Care: limit $1,500 per treatment; deductible $100 per claim.
- **2.2** Vision Care: limit $500 per treatment; deductible $40 per claim.
- **2.3** Therapy Services: limit $2,000 per treatment; deductible $50 per claim.
- **2.4** Hearing Care: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $100 per claim.
- **2.5** Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the deductible is then deducted from the result.

## 3. Optional cover: Hearing Care
- **3.1** We will reimburse hearing tests and hearing aids.
- **3.2** This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
- **3.3** The most we will pay for Hearing accessories under this section is $100 per treatment.
- **3.4** We will not pay for replacement hearing aids bought within the hearing aid replacement period.

## 4. Vision Care
- **4.1** We will reimburse eye tests and prescription eyewear.
- **4.2** The most we will pay for Frames under this section is $120 per treatment.
- **4.3** We will not pay for eyewear without prescription lenses.
- **4.4** We will not pay for a further eyewear claim within the replacement period.

## 5. General exclusions
- **5.1** We will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
- **5.2** We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
- **5.3** We will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits us from paying.

## 6. Interest
- **6.1** We will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

## 7. Geographical limits
- **7.1** Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
- **7.2** Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

## 8. Making a claim
- **8.1** We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
- **8.2** You must notify us of a claim within 21 days of the treatment. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.
- **8.3** You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.

Issued by Meridian Travel Insurance Ltd
In this policy, "the Insurer" means Meridian Travel Insurance Ltd and "the Insured Person" means the person named in the schedule.

Article 1. Definitions
(a) Dental treatment means treatment of the teeth or gums.
(b) Family means the Insured Person's spouse or partner and any children who live with the Insured Person.
(c) Hazardous activity means skydiving, motor racing, or trekking or climbing above 4,500 metres.
(d) Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
(e) Physiotherapy means treatment of muscles and joints by a physiotherapist.
(f) Pre-existing condition means any illness or injury for which the Insured Person received treatment or advice in the 3 months before the policy start date.
(g) Sports equipment means skis, snowboards, golf clubs, surfboards and bicycles.
(h) Travelling companion means a person who has booked to travel with the Insured Person on the same trip.
(i) Valuables means laptops, tablets, mobile phones, cameras, watches and jewellery.

Article 2. Limits and excess
(a) Baggage and Personal Belongings: limit $1,500 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
(b) Emergency Medical Expenses: limit $50,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
(c) Trip Cancellation: limit $5,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
(d) Travel Delay: limit $300 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
(e) The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

Article 3. Baggage and Personal Belongings
(a) The Insurer will pay for the loss of, theft of, or damage to the Insured Person's baggage and personal belongings during the trip.
(b) The most the Insurer will pay for Valuables under this section is $250 per incident.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Sports equipment under this section is $450 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for loss or theft of property left unattended in a vehicle or in a public place. This exclusion does not apply to property locked out of sight in the boot or trunk of a locked vehicle.
(e) The Insurer will not pay for loss caused by confiscation or detention by customs or other officials.
(f) The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by wear and tear or gradual deterioration.

Article 4. Emergency Medical Expenses
(a) The Insurer will pay reasonable and necessary emergency medical costs incurred during the trip.
(b) The most the Insurer will pay for Dental treatment under this section is $250 per incident.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Physiotherapy under this section is $300 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for treatment of a pre-existing condition.
(e) The Insurer will not pay for injury or illness arising from a hazardous activity. This exclusion does not apply if the Adventure Sports extension is shown in the Insured Person's schedule.
(f) The Insurer will not pay for any claim arising from the Insured Person's being under the influence of alcohol or drugs.

Article 5. General exclusions
(a) The Insurer will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Insured Person.
(b) The Insurer will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.

Article 6. Making a claim
(a) The Insured Person must notify the Insurer of a claim within 21 days of the incident. The Insurer will not pay any claim notified after that time.
(b) The Insurer may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
(c) The Insured Person must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.

# Renters Contents Protection
Issued by Oakfield Assurance

## 1. Definitions
- **1.1** Art and antiques means paintings, antiques, rugs and other works of art.
- **1.2** Bicycles means bicycles and electric scooters.
- **1.3** Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
- **1.4** Family means your spouse or partner and any children who live with you.
- **1.5** High-risk items means jewellery, watches, laptops, games consoles and cameras.
- **1.6** Portable electronics means laptops, tablets and mobile phones.
- **1.7** Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows your details, the covers you bought and any extensions.
- **1.8** Unoccupied means not lived in by you or a member of your family for more than 60 consecutive days.

## 2. Limits and excess
- **2.1** Theft: limit $40,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
- **2.2** Escape of Water: limit $15,000 per incident; excess $250 per claim.
- **2.3** Accidental Damage: limit $2,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
- **2.4** Flood: limit $40,000 per incident; excess $1,000 per claim.
- **2.5** The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

## 3. Theft
- **3.1** We will pay for contents stolen from your home.
- **3.2** The most we will pay for High-risk items under this section is $1,000 per incident.
- **3.3** The most we will pay for Bicycles under this section is $500 per incident.
- **3.4** We will not pay for theft while the home is unoccupied.
- **3.5** We will not pay for theft where there is no sign of forced entry to the home. This exclusion does not apply where the thief gained entry by deception, for example by posing as a utility worker.
- **3.6** We will not pay for theft from sheds, garages or other outbuildings. This exclusion does not apply if the outbuilding was locked and the theft involved forcible entry.

## 4. Optional cover: Accidental Damage
- **4.1** We will pay for sudden and unexpected accidental damage to your contents inside the home.
- **4.2** This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
- **4.3** The most we will pay for Portable electronics under this section is $750 per incident.
- **4.4** We will not pay for damage caused by pets.
- **4.5** We will not pay for wear and tear, or damage that happens gradually.

## 5. Escape of Water
- **5.1** We will pay for contents damaged by water escaping from a fixed pipe, tank or domestic appliance.
- **5.2** The most we will pay for Art and antiques under this section is $2,000 per incident.
- **5.3** We will not pay for damage caused by water leaking gradually over a period of time.
- **5.4** We will not pay for damage caused by the failure of grout or sealant around baths and showers.

## 6. General exclusions
- **6.1** We will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits us from paying.
- **6.2** We will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by you.

## 7. Making a claim
- **7.1** You must notify us of a claim within 14 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.
- **7.2** We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
- **7.3** You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.

# Single-Trip Travel Protection Plan
Issued by Meridian Travel Insurance Ltd

## 1. Definitions
- **1.1** Excursions and tickets means pre-booked excursions, tours, and event or theatre tickets.
- **1.2** Qualifying delay means a delay to the scheduled departure of more than 12 hours.
- **1.3** Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
- **1.4** Territory means the countries in which cover applies, as shown in the schedule.

## 2. Limits and excess
- **2.1** Baggage and Personal Belongings: limit $1,500 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
- **2.2** Emergency Medical Expenses: limit $50,000 per incident; excess $250 per claim.
- **2.3** Trip Cancellation: limit $3,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
- **2.4** Travel Delay: limit $300 per incident; excess $25 per claim.
- **2.5** The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

## 3. Optional cover: Travel Delay
- **3.1** We will pay reasonable costs of meals and accommodation if your outbound departure is delayed.
- **3.2** This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
- **3.3** We will not pay for any delay that is not a qualifying delay.

## 4. Trip Cancellation
- **4.1** We will pay non-refundable travel and accommodation costs if you must cancel the trip for a reason beyond your control.
- **4.2** No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 14 days after the policy start date.
- **4.3** The most we will pay for Excursions and tickets under this section is $200 per incident.
- **4.4** We will not pay for cancellation caused by a strike or other event that had been publicly announced before you bought the policy.
- **4.5** We will not pay for cancellation because you no longer wish to travel.

## 5. General exclusions
- **5.1** We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
- **5.2** We will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by you.

## 6. Making a claim
- **6.1** You must notify us of a claim within 90 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.
- **6.2** You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
- **6.3** We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

## 7. Taxes
- **7.1** The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
- **7.2** If the tax rate changes, we may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

## 8. Emergency assistance
- **8.1** Our emergency assistance service is available 24 hours a day on the number shown in the schedule.
- **8.2** You must contact the assistance service before being admitted to hospital as an in-patient, unless it is an emergency.
- **8.3** The assistance service can arrange payment guarantees, interpreters and transport home.

# Electronics Care Plan
Issued by Brightline Device Cover

## 1. Definitions
- **1.1** Accessories means cases, chargers and earbuds.
- **1.2** Battery replacement means replacement batteries and battery repairs.
- **1.3** Manufacturer's warranty period means the first 24 months after the device was bought.
- **1.4** Replacement device means a device of the same or similar specification, which may be refurbished.

## 2. Limits and service fee
- **2.1** Accidental Damage: limit $1,200 per incident; service fee $49 per claim.
- **2.2** Breakdown: limit $1,500 per incident; service fee $25 per claim.
- **2.3** Theft and Loss: limit $1,200 per incident; service fee $149 per claim.
- **2.4** The service fee is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

## 3. Breakdown
- **3.1** We will repair or replace your device if it stops working because of an electrical or mechanical fault.
- **3.2** No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 30 days after the policy start date.
- **3.3** The most we will pay for Battery replacement under this section is $80 per incident.
- **3.4** We will not pay for breakdowns during the manufacturer's warranty period.
- **3.5** We will not pay for breakdown caused by liquid getting into the device.

## 4. Optional cover: Theft and Loss
- **4.1** We will replace your device if it is stolen or lost.
- **4.2** This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
- **4.3** The most we will pay for Accessories under this section is $100 per incident.
- **4.4** We will not pay for loss or theft of property left unattended in a vehicle or in a public place. This exclusion does not apply to property locked out of sight in the boot or trunk of a locked vehicle.
- **4.5** We will not pay for theft that was not reported to the police.

## 5. General exclusions
- **5.1** We will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
- **5.2** We will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits us from paying.

## 6. Making a claim
- **6.1** We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
- **6.2** You must notify us of a claim within 60 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.
- **6.3** You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
