# Employee Health Benefits Plan: Summary Plan Description
Issued by the Benefits Trust

## 1. Definitions
- **1.1** Hearing accessories means batteries, chargers and cleaning kits.
- **1.2** Hearing aid replacement period means 36 months from the purchase of hearing aids funded by the plan.
- **1.3** Plan year means the twelve months starting on your coverage start date.

## 2. Limits and deductible
- **2.1** Dental Care: limit $1,500 per treatment; deductible $50 per claim.
- **2.2** Vision Care: limit $500 per treatment; deductible $25 per claim.
- **2.3** Therapy Services: limit $1,500 per treatment; deductible $50 per claim.
- **2.4** Hearing Care: limit $2,000 per treatment; deductible $100 per claim.
- **2.5** The deductible is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

## 3. Customer support
- **3.1** Our helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
- **3.2** Outside these hours you can leave a message and we will call back on the next working day.

## 4. Fraud
- **4.1** If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, we will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
- **4.2** We may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

## 5. Wellness allowance
- **5.1** Each plan year you may claim up to $250 towards a gym membership or fitness class.
- **5.2** The wellness allowance is not subject to any deductible and does not count towards other limits.

## 6. Exchange of information
- **6.1** To prevent fraud, we may check the details you give against public records and industry databases.
- **6.2** We may contact previous insurers to confirm your claims history.

## 7. Instalment agreements
- **7.1** If you pay by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
- **7.2** Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

## 8. Optional cover: Hearing Care

- **8.2** This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
- **8.3** The most we will pay for Hearing accessories under this section is $100 per treatment.
- **8.4** We will not pay for replacement hearing aids bought within the hearing aid replacement period.

## 9. General exclusions
- **9.1** We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.

## 1. Definitions

My roommate and I came later in the evening, and there was no wait to be seated. The margaritas were on special for happy hour, and even though it was only lime & rocks for the special, I got one and was pleasantly surprised. The chips and salsa were really good--the salsa was thick but not chunky--the kind I love, and the chips were crisp but not oily how they can sometimes be at restaurants.

For our free appetizer we got queso con carne. I just thought it was so-so. It tasted too much like ground beef--I guess I was expecting something that tasted more like cheesy chili. Oh well, it was free.

I got the chimichangas for my entree, and I thought they were good, nothing special, but good. I really liked the rice and beans on the side though.

Since I only live a few blocks away, I'll probably be back.

state: An acoustic-electric guitar (also called an electro-acoustic guitar) is an acoustic guitar fitted with a magnetic pickup, a piezoelectric pickup or a microphone. In electric-acoustic nylon string guitars, piezoelectric pickups and microphones are always used because magnetic pickups are not capable of picking up vibrations of non-magnetic materials. The design is distinct from a semi-acoustic guitar, which is an electric guitar but with the addition of sound chambers within the guitar body. Usually, acoustic-electric guitars are fitted with piezoelectric pickups, and hence require a preamplifier incorporated into the guitar body to amplify the signal before it travels to the main guitar amplifier. These preamps may also come with tone controls of varying types, but usually equalizers with up to six frequency bands are used. They are also referred to as a ``plug-in acoustic guitar'', due to their ability to simply ``plug in'' to a speaker system without the need for microphones.

policy: ELECTRONICS CARE PLAN
Issued by Tessera Warranty Company
In this policy, "the Provider" means Tessera Warranty Company and "the Customer" means the person named in the schedule.

Article 1. Definitions
(a) Accessories means cases, chargers and earbuds.
(b) Battery replacement means replacement batteries and battery repairs.
(c) Breakdown means the failure of a part to work as the manufacturer intended, from an internal electrical or mechanical fault.
(d) Manufacturer's warranty period means the first 24 months after the device was bought.
(e) Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.

Article 2. Limits and service fee
(a) Accidental Damage: limit $800 per incident; service fee $79 per claim.
(b) Breakdown: limit $600 per incident; service fee $25 per claim.
(c) Theft and Loss: limit $1,200 per incident; service fee $149 per claim.
(d) Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the service fee is then deducted from the result.

Article 3. Breakdown
(a) The Provider will repair or replace the Customer's device if it stops working because of an electrical or mechanical fault.
(b) No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 30 days after the policy start date.
(c) The most the Provider will pay for Battery replacement under this section is $120 per incident.
(d) The Provider will not pay for breakdowns during the manufacturer's warranty period.
(e) The Provider will not pay for breakdown caused by liquid getting into the device.

Article 4. Optional cover: Theft and Loss
(a) The Provider will replace the Customer's device if it is stolen or lost.
(b) This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Customer's schedule.
(c) The most the Provider will pay for Accessories under this section is $50 per incident.
(d) The Provider will not pay for loss or theft of property left unattended in a vehicle or in a public place. This exclusion does not apply to property locked out of sight in the boot or trunk of a locked vehicle.
(e) The Provider will not pay for theft that was not reported to the police.

Article 5. General exclusions
(a) The Provider will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Customer.
(b) The Provider will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.

Article 6. Making a claim
(a) The Provider may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
(b) The Customer must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
(c) The Customer must notify the Provider of a claim within 14 days of the incident. The Provider will not pay any claim notified after that time.

Article 7. Compensation scheme
(a) The Provider is covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
(b) If the Provider cannot meet the Provider's obligations, the Customer may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

Article 8. Salvage
(a) When the Provider replaces an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes the Provider's property.
(b) If stolen property is recovered after the Provider has paid a claim, the Customer must tell the Provider and either return the payment or give the Provider the property.

SECTION 1 - DEFINITIONS
1.1 Accessories means cases, chargers, earbuds and styluses.

SECTION 3 - ACCIDENTAL DAMAGE
3.1 We will repair or replace your device if it is accidentally damaged.
3.2 The most we will pay for Accessories under this section is $50 per incident.
3.3 The most we will pay for Wearables under this section is $250 per incident.
3.4 We will not pay for cosmetic damage, such as scratches or dents, that does not affect how the device works.
3.5 We will not pay for damage following a repair by anyone other than us or an authorised repairer. This exclusion does not apply if we approved the repair in writing beforehand.

SECTION 4 - GENERAL EXCLUSIONS
4.1 We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
4.2 We will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.

5.1 You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.

SECTION 8 - INSTALMENT AGREEMENTS

policy: ANNUAL MULTI-TRIP TRAVEL COVER
Issued by Bluewater Assurance
In this policy, "the Insurer" means Bluewater Assurance and "the Insured Person" means the person named in the schedule.

Article 1. Definitions
(a) Excursions and tickets means pre-booked excursions, tours, and event or theatre tickets.
(b) Qualifying delay means a delay to the scheduled departure of more than 8 hours.
(c) Sports equipment means skis, snowboards, golf clubs, surfboards and bicycles.
(d) Trip means a journey that starts and ends in the Insured Person's home country during the policy period.
(e) Valuables means laptops, tablets, mobile phones, cameras, watches and jewellery.

Article 2. Limits and excess
(a) Baggage and Personal Belongings: limit $2,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
(b) Emergency Medical Expenses: limit $50,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
(c) Trip Cancellation: limit $3,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
(d) Travel Delay: limit $750 per incident; excess $25 per claim.
(e) The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

Article 3. Optional cover: Travel Delay
(a) The Insurer will pay reasonable costs of meals and accommodation if the Insured Person's outbound departure is delayed.
(b) This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Insured Person's schedule.
(c) The Insurer will not pay for any delay that is not a qualifying delay.

Article 4. Trip Cancellation
(a) The Insurer will pay non-refundable travel and accommodation costs if the Insured Person must cancel the trip for a reason beyond the Insured Person's control.
(b) No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 10 days after the policy start date.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Excursions and tickets under this section is $200 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for cancellation caused by a strike or other event that had been publicly announced before the Insured Person bought the policy.
(e) The Insurer will not pay for cancellation because the Insured Person no longer wish to travel.

Article 5. Baggage and Personal Belongings
(a) The Insurer will pay for the loss of, theft of, or damage to the Insured Person's baggage and personal belongings during the trip.
(b) The most the Insurer will pay for Valuables under this section is $400 per incident.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Sports equipment under this section is $300 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for loss or theft of property left unattended in a vehicle or in a public place. This exclusion does not apply to property locked out of sight in the boot or trunk of a locked vehicle.
(e) The Insurer will not pay for loss caused by confiscation or detention by customs or other officials.
(f) The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by wear and tear or gradual deterioration.

Article 6. General exclusions
(a) The Insurer will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
(b) The Insurer will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Insured Person.

Article 7. Making a claim
(a) The Insured Person must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
(b) The Insured Person must notify the Insurer of a claim within 90 days of the incident. The Insurer will not pay any claim notified after that time.
(c) The Insurer may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

state: Spacecamp is my favorite movie. It is a great story and also inspires others. The acting was excellent and my wife and I went to see Lea Thompson in Cabaret years later due to her performance in the movie. It is unfortunate that the Challenger Accident delayed and hurt the movie. The 20th Anniversary of the Challenger Accident is coming up. I knew one of the Challenger Astronauts off and on since childhood on the Carnegie Mellon campus where my father went to school; I also know a close friend of the late pilot. I was the technical review last year for National BSA for the Boy Scout Astronomy Merit Badge and I still find Spacecamp a great movie to recommend to Scouts doing the Space related merit badges I teach. I ran into the late astronaut again as an adult and was following a schedule of engineering education we had put together when Challenger blew up. I wound up sitting in with Willard Rockwell and his engineers,"invisible", going over things after the Accident at the Astrotech stockholders meeting by chance as a result, so I'm much closer to the Accident and any movie similarities. I made sure that I was a good student and finished the degree four years later, strangely enough, on the recommendation of the Rockwell engineer

- **1.2** Breakdown means the failure of a part to work as the manufacturer intended, from an internal electrical or mechanical fault.
- **1.3** Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
- **1.4** Premium means the amount you must pay for this policy, including any taxes.

## 2. Limits and service fee
- **2.1** Accidental Damage: limit $800 per incident; service fee $79 per claim.
- **2.2** Breakdown: limit $600 per incident; service fee $49 per claim.
- **2.3** Theft and Loss: limit $1,200 per incident; service fee $149 per claim.

## 3. Optional cover: Theft and Loss
- **3.1** We will replace your device if it is stolen or lost.
- **3.2** This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
- **3.3** The most we will pay for Accessories under this section is $50 per incident.
- **3.4** We will not pay for loss or theft of property left unattended in a vehicle or in a public place. This exclusion does not apply to property locked out of sight in the boot or trunk of a locked vehicle.
- **3.5** We will not pay for theft that was not reported to the police.

## 4. General exclusions
- **4.1** We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
- **4.2** We will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits us from paying.

## 5. Renewal
- **5.1** We will write to you at least 21 days before the end of the policy period with the renewal terms.
- **5.2** We are not obliged to offer renewal.

## 6. Taxes
- **6.1** The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
- **6.2** If the tax rate changes, we may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

## 7. Changes in circumstances
- **7.1** You must tell us as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
- **7.2** We may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

## 8. Claims documents
- **8.1** You must provide, at your own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence we reasonably ask for.
- **8.2** We may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

## 9. Making a claim
- **9.1** You must notify us of a claim within 21 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.
- **9.2** You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
- **9.3** We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

## 10. Geographical limits
- **10.1** Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
- **10.2** Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

## 11. Software support
- **11.1** Our helpline can give advice on setting up and using your device.
- **11.2** Software support does not include fixing problems caused by third-party apps or unofficial operating systems.

## 12. Recovery of costs
- **12.1** If we pay a claim that is later found not to be covered, we may ask you to repay the amount.

Meskerem is to Red Sea as Harris Teeter is to Food Lion. 

As in, less atmosphere, spottier service, but good deals and (in some cases) surprisingly good food. 

A complaint I often hear about Ethiopian is that it all tastes the same - whether that's actually true (I don't think so) or it's a result of our western minds being so used to each separate dish having, well, it's own, separate dish, that when it's all piled onto a delicious piece of Injera, the way we experience flavor shifts is a mystery to me. At Red Sea, there is no mistaking Wat for Alicha - the flavors in each dish (even just stewed lentils) are distinct. Some things are sweet - others salty. And there's none of this "spice level" stuff - you get the full range, when ordering a combo (at 10.99, veggie combo is a steal).

Dings - nuked Sambusas. Service was both good (presence, smiles) and cranky (unhappiness about splitting a bill 3 ways, each portion on a card). Warm, as in tired A/C. But really good, thoughtfully prepared food. Lovely.

Article 1. Definitions
(a) Accessories means cases, chargers, earbuds and styluses.

(d) Manufacturer's warranty period means the first 24 months after the device was bought.
(e) Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in the Customer's schedule.
(f) Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
(g) Wearables means smartwatches and fitness trackers.

Article 2. Limits and service fee
(a) Accidental Damage: limit $1,200 per incident; service fee $79 per claim.
(b) Breakdown: limit $600 per incident; service fee $49 per claim.
(c) Theft and Loss: limit $1,200 per incident; service fee $149 per claim.
(d) The service fee is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

Article 3. Breakdown
(a) The Provider will repair or replace the Customer's device if it stops working because of an electrical or mechanical fault.
(b) No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 45 days after the policy start date.
(c) The most the Provider will pay for Battery replacement under this section is $80 per incident.
(d) The Provider will not pay for breakdowns during the manufacturer's warranty period.
(e) The Provider will not pay for breakdown caused by liquid getting into the device.

Article 4. Accidental Damage
(a) The Provider will repair or replace the Customer's device if it is accidentally damaged.
(b) The most the Provider will pay for Accessories under this section is $50 per incident.
(c) The most the Provider will pay for Wearables under this section is $250 per incident.
(d) The Provider will not pay for cosmetic damage, such as scratches or dents, that does not affect how the device works.
(e) The Provider will not pay for damage following a repair by anyone other than the Provider or an authorised repairer. This exclusion does not apply if the Provider approved the repair in writing beforehand.

Article 5. General exclusions
(a) The Provider will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
(b) The Provider will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
(c) The Provider will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Customer.

Article 6. Making a claim
(a) The Provider may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
(b) The Customer must notify the Provider of a claim within 14 days of the incident. The Provider will not pay any claim notified after that time.
(c) The Customer must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.

state: Medellin is a fabulous place to live, work, and study. I've been there twice, and never did I hear anything about guerrilla activities, paramilitaries taking tourists hostage, or anything of the sort. There are "invisible police," but it is *not* a Big Brother system. There are just enough police so that they are visible in everyday life, but they do not hassle someone without good reasons. La Sierra is an interesting documentary in that the youths it depicts in the movie essentially become its characters. The directors of the movie carefully carve out plot lines among the daily actions of the inhabitants of La Sierra, and when a "character" dies, there is genuine pathos. It is difficult to imagine, however, that the three youths are all members of the Bloque Metro, a gang that used to terrorize La Sierra before the Colombian government began to restructure the country. La Sierra is not an accurate depiction of life in Colombia; there are, of course, things to be wary of such as petty crime, but when one considers pickpocketing happens in "modern" cities such as London, New York, or Tokyo, Colombia doesn't seem that different after all. Colombians are eagerly awaiting their chance to show to the world that the once war-torn country is now prospering more than ever.

state: document: Solifugae is an order of animals in the class Arachnida known variously as camel spiders, wind scorpions, sun spiders, or solifuges. The order includes more than 1,000 described species in about 153 genera. Despite the common names, they are neither true scorpions (order Scorpiones) nor true spiders (order Araneae). Much like a spider, the body of a solifugid has two tagmata: an opisthosoma (abdomen) behind the prosoma (that is, in effect, a combined head and thorax). At the front end, the prosoma bears two chelicerae that, in most species, are conspicuously large. The chelicerae serve as jaws and in many species also are used for stridulation. Unlike scorpions, solifugids do not have a third tagma that forms a ``tail''. Most species of Solifugae live in dry climates and feed opportunistically on ground-dwelling arthropods and other small animals. The largest species grow to a length of 12--15 cm (5--6 in), including legs. A number of urban legends exaggerate the size and speed of the Solifugae, and their potential danger to humans, which is negligible.

policy: EMPLOYEE HEALTH BENEFITS PLAN: SUMMARY PLAN DESCRIPTION
Issued by Cedar Benefits Services
In this policy, "the Plan" means Cedar Benefits Services and "the Member" means the person named in the schedule.

Article 1. Definitions
(a) Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
(b) Hearing accessories means batteries, chargers and cleaning kits.
(c) Hearing aid replacement period means 24 months from the purchase of hearing aids funded by the plan.
(d) Major restorative work means crowns, bridges, root canal treatment and implants.
(e) Massage therapy means sports massage, massage therapy and reflexology.
(f) Orthodontics means braces and clear aligners.
(g) Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.

Article 2. Limits and deductible
(a) Dental Care: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $100 per claim.
(b) Vision Care: limit $500 per treatment; deductible $25 per claim.
(c) Therapy Services: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $50 per claim.
(d) Hearing Care: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $100 per claim.
(e) The deductible is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

Article 3. Therapy Services
(a) The Plan will reimburse physiotherapy, osteopathy and counselling provided by a registered practitioner.
(b) The most the Plan will pay for Massage therapy under this section is $300 per treatment.
(c) The Plan will not pay for treatment of an injury covered by workers' compensation.
(d) The Plan will not pay for treatment by a practitioner who is not registered with the relevant professional body.

Article 4. Dental Care
(a) The Plan will reimburse the cost of dental treatment provided by a licensed dentist.
(b) No cover applies under this section to any treatment that happens within the first 90 days after the policy start date.
(c) The most the Plan will pay for Major restorative work under this section is $500 per treatment.
(d) The most the Plan will pay for Orthodontics under this section is $600 per treatment.
(e) The Plan will not pay for treatment that is mainly cosmetic, such as whitening or veneers. This exclusion does not apply to treatment needed to repair damage caused by an accident.
(f) The Plan will not pay for treatment by a provider outside the plan's network. This exclusion does not apply to emergency treatment for sudden severe pain.

Article 5. Optional cover: Hearing Care
(a) The Plan will reimburse hearing tests and hearing aids.
(b) This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Member's schedule.
(c) The most the Plan will pay for Hearing accessories under this section is $100 per treatment.
(d) The Plan will not pay for replacement hearing aids bought within the hearing aid replacement period.

Article 6. General exclusions
(a) The Plan will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
(b) The Plan will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Member.
(c) The Plan will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits the Plan from paying.

Article 7. Making a claim
(a) The Member must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
(b) The Member must notify the Plan of a claim within 90 days of the treatment. The Plan will not pay any claim notified after that time.
(c) The Plan may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

# Electronics Care Plan
Issued by Voltguard Protection Ltd

## 1. Definitions
- **1.1** Accessories means cases, chargers, earbuds and styluses.
- **1.2** Accessories means cases, chargers and earbuds.
- **1.3** Breakdown means the failure of a part to work as the manufacturer intended, from an internal electrical or mechanical fault.
- **1.4** Replacement device means a device of the same or similar specification, which may be refurbished.
- **1.5** Wearables means smartwatches and fitness trackers.

## 2. Limits and service fee
- **2.1** Accidental Damage: limit $1,500 per incident; service fee $99 per claim.
- **2.2** Breakdown: limit $600 per incident; service fee $25 per claim.
- **2.3** Theft and Loss: limit $800 per incident; service fee $99 per claim.
- **2.4** The service fee is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

## 3. Accidental Damage
- **3.1** We will repair or replace your device if it is accidentally damaged.
- **3.2** The most we will pay for Accessories under this section is $100 per incident.
- **3.3** The most we will pay for Wearables under this section is $300 per incident.
- **3.4** We will not pay for cosmetic damage, such as scratches or dents, that does not affect how the device works.
- **3.5** We will not pay for damage following a repair by anyone other than us or an authorised repairer. This exclusion does not apply if we approved the repair in writing beforehand.

## 4. Optional cover: Theft and Loss
- **4.1** We will replace your device if it is stolen or lost.
- **4.2** This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
- **4.3** The most we will pay for Accessories under this section is $50 per incident.
- **4.4** We will not pay for loss or theft of property left unattended in a vehicle or in a public place. This exclusion does not apply to property locked out of sight in the boot or trunk of a locked vehicle.
- **4.5** We will not pay for theft that was not reported to the police.

## 5. General exclusions
- **5.1** We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
- **5.2** We will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits us from paying.
- **5.3** We will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by you.

## 6. Making a claim
- **6.1** You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
- **6.2** You must notify us of a claim within 90 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.
- **6.3** We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

SECTION 4 - GENERAL EXCLUSIONS
4.1 We will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.

7.1 If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, we will pay only our proportionate share.

policy: ANNUAL MULTI-TRIP TRAVEL COVER
Issued by Northstar Underwriting
In this policy, "the Insurer" means Northstar Underwriting and "the Insured Person" means the person named in the schedule.

Article 1. Definitions
(a) Excursions and tickets means pre-booked excursions, tours, and event or theatre tickets.
(b) Public transport means any scheduled train, bus, coach, ferry or aircraft.
(c) Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows the Insured Person's details, the covers the Insured Person bought and any extensions.
(d) Travelling companion means a person who has booked to travel with the Insured Person on the same trip.

Article 2. Limits and excess
(a) Baggage and Personal Belongings: limit $1,500 per incident; excess $75 per claim.
(b) Emergency Medical Expenses: limit $10,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
(c) Trip Cancellation: limit $2,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
(d) Travel Delay: limit $500 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
(e) Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the excess is then deducted from the result.

Article 3. Trip Cancellation
(a) The Insurer will pay non-refundable travel and accommodation costs if the Insured Person must cancel the trip for a reason beyond the Insured Person's control.
(b) No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 14 days after the policy start date.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Excursions and tickets under this section is $200 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for cancellation caused by a strike or other event that had been publicly announced before the Insured Person bought the policy.
(e) The Insurer will not pay for cancellation because the Insured Person no longer wish to travel.

Article 4. General exclusions
(a) The Insurer will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
(b) The Insurer will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.

Article 5. Complaints
(a) If the Insured Person has a complaint, the Insured Person should first contact the Insurer's customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
(b) The Insurer will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
(c) If the Insured Person remains dissatisfied, the Insured Person may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

Article 6. Making a claim
(a) The Insurer may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
(b) The Insured Person must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
(c) The Insured Person must notify the Insurer of a claim within 14 days of the incident. The Insurer will not pay any claim notified after that time.

Article 7. Communication
(a) The Insurer will communicate with the Insured Person in English.
(b) The Insurer may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

Article 8. Legal expenses abroad
(a) The Insurer will pay legal costs to pursue compensation for the Insured Person's injury or death caused by a third party during the trip.
(b) The Insurer will not pay legal costs unless the Insurer's legal adviser agrees that the claim has a reasonable prospect of success.

Article 9. Exchange of information
(a) To prevent fraud, the Insurer may check the details the Insured Person gives against public records and industry databases.
(b) The Insurer may contact previous insurers to confirm the Insured Person's claims history.

Article 10. Payment of claims
(a) The Insurer will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in the Insured Person's name.
(b) The Insurer aims to pay accepted claims within 10 working days of receiving all the documents the Insurer needs.

Article 11. Change of address
(a) The Insured Person must tell the Insurer within 30 days if the Insured Person changes the Insured Person's address.
(b) The Insurer may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

Article 12. Contracts (Rights of Third Parties)
(a) A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

state: document: I don't hand out ten star ratings easily. A movie really has to impress me, and The Bourne Ultimatum has gone far beyond that. Though all three films could not be any more different from the Ludlum novels, they still stand as a powerful landmark in cinematic achievement. The Bourne Ultimatum made me want to cry that the series was complete, yet I could not even attempt to stop smiling for hours. From the moment that the opening title appeared, I knew we were in for a ride. Paul Greengrass has done it again. Everything we love from the previous Bourne films is here once again: the action, the dialogue, and of course the shaky camera. However for me, that last one was never a problem. I think it adds to the suspense. I will be back to see this film several times before it is released on DVD, simply because it is genius. policy: ANNUAL MULTI-TRIP TRAVEL COVER
Issued by Northstar Underwriting
In this policy, "the Insurer" means Northstar Underwriting and "the Insured Person" means the person named in the schedule.

Article 1. Definitions
(a) Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
(b) Excursions and tickets means pre-booked excursions, tours, and event or theatre tickets.
(c) Qualifying delay means a delay to the scheduled departure of more than 8 hours.
(d) Travelling companion means a person who has booked to travel with the Insured Person on the same trip.

Article 2. Limits and excess
(a) Baggage and Personal Belongings: limit $2,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
(b) Emergency Medical Expenses: limit $50,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
(c) Trip Cancellation: limit $3,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
(d) Travel Delay: limit $500 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
(e) Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the excess is then deducted from the result.

Article 3. Trip Cancellation
(a) The Insurer will pay non-refundable travel and accommodation costs if the Insured Person must cancel the trip for a reason beyond the Insured Person's control.
(b) No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 10 days after the policy start date.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Excursions and tickets under this section is $300 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for cancellation caused by a strike or other event that had been publicly announced before the Insured Person bought the policy.
(e) The Insurer will not pay for cancellation because the Insured Person no longer wish to travel.

Article 4. Optional cover: Travel Delay
(a) The Insurer will pay reasonable costs of meals and accommodation if the Insured Person's outbound departure is delayed.
(b) This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Insured Person's schedule.
(c) The Insurer will not pay for any delay that is not a qualifying delay.

Article 5. General exclusions
(a) The Insurer will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
(b) The Insurer will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Insured Person.

Article 6. Making a claim
(a) The Insurer may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
(b) The Insured Person must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
(c) The Insured Person must notify the Insurer of a claim within 21 days of the incident. The Insurer will not pay any claim notified after that time.

(c) Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in the Insured Person's schedule.
(d) Sports equipment means skis, snowboards, golf clubs, surfboards and bicycles.
(e) Valuables means laptops, tablets, mobile phones, cameras, watches and jewellery.

Article 2. Limits and excess
(a) Baggage and Personal Belongings: limit $3,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
(b) Emergency Medical Expenses: limit $10,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
(c) Trip Cancellation: limit $2,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
(d) Travel Delay: limit $750 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
(e) The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

Article 3. Baggage and Personal Belongings
(a) The Insurer will pay for the loss of, theft of, or damage to the Insured Person's baggage and personal belongings during the trip.
(b) The most the Insurer will pay for Valuables under this section is $500 per incident.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Sports equipment under this section is $450 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for loss or theft of property left unattended in a vehicle or in a public place. This exclusion does not apply to property locked out of sight in the boot or trunk of a locked vehicle.
(e) The Insurer will not pay for loss caused by confiscation or detention by customs or other officials.
(f) The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by wear and tear or gradual deterioration.

Article 4. Trip Cancellation
(a) The Insurer will pay non-refundable travel and accommodation costs if the Insured Person must cancel the trip for a reason beyond the Insured Person's control.
(b) No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 10 days after the policy start date.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Excursions and tickets under this section is $300 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for cancellation caused by a strike or other event that had been publicly announced before the Insured Person bought the policy.
(e) The Insurer will not pay for cancellation because the Insured Person no longer wish to travel.

Article 5. General exclusions
(a) The Insurer will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Insured Person.
(b) The Insurer will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits the Insurer from paying.

Article 6. Making a claim
(a) The Insured Person must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
(b) The Insurer may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
(c) The Insured Person must notify the Insurer of a claim within 21 days of the incident. The Insurer will not pay any claim notified after that time.

state: When synthesizing new DNA, DNA polymerase can add free nucleotides only to the 3' end of the newly forming strand. This results in elongation of the newly forming strand in a 5'--3' direction. No known DNA polymerase is able to begin a new chain (de novo); it can only add a nucleotide onto a pre-existing 3'-OH group, and therefore needs a primer at which it can add the first nucleotide. Primers consist of RNA or DNA bases (or both). In DNA replication, the first two bases are always RNA, and are synthesized by another enzyme called primase. Helicase and topoisomerase II are required to unwind DNA from a double-strand structure to a single-strand structure to facilitate replication of each strand consistent with the semiconservative model of DNA replication.

policy: DEVICE PROTECTION PLAN TERMS
Issued by Circuit Care Services
In this policy, "the Provider" means Circuit Care Services and "the Customer" means the person named in the schedule.

Article 1. Definitions
(a) Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by the Provider, before any service fee, limit or sublimit is applied.
(b) Battery replacement means replacement batteries and battery repairs.
(c) Family means the Customer's spouse or partner and any children who live with the Customer.
(d) Manufacturer's warranty period means the first 12 months after the device was bought.
(e) Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.

Article 2. Limits and service fee
(a) Accidental Damage: limit $800 per incident; service fee $79 per claim.
(b) Breakdown: limit $1,500 per incident; service fee $25 per claim.
(c) Theft and Loss: limit $800 per incident; service fee $149 per claim.
(d) Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the service fee is then deducted from the result.

Article 3. Exchange of information
(a) To prevent fraud, the Provider may check the details the Customer gives against public records and industry databases.
(b) The Provider may contact previous insurers to confirm the Customer's claims history.

Article 4. Breakdown
(a) The Provider will repair or replace the Customer's device if it stops working because of an electrical or mechanical fault.
(b) No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 45 days after the policy start date.
(c) The most the Provider will pay for Battery replacement under this section is $80 per incident.
(d) The Provider will not pay for breakdowns during the manufacturer's warranty period.
(e) The Provider will not pay for breakdown caused by liquid getting into the device.

Article 5. Payment of claims
(a) The Provider will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in the Customer's name.
(b) The Provider aims to pay accepted claims within 5 working days of receiving all the documents the Provider needs.

Article 6. Electronic documents
(a) The Provider will send documents by email unless the Customer asks for paper copies.
(b) The Customer must tell the Provider if the Customer's email address changes.
(c) Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

Article 7. General exclusions
(a) The Provider will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
(b) The Provider will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
(c) The Provider will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits the Provider from paying.

Article 8. Making a claim
(a) The Customer must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
(b) The Provider may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
(c) The Customer must notify the Provider of a claim within 30 days of the incident. The Provider will not pay any claim notified after that time.

Article 9. Assignment
(a) The Customer cannot transfer the Customer's interest in this policy to anyone else without the Provider's written consent.

Article 10. Software support
(a) The Provider's helpline can give advice on setting up and using the Customer's device.
(b) Software support does not include fixing problems caused by third-party apps or unofficial operating systems.

Article 11. Cooperation
(a) The Customer must give the Provider all the help and information the Provider reasonably need to settle a claim.
(b) The Customer must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without the Provider's written permission.

I'm not a fan of milkshakes but there's a good range offered including beers and the usual soda drinks.

state: Anyone who has watched Comedy Central around midnight in the past few years has probably seen ads for this movie. I first saw ads for this movie back in 2001. It looked like it could be funny, but I wasn't about to call up the number on the television screen and order it without seeing the movie first. I figured I would wait until the movie was available to rent at Blockbuster. About a year and a half later, I was at Tower Records and in the "DVDS for less than $20" pile, there was a copy of this movie. Seeing that the DVD was only $6.99 I decided to buy it. I got home, put the disc in the DVD player, and waited for the laughs to start...and I waited some more. The laughs never came. I'd have to agree with almost every other comment on this page when I say that this movie was horrible. Sick, desperately tasteless, and poorly written and directed, THE UNDERGROUND COMEDY MOVIE is an atrocious piece of garbage and is in my opinion the worst movie of all time. No stars.

policy: ANNUAL MULTI-TRIP TRAVEL COVER
Issued by Compass Mutual
In this policy, "the Insurer" means Compass Mutual and "the Insured Person" means the person named in the schedule.

Article 1. Definitions
(a) Excursions and tickets means pre-booked excursions, tours, and event or theatre tickets.
(b) Family means the Insured Person's spouse or partner and any children who live with the Insured Person.
(c) Qualifying delay means a delay to the scheduled departure of more than 12 hours.
(d) Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows the Insured Person's details, the covers the Insured Person bought and any extensions.
(e) Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.

Article 2. Limits and excess
(a) Baggage and Personal Belongings: limit $1,500 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
(b) Emergency Medical Expenses: limit $10,000 per incident; excess $250 per claim.
(c) Trip Cancellation: limit $2,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
(d) Travel Delay: limit $750 per incident; excess $25 per claim.
(e) Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the excess is then deducted from the result.

Article 3. Optional cover: Travel Delay
(a) The Insurer will pay reasonable costs of meals and accommodation if the Insured Person's outbound departure is delayed.
(b) This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Insured Person's schedule.
(c) The Insurer will not pay for any delay that is not a qualifying delay.

Article 4. Trip Cancellation
(a) The Insurer will pay non-refundable travel and accommodation costs if the Insured Person must cancel the trip for a reason beyond the Insured Person's control.
(b) No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 10 days after the policy start date.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Excursions and tickets under this section is $300 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for cancellation caused by a strike or other event that had been publicly announced before the Insured Person bought the policy.
(e) The Insurer will not pay for cancellation because the Insured Person no longer wish to travel.

Article 5. General exclusions
(a) The Insurer will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Insured Person.
(b) The Insurer will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
(c) The Insurer will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.

Article 6. Making a claim
(a) The Insured Person must notify the Insurer of a claim within 60 days of the incident. The Insurer will not pay any claim notified after that time.
(b) The Insured Person must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
(c) The Insurer may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

Article 7. Interpretation
(a) Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
(b) Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
(c) Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

Article 8. Exchange of information
(a) To prevent fraud, the Insurer may check the details the Insured Person gives against public records and industry databases.
(b) The Insurer may contact previous insurers to confirm the Insured Person's claims history.

Issued by the Benefits Trust

PART I: Definitions
I.1  Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by the Plan, before any deductible, limit or sublimit is applied.
I.2  Frames means spectacle frames bought without new lenses.
I.3  Hearing accessories means batteries, chargers and cleaning kits.
I.4  Hearing aid replacement period means 24 months from the purchase of hearing aids funded by the plan.
I.5  Massage therapy means sports massage, massage therapy and reflexology.
I.6  Plan year means the twelve months starting on the Member's coverage start date.
I.7  Replacement period means 12 months from the date of the Member's last eyewear claim.
I.8  Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.

PART II: Limits and deductible
II.1  Dental Care: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $100 per claim.
II.2  Vision Care: limit $300 per treatment; deductible $40 per claim.
II.3  Therapy Services: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $75 per claim.
II.4  Hearing Care: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $150 per claim.
II.5  The deductible is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

PART III: Optional cover: Hearing Care
III.1  The Plan will reimburse hearing tests and hearing aids.
III.2  This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Member's schedule.
III.3  The most the Plan will pay for Hearing accessories under this section is $100 per treatment.
III.4  The Plan will not pay for replacement hearing aids bought within the hearing aid replacement period.

PART IV: Vision Care
IV.1  The Plan will reimburse eye tests and prescription eyewear.
IV.2  The most the Plan will pay for Frames under this section is $150 per treatment.
IV.3  The Plan will not pay for eyewear without prescription lenses.
IV.4  The Plan will not pay for a further eyewear claim within the replacement period.

PART V: Therapy Services
V.1  The Plan will reimburse physiotherapy, osteopathy and counselling provided by a registered practitioner.
V.2  The most the Plan will pay for Massage therapy under this section is $300 per treatment.
V.3  The Plan will not pay for treatment of an injury covered by workers' compensation.
V.4  The Plan will not pay for treatment by a practitioner who is not registered with the relevant professional body.

PART VI: General exclusions
VI.1  The Plan will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
VI.2  The Plan will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.

PART VII: Making a claim
VII.1  The Member must notify the Plan of a claim within 21 days of the treatment. The Plan will not pay any claim notified after that time.
VII.2  The Plan may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
VII.3  The Member must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.

PART VIII: Cancellation
VIII.1  The Member can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
VIII.2  After the first 14 days the Member can cancel at any time; the Plan will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $25.
VIII.3  The Plan can cancel this policy by giving the Member 30 days' written notice to the last address the Plan holds.

policy: SINGLE-TRIP TRAVEL PROTECTION PLAN
Issued by Bluewater Assurance
In this policy, "the Insurer" means Bluewater Assurance and "the Insured Person" means the person named in the schedule.

Article 1. Definitions
(a) Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by the Insurer, before any excess, limit or sublimit is applied.
(b) Dental treatment means treatment of the teeth or gums.
(c) Hazardous activity means skydiving, motor racing, or trekking or climbing above 4,500 metres.
(d) Physiotherapy means treatment of muscles and joints by a physiotherapist.
(e) Pre-existing condition means any illness or injury for which the Insured Person received treatment or advice in the 3 months before the policy start date.
(f) Qualifying delay means a delay to the scheduled departure of more than 12 hours.
(g) Sports equipment means skis, snowboards, golf clubs, surfboards and bicycles.
(h) Valuables means laptops, tablets, mobile phones, cameras, watches and jewellery.

Article 2. Limits and excess
(a) Baggage and Personal Belongings: limit $2,000 per incident; excess $75 per claim.
(b) Emergency Medical Expenses: limit $50,000 per incident; excess $150 per claim.
(c) Trip Cancellation: limit $5,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
(d) Travel Delay: limit $300 per incident; excess $25 per claim.
(e) The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

Article 3. Optional cover: Travel Delay
(a) The Insurer will pay reasonable costs of meals and accommodation if the Insured Person's outbound departure is delayed.
(b) This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Insured Person's schedule.
(c) The Insurer will not pay for any delay that is not a qualifying delay.

Article 4. Emergency Medical Expenses
(a) The Insurer will pay reasonable and necessary emergency medical costs incurred during the trip.
(b) The most the Insurer will pay for Dental treatment under this section is $400 per incident.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Physiotherapy under this section is $300 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for treatment of a pre-existing condition.
(e) The Insurer will not pay for injury or illness arising from a hazardous activity. This exclusion does not apply if the Adventure Sports extension is shown in the Insured Person's schedule.
(f) The Insurer will not pay for any claim arising from the Insured Person's being under the influence of alcohol or drugs.

Article 5. Baggage and Personal Belongings
(a) The Insurer will pay for the loss of, theft of, or damage to the Insured Person's baggage and personal belongings during the trip.
(b) The most the Insurer will pay for Valuables under this section is $500 per incident.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Sports equipment under this section is $300 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for loss or theft of property left unattended in a vehicle or in a public place. This exclusion does not apply to property locked out of sight in the boot or trunk of a locked vehicle.
(e) The Insurer will not pay for loss caused by confiscation or detention by customs or other officials.
(f) The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by wear and tear or gradual deterioration.

Article 6. General exclusions
(a) The Insurer will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Insured Person.
(b) The Insurer will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.

Article 7. Making a claim
(a) The Insured Person must notify the Insurer of a claim within 90 days of the incident. The Insurer will not pay any claim notified after that time.
(b) The Insured Person must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
(c) The Insurer may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

The showtimes vary a bit day-to-day, but generally they show more recent independent features during the daytime and second-runs at night. I don't like popcorn, but the cookies are $3 (and Pekara made, sweet!) and they offer mixed drinks for $6. I'm especially fond of the mixed drinks, which feature really good spirits (their bourbon is Makers 46, which... wow.) 

The movie selection is also great. The independent films are almost always good and very rarely super-pretentious, and the late night films are always good. The first time I saw Cabin In the Woods here was my second favorite movie experience ever; the crowd was raucous and engaged. Plus, they show cult films (do not miss the annual showing of The Room in February- weekend showings are the best) and occasionally have film festivals or special events. Recently, they brought in the Andrew Alden Ensemble to play a live score to Vampyr, which was unbelievably cool.

Instead we get risibly bad song and dance sequences featuring picturesque beggars and whores, and the final alienation is accomplished by pulling back to reveal the action has taken place on a music-hall stage, appropriately enough for a production that's more Lionel 'Oliver' Blair than Brecht. The acting talent is shamefully misused: Migenes and Walters are good but don't have to try very hard: Migenes at least has a great voice and some feel for the material. Julia looks perfect as Mack, but struggles with the character, straitjacketed by a fake plummy accent. Harris's Peachum is embarrassingly mannered and Polly is atrocious. The adaptations of lyrics, script and music are often awkward: it was a bad move to base the film on Marc Blitzstein's bowdlerised Broadway version, but at least his words were singable, unlike most of what's been interpolated in gestures of faithfulness. policy: RENTERS CONTENTS PROTECTION
Issued by Keystone Home Mutual
In this policy, "the Insurer" means Keystone Home Mutual and "the Policyholder" means the person named in the schedule.

Article 1. Definitions
(a) Bicycles means bicycles and electric scooters.
(b) Garden items means garden furniture, plants and outdoor tools.
(c) High-risk items means jewellery, watches, laptops, games consoles and cameras.
(d) Home means the private residence at the address shown in the schedule.
(e) Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
(f) Unoccupied means not lived in by the Policyholder or a member of the Policyholder's family for more than 30 consecutive days.

Article 2. Limits and excess
(a) Theft: limit $20,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
(b) Escape of Water: limit $30,000 per incident; excess $1,000 per claim.
(c) Accidental Damage: limit $5,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
(d) Flood: limit $40,000 per incident; excess $1,000 per claim.
(e) Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the excess is then deducted from the result.

Article 3. Flood
(a) The Insurer will pay for contents damaged by flood water entering the Policyholder's home.
(b) No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 60 days after the policy start date.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Garden items under this section is $1,000 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for flood damage where a flood warning for the Policyholder's area had been issued before the policy started.

Article 4. Theft
(a) The Insurer will pay for contents stolen from the Policyholder's home.
(b) The most the Insurer will pay for High-risk items under this section is $1,000 per incident.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Bicycles under this section is $800 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for theft while the home is unoccupied.
(e) The Insurer will not pay for theft where there is no sign of forced entry to the home. This exclusion does not apply where the thief gained entry by deception, for example by posing as a utility worker.
(f) The Insurer will not pay for theft from sheds, garages or other outbuildings. This exclusion does not apply if the outbuilding was locked and the theft involved forcible entry.

Article 5. General exclusions
(a) The Insurer will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
(b) The Insurer will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Policyholder.
(c) The Insurer will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.

Article 6. Making a claim
(a) The Insurer may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
(b) The Policyholder must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
(c) The Policyholder must notify the Insurer of a claim within 21 days of the incident. The Insurer will not pay any claim notified after that time.

policy: ANNUAL MULTI-TRIP TRAVEL COVER
Issued by Bluewater Assurance
In this policy, "the Insurer" means Bluewater Assurance and "the Insured Person" means the person named in the schedule.

Article 1. Definitions
(a) Dental treatment means treatment of the teeth or gums.
(b) Family means the Insured Person's spouse or partner and any children who live with the Insured Person.
(c) Hazardous activity means skydiving, motor racing, or trekking or climbing above 3,000 metres.
(d) Physiotherapy means treatment of muscles and joints by a physiotherapist.
(e) Pre-existing condition means any illness or injury for which the Insured Person received treatment or advice in the 6 months before the policy start date.
(f) Public transport means any scheduled train, bus, coach, ferry or aircraft.

Article 2. Limits and excess
(a) Baggage and Personal Belongings: limit $3,000 per incident; excess $75 per claim.
(b) Emergency Medical Expenses: limit $25,000 per incident; excess $150 per claim.
(c) Trip Cancellation: limit $3,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
(d) Travel Delay: limit $750 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
(e) The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

Article 3. Emergency Medical Expenses
(a) The Insurer will pay reasonable and necessary emergency medical costs incurred during the trip.
(b) The most the Insurer will pay for Dental treatment under this section is $250 per incident.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Physiotherapy under this section is $500 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for treatment of a pre-existing condition.
(e) The Insurer will not pay for injury or illness arising from a hazardous activity. This exclusion does not apply if the Adventure Sports extension is shown in the Insured Person's schedule.
(f) The Insurer will not pay for any claim arising from the Insured Person's being under the influence of alcohol or drugs.

Article 4. General exclusions
(a) The Insurer will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
(b) The Insurer will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
(c) The Insurer will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.

Article 5. Making a claim
(a) The Insurer may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
(b) The Insured Person must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
(c) The Insured Person must notify the Insurer of a claim within 21 days of the incident. The Insurer will not pay any claim notified after that time.

Article 6. Market conditions
(a) If the replacement item is no longer available, the Insurer will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

Article 7. Personal liability
(a) The Insurer will pay damages the Insured Person becomes legally liable to pay for accidental injury to another person or accidental damage to their property during the trip.
(b) This section does not cover liability arising from the use of motor vehicles, boats or aircraft.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay under this section is $5,000,000 for all claims arising from one event.

Article 8. Compensation scheme
(a) The Insurer is covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
(b) If the Insurer cannot meet the Insurer's obligations, the Insured Person may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

PART I: Definitions
I.1  Accessories means cases, chargers, earbuds and styluses.

PART V: General exclusions
V.1  The Provider will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
V.2  The Provider will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits the Provider from paying.

VI.1  The Customer must notify the Provider of a claim within 21 days of the incident. The Provider will not pay any claim notified after that time.

(b) Where arbitration applies, obtaining an award is a condition precedent to any legal action against the Plan.

(a) The Plan will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.

V.1  The Insurer will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.

# Travel Insurance Policy Wording
Issued by Meridian Travel Insurance Ltd

## 1. Definitions
- **1.1** Excursions and tickets means pre-booked excursions, tours, and event or theatre tickets.
- **1.2** Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
- **1.3** Qualifying delay means a delay to the scheduled departure of more than 12 hours.
- **1.4** Sports equipment means skis, snowboards, golf clubs, surfboards and bicycles.
- **1.5** Valuables means laptops, tablets, mobile phones, cameras, watches and jewellery.

## 2. Limits and excess
- **2.1** Baggage and Personal Belongings: limit $3,000 per incident; excess $75 per claim.
- **2.2** Emergency Medical Expenses: limit $25,000 per incident; excess $150 per claim.
- **2.3** Trip Cancellation: limit $2,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
- **2.4** Travel Delay: limit $750 per incident; excess $25 per claim.
- **2.5** The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

## 3. Baggage and Personal Belongings
- **3.1** We will pay for the loss of, theft of, or damage to your baggage and personal belongings during the trip.
- **3.2** The most we will pay for Valuables under this section is $250 per incident.
- **3.3** The most we will pay for Sports equipment under this section is $450 per incident.
- **3.4** We will not pay for loss or theft of property left unattended in a vehicle or in a public place. This exclusion does not apply to property locked out of sight in the boot or trunk of a locked vehicle.
- **3.5** We will not pay for loss caused by confiscation or detention by customs or other officials.
- **3.6** We will not pay for damage caused by wear and tear or gradual deterioration.

## 4. Trip Cancellation
- **4.1** We will pay non-refundable travel and accommodation costs if you must cancel the trip for a reason beyond your control.
- **4.2** No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 7 days after the policy start date.
- **4.3** The most we will pay for Excursions and tickets under this section is $300 per incident.
- **4.4** We will not pay for cancellation caused by a strike or other event that had been publicly announced before you bought the policy.
- **4.5** We will not pay for cancellation because you no longer wish to travel.

## 5. Optional cover: Travel Delay
- **5.1** We will pay reasonable costs of meals and accommodation if your outbound departure is delayed.
- **5.2** This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
- **5.3** We will not pay for any delay that is not a qualifying delay.

HOME CONTENTS INSURANCE POLICY
Issued by Hearthstone Insurance plc

SECTION 1 - DEFINITIONS
1.1 Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
1.2 Family means your spouse or partner and any children who live with you.
1.3 Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
1.4 Portable electronics means laptops, tablets and mobile phones.

SECTION 2 - LIMITS AND EXCESS
2.1 Theft: limit $10,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
2.2 Escape of Water: limit $30,000 per incident; excess $250 per claim.
2.3 Accidental Damage: limit $2,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
2.4 Flood: limit $40,000 per incident; excess $1,000 per claim.
2.5 The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

SECTION 3 - OPTIONAL COVER: ACCIDENTAL DAMAGE
3.1 We will pay for sudden and unexpected accidental damage to your contents inside the home.
3.2 This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
3.3 The most we will pay for Portable electronics under this section is $500 per incident.
3.4 We will not pay for damage caused by pets.
3.5 We will not pay for wear and tear, or damage that happens gradually.

SECTION 4 - GENERAL EXCLUSIONS
4.1 We will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
4.2 We will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by you.

SECTION 5 - MAKING A CLAIM
5.1 We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
5.2 You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
5.3 You must notify us of a claim within 60 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.

SECTION 6 - ENVIRONMENTAL COMMITMENT
6.1 Where practical, we will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
6.2 You may ask for a new part instead, and we will tell you whether any additional cost would apply.

SECTION 7 - CANCELLATION
7.1 You can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
7.2 After the first 14 days you can cancel at any time; we will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $15.
7.3 We can cancel this policy by giving you 30 days' written notice to the last address we hold.

SECTION 8 - REASONABLE PRECAUTIONS
8.1 You must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
8.2 You must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

SECTION 9 - CHANGES IN CIRCUMSTANCES
9.1 You must tell us as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
9.2 We may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

SECTION 10 - JOINT POLICYHOLDERS
10.1 Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.
10.2 A notice sent to one named person is treated as sent to all of them.

policy: STAFF HEALTH REIMBURSEMENT PLAN RULES
Issued by the Benefits Trust
In this policy, "the Plan" means the Benefits Trust and "the Member" means the person named in the schedule.

Article 1. Definitions
(a) Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
(b) Frames means spectacle frames bought without new lenses.
(c) Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
(d) Limit means the most the Plan will pay for all claims under a section arising from one treatment.
(e) Major restorative work means crowns, bridges, root canal treatment and implants.
(f) Orthodontics means braces and clear aligners.
(g) Replacement period means 24 months from the date of the Member's last eyewear claim.

Article 2. Limits and deductible
(a) Dental Care: limit $2,000 per treatment; deductible $100 per claim.
(b) Vision Care: limit $500 per treatment; deductible $40 per claim.
(c) Therapy Services: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $50 per claim.
(d) Hearing Care: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $150 per claim.
(e) Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the deductible is then deducted from the result.

Article 3. Dental Care
(a) The Plan will reimburse the cost of dental treatment provided by a licensed dentist.
(b) No cover applies under this section to any treatment that happens within the first 60 days after the policy start date.
(c) The most the Plan will pay for Major restorative work under this section is $500 per treatment.

# Travel Insurance Policy Wording
Issued by Meridian Travel Insurance Ltd

## 1. Definitions
- **1.1** Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
- **1.2** Dental treatment means treatment of the teeth or gums.
- **1.3** Excursions and tickets means pre-booked excursions, tours, and event or theatre tickets.
- **1.4** Hazardous activity means skydiving, motor racing, or trekking or climbing above 4,000 metres.
- **1.5** Physiotherapy means treatment of muscles and joints by a physiotherapist.
- **1.6** Pre-existing condition means any illness or injury for which you received treatment or advice in the 12 months before the policy start date.
- **1.7** Premium means the amount you must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
- **1.8** Qualifying delay means a delay to the scheduled departure of more than 8 hours.
- **1.9** Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.

## 2. Limits and excess
- **2.1** Baggage and Personal Belongings: limit $3,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
- **2.2** Emergency Medical Expenses: limit $25,000 per incident; excess $250 per claim.
- **2.3** Trip Cancellation: limit $5,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
- **2.4** Travel Delay: limit $500 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
- **2.5** The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

## 3. Optional cover: Travel Delay
- **3.1** We will pay reasonable costs of meals and accommodation if your outbound departure is delayed.
- **3.2** This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
- **3.3** We will not pay for any delay that is not a qualifying delay.

## 4. Emergency Medical Expenses
- **4.1** We will pay reasonable and necessary emergency medical costs incurred during the trip.
- **4.2** The most we will pay for Dental treatment under this section is $400 per incident.

- **4.6** We will not pay for any claim arising from your being under the influence of alcohol or drugs.

## 5. Trip Cancellation
- **5.1** We will pay non-refundable travel and accommodation costs if you must cancel the trip for a reason beyond your control.
- **5.2** No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 7 days after the policy start date.

- **6.2** We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.

- **7.2** You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.

In 1927 the club was purchased by Conn Smythe and renamed the Maple Leafs. A member of the ``Original Six'', the club was one of six NHL teams to have endured through the period of League retrenchment during the Great Depression. Director John "Bud" Cardos begins the film on a compellingly mysterious note and gradually allows things to get stranger, crazier and more exciting as the loopy story unfolds. Moreover, Cardos fills the screen with plenty of dazzling visuals and does a nice job of creating a genuine sense of awe and wonder. The admirably sincere acting from a game cast qualifies as another major plus: Jim Davis as hearty patriarch Grant Williams, Dorothy Malone as his cheery wife Ana, Christopher Mitchum as the concerned Richard, Marcy Lafferty as his lovely wife Beth, Natasha Ryan as sweet little girl Jenny, and Scott C. Kolden as the gutsy Steve. The funky special effects offer an inspired combo of gnarly miniatures, neat stop-motion animation monsters (said creatures include a tiny spindly hairless guy, a big, lumpy, fanged beast, and a scrawny lizard dude), and nifty matte paintings. Richard Band's rousing full-bore orchestral score really hits the stirring spot. John Arthur Morrill's crisp, sunny cinematography likewise does the trick. A fun flick.

But for everything else, the place shines. There are literally hundreds of dishes on the menu but good luck if you don't read Chinese! The menu is handwritten and posted on the wall as you enter the place. There is an English menu but I don't think it does the place justice. I knew it would be good on the recommendation of my mother who is a very picky Chinese lady and by the crowds of Chinese people lining up to order and eat.

We went for lunch with a group of 6. We ordered beef soup noodle, beef tendon soup noodles, seafood fried noodles. Steamed buns that you fill with braised pork belly, pickled cabbage, peanuts and cilantro - WOW. Tempura fried soft shell crab. Smoked chicken. Stir-fried "sih gua" melon. Everything was hot, fresh, and delicious. $16 per person for this feast.

My advice: bring your favorite Chinese reading/speaking friend and check this place out.

(b) Hearing accessories means batteries, chargers and cleaning kits.
(c) Hearing aid replacement period means 24 months from the purchase of hearing aids funded by the plan.
(d) Major restorative work means crowns, bridges, root canal treatment and implants.
(e) Network provider means a practitioner or clinic that has an agreement with the Plan to provide treatment.
(f) Orthodontics means braces and clear aligners.

Article 2. Limits and deductible
(a) Dental Care: limit $1,500 per treatment; deductible $100 per claim.
(b) Vision Care: limit $400 per treatment; deductible $25 per claim.
(c) Therapy Services: limit $2,000 per treatment; deductible $50 per claim.
(d) Hearing Care: limit $2,000 per treatment; deductible $100 per claim.
(e) The deductible is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

Article 3. Optional cover: Hearing Care
(a) The Plan will reimburse hearing tests and hearing aids.
(b) This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Member's schedule.
(c) The most the Plan will pay for Hearing accessories under this section is $150 per treatment.
(d) The Plan will not pay for replacement hearing aids bought within the hearing aid replacement period.

Article 4. Dental Care
(a) The Plan will reimburse the cost of dental treatment provided by a licensed dentist.
(b) No cover applies under this section to any treatment that happens within the first 60 days after the policy start date.
(c) The most the Plan will pay for Major restorative work under this section is $500 per treatment.
(d) The most the Plan will pay for Orthodontics under this section is $800 per treatment.
(e) The Plan will not pay for treatment that is mainly cosmetic, such as whitening or veneers. This exclusion does not apply to treatment needed to repair damage caused by an accident.
(f) The Plan will not pay for treatment by a provider outside the plan's network. This exclusion does not apply to emergency treatment for sudden severe pain.

Article 5. General exclusions
(a) The Plan will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
(b) The Plan will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
(c) The Plan will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Member.

Article 6. Making a claim
(a) The Plan may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
(b) The Member must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
(c) The Member must notify the Plan of a claim within 60 days of the treatment. The Plan will not pay any claim notified after that time.
