Issued by Oakfield Assurance

PART I: Definitions
I.1  Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by the Insurer, before any excess, limit or sublimit is applied.
I.2  Bicycles means bicycles and electric scooters.
I.3  High-risk items means jewellery, watches, laptops, games consoles and cameras.
I.4  Limit means the most the Insurer will pay for all claims under a section arising from one incident.
I.5  Portable electronics means laptops, tablets and mobile phones.
I.6  Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows the Policyholder's details, the covers the Policyholder bought and any extensions.
I.7  Unoccupied means not lived in by the Policyholder or a member of the Policyholder's family for more than 45 consecutive days.

PART II: Limits and excess
II.1  Theft: limit $10,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
II.2  Escape of Water: limit $15,000 per incident; excess $250 per claim.
II.3  Accidental Damage: limit $2,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
II.4  Flood: limit $40,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
II.5  The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

PART III: Theft
III.1  The Insurer will pay for contents stolen from the Policyholder's home.
III.2  The most the Insurer will pay for High-risk items under this section is $1,500 per incident.
III.3  The most the Insurer will pay for Bicycles under this section is $500 per incident.
III.4  The Insurer will not pay for theft while the home is unoccupied.
III.5  The Insurer will not pay for theft where there is no sign of forced entry to the home. This exclusion does not apply where the thief gained entry by deception, for example by posing as a utility worker.
III.6  The Insurer will not pay for theft from sheds, garages or other outbuildings. This exclusion does not apply if the outbuilding was locked and the theft involved forcible entry.

PART IV: Optional cover: Accidental Damage
IV.1  The Insurer will pay for sudden and unexpected accidental damage to the Policyholder's contents inside the home.
IV.2  This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Policyholder's schedule.
IV.3  The most the Insurer will pay for Portable electronics under this section is $750 per incident.
IV.4  The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by pets.
IV.5  The Insurer will not pay for wear and tear, or damage that happens gradually.

PART V: General exclusions
V.1  The Insurer will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Policyholder.
V.2  The Insurer will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits the Insurer from paying.

PART VI: Making a claim
VI.1  The Insurer may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
VI.2  The Policyholder must notify the Insurer of a claim within 21 days of the incident. The Insurer will not pay any claim notified after that time.
VI.3  The Policyholder must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.

PART VII: Tenant's improvements
VII.1  If the Policyholder rents the home, the Insurer will pay for damage to fixtures and fittings that the Policyholder installed and are responsible for.
VII.2  This cover applies only to improvements the Policyholder paid for, not to items provided by the landlord.

5.1 We will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits us from paying.

policy: RENTERS CONTENTS PROTECTION
Issued by Hearthstone Insurance plc
In this policy, "the Insurer" means Hearthstone Insurance plc and "the Policyholder" means the person named in the schedule.

Article 1. Definitions
(a) Garden items means garden furniture, plants and outdoor tools.
(b) Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
(c) Portable electronics means laptops, tablets and mobile phones.

Article 2. Limits and excess
(a) Theft: limit $40,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
(b) Escape of Water: limit $15,000 per incident; excess $1,000 per claim.
(c) Accidental Damage: limit $5,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
(d) Flood: limit $40,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
(e) The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

Article 3. Optional cover: Accidental Damage
(a) The Insurer will pay for sudden and unexpected accidental damage to the Policyholder's contents inside the home.
(b) This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Policyholder's schedule.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Portable electronics under this section is $500 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by pets.
(e) The Insurer will not pay for wear and tear, or damage that happens gradually.

Article 4. Market conditions
(a) If the replacement item is no longer available, the Insurer will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

Article 5. Flood
(a) The Insurer will pay for contents damaged by flood water entering the Policyholder's home.
(b) No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 14 days after the policy start date.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Garden items under this section is $500 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for flood damage where a flood warning for the Policyholder's area had been issued before the policy started.

Article 6. Instalment agreements
(a) If the Policyholder pays by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
(b) Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

Article 7. Renewal
(a) The Insurer will write to the Policyholder at least 21 days before the end of the policy period with the renewal terms.
(b) The Insurer is not obliged to offer renewal.

Article 8. Recovery of costs
(a) If the Insurer pays a claim that is later found not to be covered, the Insurer may ask the Policyholder to repay the amount.

Article 9. General exclusions
(a) The Insurer will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
(b) The Insurer will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Policyholder.
(c) The Insurer will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.

Article 10. Customer support
(a) The Insurer's helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
(b) Outside these hours the Policyholder can leave a message and the Insurer will call back on the next working day.

Article 11. Tenant's improvements
(a) If the Policyholder rents the home, the Insurer will pay for damage to fixtures and fittings that the Policyholder installed and are responsible for.
(b) This cover applies only to improvements the Policyholder paid for, not to items provided by the landlord.

Article 12. Making a claim
(a) The Policyholder must notify the Insurer of a claim within 21 days of the incident. The Insurer will not pay any claim notified after that time.
(b) The Policyholder must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
(c) The Insurer may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

Article 13. Currency
(a) All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
(b) Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

# Gadget Cover: Terms and Conditions
Issued by Voltguard Protection Ltd

## 1. Definitions
- **1.1** Accessories means cases, chargers, earbuds and styluses.
- **1.2** Authorised repairer means a repairer approved in writing by us.
- **1.3** Battery replacement means replacement batteries and battery repairs.
- **1.4** Manufacturer's warranty period means the first 24 months after the device was bought.
- **1.5** Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
- **1.6** Wearables means smartwatches and fitness trackers.

## 2. Limits and service fee
- **2.1** Accidental Damage: limit $800 per incident; service fee $49 per claim.
- **2.2** Breakdown: limit $1,000 per incident; service fee $49 per claim.
- **2.3** Theft and Loss: limit $1,200 per incident; service fee $99 per claim.
- **2.4** Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the service fee is then deducted from the result.

## 3. Breakdown
- **3.1** We will repair or replace your device if it stops working because of an electrical or mechanical fault.
- **3.2** No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 45 days after the policy start date.
- **3.3** The most we will pay for Battery replacement under this section is $120 per incident.
- **3.4** We will not pay for breakdowns during the manufacturer's warranty period.
- **3.5** We will not pay for breakdown caused by liquid getting into the device.

## 4. Accidental Damage
- **4.1** We will repair or replace your device if it is accidentally damaged.
- **4.2** The most we will pay for Accessories under this section is $100 per incident.
- **4.3** The most we will pay for Wearables under this section is $300 per incident.
- **4.4** We will not pay for cosmetic damage, such as scratches or dents, that does not affect how the device works.
- **4.5** We will not pay for damage following a repair by anyone other than us or an authorised repairer. This exclusion does not apply if we approved the repair in writing beforehand.

## 5. General exclusions
- **5.1** We will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
- **5.2** We will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits us from paying.

## 6. Making a claim
- **6.1** You must notify us of a claim within 14 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.
- **6.2** You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
- **6.3** We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

Knowing Pitt, as we all do, as one of the most enduring heart-throbs Hollywood has ever had, it is refreshing to see him play such a vile, unattractive character. policy: HOME CONTENTS INSURANCE POLICY
Issued by Oakfield Assurance
In this policy, "the Insurer" means Oakfield Assurance and "the Policyholder" means the person named in the schedule.

Article 1. Definitions
(a) Forcible entry means entry to the home that leaves visible damage to doors, windows or locks.
(b) Portable electronics means laptops, tablets and mobile phones.
(c) Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.

Article 2. Limits and excess
(a) Theft: limit $40,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
(b) Escape of Water: limit $15,000 per incident; excess $250 per claim.
(c) Accidental Damage: limit $2,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
(d) Flood: limit $40,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
(e) The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

Article 3. Optional cover: Accidental Damage
(a) The Insurer will pay for sudden and unexpected accidental damage to the Policyholder's contents inside the home.
(b) This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Policyholder's schedule.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Portable electronics under this section is $750 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by pets.
(e) The Insurer will not pay for wear and tear, or damage that happens gradually.

Article 4. General exclusions
(a) The Insurer will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
(b) The Insurer will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits the Insurer from paying.
(c) The Insurer will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Policyholder.

Article 5. Making a claim
(a) The Policyholder must notify the Insurer of a claim within 21 days of the incident. The Insurer will not pay any claim notified after that time.
(b) The Policyholder must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
(c) The Insurer may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

Article 6. Locks and keys
(a) If the keys to the Policyholder's home are lost or stolen, the Insurer will pay the cost of replacing the locks to the outside doors.
(b) The most the Insurer will pay under this clause is $300 for any one claim.

# Renters Contents Protection
Issued by Lantern General Insurance

## 1. Definitions
- **1.1** Contents means household goods and personal possessions that belong to you or your family.
- **1.2** Portable electronics means laptops, tablets and mobile phones.
- **1.3** Premium means the amount you must pay for this policy, including any taxes.

## 2. Limits and excess
- **2.1** Theft: limit $10,000 per incident; excess $250 per claim.
- **2.2** Escape of Water: limit $15,000 per incident; excess $250 per claim.
- **2.3** Accidental Damage: limit $3,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
- **2.4** Flood: limit $20,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
- **2.5** The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

## 3. Optional cover: Accidental Damage
- **3.1** We will pay for sudden and unexpected accidental damage to your contents inside the home.
- **3.2** This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
- **3.3** The most we will pay for Portable electronics under this section is $500 per incident.
- **3.4** We will not pay for damage caused by pets.
- **3.5** We will not pay for wear and tear, or damage that happens gradually.

## 4. Governing law
- **4.1** This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
- **4.2** Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

## 5. Currency
- **5.1** All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
- **5.2** Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

## 6. General exclusions
- **6.1** We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
- **6.2** We will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by you.

## 7. Discounts
- **7.1** Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
- **7.2** If a condition for a discount stops being met, we may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

## 8. Claims documents
- **8.1** You must provide, at your own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence we reasonably ask for.
- **8.2** We may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

## 9. Making a claim
- **9.1** We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
- **9.2** You must notify us of a claim within 14 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.
- **9.3** You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.

## 10. Taxes
- **10.1** The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
- **10.2** If the tax rate changes, we may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

# Single-Trip Travel Protection Plan
Issued by Northstar Underwriting

## 1. Definitions
- **1.1** Public transport means any scheduled train, bus, coach, ferry or aircraft.
- **1.2** Sports equipment means skis, snowboards, golf clubs, surfboards and bicycles.
- **1.3** Valuables means laptops, tablets, mobile phones, cameras, watches and jewellery.

## 2. Limits and excess
- **2.1** Baggage and Personal Belongings: limit $3,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
- **2.2** Emergency Medical Expenses: limit $50,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
- **2.3** Trip Cancellation: limit $3,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
- **2.4** Travel Delay: limit $750 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
- **2.5** Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the excess is then deducted from the result.

## 3. Other insurance
- **3.1** If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, we will pay only our proportionate share.
- **3.2** You must tell us about any other insurance that covers the same loss when you make a claim.

## 4. Baggage and Personal Belongings
- **4.1** We will pay for the loss of, theft of, or damage to your baggage and personal belongings during the trip.
- **4.2** The most we will pay for Valuables under this section is $400 per incident.
- **4.3** The most we will pay for Sports equipment under this section is $450 per incident.
- **4.4** We will not pay for loss or theft of property left unattended in a vehicle or in a public place. This exclusion does not apply to property locked out of sight in the boot or trunk of a locked vehicle.
- **4.5** We will not pay for loss caused by confiscation or detention by customs or other officials.
- **4.6** We will not pay for damage caused by wear and tear or gradual deterioration.

## 5. General exclusions
- **5.1** We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
- **5.2** We will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.

## 6. Currency
- **6.1** All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
- **6.2** Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

## 7. Making a claim
- **7.1** You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
- **7.2** You must notify us of a claim within 30 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.
- **7.3** We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

I am sending this on February 7, 2026, which is when I first notified you. Your adjuster assessed the loss at $389.

# Household Contents Cover: Policy Booklet
Issued by Keystone Home Mutual

## 1. Definitions
- **1.1** Art and antiques means paintings, antiques, rugs and other works of art.
- **1.2** Contents means household goods and personal possessions that belong to you or your family.
- **1.3** Garden items means garden furniture, plants and outdoor tools.

## 2. Limits and excess
- **2.1** Theft: limit $20,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
- **2.2** Escape of Water: limit $15,000 per incident; excess $1,000 per claim.
- **2.3** Accidental Damage: limit $3,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
- **2.4** Flood: limit $20,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
- **2.5** The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

## 3. Escape of Water
- **3.1** We will pay for contents damaged by water escaping from a fixed pipe, tank or domestic appliance.
- **3.2** The most we will pay for Art and antiques under this section is $2,000 per incident.
- **3.3** We will not pay for damage caused by water leaking gradually over a period of time.
- **3.4** We will not pay for damage caused by the failure of grout or sealant around baths and showers.

## 4. Flood
- **4.1** We will pay for contents damaged by flood water entering your home.
- **4.2** No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 60 days after the policy start date.
- **4.3** The most we will pay for Garden items under this section is $500 per incident.
- **4.4** We will not pay for flood damage where a flood warning for your area had been issued before the policy started.

## 5. General exclusions
- **5.1** We will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
- **5.2** We will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits us from paying.

## 6. Making a claim
- **6.1** We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
- **6.2** You must notify us of a claim within 14 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.
- **6.3** You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.

## 7. Inflation
- **7.1** We may adjust limits at renewal in line with a published index of consumer prices.
- **7.2** Any adjustment will be shown in your renewal documents; limits do not change during a policy period.

## 8. Subrogation
- **8.1** We will be entitled to take over and conduct in your name the defence or settlement of any claim.
- **8.2** We can take action in your name to recover any payment we make from anyone responsible for the loss.

## 9. Interest
- **9.1** We will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

## 10. Taxes
- **10.1** The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
- **10.2** If the tax rate changes, we may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

## 11. Garden and outdoor cover
- **11.1** We will pay for plants, trees and shrubs in the garden of the home that are damaged by fire, lightning or theft.
- **11.2** We will not pay for damage caused by frost, storms, drought or animals.

state: document: This early role for Barbara Shelley(in fact,her first in Britain after working in Italy),was made when she was 24 years old,and it's certainly safe to say that she made a stunning debut in 1957's "Cat Girl." While blondes and brunettes get most of the attention(I'll always cherish Yutte Stensgaard),the lovely auburn-haired actress with the deep voice always exuded intelligence as well as vulnerability(one such example being 1960's "Village of the Damned," in which her screen time was much less than her character's husband,George Sanders).She is the sole reason for seeing this drab update of "Cat People," and is seen to great advantage throughout(it's difficult to say if her beauty found an even better showcase).Her character apparently sleeps in the nude,and we are exposed to her luscious bare back when she is awakened(also exposed 8 years later in 1965's "Rasputin-The Mad Monk").The ravishing gown she wears during most of the film is a stunning strapless wonder(I don't see what held that dress up,but I'd sure like to).All in all,proof positive that Barbara Shelley,in a poorly written role that would defeat most actresses,rises above her material and makes the film consistently watchable,a real test of star power,which she would find soon enough at Hammer's studios in Bray,for the duration of the 1960's.

policy: HOUSEHOLD CONTENTS COVER: POLICY BOOKLET
Issued by Lantern General Insurance
In this policy, "the Insurer" means Lantern General Insurance and "the Policyholder" means the person named in the schedule.

Article 1. Definitions
(a) Art and antiques means paintings, antiques, rugs and other works of art.
(b) Bicycles means bicycles and electric scooters.
(c) High-risk items means jewellery, watches, laptops, games consoles and cameras.
(d) Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in the Policyholder's schedule.
(e) Portable electronics means laptops, tablets and mobile phones.
(f) Unoccupied means not lived in by the Policyholder or a member of the Policyholder's family for more than 30 consecutive days.

Article 2. Limits and excess
(a) Theft: limit $10,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
(b) Escape of Water: limit $15,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
(c) Accidental Damage: limit $5,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
(d) Flood: limit $20,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
(e) The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

Article 3. Theft
(a) The Insurer will pay for contents stolen from the Policyholder's home.
(b) The most the Insurer will pay for High-risk items under this section is $1,500 per incident.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Bicycles under this section is $500 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for theft while the home is unoccupied.
(e) The Insurer will not pay for theft where there is no sign of forced entry to the home. This exclusion does not apply where the thief gained entry by deception, for example by posing as a utility worker.
(f) The Insurer will not pay for theft from sheds, garages or other outbuildings. This exclusion does not apply if the outbuilding was locked and the theft involved forcible entry.

Article 4. Optional cover: Accidental Damage
(a) The Insurer will pay for sudden and unexpected accidental damage to the Policyholder's contents inside the home.
(b) This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Policyholder's schedule.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Portable electronics under this section is $750 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by pets.
(e) The Insurer will not pay for wear and tear, or damage that happens gradually.

Article 5. Escape of Water
(a) The Insurer will pay for contents damaged by water escaping from a fixed pipe, tank or domestic appliance.
(b) The most the Insurer will pay for Art and antiques under this section is $2,000 per incident.
(c) The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by water leaking gradually over a period of time.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by the failure of grout or sealant around baths and showers.

Article 6. Interest
(a) The Insurer will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

Article 7. General exclusions
(a) The Insurer will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Policyholder.
(b) The Insurer will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits the Insurer from paying.
(c) The Insurer will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.

Article 8. Making a claim
(a) The Policyholder must notify the Insurer of a claim within 30 days of the incident. The Insurer will not pay any claim notified after that time.
(b) The Policyholder must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
(c) The Insurer may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

# Electronics Care Plan
Issued by Tessera Warranty Company

## 1. Definitions
- **1.1** Accessories means cases, chargers and earbuds.
- **1.2** Battery replacement means replacement batteries and battery repairs.
- **1.3** Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
- **1.4** Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
- **1.5** Limit means the most we will pay for all claims under a section arising from one incident.
- **1.6** Manufacturer's warranty period means the first 12 months after the device was bought.

## 2. Limits and service fee
- **2.1** Accidental Damage: limit $1,500 per incident; service fee $49 per claim.
- **2.2** Breakdown: limit $600 per incident; service fee $25 per claim.
- **2.3** Theft and Loss: limit $1,200 per incident; service fee $149 per claim.
- **2.4** The service fee is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

## 3. Optional cover: Theft and Loss
- **3.1** We will replace your device if it is stolen or lost.
- **3.2** This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
- **3.3** The most we will pay for Accessories under this section is $100 per incident.
- **3.4** We will not pay for loss or theft of property left unattended in a vehicle or in a public place. This exclusion does not apply to property locked out of sight in the boot or trunk of a locked vehicle.
- **3.5** We will not pay for theft that was not reported to the police.

## 4. Breakdown
- **4.1** We will repair or replace your device if it stops working because of an electrical or mechanical fault.
- **4.2** No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 45 days after the policy start date.
- **4.3** The most we will pay for Battery replacement under this section is $120 per incident.
- **4.4** We will not pay for breakdowns during the manufacturer's warranty period.
- **4.5** We will not pay for breakdown caused by liquid getting into the device.

## 5. General exclusions
- **5.1** We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
- **5.2** We will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by you.
- **5.3** We will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.

## 6. Making a claim
- **6.1** We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
- **6.2** You must notify us of a claim within 21 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.
- **6.3** You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.

# Single-Trip Travel Protection Plan
Issued by Northstar Underwriting

## 1. Definitions
- **1.1** Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
- **1.2** Dental treatment means treatment of the teeth or gums.
- **1.3** Hazardous activity means skydiving, motor racing, or trekking or climbing above 3,000 metres.
- **1.4** Physiotherapy means treatment of muscles and joints by a physiotherapist.
- **1.5** Pre-existing condition means any illness or injury for which you received treatment or advice in the 3 months before the policy start date.
- **1.6** Public transport means any scheduled train, bus, coach, ferry or aircraft.
- **1.7** Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.

## 2. Limits and excess
- **2.1** Baggage and Personal Belongings: limit $1,500 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
- **2.2** Emergency Medical Expenses: limit $25,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
- **2.3** Trip Cancellation: limit $2,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
- **2.4** Travel Delay: limit $300 per incident; excess $25 per claim.
- **2.5** Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the excess is then deducted from the result.

## 3. Payment of claims
- **3.1** We will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in your name.
- **3.2** We aim to pay accepted claims within 5 working days of receiving all the documents we need.

## 4. Salvage
- **4.1** When we replace an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes our property.
- **4.2** If stolen property is recovered after we have paid a claim, you must tell us and either return the payment or give us the property.

## 5. Emergency Medical Expenses
- **5.1** We will pay reasonable and necessary emergency medical costs incurred during the trip.
- **5.2** The most we will pay for Dental treatment under this section is $400 per incident.
- **5.3** The most we will pay for Physiotherapy under this section is $500 per incident.
- **5.4** We will not pay for treatment of a pre-existing condition.
- **5.5** We will not pay for injury or illness arising from a hazardous activity. This exclusion does not apply if the Adventure Sports extension is shown in your schedule.
- **5.6** We will not pay for any claim arising from your being under the influence of alcohol or drugs.

## 6. General exclusions
- **6.1** We will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by you.
- **6.2** We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
- **6.3** We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.

## 7. Making a claim
- **7.1** We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
- **7.2** You must notify us of a claim within 90 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.
- **7.3** You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.

## 8. Repatriation
- **8.1** If our medical adviser agrees it is necessary, we will arrange and pay for you to be brought home.
- **8.2** We will decide the method of transport and the time of repatriation after speaking to the treating doctor.

Hi all,

Outages propagate along hard dependencies: if a service goes down, every service that depends on it, directly or through other hard dependencies, is affected. Thanks.

PART I: Definitions
I.1  Frames means spectacle frames bought without new lenses.

PART VII: General exclusions
VII.1  The Plan will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
VII.2  The Plan will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Member.

V.3  The Provider will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.

VIII.2  Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

# Household Contents Cover: Policy Booklet
Issued by Keystone Home Mutual

## 1. Definitions
- **1.1** Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by us, before any excess, limit or sublimit is applied.
- **1.2** Bicycles means bicycles and electric scooters.
- **1.3** Garden items means garden furniture, plants and outdoor tools.
- **1.4** High-risk items means jewellery, watches, laptops, games consoles and cameras.
- **1.5** Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
- **1.6** Unoccupied means not lived in by you or a member of your family for more than 30 consecutive days.

## 2. Limits and excess
- **2.1** Theft: limit $20,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
- **2.2** Escape of Water: limit $15,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
- **2.3** Accidental Damage: limit $5,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
- **2.4** Flood: limit $20,000 per incident; excess $1,000 per claim.
- **2.5** Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the excess is then deducted from the result.

## 3. Flood
- **3.1** We will pay for contents damaged by flood water entering your home.
- **3.2** No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 30 days after the policy start date.
- **3.3** The most we will pay for Garden items under this section is $500 per incident.
- **3.4** We will not pay for flood damage where a flood warning for your area had been issued before the policy started.

## 4. Theft
- **4.1** We will pay for contents stolen from your home.
- **4.2** The most we will pay for High-risk items under this section is $2,500 per incident.
- **4.3** The most we will pay for Bicycles under this section is $500 per incident.
- **4.4** We will not pay for theft while the home is unoccupied.
- **4.5** We will not pay for theft where there is no sign of forced entry to the home. This exclusion does not apply where the thief gained entry by deception, for example by posing as a utility worker.
- **4.6** We will not pay for theft from sheds, garages or other outbuildings. This exclusion does not apply if the outbuilding was locked and the theft involved forcible entry.

## 5. General exclusions
- **5.1** We will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
- **5.2** We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
- **5.3** We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.

## 6. Making a claim
- **6.1** You must notify us of a claim within 14 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.
- **6.2** We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
- **6.3** You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.

## 7. Interest
- **7.1** We will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

## 8. Compensation scheme
- **8.1** We are covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
- **8.2** If we cannot meet our obligations, you may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

## 9. Inflation
- **9.1** We may adjust limits at renewal in line with a published index of consumer prices.
- **9.2** Any adjustment will be shown in your renewal documents; limits do not change during a policy period.

state: Presidents of the United States have repeatedly asked the Congress to give them a line-item veto power. According to Louis Fisher in The Politics of Shared Power, Ronald Reagan said to Congress in his 1986 State of the Union address, ``Tonight I ask you to give me what forty-three governors have: Give me a line-item veto this year. Give me the authority to veto waste, and I'll take the responsibility, I'll make the cuts, I'll take the heat.'' Bill Clinton echoed the request in his State of the Union address in 1995. Congress attempted to grant this power to the president by the Line Item Veto Act of 1996 to control ``pork barrel spending'', but in 1998 the U.S. Supreme Court ruled the act to be unconstitutional in a 6-3 decision in Clinton v. City of New York. The court found that exercise of the line-item veto is tantamount to a unilateral amendment or repeal by the executive of only parts of statutes authorizing federal spending, and therefore violated the Presentment Clause of the United States Constitution. Thus a federal line-item veto, at least in this particular formulation, would only be possible through a constitutional amendment. Prior to that ruling, President Clinton applied the line-item veto to the federal budget 82 times.

policy: HOME CONTENTS INSURANCE POLICY
Issued by Hearthstone Insurance plc
In this policy, "the Insurer" means Hearthstone Insurance plc and "the Policyholder" means the person named in the schedule.

Article 1. Definitions
(a) Bicycles means bicycles and electric scooters.
(b) High-risk items means jewellery, watches, laptops, games consoles and cameras.
(c) Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in the Policyholder's schedule.
(d) Premium means the amount the Policyholder must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
(e) Unoccupied means not lived in by the Policyholder or a member of the Policyholder's family for more than 45 consecutive days.

Article 2. Limits and excess
(a) Theft: limit $10,000 per incident; excess $250 per claim.
(b) Escape of Water: limit $30,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
(c) Accidental Damage: limit $3,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
(d) Flood: limit $20,000 per incident; excess $1,000 per claim.
(e) Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the excess is then deducted from the result.

Article 3. Theft
(a) The Insurer will pay for contents stolen from the Policyholder's home.
(b) The most the Insurer will pay for High-risk items under this section is $2,500 per incident.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Bicycles under this section is $500 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for theft while the home is unoccupied.
(e) The Insurer will not pay for theft where there is no sign of forced entry to the home. This exclusion does not apply where the thief gained entry by deception, for example by posing as a utility worker.
(f) The Insurer will not pay for theft from sheds, garages or other outbuildings. This exclusion does not apply if the outbuilding was locked and the theft involved forcible entry.

Article 4. General exclusions
(a) The Insurer will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
(b) The Insurer will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
(c) The Insurer will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Policyholder.

Article 5. Making a claim
(a) The Insurer may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
(b) The Policyholder must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
(c) The Policyholder must notify the Insurer of a claim within 30 days of the incident. The Insurer will not pay any claim notified after that time.

# Annual Multi-Trip Travel Cover
Issued by Bluewater Assurance

## 1. Definitions
- **1.1** Excursions and tickets means pre-booked excursions, tours, and event or theatre tickets.
- **1.2** Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in your schedule.
- **1.3** Qualifying delay means a delay to the scheduled departure of more than 6 hours.
- **1.4** Trip means a journey that starts and ends in your home country during the policy period.

## 2. Limits and excess
- **2.1** Baggage and Personal Belongings: limit $2,000 per incident; excess $75 per claim.
- **2.2** Emergency Medical Expenses: limit $50,000 per incident; excess $150 per claim.
- **2.3** Trip Cancellation: limit $5,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
- **2.4** Travel Delay: limit $300 per incident; excess $25 per claim.
- **2.5** Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the excess is then deducted from the result.

## 3. Trip Cancellation
- **3.1** We will pay non-refundable travel and accommodation costs if you must cancel the trip for a reason beyond your control.
- **3.2** No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 10 days after the policy start date.
- **3.3** The most we will pay for Excursions and tickets under this section is $200 per incident.
- **3.4** We will not pay for cancellation caused by a strike or other event that had been publicly announced before you bought the policy.
- **3.5** We will not pay for cancellation because you no longer wish to travel.

## 4. Optional cover: Travel Delay
- **4.1** We will pay reasonable costs of meals and accommodation if your outbound departure is delayed.
- **4.2** This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
- **4.3** We will not pay for any delay that is not a qualifying delay.

## 5. General exclusions
- **5.1** We will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
- **5.2** We will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
- **5.3** We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.

## 6. Making a claim
- **6.1** We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
- **6.2** You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
- **6.3** You must notify us of a claim within 30 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.

state: document: A motor vehicle in a public place is potentially a dangerous and lethal instrument. Even when it is without its engine or without petrol, if it is moved down on an incline, even unintentionally, it can cause considerable damage and human injury. Hence, unlike other properties which may be insured or not at the option of the owner, a motor vehicle is required by law to be insured in respect of the user's liability for death, bodily injury or damage to property of third party. These kinds of insurance contracts are based on indemnity and only cover the damage, and the whole insurance amount is not given every time. As sometimes the driver of the vehicle is often a person of small means and injured person goes without adequate compensation, insurance of motor vehicle covering the third party risk is made compulsory in India and the Motor Vehicles Act provides that, vehicle should not be used in public place without having insurance policy covering third party risks. Third party risk means risk covered for bodily injury, death and damage of property of third party. Third party means any person except owner or passenger in the private vehicle. So pillion rider of the motor cycle, passengers in private cars, jeeps etc. are not third party. However, passengers in public vehicle such as bus. contract carriage vehicle, taxi etc. are also third party and hence covered by third party or statutory policy.

state: Wasn't quite sure what to expect with this one, outside of the uniform positive reviews I've read. Turns out, I could have never imagined this movie, because it's very close to "The Bride with White Hair" in being operatic and dealing with the fantastic. This walks a fine line between being a farce, a comedy, and just plain good old fashion ghost story telling. There's nothing scary about it, that's not the theme, it's really mostly a love story dealing with a bumbling guy who encounters a beautiful ghost, who is in a lot of trouble with other ghosts. So the main theme is the guy trying to save the beautiful ghost. This also takes place in ancient China, with wild outlandish Kung Fu exhibitions, and a trip to hell (more or less). Some of the stop-action ghosts are pretty cool, and the visual effects are top rate all the way. I could watch this genre of Chinese movies all day, because they are highly entertaining, great visuals, and pretty much tongue-in-cheek. And I'm looking forward to watching the first sequel of this movie also. Highly recommended.

state: I was totally engrossed in this film from the first to last minute. It is brilliantly shot, with lots of interesting and original camera angles and techniques employed. The plot surrounds a deaf woman who is picked on by friends and colleagues alike. She hires an assistant at work, with her true intention being to find love. He's an ex-con and she takes advantage of him to wreak revenge on those who have hurt her. In return she must help him with a heist that requires her lip reading skills to pull it off. The film transcends into a dark film noir, with a couple of truly excellent scenes, and an even better finale. The real beauty in this film comes from the way the director takes advantage of the leading character's disability. The use of sound keeps the tension consistent, and the dramatic shifts from silence to noise keeps the blood pumping, that's for sure. Throw in a little black comedy and undertones of erotic sexual repression you've got the makings of a great film. It's the sort of film Hollywood really wants to make, but just can't.

policy: RENTERS CONTENTS PROTECTION
Issued by Oakfield Assurance
In this policy, "the Insurer" means Oakfield Assurance and "the Policyholder" means the person named in the schedule.

Article 1. Definitions
(a) Art and antiques means paintings, antiques, rugs and other works of art.
(b) Bicycles means bicycles and electric scooters.
(c) Family means the Policyholder's spouse or partner and any children who live with the Policyholder.
(d) High-risk items means jewellery, watches, laptops, games consoles and cameras.
(e) Portable electronics means laptops, tablets and mobile phones.
(f) Unoccupied means not lived in by the Policyholder or a member of the Policyholder's family for more than 45 consecutive days.

Article 2. Limits and excess
(a) Theft: limit $20,000 per incident; excess $250 per claim.
(b) Escape of Water: limit $30,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
(c) Accidental Damage: limit $5,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
(d) Flood: limit $20,000 per incident; excess $1,000 per claim.
(e) Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the excess is then deducted from the result.

Article 3. Escape of Water
(a) The Insurer will pay for contents damaged by water escaping from a fixed pipe, tank or domestic appliance.
(b) The most the Insurer will pay for Art and antiques under this section is $1,000 per incident.
(c) The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by water leaking gradually over a period of time.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by the failure of grout or sealant around baths and showers.

Article 4. Optional cover: Accidental Damage
(a) The Insurer will pay for sudden and unexpected accidental damage to the Policyholder's contents inside the home.
(b) This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Policyholder's schedule.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Portable electronics under this section is $500 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by pets.
(e) The Insurer will not pay for wear and tear, or damage that happens gradually.

Article 5. Theft
(a) The Insurer will pay for contents stolen from the Policyholder's home.
(b) The most the Insurer will pay for High-risk items under this section is $1,000 per incident.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Bicycles under this section is $800 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for theft while the home is unoccupied.
(e) The Insurer will not pay for theft where there is no sign of forced entry to the home. This exclusion does not apply where the thief gained entry by deception, for example by posing as a utility worker.
(f) The Insurer will not pay for theft from sheds, garages or other outbuildings. This exclusion does not apply if the outbuilding was locked and the theft involved forcible entry.

Article 6. General exclusions
(a) The Insurer will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
(b) The Insurer will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits the Insurer from paying.
(c) The Insurer will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.

Article 7. Making a claim
(a) The Policyholder must notify the Insurer of a claim within 90 days of the incident. The Insurer will not pay any claim notified after that time.
(b) The Insurer may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
(c) The Policyholder must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.

In this policy, "the Plan" means the Benefits Trust and "the Member" means the person named in the schedule.

Article 1. Definitions
(a) Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
(b) Frames means spectacle frames bought without new lenses.
(c) Hearing accessories means batteries, chargers and cleaning kits.
(d) Hearing aid replacement period means 24 months from the purchase of hearing aids funded by the plan.

Article 2. Limits and deductible
(a) Dental Care: limit $1,500 per treatment; deductible $50 per claim.

(c) Therapy Services: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $75 per claim.
(d) Hearing Care: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $150 per claim.

(a) The Plan will reimburse eye tests and prescription eyewear.

(a) The Plan will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
(b) The Plan will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits the Plan from paying.
(c) The Plan will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.

(a) The Member must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.

policy: EMPLOYEE HEALTH BENEFITS PLAN: SUMMARY PLAN DESCRIPTION
Issued by Cedar Benefits Services
In this policy, "the Plan" means Cedar Benefits Services and "the Member" means the person named in the schedule.

Article 1. Definitions
(a) Hearing accessories means batteries, chargers and cleaning kits.
(b) Hearing aid replacement period means 36 months from the purchase of hearing aids funded by the plan.
(c) Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in the Member's schedule.
(d) Premium means the amount the Member must pay for this policy, including any taxes.

Article 2. Limits and deductible
(a) Dental Care: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $100 per claim.
(b) Vision Care: limit $400 per treatment; deductible $40 per claim.
(c) Therapy Services: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $75 per claim.
(d) Hearing Care: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $150 per claim.
(e) The deductible is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

Article 3. Optional cover: Hearing Care
(a) The Plan will reimburse hearing tests and hearing aids.
(b) This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Member's schedule.
(c) The most the Plan will pay for Hearing accessories under this section is $150 per treatment.
(d) The Plan will not pay for replacement hearing aids bought within the hearing aid replacement period.

Article 4. Inflation
(a) The Plan may adjust limits at renewal in line with a published index of consumer prices.
(b) Any adjustment will be shown in the Member's renewal documents; limits do not change during a policy period.

Article 5. Instalment agreements
(a) If the Member pays by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
(b) Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

Article 6. General exclusions
(a) The Plan will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
(b) The Plan will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
(c) The Plan will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.

Article 7. Recovery of costs
(a) If the Plan pays a claim that is later found not to be covered, the Plan may ask the Member to repay the amount.

Article 8. Coordination of benefits
(a) If a treatment is also covered by another plan, the Plan will pay only the part of the cost that the other plan does not pay.
(b) The Member must tell the Plan about any other plan that covers the Member or the Member's dependants.

Article 9. Automatic renewal
(a) Unless the Member tells the Plan otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details the Plan holds.
(b) The Member can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting the Plan's helpline.

Article 10. Interpretation
(a) Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
(b) Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
(c) Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

Article 11. Making a claim
(a) The Member must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
(b) The Member must notify the Plan of a claim within 21 days of the treatment. The Plan will not pay any claim notified after that time.
(c) The Plan may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

Article 12. Changes in circumstances
(a) The Member must tell the Plan as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
(b) The Plan may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

## 1. Definitions
- **1.1** Accessories means cases, chargers and earbuds.

## 2. Limits and service fee
- **2.1** Accidental Damage: limit $800 per incident; service fee $79 per claim.
- **2.2** Breakdown: limit $600 per incident; service fee $25 per claim.
- **2.3** Theft and Loss: limit $1,200 per incident; service fee $149 per claim.

## 3. Optional cover: Theft and Loss
- **3.1** We will replace your device if it is stolen or lost.
- **3.2** This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
- **3.3** The most we will pay for Accessories under this section is $50 per incident.

## 4. Breakdown
- **4.1** We will repair or replace your device if it stops working because of an electrical or mechanical fault.

- **4.4** We will not pay for breakdowns during the manufacturer's warranty period.
- **4.5** We will not pay for breakdown caused by liquid getting into the device.

## 5. General exclusions
- **5.1** We will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
- **5.2** We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
- **5.3** We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.

## 6. Making a claim
- **6.1** You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.

state: War, Inc. - Corporations take over war in the future and use a lone assassin Brand Hauser (John Cusack) to do their wet-work against rival CEOs. A dark comedy satirizing the military and corporations alike. It was often difficult to figure out what exactly was going on. I kept waiting for things to make sense. There's no reason or method to the madness. It's considered by Cusack to be the "spiritual successor" to Grosse Point Blank. I.e., War is more or less a knock-off. We again see Cusack as an assassin protecting *spoiler* the person he's supposed to kill as he grips with his conscience. To be fair, John Cusack looks kind of credible taking out half a dozen guys with relative ease. The brief fights look good. The rest of the film does not. It's all quirky often bordering on bizarre. War Inc's not funny enough to be a parody, and too buoyant for anyone to even think about whatever the film's message might be, which I suppose might be the heartless ways that corporations, like war factions compete and scheme without a drop of consideration given to how they affect average citizens. Interesting, but the satire just doesn't work because it's not funny and at its heart the film has no heart. We're supposed to give a damn

# Employee Health Benefits Plan: Summary Plan Description
Issued by the Benefits Trust

## 1. Definitions
- **1.1** Dependant means your spouse or partner, or a child under 21 who is enrolled in the plan.
- **1.2** Major restorative work means crowns, bridges, root canal treatment and implants.
- **1.3** Orthodontics means braces and clear aligners.
- **1.4** Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
- **1.5** Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.

## 2. Limits and deductible
- **2.1** Dental Care: limit $1,500 per treatment; deductible $50 per claim.
- **2.2** Vision Care: limit $300 per treatment; deductible $25 per claim.
- **2.3** Therapy Services: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $75 per claim.
- **2.4** Hearing Care: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $100 per claim.
- **2.5** The deductible is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

## 3. Dental Care
- **3.1** We will reimburse the cost of dental treatment provided by a licensed dentist.
- **3.2** No cover applies under this section to any treatment that happens within the first 90 days after the policy start date.
- **3.3** The most we will pay for Major restorative work under this section is $500 per treatment.
- **3.4** The most we will pay for Orthodontics under this section is $800 per treatment.
- **3.5** We will not pay for treatment that is mainly cosmetic, such as whitening or veneers. This exclusion does not apply to treatment needed to repair damage caused by an accident.
- **3.6** We will not pay for treatment by a provider outside the plan's network. This exclusion does not apply to emergency treatment for sudden severe pain.

## 4. Appeals
- **4.1** If we decline all or part of a claim, you may appeal in writing within 60 days of the decision.
- **4.2** An appeal will be reviewed by someone who was not involved in the original decision.
- **4.3** We will give you a written decision on the appeal within 30 days.

## 5. General exclusions
- **5.1** We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
- **5.2** We will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
- **5.3** We will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by you.

## 6. Making a claim
- **6.1** You must notify us of a claim within 21 days of the treatment. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.
- **6.2** You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
- **6.3** We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

## 1. Definitions

policy: HOME CONTENTS INSURANCE POLICY
Issued by Keystone Home Mutual
In this policy, "the Insurer" means Keystone Home Mutual and "the Policyholder" means the person named in the schedule.

Article 1. Definitions
(a) Art and antiques means paintings, antiques, rugs and other works of art.
(b) Home means the private residence at the address shown in the schedule.
(c) Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in the Policyholder's schedule.

Article 2. Limits and excess
(a) Theft: limit $20,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
(b) Escape of Water: limit $30,000 per incident; excess $250 per claim.
(c) Accidental Damage: limit $5,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
(d) Flood: limit $20,000 per incident; excess $1,000 per claim.
(e) Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the excess is then deducted from the result.

Article 3. Escape of Water
(a) The Insurer will pay for contents damaged by water escaping from a fixed pipe, tank or domestic appliance.
(b) The most the Insurer will pay for Art and antiques under this section is $2,000 per incident.
(c) The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by water leaking gradually over a period of time.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by the failure of grout or sealant around baths and showers.

Article 4. Premium payment
(a) The Policyholder must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
(b) If an instalment is not paid within 14 days of its due date, the Insurer may cancel the policy after giving notice.

Article 5. Interest
(a) The Insurer will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

Article 6. Complaints
(a) If the Policyholder has a complaint, the Policyholder should first contact the Insurer's customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
(b) The Insurer will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
(c) If the Policyholder remains dissatisfied, the Policyholder may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

Article 7. General exclusions
(a) The Insurer will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
(b) The Insurer will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.

Article 8. Change of address
(a) The Policyholder must tell the Insurer within 30 days if the Policyholder changes the Policyholder's address.
(b) The Insurer may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

Article 9. Making a claim
(a) The Policyholder must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
(b) The Policyholder must notify the Insurer of a claim within 60 days of the incident. The Insurer will not pay any claim notified after that time.
(c) The Insurer may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

state: As gently as I can, I sincerely believe this movie is a waste of time. I did not find it the 'warm, emotionally satisfying' film others did. I found it boring, with music that distracted from the film. The story was thin, the characters overdrawn, and the direction pedestrian. Fooey. Now I'm going to write some more about this movie, so I make the 10 line minimum. There really isn't more to be said and brevity is important, but IMDb has its minimums, so here goes. Young eager kid finds nascent talent, seeks time with aging, embittered mentor in spite of father's cartoonish homophobia. Aging, embittered mentor turns out to drink a lot and teach very little. conflict arises. While I don't think this is a spoiler, I've added the warning in case someone feels this much information is too much. Mostly, I just found the film boring and pretentious. A waste of my time. I honestly don't understand what little fuss there seems to be, mostly on this web site, about the transcendent quality of this movie. I think it's really worth avoiding. But, as Dennis Miller used to say, "Maybe I'm wrong."

Issued by Cedar Benefits Services

PART I: Definitions
I.1  Family means the Member's spouse or partner and any children who live with the Member.
I.2  Frames means spectacle frames bought without new lenses.
I.3  Hearing accessories means batteries, chargers and cleaning kits.
I.4  Hearing aid replacement period means 36 months from the purchase of hearing aids funded by the plan.

PART II: Limits and deductible
II.1  Dental Care: limit $2,000 per treatment; deductible $50 per claim.
II.2  Vision Care: limit $400 per treatment; deductible $25 per claim.

PART IV: Vision Care

IV.2  The most the Plan will pay for Frames under this section is $120 per treatment.

policy: HOME CONTENTS INSURANCE POLICY
Issued by Oakfield Assurance

PART I: Definitions
I.1  Art and antiques means paintings, antiques, rugs and other works of art.
I.2  Bicycles means bicycles and electric scooters.
I.3  Contents means household goods and personal possessions that belong to the Policyholder or the Policyholder's family.
I.4  High-risk items means jewellery, watches, laptops, games consoles and cameras.
I.5  Portable electronics means laptops, tablets and mobile phones.
I.6  Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
I.7  Unoccupied means not lived in by the Policyholder or a member of the Policyholder's family for more than 30 consecutive days.

PART II: Limits and excess
II.1  Theft: limit $10,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
II.2  Escape of Water: limit $30,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
II.3  Accidental Damage: limit $3,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
II.4  Flood: limit $40,000 per incident; excess $1,000 per claim.
II.5  Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the excess is then deducted from the result.

PART III: Optional cover: Accidental Damage
III.1  The Insurer will pay for sudden and unexpected accidental damage to the Policyholder's contents inside the home.
III.2  This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Policyholder's schedule.
III.3  The most the Insurer will pay for Portable electronics under this section is $500 per incident.
III.4  The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by pets.
III.5  The Insurer will not pay for wear and tear, or damage that happens gradually.

PART IV: Escape of Water
IV.1  The Insurer will pay for contents damaged by water escaping from a fixed pipe, tank or domestic appliance.
IV.2  The most the Insurer will pay for Art and antiques under this section is $2,000 per incident.
IV.3  The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by water leaking gradually over a period of time.
IV.4  The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by the failure of grout or sealant around baths and showers.

PART V: Theft
V.1  The Insurer will pay for contents stolen from the Policyholder's home.
V.2  The most the Insurer will pay for High-risk items under this section is $1,000 per incident.
V.3  The most the Insurer will pay for Bicycles under this section is $800 per incident.
V.4  The Insurer will not pay for theft while the home is unoccupied.
V.5  The Insurer will not pay for theft where there is no sign of forced entry to the home. This exclusion does not apply where the thief gained entry by deception, for example by posing as a utility worker.
V.6  The Insurer will not pay for theft from sheds, garages or other outbuildings. This exclusion does not apply if the outbuilding was locked and the theft involved forcible entry.

PART VI: General exclusions
VI.1  The Insurer will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
VI.2  The Insurer will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Policyholder.
VI.3  The Insurer will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.

PART VII: Making a claim
VII.1  The Insurer may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
VII.2  The Policyholder must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
VII.3  The Policyholder must notify the Insurer of a claim within 30 days of the incident. The Insurer will not pay any claim notified after that time.

Terrible. Most recent issue is with Video OnDemand - with television shows, if you pause the show for a period time (say, while you open the door to greet and pay the pizza delivery guy), you run a risk of not being able to restart the show. At all. My husband and I have found the following workaround: we go to the non-HD version, start that, put it on mute, and let it play (since we're not allowed to fast foward) to the point where we paused, and then we watch from there. I'm currently waiting to get 40 minutes into an episode of Grey's Anatomy. Given how much we pay, it's ridiculous that this is the quality of service (and when we call Cox, they blame the network you were watching - nevermind that it happens on all of them). 

For context: I moved here from the Boston area four years ago - Comcast's offerinngs were light years ahead of Cox's at that time, and the services I have now are still well below the services I had in Boston in 2008.

Pass the buck, deliver crappy service, charge an arm and a leg. That's the business model. As soon as I have an option for television service that doesn't include Cox, I'll be taking it.

Is Claire trying to escape being a prostitute or not? Hard to tell. Why does she pick up the trick at the airport if she wants to escape that life? Why does she then not pick up tricks when she needs money in Seattle? Why do we have to see her dye her hair to what is virtually the exact same color? # Device Protection Plan Terms
Issued by Circuit Care Services

## 1. Definitions
- **1.1** Accessories means cases, chargers, earbuds and styluses.
- **1.2** Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
- **1.3** Limit means the most we will pay for all claims under a section arising from one incident.
- **1.4** Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
- **1.5** Wearables means smartwatches and fitness trackers.

## 2. Limits and service fee
- **2.1** Accidental Damage: limit $1,200 per incident; service fee $49 per claim.
- **2.2** Breakdown: limit $1,500 per incident; service fee $49 per claim.
- **2.3** Theft and Loss: limit $800 per incident; service fee $99 per claim.
- **2.4** Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the service fee is then deducted from the result.

## 3. Accidental Damage
- **3.1** We will repair or replace your device if it is accidentally damaged.
- **3.2** The most we will pay for Accessories under this section is $50 per incident.
- **3.3** The most we will pay for Wearables under this section is $250 per incident.
- **3.4** We will not pay for cosmetic damage, such as scratches or dents, that does not affect how the device works.
- **3.5** We will not pay for damage following a repair by anyone other than us or an authorised repairer. This exclusion does not apply if we approved the repair in writing beforehand.

## 4. General exclusions
- **4.1** We will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits us from paying.
- **4.2** We will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by you.
- **4.3** We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.

## 5. Making a claim
- **5.1** You must notify us of a claim within 21 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.
- **5.2** You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
- **5.3** We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

(b) Dental treatment means treatment of the teeth or gums.
(c) Hazardous activity means skydiving, motor racing, or trekking or climbing above 4,500 metres.
(d) Physiotherapy means treatment of muscles and joints by a physiotherapist.
(e) Pre-existing condition means any illness or injury for which the Insured Person received treatment or advice in the 3 months before the policy start date.
(f) Qualifying delay means a delay to the scheduled departure of more than 6 hours.

Article 2. Limits and excess
(a) Baggage and Personal Belongings: limit $1,500 per incident; excess $75 per claim.
(b) Emergency Medical Expenses: limit $50,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
(c) Trip Cancellation: limit $3,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
(d) Travel Delay: limit $300 per incident; excess $25 per claim.
(e) Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the excess is then deducted from the result.

Article 3. Emergency Medical Expenses
(a) The Insurer will pay reasonable and necessary emergency medical costs incurred during the trip.
(b) The most the Insurer will pay for Dental treatment under this section is $250 per incident.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Physiotherapy under this section is $500 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for treatment of a pre-existing condition.
(e) The Insurer will not pay for injury or illness arising from a hazardous activity. This exclusion does not apply if the Adventure Sports extension is shown in the Insured Person's schedule.
(f) The Insurer will not pay for any claim arising from the Insured Person's being under the influence of alcohol or drugs.

Article 4. Optional cover: Travel Delay
(a) The Insurer will pay reasonable costs of meals and accommodation if the Insured Person's outbound departure is delayed.
(b) This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Insured Person's schedule.
(c) The Insurer will not pay for any delay that is not a qualifying delay.

Article 5. General exclusions
(a) The Insurer will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
(b) The Insurer will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits the Insurer from paying.
(c) The Insurer will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.

Article 6. Making a claim
(a) The Insured Person must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
(b) The Insurer may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
(c) The Insured Person must notify the Insurer of a claim within 21 days of the incident. The Insurer will not pay any claim notified after that time.

Article 7. Geographical limits
(a) Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
(b) Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

HOME CONTENTS INSURANCE POLICY
Issued by Hearthstone Insurance plc

SECTION 1 - DEFINITIONS
1.1 Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
1.2 Portable electronics means laptops, tablets and mobile phones.

SECTION 2 - LIMITS AND EXCESS
2.1 Theft: limit $10,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
2.2 Escape of Water: limit $30,000 per incident; excess $250 per claim.
2.3 Accidental Damage: limit $5,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
2.4 Flood: limit $20,000 per incident; excess $1,000 per claim.
2.5 Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the excess is then deducted from the result.

SECTION 3 - OPTIONAL COVER: ACCIDENTAL DAMAGE
3.1 We will pay for sudden and unexpected accidental damage to your contents inside the home.
3.2 This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
3.3 The most we will pay for Portable electronics under this section is $750 per incident.
3.4 We will not pay for damage caused by pets.
3.5 We will not pay for wear and tear, or damage that happens gradually.

SECTION 4 - GENERAL EXCLUSIONS
4.1 We will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by you.
4.2 We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
4.3 We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.

SECTION 5 - MAKING A CLAIM
5.1 You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
5.2 We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
5.3 You must notify us of a claim within 90 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.

SECTION 6 - CLAIMS DOCUMENTS
6.1 You must provide, at your own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence we reasonably ask for.
6.2 We may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

We are drawn into strong feelings for the young, impressionable, yet highly courageous boy--who admires the American pilot. If you're looking for special effects, superman heroes, and magical endings--this movie is not for you. If you want to feel what it must have been like to dodge the persistent, amoral Nazis and their lack of compassion, then you will be enthralled by this movie. policy: RENTERS CONTENTS PROTECTION
Issued by Hearthstone Insurance plc

PART I: Definitions
I.1  Bicycles means bicycles and electric scooters.
I.2  Garden items means garden furniture, plants and outdoor tools.
I.3  High-risk items means jewellery, watches, laptops, games consoles and cameras.
I.4  Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
I.5  Outbuilding means a shed, garage or greenhouse within the boundaries of the home.
I.6  Unoccupied means not lived in by the Policyholder or a member of the Policyholder's family for more than 30 consecutive days.

PART II: Limits and excess
II.1  Theft: limit $40,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
II.2  Escape of Water: limit $30,000 per incident; excess $1,000 per claim.
II.3  Accidental Damage: limit $5,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
II.4  Flood: limit $20,000 per incident; excess $1,000 per claim.
II.5  The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

PART III: Theft
III.1  The Insurer will pay for contents stolen from the Policyholder's home.
III.2  The most the Insurer will pay for High-risk items under this section is $1,000 per incident.
III.3  The most the Insurer will pay for Bicycles under this section is $500 per incident.
III.4  The Insurer will not pay for theft while the home is unoccupied.
III.5  The Insurer will not pay for theft where there is no sign of forced entry to the home. This exclusion does not apply where the thief gained entry by deception, for example by posing as a utility worker.
III.6  The Insurer will not pay for theft from sheds, garages or other outbuildings. This exclusion does not apply if the outbuilding was locked and the theft involved forcible entry.

PART IV: Flood
IV.1  The Insurer will pay for contents damaged by flood water entering the Policyholder's home.
IV.2  No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 30 days after the policy start date.
IV.3  The most the Insurer will pay for Garden items under this section is $500 per incident.
IV.4  The Insurer will not pay for flood damage where a flood warning for the Policyholder's area had been issued before the policy started.

PART V: General exclusions
V.1  The Insurer will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
V.2  The Insurer will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
V.3  The Insurer will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.

PART VI: Making a claim
VI.1  The Insurer may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
VI.2  The Policyholder must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
VI.3  The Policyholder must notify the Insurer of a claim within 21 days of the incident. The Insurer will not pay any claim notified after that time.
