# Home Contents Insurance Policy
Issued by Hearthstone Insurance plc

## 1. Definitions
- **1.1** Portable electronics means laptops, tablets and mobile phones.
- **1.2** Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows your details, the covers you bought and any extensions.

## 2. Limits and excess
- **2.1** Theft: limit $40,000 per incident; excess $250 per claim.
- **2.2** Escape of Water: limit $30,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
- **2.3** Accidental Damage: limit $3,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
- **2.4** Flood: limit $40,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
- **2.5** The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

## 3. Interpretation
- **3.1** Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
- **3.2** Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
- **3.3** Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

## 4. Discounts
- **4.1** Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
- **4.2** If a condition for a discount stops being met, we may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

## 5. Severability
- **5.1** If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

## 6. Optional cover: Accidental Damage
- **6.1** We will pay for sudden and unexpected accidental damage to your contents inside the home.
- **6.2** This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
- **6.3** The most we will pay for Portable electronics under this section is $500 per incident.
- **6.4** We will not pay for damage caused by pets.
- **6.5** We will not pay for wear and tear, or damage that happens gradually.

## 7. General exclusions
- **7.1** We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
- **7.2** We will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by you.

## 8. Premium payment
- **8.1** You must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
- **8.2** If an instalment is not paid within 21 days of its due date, we may cancel the policy after giving notice.

## 9. Making a claim
- **9.1** You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
- **9.2** You must notify us of a claim within 21 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.
- **9.3** We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

## 10. Market conditions
- **10.1** If the replacement item is no longer available, we will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

## 11. Accessibility
- **11.1** This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

## 12. Tenant's improvements
- **12.1** If you rent the home, we will pay for damage to fixtures and fittings that you installed and are responsible for.
- **12.2** This cover applies only to improvements you paid for, not to items provided by the landlord.

## 13. Reasonable precautions
- **13.1** You must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
- **13.2** You must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

# Household Contents Cover: Policy Booklet

## 1. Definitions
- **1.1** Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by us, before any excess, limit or sublimit is applied.

## 2. Limits and excess

- **2.4** Flood: limit $20,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
- **2.5** Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the excess is then deducted from the result.

## 3. Optional cover: Accidental Damage
- **3.1** We will pay for sudden and unexpected accidental damage to your contents inside the home.

## 4. General exclusions
- **4.1** We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
- **4.2** We will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits us from paying.
- **4.3** We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.

## 5. Making a claim
- **5.1** You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
- **5.2** We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

- **7.1** You should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.

## 8. Interest
- **8.1** We will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

- **9.1** If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, we will pay only our proportionate share.
- **9.2** You must tell us about any other insurance that covers the same loss when you make a claim.

II.5  The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

PART III: Flood
III.1  The Insurer will pay for contents damaged by flood water entering the Policyholder's home.
III.2  No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 30 days after the policy start date.
III.3  The most the Insurer will pay for Garden items under this section is $500 per incident.
III.4  The Insurer will not pay for flood damage where a flood warning for the Policyholder's area had been issued before the policy started.

PART IV: General exclusions
IV.1  The Insurer will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.

PART V: Making a claim

VI.1  A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

PART VII: Geographical limits

PART VIII: Duty of fair presentation

IX.1  The Insurer will pay for food in a domestic freezer that spoils because of a rise or fall in temperature.
IX.2  The Insurer will not pay if the freezer is more than fifteen years old, or if the electricity supplier cut the supply deliberately.

PART X: Recovery of costs
X.1  If the Insurer pays a claim that is later found not to be covered, the Insurer may ask the Policyholder to repay the amount.

PART XI: Claims documents
XI.1  The Policyholder must provide, at the Policyholder's own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence the Insurer reasonably ask for.
XI.2  The Insurer may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

Usually I cut my own wood, but middle of last winter I found myself in a pinch running out of wood and having no time to cut more.

Went to Berry Bros and purchased a cord of mesquite. Apparently they get it from Hyder AZ. It's good, dry mesquite and has burned well, and I still have some leftover for this winter.

Many of the pieces are very large, and since it's mesquite, you would need a VERY big fire to get some of these pieces to burn. I used my axe (and even my maul a couple times) to split the pieces into smaller burnable ones. My only gripe would be that most of the pieces of their mesquite are not cut at even angles on the ends, so they will not stand up on their own when you set them down vertically to split. I needed to use a wedge the majority of the time so the logs would stand up on their own

Again this is a small gripe, but for what I spent I would like the wood to have even 90 degree angles on each side to facilitate easier splitting.

I will be back again if I find myself running out of wood this winter.

state: Decades of poor maintenance, the construction of a fourth story attic during the Coolidge administration, and the addition of a second-floor balcony over the south portico for Harry S. Truman took a great toll on the brick and sandstone structure built around a timber frame. By 1948, the house was declared to be in imminent danger of collapse, forcing President Truman to commission a reconstruction and to live across the street at Blair House from 1949 to 1951. The work, done by the firm of Philadelphia contractor John McShain, required the complete dismantling of the interior spaces, construction of a new load-bearing internal steel frame and the reconstruction of the original rooms within the new structure. The total cost of the renovations was about $5.7 million (US$54 million in 2018). Some modifications to the floor plan were made, the largest being the repositioning of the grand staircase to open into the Entrance Hall, rather than the Cross Hall. Central air conditioning was added, as well as two additional sub-basements providing space for workrooms, storage, and a bomb shelter. The Trumans moved back into the White House on March 27, 1952. While the house's structure was kept intact by the Truman reconstruction, much of the new interior finishes were generic, and of little historic value. Much of the original plasterwork, some dating back to the 1814--1816 rebuilding, was too damaged to reinstall, as was the original robust Beaux Arts paneling in the East Room. President Truman had the original timber frame sawed into paneling; the walls of the Vermeil Room, Library, China Room, and Map Room on the ground floor of the main residence were paneled in wood from the timbers.

policy: DEVICE PROTECTION PLAN TERMS
Issued by Brightline Device Cover
In this policy, "the Provider" means Brightline Device Cover and "the Customer" means the person named in the schedule.

Article 1. Definitions
(a) Accessories means cases, chargers, earbuds and styluses.
(b) Battery replacement means replacement batteries and battery repairs.
(c) Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
(d) Manufacturer's warranty period means the first 12 months after the device was bought.
(e) Wearables means smartwatches and fitness trackers.

Article 2. Limits and service fee
(a) Accidental Damage: limit $1,200 per incident; service fee $49 per claim.
(b) Breakdown: limit $1,500 per incident; service fee $25 per claim.
(c) Theft and Loss: limit $1,200 per incident; service fee $99 per claim.
(d) Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the service fee is then deducted from the result.

Article 3. Accidental Damage
(a) The Provider will repair or replace the Customer's device if it is accidentally damaged.
(b) The most the Provider will pay for Accessories under this section is $50 per incident.
(c) The most the Provider will pay for Wearables under this section is $250 per incident.
(d) The Provider will not pay for cosmetic damage, such as scratches or dents, that does not affect how the device works.
(e) The Provider will not pay for damage following a repair by anyone other than the Provider or an authorised repairer. This exclusion does not apply if the Provider approved the repair in writing beforehand.

Article 4. Breakdown
(a) The Provider will repair or replace the Customer's device if it stops working because of an electrical or mechanical fault.
(b) No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 45 days after the policy start date.
(c) The most the Provider will pay for Battery replacement under this section is $120 per incident.
(d) The Provider will not pay for breakdowns during the manufacturer's warranty period.
(e) The Provider will not pay for breakdown caused by liquid getting into the device.

Article 5. General exclusions
(a) The Provider will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Customer.
(b) The Provider will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.

Article 6. Making a claim
(a) The Provider may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
(b) The Customer must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
(c) The Customer must notify the Provider of a claim within 21 days of the incident. The Provider will not pay any claim notified after that time.

Her accent is delightful and her quiet, yet firm nature matches the young governess' character exactly. Timothy Dalton is an amazing Rochester. His passion and energy in the film makes me believe that he was born to play the brooding master of Thornfield Hall. I couldn't sleep at all the night after I had watched this miniseries. The plot is both haunting and inspiring. The characters are masterfully performed, and the story is incredible. This is the best version of Jane Eyre to ever appear on film. I read the book later and was amazed at how closely this miniseries followed Charolette Bronte's writing. Jane Eyre is now my favorite film and book. Issued by Northstar Underwriting

PART I: Definitions
I.1  Excursions and tickets means pre-booked excursions, tours, and event or theatre tickets.
I.2  Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in the Insured Person's schedule.
I.3  Travelling companion means a person who has booked to travel with the Insured Person on the same trip.

PART II: Limits and excess
II.1  Baggage and Personal Belongings: limit $1,500 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
II.2  Emergency Medical Expenses: limit $10,000 per incident; excess $250 per claim.
II.3  Trip Cancellation: limit $2,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
II.4  Travel Delay: limit $750 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
II.5  Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the excess is then deducted from the result.

PART III: Trip Cancellation
III.1  The Insurer will pay non-refundable travel and accommodation costs if the Insured Person must cancel the trip for a reason beyond the Insured Person's control.
III.2  No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 10 days after the policy start date.
III.3  The most the Insurer will pay for Excursions and tickets under this section is $300 per incident.
III.4  The Insurer will not pay for cancellation caused by a strike or other event that had been publicly announced before the Insured Person bought the policy.
III.5  The Insurer will not pay for cancellation because the Insured Person no longer wish to travel.

PART IV: Change of address
IV.1  The Insured Person must tell the Insurer within 30 days if the Insured Person changes the Insured Person's address.
IV.2  The Insurer may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

PART V: General exclusions
V.1  The Insurer will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
V.2  The Insurer will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.

PART VI: Making a claim
VI.1  The Insured Person must notify the Insurer of a claim within 14 days of the incident. The Insurer will not pay any claim notified after that time.
VI.2  The Insured Person must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
VI.3  The Insurer may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

STAFF HEALTH REIMBURSEMENT PLAN RULES
Issued by the Staff Welfare Fund

SECTION 1 - DEFINITIONS
1.1 Family means your spouse or partner and any children who live with you.
1.2 Hearing accessories means batteries, chargers and cleaning kits.
1.3 Hearing aid replacement period means 24 months from the purchase of hearing aids funded by the plan.
1.4 Massage therapy means sports massage, massage therapy and reflexology.

SECTION 2 - LIMITS AND DEDUCTIBLE
2.1 Dental Care: limit $2,000 per treatment; deductible $50 per claim.
2.2 Vision Care: limit $300 per treatment; deductible $25 per claim.
2.3 Therapy Services: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $50 per claim.
2.4 Hearing Care: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $100 per claim.
2.5 Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the deductible is then deducted from the result.

SECTION 3 - OPTIONAL COVER: HEARING CARE
3.1 We will reimburse hearing tests and hearing aids.
3.2 This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
3.3 The most we will pay for Hearing accessories under this section is $100 per treatment.
3.4 We will not pay for replacement hearing aids bought within the hearing aid replacement period.

SECTION 4 - THERAPY SERVICES
4.1 We will reimburse physiotherapy, osteopathy and counselling provided by a registered practitioner.
4.2 The most we will pay for Massage therapy under this section is $300 per treatment.
4.3 We will not pay for treatment of an injury covered by workers' compensation.
4.4 We will not pay for treatment by a practitioner who is not registered with the relevant professional body.

SECTION 5 - GENERAL EXCLUSIONS
5.1 We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
5.2 We will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
5.3 We will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.

SECTION 6 - MAKING A CLAIM
6.1 You must notify us of a claim within 21 days of the treatment. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.
6.2 You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
6.3 We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

SECTION 7 - DISCOUNTS
7.1 Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
7.2 If a condition for a discount stops being met, we may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

SECTION 8 - CONTRACTS (RIGHTS OF THIRD PARTIES)
8.1 A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

SECTION 9 - LEAVING THE PLAN
9.1 Cover ends on the day your employment ends or the day you stop being eligible, whichever is earlier.
9.2 Claims for treatment received before cover ended may be submitted up to 90 days afterwards.

SECTION 10 - NOTICES
10.1 Any notice we give under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address we hold.
10.2 Notices from you should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

SECTION 11 - DATA PROTECTION
11.1 We will use the personal information you provide to administer this policy and to handle claims.
11.2 We will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.

HOME CONTENTS INSURANCE POLICY
Issued by Oakfield Assurance

SECTION 1 - DEFINITIONS
1.1 Art and antiques means paintings, antiques, rugs and other works of art.
1.2 Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by us, before any excess, limit or sublimit is applied.
1.3 Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
1.4 Forcible entry means entry to the home that leaves visible damage to doors, windows or locks.

SECTION 2 - LIMITS AND EXCESS
2.1 Theft: limit $40,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
2.2 Escape of Water: limit $15,000 per incident; excess $1,000 per claim.
2.3 Accidental Damage: limit $5,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
2.4 Flood: limit $20,000 per incident; excess $1,000 per claim.
2.5 Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the excess is then deducted from the result.

SECTION 3 - ESCAPE OF WATER
3.1 We will pay for contents damaged by water escaping from a fixed pipe, tank or domestic appliance.
3.2 The most we will pay for Art and antiques under this section is $2,000 per incident.
3.3 We will not pay for damage caused by water leaking gradually over a period of time.
3.4 We will not pay for damage caused by the failure of grout or sealant around baths and showers.

SECTION 4 - GENERAL EXCLUSIONS
4.1 We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
4.2 We will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits us from paying.
4.3 We will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.

SECTION 5 - MAKING A CLAIM
5.1 We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
5.2 You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
5.3 You must notify us of a claim within 30 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.

SECTION 6 - RENEWAL
6.1 We will write to you at least 21 days before the end of the policy period with the renewal terms.
6.2 We are not obliged to offer renewal.

SECTION 7 - AUTOMATIC RENEWAL
7.1 Unless you tell us otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details we hold.
7.2 You can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting our helpline.

SECTION 8 - ASSIGNMENT
8.1 You cannot transfer your interest in this policy to anyone else without our written consent.

SECTION 9 - GOVERNING LAW
9.1 This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
9.2 Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

SECTION 10 - TAXES
10.1 The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
10.2 If the tax rate changes, we may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

SECTION 11 - SUBROGATION
11.1 We will be entitled to take over and conduct in your name the defence or settlement of any claim.
11.2 We can take action in your name to recover any payment we make from anyone responsible for the loss.

SECTION 12 - INTEREST
12.1 We will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

SECTION 13 - CLAIMS DOCUMENTS
13.1 You must provide, at your own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence we reasonably ask for.
13.2 We may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

SECTION 14 - THIRD-PARTY ADMINISTRATORS
14.1 We may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on our behalf.
14.2 Any company we appoint must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

# Annual Multi-Trip Travel Cover
Issued by Bluewater Assurance

## 1. Definitions
- **1.1** Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by us, before any excess, limit or sublimit is applied.
- **1.2** Dental treatment means treatment of the teeth or gums.
- **1.3** Family means your spouse or partner and any children who live with you.
- **1.4** Hazardous activity means skydiving, motor racing, or trekking or climbing above 4,000 metres.
- **1.5** Physiotherapy means treatment of muscles and joints by a physiotherapist.
- **1.6** Pre-existing condition means any illness or injury for which you received treatment or advice in the 6 months before the policy start date.
- **1.7** Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
- **1.8** Sports equipment means skis, snowboards, golf clubs, surfboards and bicycles.
- **1.9** Valuables means laptops, tablets, mobile phones, cameras, watches and jewellery.

## 2. Limits and excess
- **2.1** Baggage and Personal Belongings: limit $3,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
- **2.2** Emergency Medical Expenses: limit $25,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
- **2.3** Trip Cancellation: limit $3,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
- **2.4** Travel Delay: limit $500 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
- **2.5** The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

## 3. Baggage and Personal Belongings
- **3.1** We will pay for the loss of, theft of, or damage to your baggage and personal belongings during the trip.
- **3.2** The most we will pay for Valuables under this section is $500 per incident.
- **3.3** The most we will pay for Sports equipment under this section is $300 per incident.
- **3.4** We will not pay for loss or theft of property left unattended in a vehicle or in a public place. This exclusion does not apply to property locked out of sight in the boot or trunk of a locked vehicle.
- **3.5** We will not pay for loss caused by confiscation or detention by customs or other officials.
- **3.6** We will not pay for damage caused by wear and tear or gradual deterioration.

## 4. Emergency Medical Expenses
- **4.1** We will pay reasonable and necessary emergency medical costs incurred during the trip.
- **4.2** The most we will pay for Dental treatment under this section is $250 per incident.
- **4.3** The most we will pay for Physiotherapy under this section is $500 per incident.
- **4.4** We will not pay for treatment of a pre-existing condition.
- **4.5** We will not pay for injury or illness arising from a hazardous activity. This exclusion does not apply if the Adventure Sports extension is shown in your schedule.
- **4.6** We will not pay for any claim arising from your being under the influence of alcohol or drugs.

## 5. General exclusions
- **5.1** We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
- **5.2** We will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by you.

## 6. Making a claim
- **6.1** We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
- **6.2** You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
- **6.3** You must notify us of a claim within 30 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.

policy: SINGLE-TRIP TRAVEL PROTECTION PLAN
Issued by Compass Mutual

PART I: Definitions
I.1  Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
I.2  Excursions and tickets means pre-booked excursions, tours, and event or theatre tickets.
I.3  Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
I.4  Qualifying delay means a delay to the scheduled departure of more than 12 hours.
I.5  Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.

PART II: Limits and excess
II.1  Baggage and Personal Belongings: limit $3,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
II.2  Emergency Medical Expenses: limit $10,000 per incident; excess $250 per claim.
II.3  Trip Cancellation: limit $5,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
II.4  Travel Delay: limit $300 per incident; excess $25 per claim.
II.5  The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

PART III: Optional cover: Travel Delay
III.1  The Insurer will pay reasonable costs of meals and accommodation if the Insured Person's outbound departure is delayed.
III.2  This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Insured Person's schedule.
III.3  The Insurer will not pay for any delay that is not a qualifying delay.

PART IV: Trip Cancellation
IV.1  The Insurer will pay non-refundable travel and accommodation costs if the Insured Person must cancel the trip for a reason beyond the Insured Person's control.
IV.2  No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 14 days after the policy start date.
IV.3  The most the Insurer will pay for Excursions and tickets under this section is $200 per incident.
IV.4  The Insurer will not pay for cancellation caused by a strike or other event that had been publicly announced before the Insured Person bought the policy.
IV.5  The Insurer will not pay for cancellation because the Insured Person no longer wish to travel.

PART V: General exclusions
V.1  The Insurer will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits the Insurer from paying.
V.2  The Insurer will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
V.3  The Insurer will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.

PART VI: Making a claim
VI.1  The Insurer may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
VI.2  The Insured Person must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
VI.3  The Insured Person must notify the Insurer of a claim within 14 days of the incident. The Insurer will not pay any claim notified after that time.

The film's main theme is fate and small, seemingly insignificant things that can greatly change the future. In some ways this reminds me of the film SLIDING DOORS, though instead of focusing on one random event, seemingly random stuff happens repeatedly and each one helps build to the cute conclusion. Plus, an odd bald guy seems to understand all this and he talks about this during one brief scene--like he's some sort of omnipotent being but there's absolutely no explanation of him in the film (like the two guys that fight each other in the clock tower in THE HUDSUCKER PROXY). The DVD jacket shows just Audrey Tautou. This is capitalize on her success in AMELIE, though she is only one of many actors in the film and there is no one starring role. The pace is brisk, the acting fine and the conclusion isn't bad at all. The only reason I didn't score it higher is that some of the characters were a bit uninteresting and I think the movie could have perhaps been tightened up with a few less subplots.

(a) The Plan will reimburse the cost of dental treatment provided by a licensed dentist.
(b) No cover applies under this section to any treatment that happens within the first 60 days after the policy start date.
(c) The most the Plan will pay for Major restorative work under this section is $500 per treatment.
(d) The most the Plan will pay for Orthodontics under this section is $800 per treatment.
(e) The Plan will not pay for treatment that is mainly cosmetic, such as whitening or veneers. This exclusion does not apply to treatment needed to repair damage caused by an accident.
(f) The Plan will not pay for treatment by a provider outside the plan's network. This exclusion does not apply to emergency treatment for sudden severe pain.

Article 4. General exclusions
(a) The Plan will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
(b) The Plan will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
(c) The Plan will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.

Article 5. Environmental commitment
(a) Where practical, the Plan will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
(b) The Member may ask for a new part instead, and the Plan will tell the Member whether any additional cost would apply.

Article 6. Wellness allowance
(a) Each plan year the Member may claim up to $100 towards a gym membership or fitness class.
(b) The wellness allowance is not subject to any deductible and does not count towards other limits.

Article 7. Making a claim
(a) The Member must notify the Plan of a claim within 60 days of the treatment. The Plan will not pay any claim notified after that time.
(b) The Plan may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
(c) The Member must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.

Article 8. Customer support
(a) The Plan's helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
(b) Outside these hours the Member can leave a message and the Plan will call back on the next working day.

state: This is a fantastic series first and foremost. It is very well done and very interesting. As a huge WWII buff, I had learned a lot before seeing this series. One of the best things this has going for it is all the interviews with past individuals back when the war was relatively fresh in their minds, comparatively speaking that is. It is nothing against the men that you see getting interviewed in the programs of today, it is just that most of these men weren't really involved in the upper echelons of what was happening then. One of the best parts is the narrating by Sir Laurence Oliver. I would recommend this to anyone that wants to learn about WWII, but really think only the die-hards (such as myself) will want to buy this or watch it more than once. My only real complaint about this entire series is that some of the facts aren't quite as accurate as we now know. Especially with the information about Soviet Union is exaggerated or just plain inaccurate in places. That information is now different we now know because of the fall of the USSR. policy: TRAVEL INSURANCE POLICY WORDING
Issued by Compass Mutual
In this policy, "the Insurer" means Compass Mutual and "the Insured Person" means the person named in the schedule.

Article 1. Definitions
(a) Dental treatment means treatment of the teeth or gums.
(b) Excursions and tickets means pre-booked excursions, tours, and event or theatre tickets.
(c) Hazardous activity means skydiving, motor racing, or trekking or climbing above 4,500 metres.
(d) Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
(e) Physiotherapy means treatment of muscles and joints by a physiotherapist.
(f) Pre-existing condition means any illness or injury for which the Insured Person received treatment or advice in the 6 months before the policy start date.
(g) Qualifying delay means a delay to the scheduled departure of more than 12 hours.

Article 2. Limits and excess
(a) Baggage and Personal Belongings: limit $3,000 per incident; excess $75 per claim.
(b) Emergency Medical Expenses: limit $10,000 per incident; excess $150 per claim.
(c) Trip Cancellation: limit $3,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
(d) Travel Delay: limit $300 per incident; excess $25 per claim.
(e) Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the excess is then deducted from the result.

Article 3. Emergency Medical Expenses
(a) The Insurer will pay reasonable and necessary emergency medical costs incurred during the trip.
(b) The most the Insurer will pay for Dental treatment under this section is $250 per incident.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Physiotherapy under this section is $500 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for treatment of a pre-existing condition.
(e) The Insurer will not pay for injury or illness arising from a hazardous activity. This exclusion does not apply if the Adventure Sports extension is shown in the Insured Person's schedule.
(f) The Insurer will not pay for any claim arising from the Insured Person's being under the influence of alcohol or drugs.

Article 4. Trip Cancellation
(a) The Insurer will pay non-refundable travel and accommodation costs if the Insured Person must cancel the trip for a reason beyond the Insured Person's control.
(b) No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 10 days after the policy start date.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Excursions and tickets under this section is $200 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for cancellation caused by a strike or other event that had been publicly announced before the Insured Person bought the policy.
(e) The Insurer will not pay for cancellation because the Insured Person no longer wish to travel.

Article 5. Optional cover: Travel Delay
(a) The Insurer will pay reasonable costs of meals and accommodation if the Insured Person's outbound departure is delayed.
(b) This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Insured Person's schedule.
(c) The Insurer will not pay for any delay that is not a qualifying delay.

Article 6. General exclusions
(a) The Insurer will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
(b) The Insurer will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.

Article 7. Making a claim
(a) The Insured Person must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
(b) The Insurer may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
(c) The Insured Person must notify the Insurer of a claim within 14 days of the incident. The Insurer will not pay any claim notified after that time.

I look for story and movement and a fulfillment of arrival, none of which did I find in this film. 5.1 We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.

state: If you "get it", it's magnificent. If you don't, it's decent. Please understand that "getting it" does not necessarily mean you've gone through a school shooting. There is so much more to this movie that, at times, the school shooting becomes insignificant. Above all, it's a movie about acceptance, both superficially--of a traumatic event, but also of people who are different for whatever reason. It's also a movie about unendurable pain, and how different people endure it. In this case, the contrast between Alicia's rage and Deanna's obsession creates an atmosphere of such palpable anxiety that halfway through the movie we wonder how the director could possibly pull a happy ending out of his hat. Thankfully, the audience is given credit for being human beings; our intelligence is not insulted by a sappy, implausibly moralistic ending. Above and beyond that, I try to keep a clear head about movies being fiction and all that. Yet I must admit, I cried like a lost little baby during this movie. There were certain things about it that hit *very* close to home and opened up some old wounds that never quite healed. But that is not necessarily a bad thing.

Issued by the Staff Welfare Fund

PART I: Definitions
I.1  Dependant means the Member's spouse or partner, or a child under 21 who is enrolled in the plan.
I.2  Frames means spectacle frames bought without new lenses.
I.3  Major restorative work means crowns, bridges, root canal treatment and implants.
I.4  Orthodontics means braces and clear aligners.
I.5  Replacement period means 24 months from the date of the Member's last eyewear claim.

PART II: Limits and deductible
II.1  Dental Care: limit $1,500 per treatment; deductible $100 per claim.
II.2  Vision Care: limit $300 per treatment; deductible $25 per claim.
II.3  Therapy Services: limit $1,500 per treatment; deductible $75 per claim.
II.4  Hearing Care: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $100 per claim.
II.5  Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the deductible is then deducted from the result.

PART III: Dental Care
III.1  The Plan will reimburse the cost of dental treatment provided by a licensed dentist.
III.2  No cover applies under this section to any treatment that happens within the first 60 days after the policy start date.
III.3  The most the Plan will pay for Major restorative work under this section is $500 per treatment.
III.4  The most the Plan will pay for Orthodontics under this section is $600 per treatment.
III.5  The Plan will not pay for treatment that is mainly cosmetic, such as whitening or veneers. This exclusion does not apply to treatment needed to repair damage caused by an accident.
III.6  The Plan will not pay for treatment by a provider outside the plan's network. This exclusion does not apply to emergency treatment for sudden severe pain.

PART IV: Vision Care

IV.2  The most the Plan will pay for Frames under this section is $120 per treatment.
IV.3  The Plan will not pay for eyewear without prescription lenses.
IV.4  The Plan will not pay for a further eyewear claim within the replacement period.

PART V: General exclusions
V.1  The Plan will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Member.
V.2  The Plan will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.

PART VI: Making a claim
VI.1  The Plan may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
VI.2  The Member must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
VI.3  The Member must notify the Plan of a claim within 30 days of the treatment. The Plan will not pay any claim notified after that time.

PART VII: Appeals
VII.1  If the Plan declines all or part of a claim, the Member may appeal in writing within 60 days of the decision.
VII.2  An appeal will be reviewed by someone who was not involved in the original decision.
VII.3  The Plan will give the Member a written decision on the appeal within 30 days.

PART VIII: Eligibility
VIII.1  Employees who work at least 20 hours a week are eligible to join the plan from their first day of employment.
VIII.2  Contractors, agency workers and employees on unpaid leave of more than three months are not eligible.

PART IX: Arbitration
IX.1  If the Plan accepts a claim but disagree with the Member about the amount, the difference will be referred to an arbitrator appointed by both parties.
IX.2  Where arbitration applies, obtaining an award is a condition precedent to any legal action against the Plan.

In this policy, "the Provider" means Tessera Warranty Company and "the Customer" means the person named in the schedule.

Article 1. Definitions
(a) Battery replacement means replacement batteries and battery repairs.

(c) Theft and Loss: limit $800 per incident; service fee $149 per claim.
(d) Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the service fee is then deducted from the result.

Article 3. Breakdown
(a) The Provider will repair or replace the Customer's device if it stops working because of an electrical or mechanical fault.
(b) No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 45 days after the policy start date.
(c) The most the Provider will pay for Battery replacement under this section is $80 per incident.
(d) The Provider will not pay for breakdowns during the manufacturer's warranty period.
(e) The Provider will not pay for breakdown caused by liquid getting into the device.

Article 4. General exclusions
(a) The Provider will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits the Provider from paying.
(b) The Provider will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
(c) The Provider will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.

Article 5. Notices
(a) Any notice the Provider gives under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address the Provider holds.
(b) Notices from the Customer should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

Article 6. Records and evidence
(a) The Customer should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.
(b) Where proof of value is missing, the Provider may base any settlement on the price of a comparable item.
(c) The Provider may ask for evidence of how and when an item was acquired.

Article 7. Complaints
(a) If the Customer has a complaint, the Customer should first contact the Provider's customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
(b) The Provider will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
(c) If the Customer remains dissatisfied, the Customer may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

Article 8. Making a claim
(a) The Customer must notify the Provider of a claim within 90 days of the incident. The Provider will not pay any claim notified after that time.
(b) The Customer must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
(c) The Provider may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

Article 9. Interpretation
(a) Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
(b) Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
(c) Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

Article 10. Software support
(a) The Provider's helpline can give advice on setting up and using the Customer's device.
(b) Software support does not include fixing problems caused by third-party apps or unofficial operating systems.

policy: HOME CONTENTS INSURANCE POLICY
Issued by Keystone Home Mutual

PART I: Definitions
I.1  Bicycles means bicycles and electric scooters.
I.2  Garden items means garden furniture, plants and outdoor tools.
I.3  High-risk items means jewellery, watches, laptops, games consoles and cameras.
I.4  Outbuilding means a shed, garage or greenhouse within the boundaries of the home.
I.5  Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
I.6  Unoccupied means not lived in by the Policyholder or a member of the Policyholder's family for more than 30 consecutive days.

PART II: Limits and excess
II.1  Theft: limit $10,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
II.2  Escape of Water: limit $15,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
II.3  Accidental Damage: limit $2,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
II.4  Flood: limit $20,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
II.5  The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

PART III: Flood
III.1  The Insurer will pay for contents damaged by flood water entering the Policyholder's home.
III.2  No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 14 days after the policy start date.
III.3  The most the Insurer will pay for Garden items under this section is $500 per incident.
III.4  The Insurer will not pay for flood damage where a flood warning for the Policyholder's area had been issued before the policy started.

PART IV: Theft
IV.1  The Insurer will pay for contents stolen from the Policyholder's home.
IV.2  The most the Insurer will pay for High-risk items under this section is $2,500 per incident.
IV.3  The most the Insurer will pay for Bicycles under this section is $800 per incident.
IV.4  The Insurer will not pay for theft while the home is unoccupied.
IV.5  The Insurer will not pay for theft where there is no sign of forced entry to the home. This exclusion does not apply where the thief gained entry by deception, for example by posing as a utility worker.
IV.6  The Insurer will not pay for theft from sheds, garages or other outbuildings. This exclusion does not apply if the outbuilding was locked and the theft involved forcible entry.

PART V: General exclusions
V.1  The Insurer will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
V.2  The Insurer will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.

PART VI: Making a claim
VI.1  The Policyholder must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
VI.2  The Policyholder must notify the Insurer of a claim within 30 days of the incident. The Insurer will not pay any claim notified after that time.
VI.3  The Insurer may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

PART VII: Interpretation
VII.1  Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
VII.2  Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
VII.3  Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

PART VIII: Severability
VIII.1  If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

PART IX: Renewal
IX.1  The Insurer will write to the Policyholder at least 21 days before the end of the policy period with the renewal terms.
IX.2  The Insurer is not obliged to offer renewal.

PART X: Tenant's improvements
X.1  If the Policyholder rents the home, the Insurer will pay for damage to fixtures and fittings that the Policyholder installed and are responsible for.
X.2  This cover applies only to improvements the Policyholder paid for, not to items provided by the landlord.

Issued by the Benefits Trust

SECTION 1 - DEFINITIONS

2.1 Dental Care: limit $2,000 per treatment; deductible $100 per claim.
2.2 Vision Care: limit $400 per treatment; deductible $25 per claim.
2.3 Therapy Services: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $50 per claim.
2.4 Hearing Care: limit $2,000 per treatment; deductible $100 per claim.
2.5 Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the deductible is then deducted from the result.

SECTION 3 - VISION CARE
3.1 We will reimburse eye tests and prescription eyewear.
3.2 The most we will pay for Frames under this section is $120 per treatment.
3.3 We will not pay for eyewear without prescription lenses.
3.4 We will not pay for a further eyewear claim within the replacement period.

SECTION 4 - OPTIONAL COVER: HEARING CARE
4.1 We will reimburse hearing tests and hearing aids.
4.2 This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
4.3 The most we will pay for Hearing accessories under this section is $100 per treatment.
4.4 We will not pay for replacement hearing aids bought within the hearing aid replacement period.

SECTION 5 - DENTAL CARE
5.1 We will reimburse the cost of dental treatment provided by a licensed dentist.
5.2 No cover applies under this section to any treatment that happens within the first 90 days after the policy start date.
5.3 The most we will pay for Major restorative work under this section is $750 per treatment.

SECTION 6 - GENERAL EXCLUSIONS
6.1 We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
6.2 We will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.

Issued by Bluewater Assurance

PART I: Definitions
I.1  Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by the Insurer, before any excess, limit or sublimit is applied.
I.2  Excursions and tickets means pre-booked excursions, tours, and event or theatre tickets.
I.3  Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
I.4  Public transport means any scheduled train, bus, coach, ferry or aircraft.
I.5  Qualifying delay means a delay to the scheduled departure of more than 6 hours.

PART II: Limits and excess
II.1  Baggage and Personal Belongings: limit $1,500 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
II.2  Emergency Medical Expenses: limit $10,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
II.3  Trip Cancellation: limit $2,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
II.4  Travel Delay: limit $300 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
II.5  Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the excess is then deducted from the result.

PART III: Optional cover: Travel Delay
III.1  The Insurer will pay reasonable costs of meals and accommodation if the Insured Person's outbound departure is delayed.
III.2  This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Insured Person's schedule.
III.3  The Insurer will not pay for any delay that is not a qualifying delay.

PART IV: Trip Cancellation
IV.1  The Insurer will pay non-refundable travel and accommodation costs if the Insured Person must cancel the trip for a reason beyond the Insured Person's control.
IV.2  No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 10 days after the policy start date.
IV.3  The most the Insurer will pay for Excursions and tickets under this section is $200 per incident.
IV.4  The Insurer will not pay for cancellation caused by a strike or other event that had been publicly announced before the Insured Person bought the policy.
IV.5  The Insurer will not pay for cancellation because the Insured Person no longer wish to travel.

PART V: General exclusions
V.1  The Insurer will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
V.2  The Insurer will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Insured Person.

PART VI: Making a claim
VI.1  The Insurer may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
VI.2  The Insured Person must notify the Insurer of a claim within 14 days of the incident. The Insurer will not pay any claim notified after that time.
VI.3  The Insured Person must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.

state: 'Five Days' is billed as something special, a crime drama that consists of a series of episodes, each set on one particular day of a police enquiry. But in fact, this element of the story turns out to be rather less significant than might at first be thought, as the fact that the action in each episode is confined to 24 hours is hardly noticeable, and very little distinguishes the program from countless other crime stories. In fact one almost can't help drawing comparisons to the last 'Prime Suspect', as one of the sub-plots focuses on a single, cynical female cop approaching retirement: and it's not just the absence of Helen Mirren that makes the comparisons unfavourable. There's a lot of earnest over-emoting, manipulative music and a set of characters seemingly contrived so that each one is in some sense sympathetic, in another suspicious. And it's possible to guess the guilty party well before the end, not because of the internal dynamic of the story, but rather because of the construction of the drama as a whole: certain things must be true, to justify the way that the series focuses on certain characters at certain times. state: A not bad but also not so great heist film. Kirk Douglas is a recently released from prison safe-cracker who, after turning down an offer from the Mob, decides to pull the job himself. He recruits circus gymnast Giuliano Gemma. Mayhem ensues. Douglas and Gemma soon find themselves pursued by mafia goon Romano Puppo as well as entangled in a really goofy love triangle with Douglas's infinitely patient girlfriend (Florinda Bolkan). Director Michele Lupo keeps the pace moving quickly and there's at least one excellent and creative car chase sequence involving Puppo & Gemma. Though an Italian production, most of the filming appears to have been done in Germany. Douglas is fine, not just slumming it in an Giallo quickie. The striking Bolkan gives a terrific performance. The music is by Ennio Morricone and the cinematography is by the great Tonino Delli Colli, who managed to work with everyone in Italy (from Wertmuller and Fellini to Pasolini and Leone).

STAFF HEALTH REIMBURSEMENT PLAN RULES
Issued by Cedar Benefits Services

SECTION 1 - DEFINITIONS
1.1 Family means your spouse or partner and any children who live with you.
1.2 Major restorative work means crowns, bridges, root canal treatment and implants.
1.3 Orthodontics means braces and clear aligners.
1.4 Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows your details, the covers you bought and any extensions.

SECTION 2 - LIMITS AND DEDUCTIBLE
2.1 Dental Care: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $100 per claim.
2.2 Vision Care: limit $500 per treatment; deductible $25 per claim.
2.3 Therapy Services: limit $1,500 per treatment; deductible $75 per claim.
2.4 Hearing Care: limit $2,000 per treatment; deductible $100 per claim.
2.5 Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the deductible is then deducted from the result.

SECTION 3 - DENTAL CARE
3.1 We will reimburse the cost of dental treatment provided by a licensed dentist.
3.2 No cover applies under this section to any treatment that happens within the first 90 days after the policy start date.
3.3 The most we will pay for Major restorative work under this section is $500 per treatment.
3.4 The most we will pay for Orthodontics under this section is $800 per treatment.
3.5 We will not pay for treatment that is mainly cosmetic, such as whitening or veneers. This exclusion does not apply to treatment needed to repair damage caused by an accident.
3.6 We will not pay for treatment by a provider outside the plan's network. This exclusion does not apply to emergency treatment for sudden severe pain.

SECTION 4 - GENERAL EXCLUSIONS
4.1 We will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
4.2 We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
4.3 We will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by you.

SECTION 5 - MAKING A CLAIM
5.1 You must notify us of a claim within 30 days of the treatment. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.
5.2 You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
5.3 We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

SECTION 6 - ELIGIBILITY
6.1 Employees who work at least 20 hours a week are eligible to join the plan from their first day of employment.
6.2 Contractors, agency workers and employees on unpaid leave of more than three months are not eligible.

SECTION 7 - EXCHANGE OF INFORMATION
7.1 To prevent fraud, we may check the details you give against public records and industry databases.
7.2 We may contact previous insurers to confirm your claims history.

SECTION 8 - CUSTOMER SUPPORT
8.1 Our helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
8.2 Outside these hours you can leave a message and we will call back on the next working day.

SECTION 9 - CLAIMS DOCUMENTS
9.1 You must provide, at your own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence we reasonably ask for.
9.2 We may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

SECTION 10 - CHANGES IN CIRCUMSTANCES
10.1 You must tell us as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
10.2 We may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

SECTION 11 - INTERPRETATION
11.1 Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
11.2 Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
11.3 Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

state: This film should have been fun. A young Lea Thompson, a young Joaquin Phoenix... and Terry O'Quinn. In space. But it dragged on, had unlovable characters and had no target audience. Some kids go to a space camp and are accidentally launched into space by a robot friend of theirs (named, appropriately, Jinx). The space scenes are then long, repetitive (the same accident happens twice) and either cheesy or frightening depending on your point of view. Adults will be bored and cheesed out, kids might be scared as the way this was filmed really leaves an eerie sense about it. There is a budding romance, but unlike the shuttle -- this never takes off. Why it is included in the first place is unclear, except maybe to add extra tension between the characters - but it failed if that was the idea. A young Lea Thompson should be quirky and attractive, right? I mean, "Back to the Future" is great. But no, she was irritating and average-looking. Not someone you'd want to date, have as a friend or even consider as a role model. Joaquin Phoenix? He's really lucky he ever appeared in movies again this performance. Maybe he can act like Mikey in the Life Cereal commercials, but he doesn't seem to know how to be a normal boy.

state: A pendulum is a weight suspended from a pivot so that it can swing freely. When a pendulum is displaced sideways from its resting, equilibrium position, it is subject to a restoring force due to gravity that will accelerate it back toward the equilibrium position. When released, the restoring force acting on the pendulum's mass causes it to oscillate about the equilibrium position, swinging back and forth. The time for one complete cycle, a left swing and a right swing, is called the period. The period depends on the length of the pendulum and also to a slight degree on the amplitude, the width of the pendulum's swing.

You see brilliantly downplayed idiots who yet again find themselves in a situation too big for their brains. Throw a Bruce Willis or a Arnold Schwarzeneggar into this plot and it becomes a big blockbuster movie. Bill and Ted go into the story with the same level of sincerity, only it's Bill and Ted. PART V: Optional cover: Travel Delay
V.1  The Insurer will pay reasonable costs of meals and accommodation if the Insured Person's outbound departure is delayed.
V.2  This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Insured Person's schedule.

PART VI: Missed departure
VI.1  The Insurer will pay reasonable additional travel and accommodation costs to reach the Insured Person's destination if the Insured Person arrives too late to board the Insured Person's booked transport because public transport fails.

PART VII: Other insurance
VII.1  If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, the Insurer will pay only the Insurer's proportionate share.
VII.2  The Insured Person must tell the Insurer about any other insurance that covers the same loss when the Insured Person makes a claim.

PART VIII: General exclusions
VIII.1  The Insurer will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.

PART XII: Changes in circumstances
XII.1  The Insured Person must tell the Insurer as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.

I'm not sure if it's because of the day and time but they are typically understaffed, service is slow and the food is poor. The burger I had last night tasted like it had been under a heat lamp for a while, along with the onion rings.

My wife's cup of chili was supposed to be "spicy", but was neither spicy nor hot, as in temperature. Her fries also seemed to suffer from being scraped from the bottom of the pile.

Next is the noise. I know its a sports bar and it's going to get noisy, but why play loud rock music on top of that? We couldn't hear ourselves think and when we asked for the music to be turned down they did it, but only for about five minutes. There were about six couples at tables, and another dozen or so at the bar, and nobody was watching the games or, it seemed, listening to the music. 

Lastly, no Wi-Fi. What's up with that? I asked and they said it's because they don't want people "camping out". People camp out in a sports bar? Really?

Gave this place several chances but likely won't be back.

# Annual Multi-Trip Travel Cover
Issued by Northstar Underwriting

## 1. Definitions
- **1.1** Excursions and tickets means pre-booked excursions, tours, and event or theatre tickets.
- **1.2** Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
- **1.3** Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
- **1.4** Sports equipment means skis, snowboards, golf clubs, surfboards and bicycles.
- **1.5** Valuables means laptops, tablets, mobile phones, cameras, watches and jewellery.

## 2. Limits and excess
- **2.1** Baggage and Personal Belongings: limit $1,500 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
- **2.2** Emergency Medical Expenses: limit $10,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
- **2.3** Trip Cancellation: limit $5,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
- **2.4** Travel Delay: limit $500 per incident; excess $25 per claim.
- **2.5** The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

## 3. Trip Cancellation
- **3.1** We will pay non-refundable travel and accommodation costs if you must cancel the trip for a reason beyond your control.
- **3.2** No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 10 days after the policy start date.
- **3.3** The most we will pay for Excursions and tickets under this section is $300 per incident.
- **3.4** We will not pay for cancellation caused by a strike or other event that had been publicly announced before you bought the policy.
- **3.5** We will not pay for cancellation because you no longer wish to travel.

## 4. Baggage and Personal Belongings
- **4.1** We will pay for the loss of, theft of, or damage to your baggage and personal belongings during the trip.
- **4.2** The most we will pay for Valuables under this section is $250 per incident.
- **4.3** The most we will pay for Sports equipment under this section is $300 per incident.
- **4.4** We will not pay for loss or theft of property left unattended in a vehicle or in a public place. This exclusion does not apply to property locked out of sight in the boot or trunk of a locked vehicle.
- **4.5** We will not pay for loss caused by confiscation or detention by customs or other officials.
- **4.6** We will not pay for damage caused by wear and tear or gradual deterioration.

## 5. General exclusions
- **5.1** We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
- **5.2** We will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by you.

## 6. Making a claim
- **6.1** You must notify us of a claim within 21 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.
- **6.2** You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
- **6.3** We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

We learn that Hollywood is a nest of viper's and decadents. No big news there. More interesting we learn what a washed up director is willing to do to regain his position of power in the entertainment industry and/or political establishment. policy: RENTERS CONTENTS PROTECTION
Issued by Keystone Home Mutual

PART I: Definitions
I.1  Art and antiques means paintings, antiques, rugs and other works of art.
I.2  Bicycles means bicycles and electric scooters.
I.3  Family means the Policyholder's spouse or partner and any children who live with the Policyholder.
I.4  Garden items means garden furniture, plants and outdoor tools.
I.5  High-risk items means jewellery, watches, laptops, games consoles and cameras.
I.6  Home means the private residence at the address shown in the schedule.
I.7  Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
I.8  Unoccupied means not lived in by the Policyholder or a member of the Policyholder's family for more than 60 consecutive days.

PART II: Limits and excess
II.1  Theft: limit $20,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
II.2  Escape of Water: limit $30,000 per incident; excess $1,000 per claim.
II.3  Accidental Damage: limit $5,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
II.4  Flood: limit $20,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
II.5  Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the excess is then deducted from the result.

PART III: Escape of Water
III.1  The Insurer will pay for contents damaged by water escaping from a fixed pipe, tank or domestic appliance.
III.2  The most the Insurer will pay for Art and antiques under this section is $2,000 per incident.
III.3  The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by water leaking gradually over a period of time.
III.4  The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by the failure of grout or sealant around baths and showers.

PART IV: Theft
IV.1  The Insurer will pay for contents stolen from the Policyholder's home.
IV.2  The most the Insurer will pay for High-risk items under this section is $2,500 per incident.
IV.3  The most the Insurer will pay for Bicycles under this section is $800 per incident.
IV.4  The Insurer will not pay for theft while the home is unoccupied.
IV.5  The Insurer will not pay for theft where there is no sign of forced entry to the home. This exclusion does not apply where the thief gained entry by deception, for example by posing as a utility worker.
IV.6  The Insurer will not pay for theft from sheds, garages or other outbuildings. This exclusion does not apply if the outbuilding was locked and the theft involved forcible entry.

PART V: Flood
V.1  The Insurer will pay for contents damaged by flood water entering the Policyholder's home.
V.2  No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 14 days after the policy start date.
V.3  The most the Insurer will pay for Garden items under this section is $500 per incident.
V.4  The Insurer will not pay for flood damage where a flood warning for the Policyholder's area had been issued before the policy started.

PART VI: General exclusions
VI.1  The Insurer will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
VI.2  The Insurer will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
VI.3  The Insurer will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.

PART VII: Making a claim
VII.1  The Policyholder must notify the Insurer of a claim within 21 days of the incident. The Insurer will not pay any claim notified after that time.
VII.2  The Insurer may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
VII.3  The Policyholder must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.

policy: HOUSEHOLD CONTENTS COVER: POLICY BOOKLET
Issued by Keystone Home Mutual
In this policy, "the Insurer" means Keystone Home Mutual and "the Policyholder" means the person named in the schedule.

Article 1. Definitions
(a) Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by the Insurer, before any excess, limit or sublimit is applied.
(b) Forcible entry means entry to the home that leaves visible damage to doors, windows or locks.
(c) Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in the Policyholder's schedule.
(d) Portable electronics means laptops, tablets and mobile phones.

Article 2. Limits and excess
(a) Theft: limit $10,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
(b) Escape of Water: limit $30,000 per incident; excess $1,000 per claim.
(c) Accidental Damage: limit $3,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
(d) Flood: limit $40,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
(e) Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the excess is then deducted from the result.

Article 3. Optional cover: Accidental Damage
(a) The Insurer will pay for sudden and unexpected accidental damage to the Policyholder's contents inside the home.
(b) This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Policyholder's schedule.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Portable electronics under this section is $500 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by pets.
(e) The Insurer will not pay for wear and tear, or damage that happens gradually.

Article 4. Arbitration
(a) If the Insurer accepts a claim but disagree with the Policyholder about the amount, the difference will be referred to an arbitrator appointed by both parties.
(b) Where arbitration applies, obtaining an award is a condition precedent to any legal action against the Insurer.

Article 5. General exclusions
(a) The Insurer will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits the Insurer from paying.
(b) The Insurer will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
(c) The Insurer will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Policyholder.

Article 6. Making a claim
(a) The Insurer may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
(b) The Policyholder must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
(c) The Policyholder must notify the Insurer of a claim within 30 days of the incident. The Insurer will not pay any claim notified after that time.

state: Packet filters act by inspecting the ``packets'' which are transferred between computers on the Internet. If a packet does not match the packet filter's set of filtering rules, the packet filter will drop (silently discard) the packet or reject it (discard it, and send ``error responses'' to the source). Conversely, if the packet matches one or more of the programmed filters, the packet is allowed to pass. This type of packet filtering pays no attention to whether a packet is part of an existing stream of traffic (i.e. it stores no information on connection ``state''). Instead, it filters each packet based only on information contained in the packet itself (most commonly using a combination of the packet's source and destination address, its protocol, and, for TCP and UDP traffic, the port number). TCP and UDP protocols constitute most communication over the Internet, and because TCP and UDP traffic by convention uses well known ports for particular types of traffic, a ``stateless'' packet filter can distinguish between, and thus control, those types of traffic (such as web browsing, remote printing, email transmission, file transfer), unless the machines on each side of the packet filter are both using the same non-standard ports.

# Device Protection Plan Terms
Issued by Voltguard Protection Ltd

## 1. Definitions
- **1.1** Accessories means cases, chargers, earbuds and styluses.
- **1.2** Battery replacement means replacement batteries and battery repairs.
- **1.3** Manufacturer's warranty period means the first 24 months after the device was bought.
- **1.4** Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.
- **1.5** Wearables means smartwatches and fitness trackers.

## 2. Limits and service fee
- **2.1** Accidental Damage: limit $1,500 per incident; service fee $99 per claim.
- **2.2** Breakdown: limit $600 per incident; service fee $49 per claim.
- **2.3** Theft and Loss: limit $1,200 per incident; service fee $149 per claim.
- **2.4** Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the service fee is then deducted from the result.

## 3. Accidental Damage
- **3.1** We will repair or replace your device if it is accidentally damaged.
- **3.2** The most we will pay for Accessories under this section is $100 per incident.
- **3.3** The most we will pay for Wearables under this section is $250 per incident.
- **3.4** We will not pay for cosmetic damage, such as scratches or dents, that does not affect how the device works.
- **3.5** We will not pay for damage following a repair by anyone other than us or an authorised repairer. This exclusion does not apply if we approved the repair in writing beforehand.

## 4. Breakdown
- **4.1** We will repair or replace your device if it stops working because of an electrical or mechanical fault.
- **4.2** No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 30 days after the policy start date.
- **4.3** The most we will pay for Battery replacement under this section is $80 per incident.
- **4.4** We will not pay for breakdowns during the manufacturer's warranty period.
- **4.5** We will not pay for breakdown caused by liquid getting into the device.

## 5. General exclusions
- **5.1** We will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
- **5.2** We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
- **5.3** We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.

## 6. Making a claim
- **6.1** We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
- **6.2** You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
- **6.3** You must notify us of a claim within 14 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.

policy: GROUP HEALTH CASH PLAN
Issued by the Staff Welfare Fund
In this policy, "the Plan" means the Staff Welfare Fund and "the Member" means the person named in the schedule.

Article 1. Definitions
(a) Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by the Plan, before any deductible, limit or sublimit is applied.
(b) Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
(c) Frames means spectacle frames bought without new lenses.
(d) Major restorative work means crowns, bridges, root canal treatment and implants.
(e) Orthodontics means braces and clear aligners.
(f) Replacement period means 24 months from the date of the Member's last eyewear claim.

Article 2. Limits and deductible
(a) Dental Care: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $50 per claim.
(b) Vision Care: limit $400 per treatment; deductible $25 per claim.
(c) Therapy Services: limit $1,500 per treatment; deductible $75 per claim.
(d) Hearing Care: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $100 per claim.
(e) The deductible is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

Article 3. Dental Care
(a) The Plan will reimburse the cost of dental treatment provided by a licensed dentist.
(b) No cover applies under this section to any treatment that happens within the first 90 days after the policy start date.
(c) The most the Plan will pay for Major restorative work under this section is $500 per treatment.
(d) The most the Plan will pay for Orthodontics under this section is $800 per treatment.
(e) The Plan will not pay for treatment that is mainly cosmetic, such as whitening or veneers. This exclusion does not apply to treatment needed to repair damage caused by an accident.
(f) The Plan will not pay for treatment by a provider outside the plan's network. This exclusion does not apply to emergency treatment for sudden severe pain.

Article 4. Vision Care
(a) The Plan will reimburse eye tests and prescription eyewear.
(b) The most the Plan will pay for Frames under this section is $150 per treatment.
(c) The Plan will not pay for eyewear without prescription lenses.
(d) The Plan will not pay for a further eyewear claim within the replacement period.

Article 5. General exclusions
(a) The Plan will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Member.
(b) The Plan will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
(c) The Plan will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.

Article 6. Making a claim
(a) The Member must notify the Plan of a claim within 30 days of the treatment. The Plan will not pay any claim notified after that time.
(b) The Member must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
(c) The Plan may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

Article 7. Third-party administrators
(a) The Plan may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on the Plan's behalf.
(b) Any company the Plan appoints must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.
