Issued by Brightline Device Cover

SECTION 1 - DEFINITIONS
1.1 Accessories means cases, chargers and earbuds.
1.2 Battery replacement means replacement batteries and battery repairs.
1.3 Family means your spouse or partner and any children who live with you.
1.4 Manufacturer's warranty period means the first 12 months after the device was bought.
1.5 Replacement device means a device of the same or similar specification, which may be refurbished.

SECTION 2 - LIMITS AND SERVICE FEE
2.1 Accidental Damage: limit $1,200 per incident; service fee $79 per claim.
2.2 Breakdown: limit $600 per incident; service fee $25 per claim.
2.3 Theft and Loss: limit $800 per incident; service fee $99 per claim.
2.4 Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the service fee is then deducted from the result.

SECTION 3 - OPTIONAL COVER: THEFT AND LOSS
3.1 We will replace your device if it is stolen or lost.
3.2 This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
3.3 The most we will pay for Accessories under this section is $100 per incident.
3.4 We will not pay for loss or theft of property left unattended in a vehicle or in a public place. This exclusion does not apply to property locked out of sight in the boot or trunk of a locked vehicle.
3.5 We will not pay for theft that was not reported to the police.

SECTION 4 - BREAKDOWN
4.1 We will repair or replace your device if it stops working because of an electrical or mechanical fault.
4.2 No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 45 days after the policy start date.
4.3 The most we will pay for Battery replacement under this section is $120 per incident.
4.4 We will not pay for breakdowns during the manufacturer's warranty period.
4.5 We will not pay for breakdown caused by liquid getting into the device.

SECTION 5 - GENERAL EXCLUSIONS
5.1 We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
5.2 We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
5.3 We will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits us from paying.

SECTION 6 - MAKING A CLAIM
6.1 You must notify us of a claim within 30 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.
6.2 We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
6.3 You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.

policy: GROUP HEALTH CASH PLAN
Issued by the Benefits Trust

PART I: Definitions
I.1  Frames means spectacle frames bought without new lenses.
I.2  Hearing accessories means batteries, chargers and cleaning kits.
I.3  Hearing aid replacement period means 24 months from the purchase of hearing aids funded by the plan.
I.4  Limit means the most the Plan will pay for all claims under a section arising from one treatment.
I.5  Major restorative work means crowns, bridges, root canal treatment and implants.
I.6  Network provider means a practitioner or clinic that has an agreement with the Plan to provide treatment.
I.7  Orthodontics means braces and clear aligners.
I.8  Replacement period means 12 months from the date of the Member's last eyewear claim.

PART II: Limits and deductible
II.1  Dental Care: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $50 per claim.
II.2  Vision Care: limit $300 per treatment; deductible $25 per claim.
II.3  Therapy Services: limit $1,500 per treatment; deductible $50 per claim.
II.4  Hearing Care: limit $2,000 per treatment; deductible $100 per claim.
II.5  The deductible is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

PART III: Optional cover: Hearing Care
III.1  The Plan will reimburse hearing tests and hearing aids.
III.2  This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Member's schedule.
III.3  The most the Plan will pay for Hearing accessories under this section is $150 per treatment.
III.4  The Plan will not pay for replacement hearing aids bought within the hearing aid replacement period.

PART IV: Dental Care
IV.1  The Plan will reimburse the cost of dental treatment provided by a licensed dentist.
IV.2  No cover applies under this section to any treatment that happens within the first 60 days after the policy start date.
IV.3  The most the Plan will pay for Major restorative work under this section is $750 per treatment.
IV.4  The most the Plan will pay for Orthodontics under this section is $600 per treatment.
IV.5  The Plan will not pay for treatment that is mainly cosmetic, such as whitening or veneers. This exclusion does not apply to treatment needed to repair damage caused by an accident.
IV.6  The Plan will not pay for treatment by a provider outside the plan's network. This exclusion does not apply to emergency treatment for sudden severe pain.

PART V: Vision Care
V.1  The Plan will reimburse eye tests and prescription eyewear.
V.2  The most the Plan will pay for Frames under this section is $120 per treatment.
V.3  The Plan will not pay for eyewear without prescription lenses.
V.4  The Plan will not pay for a further eyewear claim within the replacement period.

PART VI: General exclusions
VI.1  The Plan will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
VI.2  The Plan will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits the Plan from paying.

PART VII: Making a claim
VII.1  The Plan may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
VII.2  The Member must notify the Plan of a claim within 60 days of the treatment. The Plan will not pay any claim notified after that time.
VII.3  The Member must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.

policy: ANNUAL MULTI-TRIP TRAVEL COVER
Issued by Meridian Travel Insurance Ltd
In this policy, "the Insurer" means Meridian Travel Insurance Ltd and "the Insured Person" means the person named in the schedule.

Article 1. Definitions
(a) Excursions and tickets means pre-booked excursions, tours, and event or theatre tickets.
(b) Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
(c) Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
(d) Sports equipment means skis, snowboards, golf clubs, surfboards and bicycles.
(e) Valuables means laptops, tablets, mobile phones, cameras, watches and jewellery.

Article 2. Limits and excess
(a) Baggage and Personal Belongings: limit $1,500 per incident; excess $75 per claim.
(b) Emergency Medical Expenses: limit $25,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
(c) Trip Cancellation: limit $3,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
(d) Travel Delay: limit $300 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
(e) Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the excess is then deducted from the result.

Article 3. Baggage and Personal Belongings
(a) The Insurer will pay for the loss of, theft of, or damage to the Insured Person's baggage and personal belongings during the trip.
(b) The most the Insurer will pay for Valuables under this section is $400 per incident.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Sports equipment under this section is $300 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for loss or theft of property left unattended in a vehicle or in a public place. This exclusion does not apply to property locked out of sight in the boot or trunk of a locked vehicle.
(e) The Insurer will not pay for loss caused by confiscation or detention by customs or other officials.
(f) The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by wear and tear or gradual deterioration.

Article 4. Trip Cancellation
(a) The Insurer will pay non-refundable travel and accommodation costs if the Insured Person must cancel the trip for a reason beyond the Insured Person's control.
(b) No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 7 days after the policy start date.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Excursions and tickets under this section is $200 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for cancellation caused by a strike or other event that had been publicly announced before the Insured Person bought the policy.
(e) The Insurer will not pay for cancellation because the Insured Person no longer wish to travel.

Article 5. General exclusions
(a) The Insurer will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
(b) The Insurer will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Insured Person.
(c) The Insurer will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits the Insurer from paying.

Article 6. Making a claim
(a) The Insured Person must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
(b) The Insurer may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
(c) The Insured Person must notify the Insurer of a claim within 21 days of the incident. The Insurer will not pay any claim notified after that time.

# Home Contents Insurance Policy
Issued by Lantern General Insurance

## 1. Definitions
- **1.1** Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
- **1.2** Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in your schedule.
- **1.3** Portable electronics means laptops, tablets and mobile phones.

## 2. Limits and excess
- **2.1** Theft: limit $20,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
- **2.2** Escape of Water: limit $15,000 per incident; excess $1,000 per claim.
- **2.3** Accidental Damage: limit $2,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
- **2.4** Flood: limit $20,000 per incident; excess $1,000 per claim.
- **2.5** The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

## 3. Interest
- **3.1** We will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

## 4. Optional cover: Accidental Damage
- **4.1** We will pay for sudden and unexpected accidental damage to your contents inside the home.
- **4.2** This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
- **4.3** The most we will pay for Portable electronics under this section is $500 per incident.
- **4.4** We will not pay for damage caused by pets.
- **4.5** We will not pay for wear and tear, or damage that happens gradually.

## 5. Environmental commitment
- **5.1** Where practical, we will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
- **5.2** You may ask for a new part instead, and we will tell you whether any additional cost would apply.

## 6. General exclusions
- **6.1** We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
- **6.2** We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.

## 7. Making a claim
- **7.1** We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
- **7.2** You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
- **7.3** You must notify us of a claim within 60 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.

## 8. Waiver
- **8.1** If we do not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean we have given up the right to enforce it later.

## 9. Exchange of information
- **9.1** To prevent fraud, we may check the details you give against public records and industry databases.
- **9.2** We may contact previous insurers to confirm your claims history.

## 10. Currency
- **10.1** All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
- **10.2** Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

## 11. Reasonable precautions
- **11.1** You must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
- **11.2** You must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

## 12. Electronic documents
- **12.1** We will send documents by email unless you ask for paper copies.
- **12.2** You must tell us if your email address changes.
- **12.3** Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

## 13. Accessibility
- **13.1** This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

## 14. Instalment agreements
- **14.1** If you pay by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
- **14.2** Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

state: With the MASSIVE advertising this is getting on Nickelodeon and Nick Jr. and that ilk, my son was bugging us to see it. Between DVD and the theaters, I've seen pretty much everything by now from the outstanding (Incredibles, Shrek) to the really bad (Wall-E, Brother Bear). But this was easily the worst movie I've ever seen, kids or no kids. It was a "when it this stupid thing going to end?" kind of experience? OK, it's aimed at toddlers (or it better be - it's insulting to the intelligence of anyone over 3), but I've never seen something so predictable, repetitive, and slow-moving. Then once you're finally fed up but relieved that the movie is over, there is this bizarre thing at the end that you think is the setup for a joke, but there isn't one - it's serious, though it's hard to tell what they're trying to accomplish. The 3-D effects... yeah, if you've never seen a Viewmaster they're a big deal, otherwise no (if you look at the screen without glasses, it appears to be the same process). Even my son was bored by the end. Both my wife and I looked at each other and said "wow" at the end. Bad in every respect.

PART I: Definitions
I.1  Frames means spectacle frames bought without new lenses.
I.2  Hearing accessories means batteries, chargers and cleaning kits.

I.4  Major restorative work means crowns, bridges, root canal treatment and implants.
I.5  Orthodontics means braces and clear aligners.
I.6  Premium means the amount the Member must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
I.7  Replacement period means 24 months from the date of the Member's last eyewear claim.
I.8  Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows the Member's details, the covers the Member bought and any extensions.

PART II: Limits and deductible
II.1  Dental Care: limit $1,500 per treatment; deductible $50 per claim.
II.2  Vision Care: limit $400 per treatment; deductible $40 per claim.
II.3  Therapy Services: limit $2,000 per treatment; deductible $50 per claim.
II.4  Hearing Care: limit $2,000 per treatment; deductible $100 per claim.
II.5  Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the deductible is then deducted from the result.

PART III: Dental Care
III.1  The Plan will reimburse the cost of dental treatment provided by a licensed dentist.
III.2  No cover applies under this section to any treatment that happens within the first 60 days after the policy start date.
III.3  The most the Plan will pay for Major restorative work under this section is $750 per treatment.
III.4  The most the Plan will pay for Orthodontics under this section is $800 per treatment.
III.5  The Plan will not pay for treatment that is mainly cosmetic, such as whitening or veneers. This exclusion does not apply to treatment needed to repair damage caused by an accident.
III.6  The Plan will not pay for treatment by a provider outside the plan's network. This exclusion does not apply to emergency treatment for sudden severe pain.

PART IV: Vision Care
IV.1  The Plan will reimburse eye tests and prescription eyewear.
IV.2  The most the Plan will pay for Frames under this section is $120 per treatment.
IV.3  The Plan will not pay for eyewear without prescription lenses.
IV.4  The Plan will not pay for a further eyewear claim within the replacement period.

PART V: Optional cover: Hearing Care
V.1  The Plan will reimburse hearing tests and hearing aids.
V.2  This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Member's schedule.
V.3  The most the Plan will pay for Hearing accessories under this section is $150 per treatment.
V.4  The Plan will not pay for replacement hearing aids bought within the hearing aid replacement period.

PART VI: General exclusions
VI.1  The Plan will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
VI.2  The Plan will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits the Plan from paying.

PART VII: Making a claim
VII.1  The Plan may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
VII.2  The Member must notify the Plan of a claim within 14 days of the treatment. The Plan will not pay any claim notified after that time.
VII.3  The Member must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.

state: The movie is basically the story of a Russian prostitute's return to her home village for the funeral of a sister/friend. There are a couple of other minor story lines that might actually be more interesting than the one taken, but they are not fully explored. The core of the movie is the funeral, wake, and later controversy over the future of a community of crones that make dolls and sell them to buy vodka but are now missing the artist who made their dolls marketable. Apparently, the movie is unedited. The prostitute's journey from the city to the village is an excruciatingly endless train ride and tramp through the mud. Maybe that's supposed to impress us with the immensity of the Russian landscape. The village itself, such as it is, is inhabited by a legion of widows and one male, the consort of the dead girl. Continuing the doll business is problematic for everyone involved and eventually seems impossible. Most of the film is shot with a hand-held camera that could induce nausea. Another problem for Western viewers is that subtitles don't include the songs and laments of the crones. Don't go to this movie unless you're fluent in Russian.

Issued by Keystone Home Mutual

PART I: Definitions
I.1  Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by the Insurer, before any excess, limit or sublimit is applied.
I.2  Garden items means garden furniture, plants and outdoor tools.
I.3  Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.

PART II: Limits and excess
II.1  Theft: limit $20,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
II.2  Escape of Water: limit $15,000 per incident; excess $250 per claim.
II.3  Accidental Damage: limit $5,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
II.4  Flood: limit $40,000 per incident; excess $1,000 per claim.
II.5  Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the excess is then deducted from the result.

PART III: Compensation scheme
III.1  The Insurer is covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
III.2  If the Insurer cannot meet the Insurer's obligations, the Policyholder may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

PART IV: Inflation
IV.1  The Insurer may adjust limits at renewal in line with a published index of consumer prices.
IV.2  Any adjustment will be shown in the Policyholder's renewal documents; limits do not change during a policy period.

PART V: Claims documents
V.1  The Policyholder must provide, at the Policyholder's own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence the Insurer reasonably ask for.
V.2  The Insurer may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

PART VI: Flood
VI.1  The Insurer will pay for contents damaged by flood water entering the Policyholder's home.
VI.2  No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 14 days after the policy start date.
VI.3  The most the Insurer will pay for Garden items under this section is $1,000 per incident.
VI.4  The Insurer will not pay for flood damage where a flood warning for the Policyholder's area had been issued before the policy started.

PART VII: General exclusions
VII.1  The Insurer will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
VII.2  The Insurer will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
VII.3  The Insurer will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Policyholder.

PART VIII: Making a claim
VIII.1  The Policyholder must notify the Insurer of a claim within 21 days of the incident. The Insurer will not pay any claim notified after that time.
VIII.2  The Policyholder must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
VIII.3  The Insurer may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

PART I: Definitions
I.1  Excursions and tickets means pre-booked excursions, tours, and event or theatre tickets.
I.2  Family means the Insured Person's spouse or partner and any children who live with the Insured Person.
I.3  Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in the Insured Person's schedule.
I.4  Qualifying delay means a delay to the scheduled departure of more than 12 hours.
I.5  Trip means a journey that starts and ends in the Insured Person's home country during the policy period.

PART II: Limits and excess
II.1  Baggage and Personal Belongings: limit $2,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
II.2  Emergency Medical Expenses: limit $10,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
II.3  Trip Cancellation: limit $3,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
II.4  Travel Delay: limit $300 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
II.5  Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the excess is then deducted from the result.

PART III: Trip Cancellation
III.1  The Insurer will pay non-refundable travel and accommodation costs if the Insured Person must cancel the trip for a reason beyond the Insured Person's control.
III.2  No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 10 days after the policy start date.
III.3  The most the Insurer will pay for Excursions and tickets under this section is $300 per incident.
III.4  The Insurer will not pay for cancellation caused by a strike or other event that had been publicly announced before the Insured Person bought the policy.
III.5  The Insurer will not pay for cancellation because the Insured Person no longer wish to travel.

PART IV: Optional cover: Travel Delay
IV.1  The Insurer will pay reasonable costs of meals and accommodation if the Insured Person's outbound departure is delayed.
IV.2  This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Insured Person's schedule.
IV.3  The Insurer will not pay for any delay that is not a qualifying delay.

PART V: General exclusions
V.1  The Insurer will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Insured Person.
V.2  The Insurer will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
V.3  The Insurer will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.

PART VI: Making a claim
VI.1  The Insured Person must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
VI.2  The Insured Person must notify the Insurer of a claim within 30 days of the incident. The Insurer will not pay any claim notified after that time.
VI.3  The Insurer may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

state: I was lucky enough to catch this movie while volunteering at the Maryland Film Festival. I've always been a fan of classic horror films and especially the gimmicks of William Castle, so this was definitely a must-see for me. This is about the life and work of William Castle, who in my opinion was an underrated director. True, he made some cheap budget schlocky horror films, but he added something to these films: real live theater gimmicks that you don't see anymore. For example, he had nurses in case someone had a heart attack at his movies and put vibrators at the bottoms of chairs in THE TINGLER. This is truly a well-made documentary and brings this rather shadowed director into the light, and celebrated his contributions to horror cinema. It also paints Castle as a larger than life character, who was very well-liked and had a smile on his face. Unlike most film documentaries that mostly show testaments from film historians, SPINE TINGLER! shows interviews mostly from his family members and directors who were influenced by his work, such as John Waters, John Landis, and Joe Dante. A must see for classic horror and sci-fi fans.

# Electronics Care Plan
Issued by Tessera Warranty Company

## 1. Definitions
- **1.1** Accessories means cases, chargers and earbuds.
- **1.2** Battery replacement means replacement batteries and battery repairs.
- **1.3** Family means your spouse or partner and any children who live with you.
- **1.4** Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
- **1.5** Manufacturer's warranty period means the first 24 months after the device was bought.
- **1.6** Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in your schedule.

## 2. Limits and service fee
- **2.1** Accidental Damage: limit $800 per incident; service fee $49 per claim.
- **2.2** Breakdown: limit $1,500 per incident; service fee $25 per claim.
- **2.3** Theft and Loss: limit $1,200 per incident; service fee $149 per claim.
- **2.4** The service fee is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

## 3. Breakdown
- **3.1** We will repair or replace your device if it stops working because of an electrical or mechanical fault.
- **3.2** No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 30 days after the policy start date.
- **3.3** The most we will pay for Battery replacement under this section is $80 per incident.
- **3.4** We will not pay for breakdowns during the manufacturer's warranty period.
- **3.5** We will not pay for breakdown caused by liquid getting into the device.

## 4. Optional cover: Theft and Loss
- **4.1** We will replace your device if it is stolen or lost.
- **4.2** This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
- **4.3** The most we will pay for Accessories under this section is $100 per incident.
- **4.4** We will not pay for loss or theft of property left unattended in a vehicle or in a public place. This exclusion does not apply to property locked out of sight in the boot or trunk of a locked vehicle.
- **4.5** We will not pay for theft that was not reported to the police.

## 5. General exclusions
- **5.1** We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
- **5.2** We will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by you.

## 6. Making a claim
- **6.1** You must notify us of a claim within 90 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.
- **6.2** You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
- **6.3** We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

## 7. Renewal
- **7.1** We will write to you at least 21 days before the end of the policy period with the renewal terms.
- **7.2** We are not obliged to offer renewal.

## 8. Exchange of information
- **8.1** To prevent fraud, we may check the details you give against public records and industry databases.
- **8.2** We may contact previous insurers to confirm your claims history.

state: document: This film is pure, distilled, unadulterated boredom. I knew nothing of it before I entered the dark room, took my seat. I was seduced by the "mysterious and suspenseful" blurb on the poster I suppose. Also, Lena Headey is nice and unconventionally sexy, and Richard Jenkins is always a reliable guy to have around, so the cast seemed reasonable. It may have been his name above the title that convinced me to go with this instead of whatever else was on. I should've gone to see Valkyrie for the second time instead. The thin plot revolves around Headley's Gina McVey, her boyfriend, her father, her sister and her sister's husband who for some reason are being stalked, in a very louche and unenthusiastic manner, by their evil doppelgangers who emerge from mirrors that mysteriously smash. There could be a great film behind this idea (not exactly an original idea, mind you, but still...) and in fact, if the filmmakers had shorn away all the supporting cast and simply stuck to Headey's character's story, The Broken could've made a reasonable 20-minute short. As it is, it is desperately unmotivated and boring, and terribly inconsistent. For instance, in one scene, a mirror smashes on its own in a room housing all the main characters; they look puzzled but quickly forget about it.

# Employee Health Benefits Plan: Summary Plan Description
Issued by Wellspring Benefits Administration

## 1. Definitions
- **1.1** Massage therapy means sports massage, massage therapy and reflexology.
- **1.2** Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
- **1.3** Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows your details, the covers you bought and any extensions.

## 2. Limits and deductible
- **2.1** Dental Care: limit $1,500 per treatment; deductible $50 per claim.
- **2.2** Vision Care: limit $400 per treatment; deductible $40 per claim.
- **2.3** Therapy Services: limit $2,000 per treatment; deductible $75 per claim.
- **2.4** Hearing Care: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $100 per claim.
- **2.5** The deductible is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

## 3. Therapy Services
- **3.1** We will reimburse physiotherapy, osteopathy and counselling provided by a registered practitioner.
- **3.2** The most we will pay for Massage therapy under this section is $200 per treatment.
- **3.3** We will not pay for treatment of an injury covered by workers' compensation.
- **3.4** We will not pay for treatment by a practitioner who is not registered with the relevant professional body.

## 4. General exclusions
- **4.1** We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
- **4.2** We will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits us from paying.

## 5. Making a claim
- **5.1** You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
- **5.2** You must notify us of a claim within 14 days of the treatment. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.
- **5.3** We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

## 6. Salvage
- **6.1** When we replace an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes our property.
- **6.2** If stolen property is recovered after we have paid a claim, you must tell us and either return the payment or give us the property.

## 7. Payment of claims
- **7.1** We will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in your name.
- **7.2** We aim to pay accepted claims within 15 working days of receiving all the documents we need.

## 8. Reasonable precautions
- **8.1** You must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
- **8.2** You must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

## 9. Cooperation
- **9.1** You must give us all the help and information we reasonably need to settle a claim.
- **9.2** You must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without our written permission.

## 10. Currency
- **10.1** All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
- **10.2** Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

## 11. Claims documents
- **11.1** You must provide, at your own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence we reasonably ask for.
- **11.2** We may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

SECTION 1 - DEFINITIONS
1.1 Bicycles means bicycles and electric scooters.
1.2 Garden items means garden furniture, plants and outdoor tools.
1.3 High-risk items means jewellery, watches, laptops, games consoles and cameras.
1.4 Home means the private residence at the address shown in the schedule.
1.5 Premium means the amount you must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
1.6 Unoccupied means not lived in by you or a member of your family for more than 30 consecutive days.

SECTION 2 - LIMITS AND EXCESS
2.1 Theft: limit $40,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
2.2 Escape of Water: limit $30,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
2.3 Accidental Damage: limit $3,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
2.4 Flood: limit $20,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
2.5 Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the excess is then deducted from the result.

SECTION 3 - THEFT
3.1 We will pay for contents stolen from your home.
3.2 The most we will pay for High-risk items under this section is $1,500 per incident.
3.3 The most we will pay for Bicycles under this section is $500 per incident.
3.4 We will not pay for theft while the home is unoccupied.
3.5 We will not pay for theft where there is no sign of forced entry to the home. This exclusion does not apply where the thief gained entry by deception, for example by posing as a utility worker.
3.6 We will not pay for theft from sheds, garages or other outbuildings. This exclusion does not apply if the outbuilding was locked and the theft involved forcible entry.

SECTION 4 - FLOOD
4.1 We will pay for contents damaged by flood water entering your home.
4.2 No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 60 days after the policy start date.
4.3 The most we will pay for Garden items under this section is $500 per incident.
4.4 We will not pay for flood damage where a flood warning for your area had been issued before the policy started.

SECTION 5 - GENERAL EXCLUSIONS
5.1 We will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits us from paying.
5.2 We will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.

SECTION 6 - MAKING A CLAIM
6.1 You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
6.2 You must notify us of a claim within 14 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.
6.3 We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

SECTION 7 - SALVAGE
7.1 When we replace an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes our property.
7.2 If stolen property is recovered after we have paid a claim, you must tell us and either return the payment or give us the property.

# Home Contents Insurance Policy
Issued by Lantern General Insurance

## 1. Definitions
- **1.1** Art and antiques means paintings, antiques, rugs and other works of art.
- **1.2** Family means your spouse or partner and any children who live with you.
- **1.3** Garden items means garden furniture, plants and outdoor tools.
- **1.4** Outbuilding means a shed, garage or greenhouse within the boundaries of the home.

## 2. Limits and excess
- **2.1** Theft: limit $10,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
- **2.2** Escape of Water: limit $15,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
- **2.3** Accidental Damage: limit $5,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
- **2.4** Flood: limit $20,000 per incident; excess $1,000 per claim.
- **2.5** Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the excess is then deducted from the result.

## 3. Escape of Water
- **3.1** We will pay for contents damaged by water escaping from a fixed pipe, tank or domestic appliance.
- **3.2** The most we will pay for Art and antiques under this section is $2,000 per incident.
- **3.3** We will not pay for damage caused by water leaking gradually over a period of time.
- **3.4** We will not pay for damage caused by the failure of grout or sealant around baths and showers.

## 4. Flood
- **4.1** We will pay for contents damaged by flood water entering your home.
- **4.2** No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 30 days after the policy start date.
- **4.3** The most we will pay for Garden items under this section is $500 per incident.
- **4.4** We will not pay for flood damage where a flood warning for your area had been issued before the policy started.

## 5. General exclusions
- **5.1** We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
- **5.2** We will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.

## 6. Making a claim
- **6.1** You must notify us of a claim within 30 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.
- **6.2** You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
- **6.3** We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

The building is a converted warehouse with six flats.

I am sending this on June 7, 2026, which is when I first notified you. Your adjuster assessed the loss at $844.

Thanks,
Rosa

This is not the same as the atomic number (Z) which denotes the number of protons in a nucleus, and thus uniquely identifies an element. policy: EMPLOYEE HEALTH BENEFITS PLAN: SUMMARY PLAN DESCRIPTION
Issued by Cedar Benefits Services
In this policy, "the Plan" means Cedar Benefits Services and "the Member" means the person named in the schedule.

Article 1. Definitions
(a) Major restorative work means crowns, bridges, root canal treatment and implants.
(b) Massage therapy means sports massage, massage therapy and reflexology.
(c) Orthodontics means braces and clear aligners.
(d) Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.

Article 2. Limits and deductible
(a) Dental Care: limit $2,000 per treatment; deductible $50 per claim.
(b) Vision Care: limit $400 per treatment; deductible $25 per claim.
(c) Therapy Services: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $75 per claim.
(d) Hearing Care: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $150 per claim.
(e) The deductible is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

Article 3. Dental Care
(a) The Plan will reimburse the cost of dental treatment provided by a licensed dentist.
(b) No cover applies under this section to any treatment that happens within the first 60 days after the policy start date.
(c) The most the Plan will pay for Major restorative work under this section is $750 per treatment.
(d) The most the Plan will pay for Orthodontics under this section is $800 per treatment.
(e) The Plan will not pay for treatment that is mainly cosmetic, such as whitening or veneers. This exclusion does not apply to treatment needed to repair damage caused by an accident.
(f) The Plan will not pay for treatment by a provider outside the plan's network. This exclusion does not apply to emergency treatment for sudden severe pain.

Article 4. Therapy Services
(a) The Plan will reimburse physiotherapy, osteopathy and counselling provided by a registered practitioner.
(b) The most the Plan will pay for Massage therapy under this section is $300 per treatment.
(c) The Plan will not pay for treatment of an injury covered by workers' compensation.
(d) The Plan will not pay for treatment by a practitioner who is not registered with the relevant professional body.

Article 5. Interpretation
(a) Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
(b) Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
(c) Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

Article 6. Complaints
(a) If the Member has a complaint, the Member should first contact the Plan's customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
(b) The Plan will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
(c) If the Member remains dissatisfied, the Member may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

Article 7. General exclusions
(a) The Plan will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Member.
(b) The Plan will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
(c) The Plan will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits the Plan from paying.

Article 8. Fraud
(a) If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, the Plan will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
(b) The Plan may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

Article 9. Making a claim
(a) The Plan may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
(b) The Member must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
(c) The Member must notify the Plan of a claim within 30 days of the treatment. The Plan will not pay any claim notified after that time.

Article 10. Renewal
(a) The Plan will write to the Member at least 21 days before the end of the policy period with the renewal terms.
(b) The Plan is not obliged to offer renewal.

Shirking from a frank examination of these two characters' personalities, 'The Art of Seduction' eschews anything of substance for a basis of thin, lean stereotype. 'The Art of Seduction' is insulting - insulting to its characters, insulting to men and women, and insulting to its audiences' expectations. It takes the awful beautiful people we all know and plays out their painful interactions while expecting us to idolize them. Ji-wan is an immature, spoiled, manipulative bitch. The viewer is expected to like and forgive her flaws because she's pretty. Min-jun, well, he's exactly the same. Neither are nice people. The "humour" in this film primarily revolve around Ji-wan and Min-jun's outlandish attempts at outdoing each other in the honourable art of lying and manipulation. No character development occurs, and we never learn why Ji-wan and Min-jun are like this. We are simply expected to take them as they are, and not ask questions - they're

policy: TRAVEL INSURANCE POLICY WORDING
Issued by Compass Mutual
In this policy, "the Insurer" means Compass Mutual and "the Insured Person" means the person named in the schedule.

Article 1. Definitions
(a) Excursions and tickets means pre-booked excursions, tours, and event or theatre tickets.
(b) Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
(c) Qualifying delay means a delay to the scheduled departure of more than 6 hours.

Article 2. Limits and excess
(a) Baggage and Personal Belongings: limit $3,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
(b) Emergency Medical Expenses: limit $50,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
(c) Trip Cancellation: limit $5,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
(d) Travel Delay: limit $500 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
(e) Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the excess is then deducted from the result.

Article 3. Trip Cancellation
(a) The Insurer will pay non-refundable travel and accommodation costs if the Insured Person must cancel the trip for a reason beyond the Insured Person's control.
(b) No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 10 days after the policy start date.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Excursions and tickets under this section is $200 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for cancellation caused by a strike or other event that had been publicly announced before the Insured Person bought the policy.
(e) The Insurer will not pay for cancellation because the Insured Person no longer wish to travel.

Article 4. Optional cover: Travel Delay
(a) The Insurer will pay reasonable costs of meals and accommodation if the Insured Person's outbound departure is delayed.
(b) This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Insured Person's schedule.
(c) The Insurer will not pay for any delay that is not a qualifying delay.

Article 5. General exclusions
(a) The Insurer will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
(b) The Insurer will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.

Article 6. Making a claim
(a) The Insurer may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
(b) The Insured Person must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
(c) The Insured Person must notify the Insurer of a claim within 14 days of the incident. The Insurer will not pay any claim notified after that time.

Article 7. How to read this document
(a) This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.
(b) Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
(c) Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

Article 8. Waiver

## 1. Definitions
- **1.1** Accessories means cases, chargers, earbuds and styluses.

- **5.3** We will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.

PART X: Dependants
X.1  The Member may enrol dependants at the start of each plan year or within 30 days of a qualifying life event.
X.2  Benefits paid for dependants count towards the same annual limits as the Member's own claims.

III.1  The Provider will repair or replace the Customer's device if it is accidentally damaged.
III.2  The most the Provider will pay for Accessories under this section is $100 per incident.

state: Good Samaritan laws offer legal protection to people who give reasonable assistance to those who are, or who they believe to be, injured, ill, in peril, or otherwise incapacitated. The protection is intended to reduce bystanders' hesitation to assist, for fear of being sued or prosecuted for unintentional injury or wrongful death. An example of such a law in common-law areas of Canada: a good Samaritan doctrine is a legal principle that prevents a rescuer who has voluntarily helped a victim in distress from being successfully sued for wrongdoing. Its purpose is to keep people from being reluctant to help a stranger in need for fear of legal repercussions should they make some mistake in treatment. By contrast, a duty to rescue law requires people to offer assistance and holds those who fail to do so liable.

policy: HOUSEHOLD CONTENTS COVER: POLICY BOOKLET
Issued by Hearthstone Insurance plc

PART I: Definitions
I.1  Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by the Insurer, before any excess, limit or sublimit is applied.
I.2  Bicycles means bicycles and electric scooters.
I.3  High-risk items means jewellery, watches, laptops, games consoles and cameras.
I.4  Portable electronics means laptops, tablets and mobile phones.
I.5  Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows the Policyholder's details, the covers the Policyholder bought and any extensions.
I.6  Unoccupied means not lived in by the Policyholder or a member of the Policyholder's family for more than 30 consecutive days.

PART II: Limits and excess
II.1  Theft: limit $10,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
II.2  Escape of Water: limit $15,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
II.3  Accidental Damage: limit $2,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
II.4  Flood: limit $40,000 per incident; excess $1,000 per claim.
II.5  Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the excess is then deducted from the result.

PART III: Optional cover: Accidental Damage
III.1  The Insurer will pay for sudden and unexpected accidental damage to the Policyholder's contents inside the home.
III.2  This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Policyholder's schedule.
III.3  The most the Insurer will pay for Portable electronics under this section is $500 per incident.
III.4  The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by pets.
III.5  The Insurer will not pay for wear and tear, or damage that happens gradually.

PART IV: Theft
IV.1  The Insurer will pay for contents stolen from the Policyholder's home.
IV.2  The most the Insurer will pay for High-risk items under this section is $1,500 per incident.
IV.3  The most the Insurer will pay for Bicycles under this section is $800 per incident.
IV.4  The Insurer will not pay for theft while the home is unoccupied.
IV.5  The Insurer will not pay for theft where there is no sign of forced entry to the home. This exclusion does not apply where the thief gained entry by deception, for example by posing as a utility worker.
IV.6  The Insurer will not pay for theft from sheds, garages or other outbuildings. This exclusion does not apply if the outbuilding was locked and the theft involved forcible entry.

PART V: General exclusions
V.1  The Insurer will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits the Insurer from paying.
V.2  The Insurer will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Policyholder.
V.3  The Insurer will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
